events.title: Mor Gabriel Monastery is founded and located on the Tur Abdin plateau near…
events.blurb: Mor Gabriel Monastery is founded and located on the Tur Abdin plateau near Midyat (Turkey).

events.title: The Xiongnu occupy the Gansu area, an economically important province situated…
events.blurb: The Xiongnu occupy the Gansu area, an economically important province situated along the Silk Road.

events.title: Sulpicius Severus writes the earliest biography of Martin of Tours, the first…
events.blurb: Sulpicius Severus writes the earliest biography of Martin of Tours, the first known "life of a saint" ever written.

events.title: Revolt of Alaric I
events.blurb: Revolt of Alaric I: Stilicho traps the Visigoths under King Alaric in the Peloponnese, but decides to abandon the campaign against the Visigoths in Greece, thus allowing King Alaric to escape north to Epirus with his loot.

events.title: Ambrose, Archbishop of Milan, dies in his diocese after 23 years in office,…
events.blurb: Ambrose, Archbishop of Milan, dies in his diocese after 23 years in office, during which he dominated the political life of the Roman Empire.

events.title: First Council of Toledo
events.blurb: First Council of Toledo: Hispanic bishops, including Lampius, condemn Priscillianism.

events.title: John Chrysostom is appointed Archbishop of Constantinople
events.blurb: John Chrysostom is appointed Archbishop of Constantinople.

events.title: Gildonic Revolt
events.blurb: Gildonic Revolt: Gildo, a Berber serving as a high-ranking official (comes) in Mauretania, rebels against the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Eutropius, Roman general (magister militum), celebrates his victory over the…
events.blurb: Eutropius, Roman general (magister militum), celebrates his victory over the Huns ("the wolves of the North") in a parade through Constantinople (see 395).

events.title: Flavius Mallius Theodorus becomes Roman consul and official at the imperial…
events.blurb: Flavius Mallius Theodorus becomes Roman consul and official at the imperial court of emperor Arcadius.

events.title: Flavian I is acknowledged as legitimate bishop of Antioch by the Church of Rome
events.blurb: Flavian I is acknowledged as legitimate bishop of Antioch by the Church of Rome.

events.title: Fa-Hien, Chinese Buddhist monk, travels to India, Sri Lanka and Kapilavastu…
events.blurb: Fa-Hien, Chinese Buddhist monk, travels to India, Sri Lanka and Kapilavastu (modern Nepal).

events.title: King Bahram IV dies after an 11-year reign
events.blurb: King Bahram IV dies after an 11-year reign. He is succeeded by Yazdegerd I, who becomes the thirteenth Sassanid Emperor of Persia.

events.title: Gainas, a Gothic leader, is made magister militum and forms an alliance with…
events.blurb: Gainas, a Gothic leader, is made magister militum and forms an alliance with deserters of Tribigild along the Bosphorus. He proclaims himself co-regent (usurper), and installs his forces in Constantinople.

events.title: Xianbei kingdom of Southern Yan conquers Qing Province (modern central and…
events.blurb: Xianbei kingdom of Southern Yan conquers Qing Province (modern central and eastern Shandong) from the Eastern Jin.

events.title: Pope Siricius dies at Rome after a 15-year reign in which he has commanded…
events.blurb: Pope Siricius dies at Rome after a 15-year reign in which he has commanded celibacy for priests, asserted papal authority over the entire Western Church, and threatened to impose sanctions on those who do not follow his dictates.

events.title: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali are composed
events.blurb: The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali are composed.

events.title: Hypatia, Greek philosopher, distinguishes herself as one of the first female…
events.blurb: Hypatia, Greek philosopher, distinguishes herself as one of the first female scientists and becomes head of the Neo-Platonist school at Alexandria.

events.title: The Vergilius Vaticanus, an illuminated manuscript containing fragments of…
events.blurb: The Vergilius Vaticanus, an illuminated manuscript containing fragments of Virgil's Aeneid and Georgics, is made in Rome.

events.title: Danube
events.blurb: Winter – Gainas leads the remaining Goths back to their homeland across the Danube. They meet the Huns and are defeated; the Hunnic chieftain Uldin sends the head of Gainas to Constantinople, where Arcadius receives it as a diplomatic gift.

events.title: Resurrection and "Two Marys with Angel near the Empty Tomb", panel of a…
events.blurb: Resurrection and "Two Marys with Angel near the Empty Tomb", panel of a diptych, found in Rome, is made. It is now kept at Castello Sforzesco, Milan (approximate date).

events.title: The Paeonians (Illyricum) lose their identity (approximate date)
events.blurb: The Paeonians (Illyricum) lose their identity (approximate date).

events.title: Caelius Aurelianus, Roman physician, is practising his work "De morbis acutis…
events.blurb: Caelius Aurelianus, Roman physician, is practising his work "De morbis acutis et chronicis" (Concerning Acute and Chronic Illness), a guide to acute and chronic diseases.

events.title: Bishops from Gaza (Palaestina Prima) arrive at Constantinople to ask Arcadius…
events.blurb: Bishops from Gaza (Palaestina Prima) arrive at Constantinople to ask Arcadius that he close the pagan temple of Marnas.

events.title: Richū, the eldest son of Nintoku, becomes the 17th Emperor of Japan
events.blurb: Richū, the eldest son of Nintoku, becomes the 17th Emperor of Japan.

events.title: Anthemius, praetorian prefect of the East, is sent on an embassy to the…
events.blurb: Anthemius, praetorian prefect of the East, is sent on an embassy to the Persian capital, Ctesiphon, to congratulate King Yazdegerd I on his accession the year before.

events.title: Emperor Arcadius gives his wife Aelia Eudoxia the official title of Augusta
events.blurb: Emperor Arcadius gives his wife Aelia Eudoxia the official title of Augusta. She is able to wear the purple paludamentum and is depicted in Roman currency.

events.title: The old Legio II Adiutrix, part of which had always been stationed at Aquincum…
events.blurb: The old Legio II Adiutrix, part of which had always been stationed at Aquincum (modern Budapest), is divided into two comitatenses, and shipped to Britannia.

events.title: The Chronicon Pachale (Paschal Chronicle) reports that the Black Sea is…
events.blurb: The Chronicon Pachale (Paschal Chronicle) reports that the Black Sea is completely frozen.

events.title: Stilicho, Roman general (magister militum), leads his army in an extensive…
events.blurb: Stilicho, Roman general (magister militum), leads his army in an extensive campaign against the Vandals in Rhaetia (Switzerland).

events.title: The Temple of Artemis near Selçuk in Ephesus is dismantled
events.blurb: The Temple of Artemis near Selçuk in Ephesus is dismantled.

events.title: The Mahabharata, an Indian Sanskrit epic, is finalised
events.blurb: The Mahabharata, an Indian Sanskrit epic, is finalised.

events.title: The Visigoths, led by king Alaric I, cross the Alps and invade northern Italy
events.blurb: The Visigoths, led by king Alaric I, cross the Alps and invade northern Italy.

events.title: Pope Anastasius I dies at Rome after a 2-year reign, and is succeeded by…
events.blurb: Pope Anastasius I dies at Rome after a 2-year reign, and is succeeded by Innocent I as the 40th pope proclaiming his universal power over the whole of Christendom.

events.title: The Rouran, led by Shelun (Chö-louen), having defeated the Gaoju Dingling…
events.blurb: The Rouran, led by Shelun (Chö-louen), having defeated the Gaoju Dingling (Kao-kiu Ting-ling) near Kobbo, establish a nomadic empire that ranges from the Mongolian Plateau to the Irtysh.

events.title: Cynegius, acting for Emperor Arcadius at the insistence of Bishop Porphyry,…
events.blurb: Cynegius, acting for Emperor Arcadius at the insistence of Bishop Porphyry, orders the destruction of pagan temples in Gaza.

events.title: Jerome writes "Apologiae contra Rufinum" and "Liber tertius seu ultima…
events.blurb: Jerome writes "Apologiae contra Rufinum" and "Liber tertius seu ultima responsio adversus scripta Rufini".

events.title: Silseong becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla
events.blurb: Silseong becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla.

events.title: King Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo (Korea) defeats the forces of Later Yan,…
events.blurb: King Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo (Korea) defeats the forces of Later Yan, seizing some of their border fortresses.

events.title: The Pure Land school of Buddhism founds a monastery upon the top of Mount Lushan
events.blurb: The Pure Land school of Buddhism founds a monastery upon the top of Mount Lushan.

events.title: Battle of Pollentia
events.blurb: Battle of Pollentia: Stilicho recalls troops from Britain and the Rhine frontier to defend Italy. He decides to attack the Goths on Easter Sunday, and manages to capture Alaric's wife and children.

events.title: Hui Yuan argues that Buddhist monks should be exempt from bowing to the emperor
events.blurb: Hui Yuan argues that Buddhist monks should be exempt from bowing to the emperor.

events.title: The Synod of the Oak deposes and banishes John Chrysostom, bishop of…
events.blurb: The Synod of the Oak deposes and banishes John Chrysostom, bishop of Constantinople, but shortly afterward he is recalled only to be banished again.

events.title: Battle of Verona
events.blurb: Battle of Verona: The Visigoths, under command of King Alaric I, invade Italy again, and advance through the Brenner Pass. Stilicho, with an army of 30,000 men, defeats the Goths north of Verona.

events.title: The Armenian alphabet is devised by Mesrop Mashtots
events.blurb: The Armenian alphabet is devised by Mesrop Mashtots.

events.title: War of Radagaisus
events.blurb: War of Radagaisus: King Radagaisus leads an invasion with a force of 20,000 men and crosses the Alps.

events.title: In the Roman province of Africa, Augustine of Hippo opposes Donatism as a heresy
events.blurb: In the Roman province of Africa, Augustine of Hippo opposes Donatism as a heresy.

events.title: Flavius Aetius is sent as a child hostage at the court of Alaric I, king of…
events.blurb: Flavius Aetius is sent as a child hostage at the court of Alaric I, king of the Visigoths.

events.title: The Khitan are first mentioned in Chinese chronicles
events.blurb: The Khitan are first mentioned in Chinese chronicles. They wander along the boundaries of Kara-muren, and form part of the Donghu (Tong-hou) confederation.

events.title: Theon of Alexandria, Greek mathematician, dies at age 70 (approximate), having…
events.blurb: Theon of Alexandria, Greek mathematician, dies at age 70 (approximate), having been helped in his work by his daughter Hypatia.

events.title: Jeonji becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje
events.blurb: Jeonji becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

events.title: Stained glass is used for the first time in churches in Rome
events.blurb: Stained glass is used for the first time in churches in Rome.

events.title: Roman legion
events.blurb: Autumn – The remaining Roman legions in Britain decide to mutiny. The usurper Marcus is proclaimed emperor.

events.title: Hanzei succeeds his brother Richu, and becomes the 18th emperor of Japan in…
events.blurb: Hanzei succeeds his brother Richu, and becomes the 18th emperor of Japan in the traditional order of succession.

events.title: Radagaisus is forced to retreat into the hills of Fiesole
events.blurb: Radagaisus is forced to retreat into the hills of Fiesole. There he tries to escape, but is captured by the Romans.

events.title: Radagaisus is executed
events.blurb: Radagaisus is executed; 12,000 "barbarians" are incorporated into the Roman army, or sold as slaves.

events.title: Autumn - Resistance of Honorius cousins
events.blurb: Autumn - Resistance of Honorius cousins: In Spain comes Constans II into conflict with Didymus and Verinianus, nephews and followers of Honorius.

events.title: Liu Bobo (Xia Wuliedi) founds the state of Xia, and claims the title "Heavenly…
events.blurb: Liu Bobo (Xia Wuliedi) founds the state of Xia, and claims the title "Heavenly Prince" (Tian Wang).

events.title: Gratian, Roman usurper, is installed as emperor after the death of Marcus
events.blurb: Gratian, Roman usurper, is installed as emperor after the death of Marcus. According to Orosius, he is a native Briton of the urban aristocracy.

events.title: End of Roman rule in Britain
events.blurb: End of Roman rule in Britain: After 360 years of occupation, the local regional British-Roman leaders raise their own levies for defence against Saxon sea rovers. They cultivate oysters, having learned the technique from the Romans.

events.title: The Roman usurper Constantine III establishes his headquarters at Arles…
events.blurb: The Roman usurper Constantine III establishes his headquarters at Arles (Southern Gaul) and elevates his eldest son, Constans, to the rank of Caesar.

events.title: King Yazdegerd I of Persia maintains cordial relations with the Roman Empire
events.blurb: King Yazdegerd I of Persia maintains cordial relations with the Roman Empire. He becomes an executor of Arcadius' will and is entrusted with the care of the young Theodosius II until he comes of age.

events.title: The Hexamilion wall is constructed
events.blurb: The Hexamilion wall is constructed. Fortifications are built across the Isthmus of Corinth, guarding the only land route into the Peloponnese peninsula from Greece.

events.title: The Huns under Uldin cross the lower Danube and attack the Eastern Roman…
events.blurb: The Huns under Uldin cross the lower Danube and attack the Eastern Roman Empire, setting fire to frontier forts and taking control of the Castra Martis (modern Bulgaria).

events.title: Attila, age 2, is sent as a child hostage to the court at Rome and in return,…
events.blurb: Attila, age 2, is sent as a child hostage to the court at Rome and in return, the Romans send Flavius Aetius to the Huns.

events.title: During a review of troops at Pavia, the soldiers stationed at this city murder…
events.blurb: During a review of troops at Pavia, the soldiers stationed at this city murder the dignitaries present, then rage through the city, slaying anyone they suspected of being a supporter of Stilicho.

events.title: Rex Alaric I of the Visigoths crosses the Julian Alps with an army of 30,000…
events.blurb: Rex Alaric I of the Visigoths crosses the Julian Alps with an army of 30,000 men, and marches into the Roman heartland. He lays siege to Rome, and Gothic auxiliaries desert to join Alaric's forces.

events.title: Mingyuan, age 17, succeeds Daowu as emperor of the Chinese Northern Wei (one…
events.blurb: Mingyuan, age 17, succeeds Daowu as emperor of the Chinese Northern Wei (one of the Northern dynasties).

events.title: Bacaudic Rebellion
events.blurb: Bacaudic Rebellion: Peasants in Armorica, northwestern Gallia launch a revolt. The unrest continues until 417.

events.title: Gerontius (magister militum)
events.blurb: Spring – Gerontius, Roman general (magister militum), who had been a partisan of Constantine III, revolts in Hispania. He elevates Maximus, his domesticus, as emperor.

events.title: The Vandals, led by King Gunderic, cross the Pyrenees into the Iberian Peninsula
events.blurb: The Vandals, led by King Gunderic, cross the Pyrenees into the Iberian Peninsula. They receive land from the Romans, as foederati, in Baetica (Southern Spain). The Alans occupy lands in Lusitania and the Suebi control parts of Gallaecia.

events.title: The Eastern Roman Empire sends six legions (6,000 men) to aid Honorius at Ravenna
events.blurb: The Eastern Roman Empire sends six legions (6,000 men) to aid Honorius at Ravenna. He negotiates with King Alaric I, who ceremonially deposes Priscus Attalus as co-emperor.

events.title: Alaric I marches southwards into Calabria and makes plans to invade Africa
events.blurb: Alaric I marches southwards into Calabria and makes plans to invade Africa. But a storm destroys his Gothic fleet and many of his soldiers drown.

events.title: Raiders from Ireland, such as the Uí Liatháin and Laigin, harry the coasts of…
events.blurb: Raiders from Ireland, such as the Uí Liatháin and Laigin, harry the coasts of Wales.

events.title: The city of Aléria on the island of Corsica is devastated by a huge fire,…
events.blurb: The city of Aléria on the island of Corsica is devastated by a huge fire, destroying its port and most of its inhabitants.

events.title: According to Zosimus, this is the year when Emperor Honorius sends his…
events.blurb: According to Zosimus, this is the year when Emperor Honorius sends his Rescript (diplomatic letters) to the Romano-British magistrates, ending Roman rule in Great Britain. However this is likely an example of scribal error.

events.title: Council of Seleucia
events.blurb: Council of Seleucia: Persian Christians create a national church and adopt the Nicene Creed.

events.title: Honoratus founds the Monastery of Lérins on the île Saint-Honorat (France),…
events.blurb: Honoratus founds the Monastery of Lérins on the île Saint-Honorat (France), and forms a monastic community.

events.title: At around this time, one of the first Anglo-Saxon settlements in Britain,…
events.blurb: At around this time, one of the first Anglo-Saxon settlements in Britain, Mucking, is established by the mouth of the Thames River. (approximate date)

events.title: An edict of Honorius outlaws Donatism
events.blurb: An edict of Honorius outlaws Donatism.

events.title: Lazarus, bishop of Aix-en-Provence, and Heros, bishop of Arles, are expelled…
events.blurb: Lazarus, bishop of Aix-en-Provence, and Heros, bishop of Arles, are expelled from their sees on a charge of Manichaeism.

events.title: Cyril of Alexandria becomes Patriarch of Alexandria
events.blurb: Cyril of Alexandria becomes Patriarch of Alexandria.

events.title: Olympiodorus of Thebes
events.blurb: Winter – Olympiodorus, historical writer, is sent on an embassy by Honorius, and sails in stormy weather around Greece up the Black Sea, to meet the Huns who are located on the middle Danube (modern Bulgaria).

events.title: Emperor Jovinus elevates his brother Sebastianus as co-emperor (Augustus) and…
events.blurb: Emperor Jovinus elevates his brother Sebastianus as co-emperor (Augustus) and takes control of Gaul.

events.title: Heraclianus, governor (Comes Africae), revolts against Honorius and proclaims…
events.blurb: Heraclianus, governor (Comes Africae), revolts against Honorius and proclaims himself Augustus. He interrupts the grain supply to Rome. Honorius condemns him and his supporters to death with an edict at Ravenna.

events.title: Kumaragupta I succeeds his father Chandragupta II as emperor of the Gupta…
events.blurb: Kumaragupta I succeeds his father Chandragupta II as emperor of the Gupta Empire (India).

events.title: Jangsu becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo
events.blurb: Jangsu becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

events.title: The Southern Liang, a state of the Sixteen Kingdoms during the Jin Dynasty,…
events.blurb: The Southern Liang, a state of the Sixteen Kingdoms during the Jin Dynasty, comes to an end.

events.title: Abdas, bishop of Susa, burns down a Zoroastrian temple
events.blurb: Abdas, bishop of Susa, burns down a Zoroastrian temple; in retaliation, King Yazdegerd I of Persia orders the destruction of churches.

events.title: Priscus Attalus is proclaimed rival emperor by the Visigoths for a second time…
events.blurb: Priscus Attalus is proclaimed rival emperor by the Visigoths for a second time at Bordeaux, in order to impose their terms on Honorius, who has his residence in Ravenna.

events.title: Galla Placidia, half-sister of emperor Honorius, is married to the Visigothic…
events.blurb: Galla Placidia, half-sister of emperor Honorius, is married to the Visigothic king Ataulf at Narbonne. The wedding is celebrated with Roman festivities and magnificent gifts from the Gothic booty.

events.title: Emperor Theodosius II, age 13, yields power to his older sister Aelia…
events.blurb: Emperor Theodosius II, age 13, yields power to his older sister Aelia Pulcheria, who reigns as regent and proclaims herself empress (Augusta) of the Eastern Roman Empire.

events.title: The Visigoths invade the Iberian Peninsula and begin to conquer territory…
events.blurb: The Visigoths invade the Iberian Peninsula and begin to conquer territory taken previously by the Vandals. King Athaulf and his pregnant wife Galla Placidia leave Gallia Narbonensis; they relocate at Barcelona.

events.title: Wallia
events.blurb: Autumn – Wallia, brother of Athaulf, becomes king of the Visigoths. He accepts a peace treaty with emperor Honorius, in return for a supply of 600,000 measures of grain. After the negotiations he sends Placidia to Rome with hostages.

events.title: John Cassian, Christian theologian, settles at a monastery in Marseille (Gaul)
events.blurb: John Cassian, Christian theologian, settles at a monastery in Marseille (Gaul); he organizes monastic communities after an eastern model.

events.title: The Daysan River floods Edessa, Mesopotamia
events.blurb: The Daysan River floods Edessa, Mesopotamia.

events.title: Rutilius Claudius Namatianus begins his journey home from Rome to Gaul
events.blurb: Rutilius Claudius Namatianus begins his journey home from Rome to Gaul. This becomes the subject of his unfinished poem, De Reditu Suo.

events.title: Exuperantius suppresses the Bagaudae Revolt in Armorica
events.blurb: Exuperantius suppresses the Bagaudae Revolt in Armorica.

events.title: Nulji becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla
events.blurb: Nulji becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla.

events.title: Pope Innocent I condemns Pelagianism, and excommunicates the ascetic Pelagius
events.blurb: Pope Innocent I condemns Pelagianism, and excommunicates the ascetic Pelagius.

events.title: Innocent I dies after a 16-year reign in which he has restored relations…
events.blurb: Innocent I dies after a 16-year reign in which he has restored relations between the sees of Rome and Antioch, enforced celibacy of the clergy, and maintained the right of the bishop of Rome to judge appeals from other churches.

events.title: Theodoric I becomes king of the Visigoths
events.blurb: Theodoric I becomes king of the Visigoths. He completes the settlements in Gallia Aquitania and expands his military power to the south.

events.title: Eulalius is elected antipope of Rome
events.blurb: Eulalius is elected antipope of Rome. He claims in a letter to Honorius his recognition as pope.

events.title: Pope Boniface I succeeds Zosimus as the 42nd pope
events.blurb: Pope Boniface I succeeds Zosimus as the 42nd pope.

events.title: Jin Gongdi, age 33, succeeds his developmentally disabled brother Jin Andi as…
events.blurb: Jin Gongdi, age 33, succeeds his developmentally disabled brother Jin Andi as emperor of the Eastern Jin Dynasty. Andi is strangled by orders of the warlord Liu Yu.

events.title: Rugila, chieftain of the Huns, attacks the dioceses of Dacia and Thrace (Balkans)
events.blurb: Rugila, chieftain of the Huns, attacks the dioceses of Dacia and Thrace (Balkans). Theodosius II allows Pannonian Ostrogoths to settle in Thrace, to defend the Danube frontier.

events.title: The Franks conquer new territories in their kingdom and sack the old Roman…
events.blurb: The Franks conquer new territories in their kingdom and sack the old Roman capital Augusta Treverorum (modern Trier).

events.title: Constantius III is appointed co-emperor (Augustus) with his ineffectual…
events.blurb: Constantius III is appointed co-emperor (Augustus) with his ineffectual brother-in-law, Honorius, and becomes the real ruler of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Venice is founded at twelve o'clock noon (according to legend) with the…
events.blurb: Venice is founded at twelve o'clock noon (according to legend) with the dedication of the first church, San Giacomo, at the islet of Rialto (Italy).

events.title: Vandal war
events.blurb: Vandal war: The Roman commander-in-chief Castinus leads a defeat against the Vandals at Baetica.

events.title: Approximate date
events.blurb: Approximate date – A monastic community is established at the Maijishan Grottoes.

events.title: Petrus, bishop of Illyria, starts construction of the Church of Santa Sabina…
events.blurb: Petrus, bishop of Illyria, starts construction of the Church of Santa Sabina (approximate date).

events.title: Theodosius II issues a law to form provisions in peacetime
events.blurb: Theodosius II issues a law to form provisions in peacetime. He instructs landowners leasing towers in the Theodosian Walls to assist with the build-up of emergency goods.

events.title: Theodoret becomes bishop of Cyrrhus (Syria)
events.blurb: Theodoret becomes bishop of Cyrrhus (Syria). He converts more than 1,000 Marcionites in his diocese.

events.title: Emperor Honorius, age 38, dies at Ravenna of dropsy, perhaps pulmonary edema
events.blurb: Emperor Honorius, age 38, dies at Ravenna of dropsy, perhaps pulmonary edema. With no children to claim the throne, Joannes, primicerius notariorum ("chief notary", head of the civil service), seizes the throne of the Western Roman Empire,

events.title: Roman usurper Joannes sends Flavius Aetius, governor of the Palace (cura…
events.blurb: Roman usurper Joannes sends Flavius Aetius, governor of the Palace (cura palatii), to the Huns to ask for their assistance. After negotiating, he returns to Italy with a large force.

events.title: Church of the East declares itself independent, under Catholicos of the East…
events.blurb: Church of the East declares itself independent, under Catholicos of the East Dadisho.

events.title: Flavius Anthemius Isidorus becomes the new Praetorian prefect of Illyricum,…
events.blurb: Flavius Anthemius Isidorus becomes the new Praetorian prefect of Illyricum, comprising most of Greece and Serbia, taking office at the capital, Sirmium (now Sremska Mitrovica in Serbia).

events.title: , dingyou day) Prince Liu Yilong is formally enthroned as the Emperor Wen of…
events.blurb: (Yuanjia era, 1st year, 8th month (bāyuè), dingyou day) Prince Liu Yilong is formally enthroned as the Emperor Wen of Song of China at its capital in Jiankang.

events.title: Roman civil war
events.blurb: Roman civil war: Summer – Joannes, Roman usurper, is defeated at the fortified city of Ravenna and brought to Aquileia. After a humiliating parade on a donkey and the insults of the populace, he is executed.

events.title: Mausoleum of Galla Placidia
events.blurb: c. 425–426 – Mausoleum of Galla Placidia is built.

events.title: After death of Gamaliel VI, the Sanhedrin is disbanded by the Roman Empire
events.blurb: After death of Gamaliel VI, the Sanhedrin is disbanded by the Roman Empire.

events.title: Buddhism begins to spread to Southeast Asia
events.blurb: Buddhism begins to spread to Southeast Asia.

events.title: The University of Constantinople is founded by emperor Theodosius II at the…
events.blurb: The University of Constantinople is founded by emperor Theodosius II at the urging of his wife Aelia Eudocia.

events.title: Valentinian III, six-year-old son of Galla Placidia, is installed as emperor…
events.blurb: Valentinian III, six-year-old son of Galla Placidia, is installed as emperor (Augustus) of the Western Roman Empire. Real power is in the hands of his mother who becomes a regent.

events.title: Rex Flavius Gundericus of the Vandals accepts the request of the Alans in…
events.blurb: Rex Flavius Gundericus of the Vandals accepts the request of the Alans in Hispania to become their ruler (approximate date).

events.title: The Roman province of Pannonia Prima is finally assimilated into the Hunnic Empire
events.blurb: The Roman province of Pannonia Prima is finally assimilated into the Hunnic Empire.

events.title: Biyu becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje
events.blurb: Biyu becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

events.title: Frankish War (428)
events.blurb: Frankish War (428): Commander-in-chief of the Roman army Aetius put an end to the invasion of Chlodio, king of the Salian Franks in Northern Gaul.

events.title: John succeeds Theodotus as patriarch of Antioch, and gives his support to…
events.blurb: John succeeds Theodotus as patriarch of Antioch, and gives his support to Nestorius.

events.title: Flavius Felix is elected consul for the Western Empire and issues consular…
events.blurb: Flavius Felix is elected consul for the Western Empire and issues consular diptychs during his political office.

events.title: Hydatius becomes bishop of Aquae Flaviae in Gallaecia (modern Chaves) in Portugal
events.blurb: Hydatius becomes bishop of Aquae Flaviae in Gallaecia (modern Chaves) in Portugal.

events.title: Artaxias IV, last king of Greater Armenia, is deposed by Bahram V
events.blurb: Artaxias IV, last king of Greater Armenia, is deposed by Bahram V. The Arshakuni Dynasty ends and the kingdom becomes a province of the Persian Empire.

events.title: King Vortigern invites a number of Germanic warriors to aid him in…
events.blurb: King Vortigern invites a number of Germanic warriors to aid him in consolidating his position in Britain, according to the Historia Brittonum.

events.title: Euthymius the Great builds a monastery in Palestine, near the Dead Sea
events.blurb: Euthymius the Great builds a monastery in Palestine, near the Dead Sea.

events.title: Nestorius is made patriarch of Constantinople
events.blurb: Nestorius is made patriarch of Constantinople. He preaches a new doctrine, that will be called Nestorianism.

events.title: The planet Venus occults the planet Jupiter
events.blurb: The planet Venus occults the planet Jupiter.

events.title: The Temple of Goddess Athena on the Acropolis of Athens is sacked
events.blurb: The Temple of Goddess Athena on the Acropolis of Athens is sacked. Athenian Pagans are persecuted.

events.title: Domnus II, future patriarch of Antioch, is ordained as a deacon
events.blurb: Domnus II, future patriarch of Antioch, is ordained as a deacon.

events.title: Hilary succeeds his kinsman Honoratus and becomes archbishop of Arles
events.blurb: Hilary succeeds his kinsman Honoratus and becomes archbishop of Arles.

events.title: Feng Ba abdicates as emperor of the Northern Yan, one of the states vying for…
events.blurb: Feng Ba abdicates as emperor of the Northern Yan, one of the states vying for control of China. He is succeeded by his brother Feng Hong.

events.title: Saint Patrick reaches Ireland on his missionary expedition (approximate date)
events.blurb: Saint Patrick reaches Ireland on his missionary expedition (approximate date).

events.title: Peter the Iberian founds a Georgian monastery near Bethlehem
events.blurb: Peter the Iberian founds a Georgian monastery near Bethlehem.

events.title: Aetius defeats the Juthungi during his campaign in the Alps
events.blurb: Aetius defeats the Juthungi during his campaign in the Alps.

events.title: Augustine dies during the siege of Hippo Regius at age 75, leaving behind his…
events.blurb: Augustine dies during the siege of Hippo Regius at age 75, leaving behind his monumental work The City of God and other works that will have influence on Christianity.

events.title: Aetius campaign in the Alps
events.blurb: Aetius campaign in the Alps: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum), fights the rebellion in Rhaetia (Switzerland) and Noricum (Austria).

events.title: Hippo Regius becomes the capital of the Vandal Kingdom
events.blurb: Hippo Regius becomes the capital of the Vandal Kingdom. After 14 months of hunger and disease, the Vandals ravage the city. Emperor Theodosius II sends an imperial fleet with an army under command of Aspar, and lands at Carthage.

events.title: Aetius pushes the Salian Franks back across the River Somme
events.blurb: Aetius pushes the Salian Franks back across the River Somme. King Chlodio signs a peace treaty and becomes a foederatus of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Kʼukʼ Bahlam I, the first known ruler of the Mayan city-state of Palenque (the…
events.blurb: Kʼukʼ Bahlam I, the first known ruler of the Mayan city-state of Palenque (the modern-day state of Chiapas in southern Mexico) comes to power and reigns until his death four years later.

events.title: Roman civil war
events.blurb: Roman civil war: Roman forces under command of Flavius Aetius are defeated near Rimini (Italy) in battle. His rival comes Bonifacius is mortally wounded and dies several days later. Aetius flees to Dalmatia and seeks refuge with the Huns.

events.title: Sebastianus, son-in-law of Bonifacius, becomes supreme commander (magister…
events.blurb: Sebastianus, son-in-law of Bonifacius, becomes supreme commander (magister militum) of the Western Roman army. Empress Galla Placidia gives him considerable influence over imperial policy.

events.title: The Basilica of Saint Sabina at the Aventine (Rome) is finished by Priest…
events.blurb: The Basilica of Saint Sabina at the Aventine (Rome) is finished by Priest Petrus of Illyria.

events.title: Pope Celestine I dies after a 10-year reign in which he led a vigorous policy…
events.blurb: Pope Celestine I dies after a 10-year reign in which he led a vigorous policy against Nestorianism. He is succeeded by Sixtus III as the 44th pope.

events.title: Christmas is celebrated for the first time in Alexandria (approximate date)
events.blurb: Christmas is celebrated for the first time in Alexandria (approximate date).

events.title: Justa Grata Honoria, older sister of Valentinian, becomes pregnant from an…
events.blurb: Justa Grata Honoria, older sister of Valentinian, becomes pregnant from an officer in her household.

events.title: Second revolt of Bagaudae in Armorica under leading of Tibatto
events.blurb: Second revolt of Bagaudae in Armorica under leading of Tibatto.

events.title: Ibas is elected bishop of Edessa
events.blurb: Ibas is elected bishop of Edessa. He becomes associated with the growth of Nestorianism and openly preaching heretical doctrines in public.

events.title: A figure known to Mayanist scholars as "Casper" begins a 52-year reign in the…
events.blurb: A figure known to Mayanist scholars as "Casper" begins a 52-year reign in the Mayan city-state of Palenque what is now the state of Chiapas in southern Mexico, and reigns until his death in 487.

events.title: End of the Burgundian Revolt of Gunther
events.blurb: End of the Burgundian Revolt of Gunther: Flavius Aetius, Roman general (magister militum), attempts to put an end to Burgundian raids in Gaul.

events.title: Battle of Wallop
events.blurb: Battle of Wallop: Ambrosius Aurelianus, leader of the Romano-British, defeats the Anglo Saxons under King Vortigern. He is given all the kingdoms of the western side of Britain (according to Historia Brittonum).

events.title: Relics of John Chrysostom are transported to Constantinople
events.blurb: Relics of John Chrysostom are transported to Constantinople.

events.title: Aelia Eudocia, wife of Theodosius II, goes on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem,…
events.blurb: Aelia Eudocia, wife of Theodosius II, goes on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem, bringing back with her holy relics to prove her faith.

events.title: Bahram V dies after an 18-year reign as Sassanid king of the Persian Empire
events.blurb: Bahram V dies after an 18-year reign as Sassanid king of the Persian Empire. He is succeeded by his son Yazdegerd II.

events.title: King Hermeric of the Suebic Kingdom of Galicia is forced to retire after a…
events.blurb: King Hermeric of the Suebic Kingdom of Galicia is forced to retire after a seven-year illness. He hands the government over to his son Rechila.

events.title: The Codex Theodosianus, a collection of edicts of Roman law, is published
events.blurb: The Codex Theodosianus, a collection of edicts of Roman law, is published.

events.title: Isaac the Great, Armenian apostolic patriarch, dies at Ashtishat
events.blurb: Isaac the Great, Armenian apostolic patriarch, dies at Ashtishat. He helped to develop a Greek-inspired alphabet, and translate the Bible, along with various Christian writings, into Armenian.

events.title: Licinia Eudoxia, wife of emperor Valentinian III, is granted the title of…
events.blurb: Licinia Eudoxia, wife of emperor Valentinian III, is granted the title of Augusta following the birth of their daughter Eudocia.

events.title: The Historia Ecclesiastica of Socrates of Constantinople is concluded, perhaps…
events.blurb: The Historia Ecclesiastica of Socrates of Constantinople is concluded, perhaps due to the author's death.

events.title: Battle of Guoloph
events.blurb: Battle of Guoloph: Vitalinus (possibly Vortigern) is defeated at the hands of Ambrosius Aurelianus, and a combined force of Romano-British forces from across southern Britain.

events.title: The Northern Wei empire annexes Northern Liang and unifies Northern China,…
events.blurb: The Northern Wei empire annexes Northern Liang and unifies Northern China, concluding the Sixteen Kingdoms era.

events.title: Carthage falls to the Vandals
events.blurb: Carthage falls to the Vandals. Genseric makes it his capital and establishes the Vandal Kingdom.

events.title: Chaturanga, Indian war game and an ancestor of chess through the Persian game…
events.blurb: Chaturanga, Indian war game and an ancestor of chess through the Persian game of Shatranj (or Chatrang), evolves in the Indus Valley on the Indian subcontinent (approximate date).

events.title: The Hephthalites (White Huns) move south from the Altai Mountains region into…
events.blurb: The Hephthalites (White Huns) move south from the Altai Mountains region into Transoxiana, Bactria, Khorasan and eastern Persia.

events.title: Northern and Southern dynasties
events.blurb: Northern and Southern dynasties: Northern China is unified by the Northern Wei dynasty. The South is still under the control of the Song (or Liu Song) dynasty.

events.title: The Parting of Lot and Abraham, mosaic in the nave arcade, Church of Santa…
events.blurb: The Parting of Lot and Abraham, mosaic in the nave arcade, Church of Santa Maria Maggiore (Rome), is made.

events.title: Pope Sixtus III dies after an 8-year reign in which he has resisted heresy and…
events.blurb: Pope Sixtus III dies after an 8-year reign in which he has resisted heresy and sponsored major construction programs in Rome. He is succeeded by Leo I as the 45th pope.

events.title: Leo I begins to formulate Orthodoxy and condemns Eutychianism, an extreme form…
events.blurb: Leo I begins to formulate Orthodoxy and condemns Eutychianism, an extreme form of monophysitism which holds that the human nature of Christ is absorbed by His divine nature.

events.title: Theodosius II sends the Eastern imperial fleet, under the command of the…
events.blurb: Theodosius II sends the Eastern imperial fleet, under the command of the Romano-Goth Areobindus, into Sicilian waters, taking the Vandals by surprise.

events.title: Rechila invades Baetica and conquers the capital Seville
events.blurb: Rechila invades Baetica and conquers the capital Seville. The Romans are driven from the Iberian Peninsula with the exception of the Levante.

events.title: Chrysaphius, chief minister, persuades Emperor Theodosius II at Constantinople…
events.blurb: Chrysaphius, chief minister, persuades Emperor Theodosius II at Constantinople to dismiss his sister Pulcheria, for her policy of exiling the Jews, and destroying their synagogues.

events.title: King Yazdegerd II of Persia signs a peace treaty after a short war with the…
events.blurb: King Yazdegerd II of Persia signs a peace treaty after a short war with the Eastern Roman Empire.

events.title: Pulcheria leaves for the seaport Hebdomon (Turkey), and becomes a nun to…
events.blurb: Pulcheria leaves for the seaport Hebdomon (Turkey), and becomes a nun to support Nestorianism in the Holy Land (Palestine).

events.title: Gunabhadra, Indian Buddhist monk, is an invited honored guest by emperor Wen…
events.blurb: Gunabhadra, Indian Buddhist monk, is an invited honored guest by emperor Wen of Liu Song (Liu Song dynasty). He translates the Lankavatara Sutra from Sanskrit into the Chinese language.

events.title: The Burgundians sign a peace treaty with Rome, agreeing to serve as foederati…
events.blurb: The Burgundians sign a peace treaty with Rome, agreeing to serve as foederati in the Roman army.

events.title: The Irish city of Armagh is founded by Saint Patrick the Great
events.blurb: The Irish city of Armagh is founded by Saint Patrick the Great.

events.title: Eudocia, eldest daughter of Emperor Valentinian III, is betrothed to Huneric,…
events.blurb: Eudocia, eldest daughter of Emperor Valentinian III, is betrothed to Huneric, son of Vandal King Genseric (hostage in Italy).

events.title: Dioscorus I becomes Patriarch of Alexandria
events.blurb: Dioscorus I becomes Patriarch of Alexandria.

events.title: Bleda, co-ruler of the Huns, dies in a hunting accident
events.blurb: Bleda, co-ruler of the Huns, dies in a hunting accident. He is possibly murdered at the instigation of his younger brother Attila, with whom he has ruled since 434.

events.title: Bishop Germanus of Auxerre visits Ravenna, seeking to soften imperial…
events.blurb: Bishop Germanus of Auxerre visits Ravenna, seeking to soften imperial hostility towards the Bagaudae.

events.title: Flavian becomes patriarch of Constantinople
events.blurb: Flavian becomes patriarch of Constantinople.

events.title: The Britons and Anglo-Saxon mercenaries, under King Vortigern, appeal to…
events.blurb: The Britons and Anglo-Saxon mercenaries, under King Vortigern, appeal to Flavius Aetius (magister militum of Gaul) for military assistance in their struggle against the Picts and Irish.

events.title: The Synod of Toledo (Spain) tries to add the filioque clause to the Nicene Creed
events.blurb: The Synod of Toledo (Spain) tries to add the filioque clause to the Nicene Creed. The Eastern Orthodox Church refuses to go along with this idea.

events.title: Theodosius II sends an embassy to Attila
events.blurb: Theodosius II sends an embassy to Attila; Priscus of Panium, envoy for the Eastern Roman Empire. Priscus records one of the few eyewitness accounts of the Hun kingdom.

events.title: Aspar
events.blurb: Winter – Theodosius II chooses a policy to protect Constantinople against the Huns. He removes Aspar and Areobindus (magister militum) from their military commands.

events.title: The first entry in the Annales Cambriæ refers to this year
events.blurb: The first entry in the Annales Cambriæ refers to this year.

events.title: Battle of the Utus
events.blurb: Battle of the Utus: Attila defeats the Roman army near the river Utus (Vit, Bulgaria). The Huns are forced to abandon the siege of Constantinople.

events.title: The Walls of Constantinople are severely damaged by an earthquake, which…
events.blurb: The Walls of Constantinople are severely damaged by an earthquake, which destroys large parts of the structure, including 57 towers. The population is threatened by a plague.

events.title: Kou Qianzhi, Chinese Daoist reformer, dies after having converted emperor…
events.blurb: Kou Qianzhi, Chinese Daoist reformer, dies after having converted emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei and having established Daoism as the country's dominant religion. His death presages a revival of Buddhism as China's dominant faith.

events.title: Rechiar succeeds his father Rechila as king of the Suebi in Galicia (Northern…
events.blurb: Rechiar succeeds his father Rechila as king of the Suebi in Galicia (Northern Spain). He marries a daughter of the Visigoth king Theodoric I and converts to Catholicism.

events.title: Eutyches is accused of heresy at a synod held in Constantinople
events.blurb: Eutyches is accused of heresy at a synod held in Constantinople.

events.title: Attila demands in the treaty the evacuation of the territory running from…
events.blurb: Attila demands in the treaty the evacuation of the territory running from Singidunum (Belgrade, in Serbia) east along the Danube to Novae (Svishtov, in Bulgaria).

events.title: Maximus II becomes patriarch of Antioch
events.blurb: Maximus II becomes patriarch of Antioch.

events.title: Anatolius becomes patriarch of Constantinople
events.blurb: Anatolius becomes patriarch of Constantinople.

events.title: Traditional date
events.blurb: Traditional date – Hengist and Horsa, by tradition chieftains of the Jutes, land at Isle of Thanet, according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle at the invitation of Vortigern.

events.title: The Second Council of Ephesus opens, chaired by Dioscorus, patriarch of Alexandria
events.blurb: The Second Council of Ephesus opens, chaired by Dioscorus, patriarch of Alexandria. Flavian, patriarch of Constantinople, and Domnus II, patriarch of Antioch, are deposed on August 8.

events.title: Nalanda University (India) is founded (approximate date)
events.blurb: Nalanda University (India) is founded (approximate date).

events.title: All the Temples of Aphrodisias (City of Goddess Aphrodite) are demolished and…
events.blurb: All the Temples of Aphrodisias (City of Goddess Aphrodite) are demolished and its libraries burned down. The city is renamed Stauroupolis (City of the Cross).

events.title: Thorismund succeeds his father Theodoric I as king of the Visigoths
events.blurb: Thorismund succeeds his father Theodoric I as king of the Visigoths. He is crowned in the capital at Toulouse, and extends the Visigothic Kingdom in Hispania.

events.title: Attila's forces invade Gaul and sack Metz
events.blurb: Attila's forces invade Gaul and sack Metz. The major cities of Strasbourg, Worms, Mainz, Trier, Cologne, Reims, Tournai, Cambrai, Amiens and Beauvais are destroyed by the Huns.

events.title: Battle of Vartanantz
events.blurb: Battle of Vartanantz: King Yazdegerd II defeats the Armenian army (66,000 men) under their rebel leader Vartan Mamikonian on the Avarayr Plain (Armenia).

events.title: Attila approaches Aurelianum (modern Orléans) and the city's inhabitants close…
events.blurb: Attila approaches Aurelianum (modern Orléans) and the city's inhabitants close the gates, forcing him to lay siege.

events.title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains (Châlons)
events.blurb: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains (Châlons): Attila avoids a pitched battle near Orléans, and withdraws to the Catalaunian Plains (Champagne-Ardenne). The Roman coalition defeats the Huns, but Theodoric I is killed in the encounter.

events.title: Council of Chalcedon, an ecumenical council of the Church
events.blurb: Council of Chalcedon, an ecumenical council of the Church: The monophysitism of Eutyches is repudiated, and the Chalcedonian Definition set forth.

events.title: Last known usage of Demotic script in Egypt
events.blurb: Last known usage of Demotic script in Egypt.

events.title: Nan'an Yinwang succeeds his father Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei, after he is…
events.blurb: Nan'an Yinwang succeeds his father Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei, after he is assassinated by the eunuch Zong Ai. Later this year, Yinwang is murdered as well, and Ai is overthrown by a group of high officials.

events.title: March
events.blurb: c. March – Attila the Hun is found dead in bed, after a wedding feast with the Goth princess Ildico. He dies of a nosebleed at his Hungarian stronghold, drowning in his own blood, aged about 47.

events.title: Theodoric II succeeds his brother Thorismund as king of the Visigoths,…
events.blurb: Theodoric II succeeds his brother Thorismund as king of the Visigoths, Thorismund having been murdered after he violated the alliance with the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Anthemius marries Marcia Euphemia, daughter of Marcian, and is elevated to the…
events.blurb: Anthemius marries Marcia Euphemia, daughter of Marcian, and is elevated to the rank of comes. He is sent to the Danubian frontier to rebuild the border defences.

events.title: Ankō obtains the throne of his father Ingyō after the traditional order of…
events.blurb: Ankō obtains the throne of his father Ingyō after the traditional order of succession and becomes the 20th emperor of Japan.

events.title: Liu Shao is overthrown by another brother, Liu Jun who becomes Emperor Xiaowu…
events.blurb: Liu Shao is overthrown by another brother, Liu Jun who becomes Emperor Xiaowu of Song.

events.title: Empress Pulcheria dies of natural causes at Constantinople
events.blurb: Empress Pulcheria dies of natural causes at Constantinople. She has commissioned many new churches in the city during her reign. Her death leaves Flavius Aspar (magister militum) as the dominant influence on her husband, Marcian.

events.title: Ardaric unites the Gepids with other Germanic tribes, and founds the Kingdom…
events.blurb: Ardaric unites the Gepids with other Germanic tribes, and founds the Kingdom of the Gepids in the Pannonian Basin.

events.title: Battle of Nedao
events.blurb: Battle of Nedao: Allied forces of subjected peoples (Gepids, Heruli, Ostrogoths, Rugii, Sciri and Suebi), under the leadership of King Ardaric, defeat the Huns under Ellac, eldest son of Attila the Hun, in Pannonia.

events.title: Skandagupta succeeds Kumaragupta I as ruler of the Gupta Empire (India)
events.blurb: Skandagupta succeeds Kumaragupta I as ruler of the Gupta Empire (India). During his reign he crushes the Hun invasion; however, the expense of the wars drains the empire's resources and contributes to its decline.

events.title: Maximus appoints Avitus, most trusted general, to the rank of magister militum…
events.blurb: Maximus appoints Avitus, most trusted general, to the rank of magister militum and sends him on an embassy to Toulouse, to gain the support of the Visigoths.

events.title: Battle of Aylesford
events.blurb: Battle of Aylesford: At a place named Agaelesthrep (often identified as Aylesford (Kent), Hengist fight the native Britons. His brother Horsa is killed and his son Oisc takes his place.

events.title: Barter economy replaces organized trade as Romans and other citizens desert…
events.blurb: Barter economy replaces organized trade as Romans and other citizens desert their towns for the countryside, where they will be less vulnerable to barbarian raids (approximate date).

events.title: Gaero becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje
events.blurb: Gaero becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

events.title: Earliest recorded date at Chichen Itza on the Yucatán Peninsula (Mexico)…
events.blurb: Earliest recorded date at Chichen Itza on the Yucatán Peninsula (Mexico) (approximate date).

events.title: The city of Vindobona (Vienna) is struck by an epidemic that spreads through…
events.blurb: The city of Vindobona (Vienna) is struck by an epidemic that spreads through the Roman provinces. The disease is probably streptococcus or a form of scarlet fever with streptococcus pneumoniae (approximate date).

events.title: Petronius Maximus, former domesticus ("elite bodyguard") of Aetius, becomes…
events.blurb: Petronius Maximus, former domesticus ("elite bodyguard") of Aetius, becomes (with support of the Roman Senate) emperor of the Western Roman Empire. He secures the throne by bribing officials of the imperial palace.

events.title: Maximus is stoned to death by an angry mob while fleeing Rome
events.blurb: Maximus is stoned to death by an angry mob while fleeing Rome. A widespread panic occurs when many citizens hear the news that the Vandals are plundering the Italian mainland.

events.title: Sack of Rome
events.blurb: Sack of Rome: King Genseric leads the Vandals into Rome, after he has promised Pope Leo I not to burn and plunder the city. Genseric sacks the city for a period of two weeks.

events.title: Avitus is proclaimed Roman emperor at Toulouse, and later recognised by the…
events.blurb: Avitus is proclaimed Roman emperor at Toulouse, and later recognised by the Gallic chiefs in Viernum (near Arles).

events.title: Avitus enters Rome with a Gallic army
events.blurb: Avitus enters Rome with a Gallic army. He restores the imperial authority in Noricum (modern Austria) and leaves a Gothic force under Remistus, Visigoth general (magister militum), at Ravenna.

events.title: The Anglo-Saxons call the British nobles to a peace conference at Stonehenge,…
events.blurb: The Anglo-Saxons call the British nobles to a peace conference at Stonehenge, but turn on them and massacre almost everyone (approximate date).

events.title: Capua
events.blurb: Summer – Capua is destroyed by the Vandals. Ricimer is unable to end piracy in the western Mediterranean. Backed by his popularity, he gains the consent of the Senate for an expedition against Avitus.

events.title: Remistus, Roman general (magister militum), is besieged with a Gothic force at…
events.blurb: Remistus, Roman general (magister militum), is besieged with a Gothic force at Ravenna and later executed in the Palace in Classis, outside the city.

events.title: Battle of Placentia
events.blurb: Battle of Placentia: Ricimer, supported by Majorian (comes domesticorum), defeats the usurper Avitus near Piacenza (northern Italy). They compel him to renounce the purple, and Avitus is obliged to become bishop of Piacenza.

events.title: The Visigoths brutally sack the Suebi's capital of Braga (modern Portugal)
events.blurb: The Visigoths brutally sack the Suebi's capital of Braga (modern Portugal); churches are burnt to the ground. Rechiar flees wounded from the battlefield.

events.title: According to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, 4,000 Britons are slain at Crecganford…
events.blurb: According to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, 4,000 Britons are slain at Crecganford in battle against Hengist and his son Oisc of Kent.

events.title: Victorius of Aquitaine computes new tables for celebrating Easter
events.blurb: Victorius of Aquitaine computes new tables for celebrating Easter.

events.title: Emperor Marcian dies at Constantinople, possibly of foot gangrene, an…
events.blurb: Emperor Marcian dies at Constantinople, possibly of foot gangrene, an infection contracted during a long religious journey. He is buried in the Church of the Holy Apostles, together with his late wife Pulcheria.

events.title: Leo I, a Thraco-Roman (or Dacian) high-ranking officer, becomes the new…
events.blurb: Leo I, a Thraco-Roman (or Dacian) high-ranking officer, becomes the new emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire, reigning for nearly 20 years.

events.title: Majorian is crowned emperor of the Western Roman Empire and recognized by Pope…
events.blurb: Majorian is crowned emperor of the Western Roman Empire and recognized by Pope Leo I. His rule is accepted in Italy, Dalmatia and some territories in Northern Gaul.

events.title: Childeric I succeeds his father Merovech as king of the Salian Franks
events.blurb: Childeric I succeeds his father Merovech as king of the Salian Franks. He establishes his capital at Tournai (modern Belgium) and becomes a foederatus (pl. foederati) of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Gondioc
events.blurb: Winter – Majorian enters the Rhone Valley, and defeats the Burgundians under King Gondioc at Lugdunum. He forces the Bagaudae to join the western coalition against the Suebi in Spain.

events.title: Battle of Arelate
events.blurb: Battle of Arelate: Majorian defeats the Visigoths under King Theodoric II at Arles (Southern Gaul), near the Rhone River. Theodoric is forced to sign a peace treaty and becomes a foederatus (pl. foederati) of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Jabi becomes the king of the Korean kingdom of Silla
events.blurb: Jabi becomes the king of the Korean kingdom of Silla.

events.title: Gennadius I becomes patriarch of Constantinople
events.blurb: Gennadius I becomes patriarch of Constantinople.

events.title: Remigius, age 22, is elected bishop of Reims (approximate date)
events.blurb: Remigius, age 22, is elected bishop of Reims (approximate date).

events.title: The Ajanta Caves (India) are completed (cut into the volcanic rock and…
events.blurb: The Ajanta Caves (India) are completed (cut into the volcanic rock and elaborately painted).

events.title: Majorian invades Hispania
events.blurb: Majorian invades Hispania; his generals Nepotianus and Sunieric lead a Visigoth army into Gallaecia. The Suebi are defeated and Lusitania (modern Portugal) is conquered.

events.title: Swabia
events.blurb: (night) – Swabians invade the Gallic city of Lugo. The governor is killed.

events.title: Mamertus is elected bishop of Vienne (Gaul)
events.blurb: Mamertus is elected bishop of Vienne (Gaul).

events.title: Olybrius becomes the second candidate for the western throne
events.blurb: Olybrius becomes the second candidate for the western throne. He is the husband of Placidia, who is being held in Vandal captivity.

events.title: Aegidius becomes ruler over the Domain of Soissons (Gaul)
events.blurb: Aegidius becomes ruler over the Domain of Soissons (Gaul). He has friendly relations with the Romano-British (in Brittany).

events.title: Pope Leo I dies at Rome, age 61 (approximate), after a 21-year reign in which…
events.blurb: Pope Leo I dies at Rome, age 61 (approximate), after a 21-year reign in which he has resisted Manichaeism and defended the Church against Nestorianism. He is succeeded by Hilarius as the 46th pope.

events.title: Libius Severus, Roman senator from Lucania, is declared emperor of the Western…
events.blurb: Libius Severus, Roman senator from Lucania, is declared emperor of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: The Monastery of Stoudios is founded in Constantinople
events.blurb: The Monastery of Stoudios is founded in Constantinople.

events.title: Kibi Clan Rebellion
events.blurb: The Kibi Clan Rebellion against the Yamato state (Japan) in the Korean Peninsula begins.

events.title: Gothic war against Aegidius
events.blurb: In the Gothic war against Aegidius, Childeric I, king of the Salian Franks, allies with the Roman general Aegidius.

events.title: The Suebi live under a diarchy, and fight a civil war over the kingship in…
events.blurb: The Suebi live under a diarchy, and fight a civil war over the kingship in Galicia (Northern Spain).

events.title: Basiliscus, with the help of his sister Verina (wife of emperor Leo I),…
events.blurb: Basiliscus, with the help of his sister Verina (wife of emperor Leo I), becomes a consul in the Eastern Roman Empire.

events.title: Peter the Fuller becomes patriarch of Antioch (approximate date)
events.blurb: Peter the Fuller becomes patriarch of Antioch (approximate date).

events.title: Battle of Wippedesfleot
events.blurb: Battle of Wippedesfleot: The Saxons under command of Hengist and Aesc are defeated by the Britons near Ebbsfleet (Kent). During the battle 12 Welsh leaders are killed (according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle).

events.title: King Remismund establishes a policy of friendship with the Visigoths, and…
events.blurb: King Remismund establishes a policy of friendship with the Visigoths, and promotes the conversion of the Suebi into Arianism in Galicia (Northern Spain).

events.title: A fire begins in Constantinople and, over the next six days, destroys the…
events.blurb: A fire begins in Constantinople and, over the next six days, destroys the buildings in eight of the 14 sections into which the Eastern Roman Imperial capital had been divided.

events.title: Pope Hilarius convokes a synod at Rome's Church of Santa Maria Maggiore
events.blurb: Pope Hilarius convokes a synod at Rome's Church of Santa Maria Maggiore.

events.title: Tarasicodissa adopts the Greek name of Zeno and marries Ariadne, eldest…
events.blurb: Tarasicodissa adopts the Greek name of Zeno and marries Ariadne, eldest daughter of Leo I (approximate date).

events.title: King Mehama of the Alkhans was victorious in a battle against the Kidarites
events.blurb: King Mehama of the Alkhans was victorious in a battle against the Kidarites.

events.title: Ancient Hillforts in Britain are re-fortified, and the Wansdyke is built…
events.blurb: Ancient Hillforts in Britain are re-fortified, and the Wansdyke is built (approximate date).

events.title: Revolt of Euric
events.blurb: Revolt of Euric: The Goths in Aquitania revolts. Their king Euric occupies the south of Gaul.

events.title: Roman forces under Anagast defeat the Huns at the river Utus (Vit, Bulgaria)
events.blurb: Roman forces under Anagast defeat the Huns at the river Utus (Vit, Bulgaria). Dengizich is killed and his head is paraded through the streets of Constantinople. Stuck on the end of a wooden pole, it is displayed above the Xylokerkos Gate.

events.title: Dengizich, son of Attila the Hun, sends an embassy to Constantinople to demand…
events.blurb: Dengizich, son of Attila the Hun, sends an embassy to Constantinople to demand money. Leo I offers the Huns settlement in Thrace in exchange for recognition of his authority. Dengizich refuses and crosses the Danube.

events.title: Battle of Cape Bon
events.blurb: Battle of Cape Bon: The Vandals defeat the Roman navy under Basiliscus, anchored at Promontorium Mercurii, 45 miles from Carthage (Tunisia).

events.title: Jiaozhou governor Lưu Mục dies of illness
events.blurb: Jiaozhou governor Lưu Mục dies of illness. Lý Trường Nhân, a nobleman, launches a coup d'état against the Jiaozhou government, kills the Liu Song officials in Jiaozhou, seizes control of the citadel, then declares himself the governor.

events.title: Emperor Ming of Song grants Lưu Bột the title of Jiaozhou governor, along with…
events.blurb: Emperor Ming of Song grants Lưu Bột the title of Jiaozhou governor, along with an army to retake Jiaozhou from Lý Trường Nhân. After landing in Jiaozhou, Lưu Bột is quickly defeated by Lý Trường Nhân, and dies shortly afterward.

events.title: King Euric defeated the Romano-Breton army of Riothamus at Déols (modern…
events.blurb: King Euric defeated the Romano-Breton army of Riothamus at Déols (modern Châteauroux).

events.title: The Vatican makes a pact with the Salian Frankish king Childeric I, agreeing…
events.blurb: The Vatican makes a pact with the Salian Frankish king Childeric I, agreeing to call him "the new Constantine" on condition that he accept conversion to Christianity.

events.title: Adovacrius defeats Paulus in the Battle of Angers
events.blurb: Adovacrius defeats Paulus in the Battle of Angers

events.title: The Roman general Paulus is killed shortly afterwards at Angers
events.blurb: The Roman general Paulus is killed shortly afterwards at Angers.

events.title: The army of King Ceretic of Strathclyde raids the Irish coast, carries off…
events.blurb: The army of King Ceretic of Strathclyde raids the Irish coast, carries off some of Saint Patrick's followers, and sells them into slavery (approximate date).

events.title: The Goths, led by Theodoric Strabo, revolt in Thrace after the assassination…
events.blurb: The Goths, led by Theodoric Strabo, revolt in Thrace after the assassination of Aspar. Leo I sends Basiliscus to suppress the uprising.

events.title: Mount Vesuvius erupts
events.blurb: Mount Vesuvius erupts. During the volcanic eruption the whole of southern Europe is blanketed by ash.

events.title: Anthemius, besieged in the part of Rome he controls until his troops are…
events.blurb: Anthemius, besieged in the part of Rome he controls until his troops are defeated, is caught while fleeing the city disguised as a supplicant in the Old St.

events.title: Ricimer dies at his palace of malignant fever, vomiting blood
events.blurb: Ricimer dies at his palace of malignant fever, vomiting blood.

events.title: Olybrius dies of dropsy
events.blurb: Olybrius dies of dropsy. During his four months' rule he has been mainly interested in religion.

events.title: Gundobad returns to Burgundy, where his father Gondioc has died, and becomes…
events.blurb: Gundobad returns to Burgundy, where his father Gondioc has died, and becomes king of the Burgundians.

events.title: Theodoric Strabo signs a peace treaty with Leo I, and according to the terms…
events.blurb: Theodoric Strabo signs a peace treaty with Leo I, and according to the terms the Goths are paid with an annual tribute of 2,000 pounds of gold. Leo gives him an independent state in Thrace and he obtains the rank of magister militum.

events.title: Gundobad (nephew of Ricimer) nominates Glycerius as emperor of the Western…
events.blurb: Gundobad (nephew of Ricimer) nominates Glycerius as emperor of the Western Roman Empire. Emperor Leo I refuses to recognize him, and chooses Julius Nepos as candidate to the Western throne.

events.title: Leo I grants his grandson Leo II, age 6, the title of Caesar (approximate date)
events.blurb: Leo I grants his grandson Leo II, age 6, the title of Caesar (approximate date).

events.title: A statue of a Standing Buddha from Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, (during the Gupta…
events.blurb: A statue of a Standing Buddha from Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, (during the Gupta period) is made. It is now kept at the Sarnath Museum in India (source states the creation date as 1st to 2nd century BCE).

events.title: Glycerius is exiled to Dalmatia (Balkans) and becomes bishop of Salona
events.blurb: Glycerius is exiled to Dalmatia (Balkans) and becomes bishop of Salona. Neither the Senate nor the Gallo-Roman aristocracy decide to resist, and Nepos accepts the imperial purple.

events.title: Zeno, father of Leo II, is crowned as co-emperor (Augustus)
events.blurb: Zeno, father of Leo II, is crowned as co-emperor (Augustus). He rules the empire together with his son, and stabilises the Eastern frontier.

events.title: Julius Nepos arrives at Portus, and marches on Ravenna
events.blurb: Julius Nepos arrives at Portus, and marches on Ravenna. He forces Glycerius to abdicate the throne, and proclaims himself emperor of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: The Church of Saint Simeon Stylites is consecrated in Syria
events.blurb: The Church of Saint Simeon Stylites is consecrated in Syria.

events.title: Spring - Spanish War of Euric
events.blurb: Spring - Spanish War of Euric: The comes Hispaniarum Vincentius capitulates against the Aquitanian Goths; Euric completes his conquest of Spain.

events.title: A Bodhisattva (detail of a wall painting in the Ajanta Caves) in Maharashtra…
events.blurb: A Bodhisattva (detail of a wall painting in the Ajanta Caves) in Maharashtra (India) of the Gupta period) is made (approximate date).

events.title: Bodhidharma, Buddhist monk, travels to China and, begins teaching the…
events.blurb: Bodhidharma, Buddhist monk, travels to China and, begins teaching the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra (approximate date).

events.title: Gongju becomes the capital of Baekje, and is threatened by Goguryeo, who…
events.blurb: Gongju becomes the capital of Baekje, and is threatened by Goguryeo, who conquers the Han River valley (Korea).

events.title: Munju becomes king of Baekje
events.blurb: Munju becomes king of Baekje.

events.title: Magister Militum Orestes takes control of the government in Ravenna, and…
events.blurb: Magister Militum Orestes takes control of the government in Ravenna, and forces Julius Nepos to flee to Dalmatia.

events.title: Romulus Augustus is installed as emperor by his father Orestes, who becomes…
events.blurb: Romulus Augustus is installed as emperor by his father Orestes, who becomes regent in effect of the Western Roman Empire. Augustus will ultimately rule for 10 months, as the last Western Emperor.

events.title: Vandal Kingdom
events.blurb: Winter – Zeno recognizes the full extent of the Vandal Kingdom, including all of western Africa, the Balearic Islands, Corsica, Sardinia and Sicily.

events.title: Xian Wen Di, Retired Emperor of Northern Wei, is murdered by Empress Feng
events.blurb: Xian Wen Di, Retired Emperor of Northern Wei, is murdered by Empress Feng. She assumes regency over the young Xiao Wen Di.

events.title: The birth of Aryabhata is traditionally regarded as the beginning of the…
events.blurb: The birth of Aryabhata is traditionally regarded as the beginning of the classical period of Indian mathematics and astronomy.

events.title: The Roman Senate petitions Zeno to recognize Nepos as deposed and take the…
events.blurb: The Roman Senate petitions Zeno to recognize Nepos as deposed and take the sole emperorship himself, abolishing the 81-year-long east/west division of the empire and recognizing Odoacer's authority in Italy.

events.title: Odoacer crosses the Maritime Alps with a Gothic army and invades Provence…
events.blurb: Odoacer crosses the Maritime Alps with a Gothic army and invades Provence (Southern Gaul). He conquers the cities of Arles and Marseille, after a victorious battle against the Burgundians.

events.title: Odoacer, age 43, is proclaimed rex Italiae ("king of Italy") by his troops
events.blurb: Odoacer, age 43, is proclaimed rex Italiae ("king of Italy") by his troops. He leads his Ostrogoth army into the Po Valley, and advances to Ravenna while plundering the countryside.

events.title: Orestes is arrested by Odoacer near Piacenza, and swiftly executed
events.blurb: Orestes is arrested by Odoacer near Piacenza, and swiftly executed.

events.title: Shaolin Monastery is founded (according to the Continued Biographies of…
events.blurb: Shaolin Monastery is founded (according to the Continued Biographies of Eminent Monks (645) by Daoxuan;

events.title: The independent Mauro-Roman Kingdom (Kingdom of the Moors and Romans) is…
events.blurb: The independent Mauro-Roman Kingdom (Kingdom of the Moors and Romans) is formed by Christian Berbers in the Roman province of Mauretania Caesariensis (present-day northern Algeria), bordering the Vandal Kingdom to the east.

events.title: Armatus, Byzantine military commander (magister militum), is killed by order…
events.blurb: Armatus, Byzantine military commander (magister militum), is killed by order of emperor Zeno, being murdered by his own friend Onoulphus after supporting the rebellion of his uncle Basiliscus in 475.

events.title: Samgeun becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje
events.blurb: Samgeun becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

events.title: Liu Zhun, age 10, becomes Emperor Shun of the Liu Song dynasty after his…
events.blurb: Liu Zhun, age 10, becomes Emperor Shun of the Liu Song dynasty after his brother Houfei is assassinated by general Xiao Daocheng. He installs Shun as puppet ruler and sets himself up as regent.

events.title: Verina, mother-in-law of Eastern Roman Emperor Zeno, attempts to kill Isaurian…
events.blurb: Verina, mother-in-law of Eastern Roman Emperor Zeno, attempts to kill Isaurian general Illus for turning against her brother Basiliscus.

events.title: The Liu Song dynasty ends in China
events.blurb: The Liu Song dynasty ends in China.

events.title: The first Shinto shrines are built in Japan
events.blurb: The first Shinto shrines are built in Japan.

events.title: In July, emperor Qi Gao Di granted permission for Lý Thúc Hiến to continue his…
events.blurb: In July, emperor Qi Gao Di granted permission for Lý Thúc Hiến to continue his rule over Jiaozhou as its state governor.

events.title: Ambrosius Aurelianus, war leader of the Romano-British, is proclaimed king of…
events.blurb: Ambrosius Aurelianus, war leader of the Romano-British, is proclaimed king of the Britons (according to Historia Regum Britanniae). He rules probably in the south of Britain, and continues the war against the Anglo-Saxons.

events.title: Soji becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla
events.blurb: Soji becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla.

events.title: Dongseong becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje
events.blurb: Dongseong becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

events.title: King Chilperic I dies and is succeeded by his nephew Gundobad, whose realm…
events.blurb: King Chilperic I dies and is succeeded by his nephew Gundobad, whose realm covers much of eastern Gaul and has two capitals, at Lyon and Geneva. He rules the Kingdom of Burgundy with his brothers Chilperic II, Gundomar and Godegisel.

events.title: Syagrius, ruler of Domain of Soissons, manages to maintain the Roman authority…
events.blurb: Syagrius, ruler of Domain of Soissons, manages to maintain the Roman authority in northern Gaul. He defends his "kingdom" against the neighbouring Salian Franks.

events.title: Prince Seinei succeeds his father Yūryaku and becomes the 22nd emperor of Japan
events.blurb: Prince Seinei succeeds his father Yūryaku and becomes the 22nd emperor of Japan.

events.title: Constantius of Lyon begins his research for his book Vita sancta Germani ("on…
events.blurb: Constantius of Lyon begins his research for his book Vita sancta Germani ("on the Life of Germanus"). He also writes a hagiography of Germanus of Auxerre (approximate date).

events.title: Budhagupta, ruler of the Gupta Empire, establishes diplomatic relations with…
events.blurb: Budhagupta, ruler of the Gupta Empire, establishes diplomatic relations with the Kannauj Kingdom and drives the Huns out of the fertile plains of northern India.

events.title: Odoacer occupies Dalmatia and prosecutes Nepos's killers
events.blurb: Odoacer occupies Dalmatia and prosecutes Nepos's killers. He later establishes his political power with the co-operation of the Roman Senate.

events.title: The Armenians revolt against Persian rule, in an uprising that continues until 484
events.blurb: The Armenians revolt against Persian rule, in an uprising that continues until 484. Led by Vahan Mamikonian, nephew of the late Vartan, they obtain religious and political freedom in return for military aid.

events.title: Legendary founding of Kyiv, on the banks of the Dnieper River
events.blurb: Legendary founding of Kyiv, on the banks of the Dnieper River.

events.title: Prince Qi Wudi succeeds his father Qi Gaodi, and becomes emperor of Southern Qi
events.blurb: Prince Qi Wudi succeeds his father Qi Gaodi, and becomes emperor of Southern Qi.

events.title: Byzantine general Illus (magister officiorum), and Verina (widow of the late…
events.blurb: Byzantine general Illus (magister officiorum), and Verina (widow of the late emperor Leo I), attempt to overthrow Emperor Zeno and place another general named Leontius on the throne.

events.title: Pope Simplicius dies at Rome after a 15-year reign, and is succeeded by Felix…
events.blurb: Pope Simplicius dies at Rome after a 15-year reign, and is succeeded by Felix III as the 48th pope; Rome is without a pope for 10 days in the interim. Felix III is a widower with two children.

events.title: King Huneric passes the Edict of 484, a law banning Catholicism within the…
events.blurb: King Huneric passes the Edict of 484, a law banning Catholicism within the Vandal Kingdom. A few weeks later, King Huneric removes Catholic bishops from their offices and banishes some to Corsica.

events.title: Leontius, Roman usurper, is crowned emperor at Tarsus (modern Turkey)
events.blurb: Leontius, Roman usurper, is crowned emperor at Tarsus (modern Turkey). Empress dowager Verina sends a letter to the governors of the Diocese of the East and the Diocese of Egypt for support.

events.title: Huneric dies and is succeeded by his nephew Gunthamund, who becomes king of…
events.blurb: Huneric dies and is succeeded by his nephew Gunthamund, who becomes king of the Vandals. During his reign the Catholics are free from persecutions and he stabilises the kingdom's economy.

events.title: Prince Kenzō succeeds his adoptive father Seinei, and becomes the 23rd emperor…
events.blurb: Prince Kenzō succeeds his adoptive father Seinei, and becomes the 23rd emperor of Japan.

events.title: Period of Arthur's "twelve battles", during which he gains reputation for…
events.blurb: Period of Arthur's "twelve battles", during which he gains reputation for invincibility (approximate date).

events.title: Fearing of a war with the Southern Qi, Jiaozhou governor Lý Thúc Hiến…
events.blurb: Fearing of a war with the Southern Qi, Jiaozhou governor Lý Thúc Hiến surrendered, officially marking the end of nearly 20 years of Lý clan rule in the region.

events.title: Franco-Roman War of 486 – Battle of Soissons (Gaul)
events.blurb: Franco-Roman War of 486 – Battle of Soissons (Gaul): Frankish forces under King Clovis I defeat the Roman army of Syagrius. Roman rule under Syagrius ends. The land between the Somme and the Loire becomes a part of the Frankish Empire.

events.title: Clovis I establishes his new residence at Soissons
events.blurb: Clovis I establishes his new residence at Soissons. He appoints Ragnachar, Frankish petty king (regulus), as his deputy ruler.

events.title: Persian Christians who follow Nestorianism gather in the second Council of…
events.blurb: Persian Christians who follow Nestorianism gather in the second Council of Seleucia (modern Turkey).

events.title: Bʼutz Aj Sak Chiik becomes the new ruler of the Mayan city-state of Palenque,…
events.blurb: Bʼutz Aj Sak Chiik becomes the new ruler of the Mayan city-state of Palenque, in what is now the state of Chiapas in southern Mexico, and reigns until his death in 501.

events.title: The Gepids capture Belgrade
events.blurb: The Gepids capture Belgrade.

events.title: Ninken, adopted heir of Seinei, succeeds his brother Kenzō and becomes new…
events.blurb: Ninken, adopted heir of Seinei, succeeds his brother Kenzō and becomes new emperor of Japan.

events.title: The first Temple of Confucius is constructed in Northern China (outside the…
events.blurb: The first Temple of Confucius is constructed in Northern China (outside the ancestral temple at Qufu).

events.title: Battle of Sirmium in Pannonia
events.blurb: Battle of Sirmium in Pannonia: The Ostrogoths under Theodoric the Great, moving to invade Northern Italy at the behest of Eastern Roman Emperor Zeno, defeat the Gepids attempting to stop their advance.

events.title: After crossing the Julian Alps, the Ostrogoths defeat the overwhelming forces…
events.blurb: After crossing the Julian Alps, the Ostrogoths defeat the overwhelming forces of Odoacer at the Battle of Isonzo (near Roman Aquileia or modern Soča) and enter Italy.

events.title: Battle of Verona
events.blurb: Battle of Verona: Odoacer is defeated again by Theodoric for a second time. He retreats to the impregnable capital of Ravenna.

events.title: Euphemius becomes patriarch of Constantinople
events.blurb: Euphemius becomes patriarch of Constantinople.

events.title: Theodoric and his Ostrogoths lay siege to Ravenna
events.blurb: Theodoric and his Ostrogoths lay siege to Ravenna. The cities of Cesena and Rimini retain their allegiance to Odoacer.

events.title: Battle of the Adda River
events.blurb: Battle of the Adda River: Theodoric and his ally Alaric II defeat the forces of Odoacer, on the Adda River, near Milan.

events.title: Lupicinus becomes bishop of Lyon
events.blurb: Lupicinus becomes bishop of Lyon. He is the founder of the abbeys of Saint Claude (Jura Mountains).

events.title: Munjamyeong becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo
events.blurb: Munjamyeong becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

events.title: Anti-Isaurian riots break out in the Hippodrome at Constantinople
events.blurb: Anti-Isaurian riots break out in the Hippodrome at Constantinople. Longinus and several other Isaurians, including general Longinus of Cardala, are exiled to Thebaid (Egypt).

events.title: Anastasius I marries Ariadne shortly after his accession
events.blurb: Anastasius I marries Ariadne shortly after his accession. His reign is disturbed by religious distractions and a civil war started by Longinus, brother of late emperor Zeno.

events.title: Isaurian War
