events.blurb: Isaurian War: The Isaurians begin a revolt against Emperor Anastasius I in southern Central Anatolia.

events.title: Battle of Cotyaeum
events.blurb: Battle of Cotyaeum: The Isaurian rebels are defeated by the Eastern Roman army, under John the Scythian and John the Hunchback (subordinate commanders include the future Justin I).

events.title: Pope Felix III dies after a 9-year reign in which he has excommunicated…
events.blurb: Pope Felix III dies after a 9-year reign in which he has excommunicated Patriarch Acacius of Constantinople, thus dividing the Western Church and Eastern Church (Acacian schism). He is succeeded by Gelasius I as the 49th pope.

events.title: Onoulphus, brother of Odoacer, is killed during the siege of Ravenna by…
events.blurb: Onoulphus, brother of Odoacer, is killed during the siege of Ravenna by archers while seeking refuge in a church.

events.title: Mor Hananyo Monastery is established by Mor Shlemon, converting a former Roman…
events.blurb: Mor Hananyo Monastery is established by Mor Shlemon, converting a former Roman fortress (ex temple) in the Tur Abdin region on the Turkish/Syrian border.

events.title: Clovis I marries the Burgundian princess Clotilde, age 18
events.blurb: Clovis I marries the Burgundian princess Clotilde, age 18; she is brought up in the Catholic faith and is the daughter of King Chilperic II. Her father is murdered in the same year by his brother Gundobad.

events.title: Gelasius I canonizes Saint George
events.blurb: Gelasius I canonizes Saint George.

events.title: Cerdic of Wessex and his son, Cynric, land somewhere on the south coast,…
events.blurb: Cerdic of Wessex and his son, Cynric, land somewhere on the south coast, probably near the Hampshire-Dorset border. Their followers establish the beginnings of the Kingdom of Wessex.

events.title: Battle of Tolbiac
events.blurb: Battle of Tolbiac: King Clovis I defeats the Alamanni at Zülpich (Germany). Gibuld, last king of the Alamanni, is killed in battle and the territory is incorporated into the Frankish Kingdom.

events.title: Thrasamund succeeds his brother Gunthamund after his death, and becomes king…
events.blurb: Thrasamund succeeds his brother Gunthamund after his death, and becomes king of the Vandals. Under his rule, he resumes the persecution of the Catholics.

events.title: Gelasius I dies after a 4-year reign, and is succeeded by the Rome-born…
events.blurb: Gelasius I dies after a 4-year reign, and is succeeded by the Rome-born Anastasius II as the 50th pope.

events.title: Clovis I is baptized into the Catholic faith at Rheims, by Saint Remigius
events.blurb: Clovis I is baptized into the Catholic faith at Rheims, by Saint Remigius. The conversion strengthens the bonds between his Gallo-Roman subjects, led by their Catholic bishops.

events.title: The Ambrosian Iliad, an Illuminated manuscript on vellum, of the Iliad of…
events.blurb: The Ambrosian Iliad, an Illuminated manuscript on vellum, of the Iliad of Homer, is produced in Constantinople (approximate date).

events.title: Flavian II succeeds Palladius as patriarch of Antioch
events.blurb: Flavian II succeeds Palladius as patriarch of Antioch.

events.title: Prince Buretsu, age 9, succeeds his father Ninken and becomes the 25th emperor
events.blurb: Prince Buretsu, age 9, succeeds his father Ninken and becomes the 25th emperor.

events.title: Pope Anastasius II dies after a 2-year reign in which he has tried to…
events.blurb: Pope Anastasius II dies after a 2-year reign in which he has tried to conciliate followers of Acacius, late patriarch of Constantinople, who was excommunicated by Felix III.

events.title: Anastasius is succeeded by Symmachus as the 51st pope, in the official papal…
events.blurb: Anastasius is succeeded by Symmachus as the 51st pope, in the official papal selection in the Lateran Palace (Rome). Meanwhile, Antipope Laurentius is elected "pope" in the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore, causing a schism.

events.title: Crown prince Xuan Wu Di, age 16, succeeds his father Xiaowen and becomes…
events.blurb: Crown prince Xuan Wu Di, age 16, succeeds his father Xiaowen and becomes emperor of Northern Wei. He appoints his uncle Yuan Xie provincial governor, who serves temporarily as regent to form a new government.

events.title: Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei dies of starvation in his capital at Luoyang,…
events.blurb: Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei dies of starvation in his capital at Luoyang, after a 27-year reign in which he has Sinicized his tribal relatives (Tuoba clan), created a Chinese-style government and instituted a land-reform program.

events.title: Burgundian Civil War
events.blurb: Burgundian Civil War: King Gundobad breaks his promise of tribute and regains his military power. He besieges his brother Godegisel at the city of Vienne (Burgundy), and murders him in an Arian church along with the bishop.

events.title: Dong Hun Hou is killed during a siege of the capital Jiankang
events.blurb: Dong Hun Hou is killed during a siege of the capital Jiankang. He is succeeded by his brother Qi He Di, who becomes emperor of Southern Qi (China).

events.title: The Sushruta Samhita medical book becomes a classic of medicine in India
events.blurb: The Sushruta Samhita medical book becomes a classic of medicine in India. The book contains descriptions of surgery, illnesses, medicinal plants, and a detailed study on anatomy (approximate date).

events.title: The Maya are peaking in economic prosperity
events.blurb: The Maya are peaking in economic prosperity. The civilization at Teotihuacan begins to decline and its people are migrating to the greatest Mayan city, Tikal, bringing with them ideas about weaponry and new ritual practices.

events.title: Muryeong becomes king of Baekje (one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea)
events.blurb: Muryeong becomes king of Baekje (one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea). During his reign, the kingdom remains allied with Silla and expands its relationships with China and Japan.

events.title: Domangart Réti succeeds his father Fergus Mór, after he dies during a campaign…
events.blurb: Domangart Réti succeeds his father Fergus Mór, after he dies during a campaign against the Picts. He becomes the new king of Dál Riata (modern Scotland) (according to the Annals of Tigernach).

events.title: Ahkal Moʼ Nahb I becomes the new ruler of the Mayan city-state of Palenque (in…
events.blurb: Ahkal Moʼ Nahb I becomes the new ruler of the Mayan city-state of Palenque (in what is now the state of Chiapas in southern Mexico), and reigns until his death in 524.

events.title: Mundhir III, king of the Lakhmids (Arab Christians), raids Palaestina…
events.blurb: Mundhir III, king of the Lakhmids (Arab Christians), raids Palaestina Salutaris and Arabia Petraea. He captures a large number of Romans.

events.title: War with Sassanid Persia
events.blurb: War with Sassanid Persia: Emperor Anastasius I sends a Byzantine army (52,000 men) to Armenia, but is defeated. The Romans attempt an unsuccessful siege of the Persian-held city Amida, on the Tigris.

events.title: A major expansion of Copán's ceremonial center, the Acropolis complex, is…
events.blurb: A major expansion of Copán's ceremonial center, the Acropolis complex, is undertaken by B'alam Nehn (Waterlily Jaguar), the seventh ruler (ajaw) of the southeastern Maya city (approximate date).

events.title: Theodoric the Great builds the Basilica of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, originally…
events.blurb: Theodoric the Great builds the Basilica of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, originally dedicated to Christ the Redeemer.

events.title: Anastasius I decides to rebuild the village of Dara (Northern Mesopotamia)
events.blurb: Anastasius I decides to rebuild the village of Dara (Northern Mesopotamia). He constructs a new strategic fortress to guard the frontier.

events.title: The Visigoths capture the city of Dertosa in Catalonia
events.blurb: The Visigoths capture the city of Dertosa in Catalonia. They arrest and execute the Roman usurper Peter, sending his head as a trophy to Zaragoza (Spain).

events.title: Antipope Laurentius is persuaded by Theodoric the Great to resign his claim to…
events.blurb: Antipope Laurentius is persuaded by Theodoric the Great to resign his claim to the throne of Pope Symmachus, ending a schism in the Catholic Church; Laurentius then fasts until his death.

events.title: King Alaric II issues the "Lex Romana Visigothorum" or Breviary of Alaric, an…
events.blurb: King Alaric II issues the "Lex Romana Visigothorum" or Breviary of Alaric, an abstract of Roman laws and imperial decrees, compiled by a commission appointed to provide a law code for Alaric's Roman subjects.

events.title: Council of Agde
events.blurb: Council of Agde: The bishops of Visigothic Gaul under the presidency of Caesarius of Arles meet.

events.title: The town of Guilin, China, is renamed Guizhou
events.blurb: The town of Guilin, China, is renamed Guizhou.

events.title: Gesalec succeeds his father Alaric II as king of the Visigoths
events.blurb: Gesalec succeeds his father Alaric II as king of the Visigoths. He establishes his residence at Narbonne and is supported by an alliance with the Ostrogothic king Theodoric the Great.

events.title: Keitai becomes the 26th emperor of Japan (according to the Nihon Shoki)
events.blurb: Keitai becomes the 26th emperor of Japan (according to the Nihon Shoki).

events.title: Battle of Zhongli
events.blurb: Battle of Zhongli: army of Liang dynasty led by Wei Rui decisively defeated army of Northern Wei

events.title: Hermanafrid, king of the Thuringi, marries Amalaberga
events.blurb: Hermanafrid, king of the Thuringi, marries Amalaberga. He begins his rule, shared with his brothers Baderic and Bertachar.

events.title: Battle of Vouillé
events.blurb: Battle of Vouillé: A Frankish army under command of Clovis I invades the Visigothic Kingdom, and defeats King Alaric II near Poitiers. The Visigoths refuse to be enslaved, and retreat to Septimania (Southern Gaul).

events.title: Battle of Netley
events.blurb: Battle of Netley: King Cerdic of Wessex moves with an Anglo-Saxon army inland, and defeats the British king, Nudd-Lludd (according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle).

events.title: Battle of Llongborth (possibly Langport or Portsmouth)
events.blurb: Battle of Llongborth (possibly Langport or Portsmouth): King Budic II of Brittany seeks refuge at the court of Aergol Lawhir, in Dyfed (Wales) after the battle.

events.title: The Sasanian Persians conquer the independent kingdom of Caucasian Albania, a…
events.blurb: The Sasanian Persians conquer the independent kingdom of Caucasian Albania, a state converted to Christianity in the 4th century by Armenian missionaries (approximate date).

events.title: Macedonius II is deposed as patriarch of Constantinople, and replaced by Timothy I
events.blurb: Macedonius II is deposed as patriarch of Constantinople, and replaced by Timothy I.

events.title: First Council of Orléans
events.blurb: First Council of Orléans: Clovis I convenes a synod of Gallic bishops to reform the Church, and create a link between the Crown and the Catholic episcopate.

events.title: King Clovis I dies at Paris (Lutetia) at age 45, and is buried in the Abbey of St
events.blurb: King Clovis I dies at Paris (Lutetia) at age 45, and is buried in the Abbey of St. Genevieve.

events.title: Anastasius I constructs a wall from the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, to…
events.blurb: Anastasius I constructs a wall from the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, to protect Constantinople from raiding Bulgars and Slavs.

events.title: The first written text in the Arabic alphabet is recorded at Zabad (Syria)
events.blurb: The first written text in the Arabic alphabet is recorded at Zabad (Syria).

events.title: Vigor becomes bishop of Bayeux
events.blurb: Vigor becomes bishop of Bayeux. He opposes paganism and founds a monastery later known as Saint-Vigor-le-Grand (Normandy).

events.title: Vitalian defeats the Byzantines at Acris (Bulgaria), on the Black Sea coast
events.blurb: Vitalian defeats the Byzantines at Acris (Bulgaria), on the Black Sea coast. He attacks their fortified Laager in darkness, and in a crushing defeat kills a large part of the imperial army.

events.title: The Jewish community revolts at Ctesiphon against Mazdakism, and establishes…
events.blurb: The Jewish community revolts at Ctesiphon against Mazdakism, and establishes an independent Jewish kingdom that lasts for seven years.

events.title: Cissa of Sussex becomes king of the South Saxons after his father's death…
events.blurb: Cissa of Sussex becomes king of the South Saxons after his father's death (approximate date).

events.title: Beopheung becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla
events.blurb: Beopheung becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla.

events.title: Vitalian accepts the receipt of ransom money and gifts worth 5,000 pounds of…
events.blurb: Vitalian accepts the receipt of ransom money and gifts worth 5,000 pounds of gold for the release of Hypatius, a nephew of Anastasius I who has been a prisoner since the attack at Acris (see 513). Vitalian retreats back to Lower Moesia.

events.title: Vitalian, Byzantine general, marches again to Constantinople
events.blurb: Vitalian, Byzantine general, marches again to Constantinople. A fleet of 200 vessels sails from the Black Sea ports and blockades the entrance of the harbor capital.

events.title: As a sign of his victory, Anastasius I leads a procession to Sosthenion, and…
events.blurb: As a sign of his victory, Anastasius I leads a procession to Sosthenion, and attends a service of thanks at the local church dedicated to the Archangel Michael.

events.title: Amalasuintha, daughter of king Theodoric the Great, marries Eutharic, an…
events.blurb: Amalasuintha, daughter of king Theodoric the Great, marries Eutharic, an Ostrogoth noble of the old Amal line.

events.title: Battle of Badon
events.blurb: Battle of Badon, British defeat of the Saxons, traditionally associated with King Arthur (traditional date)

events.title: Emperor Wu appoints Lý Tắc, a Jiaozhou's state official, as the governor
events.blurb: Emperor Wu appoints Lý Tắc, a Jiaozhou's state official, as the governor. Lý Tắc then suppresses the rebellion of Lý Tông Lão, a former subordinate of Lý Nguyên Khải, the previous governor of Jiaozhou,

events.title: Hygelac, king of the Geats (Sweden), raids the Lower Rhine, and is defeated by…
events.blurb: Hygelac, king of the Geats (Sweden), raids the Lower Rhine, and is defeated by a Frankish force led by Theudebert (according to the "History of the Franks").

events.title: The Council of Tarragona (modern Spain) is held
events.blurb: The Council of Tarragona (modern Spain) is held.

events.title: Council of Epaone
events.blurb: Council of Epaone: Bishops of southern Gaul convene near Epao (present Anneyron) in Burgundy.

events.title: Justin I founds the Justinian dynasty and makes his nephew Flavius Petrus…
events.blurb: Justin I founds the Justinian dynasty and makes his nephew Flavius Petrus Sabbatius (later Justinian I) his trusted advisor. He becomes the emperor's close confidant and possibly acts as regent.

events.title: Jabalah IV ibn al-Harith becomes the king of the Ghassanids
events.blurb: Jabalah IV ibn al-Harith becomes the king of the Ghassanids. He invades Palestine, but is defeated by a Byzantine army under general (dux) Romanus.

events.title: Approximate date
events.blurb: Approximate date – Jewish king Dhu Nuwas (also known as Yūsuf Asar Yathar) usurps the kingship of Himyar from Ma'dikarib Ya'fur.

events.title: Emperor Anastasius I dies childless at Constantinople, age 88, after a 27-year…
events.blurb: Emperor Anastasius I dies childless at Constantinople, age 88, after a 27-year reign in which he has abolished the sale of offices, reformed taxation, and perfected the empire's monetary system,

events.title: Severus, patriarch of Antioch, is deposed by a synod for his Monophysitism
events.blurb: Severus, patriarch of Antioch, is deposed by a synod for his Monophysitism. Paul the Jew is appointed to replace him.

events.title: Anjang becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo
events.blurb: Anjang becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

events.title: Jacob of Serugh becomes bishop of Batnan (near modern Diyarbakir, Turkey)
events.blurb: Jacob of Serugh becomes bishop of Batnan (near modern Diyarbakir, Turkey).

events.title: The Memoirs of Eminent Monks is compiled
events.blurb: The Memoirs of Eminent Monks is compiled.

events.title: The Eastern and Western churches reconcile their differences, ending the…
events.blurb: The Eastern and Western churches reconcile their differences, ending the Acacian Schism.

events.title: The monastery of Seridus, where Barsanuphius and John the Prophet lived as…
events.blurb: The monastery of Seridus, where Barsanuphius and John the Prophet lived as hermits, is founded in the region of Gaza.

events.title: King Pabo Post Prydain of the Pennines (Northern England) abdicates his…
events.blurb: King Pabo Post Prydain of the Pennines (Northern England) abdicates his throne, and divides the kingdom between his two sons. He retires, as a hermit, to Anglesey.

events.title: King Budic II returns to Cornouaille (Brittany), to claim the Breton throne…
events.blurb: King Budic II returns to Cornouaille (Brittany), to claim the Breton throne (approximate date).

events.title: Priscian, Latin grammarian, writes the Institutiones Grammaticae ("Grammatical…
events.blurb: Priscian, Latin grammarian, writes the Institutiones Grammaticae ("Grammatical Foundations"). In Constantinople, he codifies this manuscript in 18 volumes, which will be widely used through the Middle Ages.

events.title: The construction of the Basilica of San Vitale in Ravenna, is started…
events.blurb: The construction of the Basilica of San Vitale in Ravenna, is started (approximate date).

events.title: The Kingdom of East Anglia is formed, by the merging of the English counties…
events.blurb: The Kingdom of East Anglia is formed, by the merging of the English counties of Norfolk and Suffolk, and perhaps the eastern part of The Fens (approximate date).

events.title: Epiphanius is elected patriarch of Constantinople by Byzantine Emperor Justin I
events.blurb: Epiphanius is elected patriarch of Constantinople by Byzantine Emperor Justin I.

events.title: Future Byzantine emperor Justinian, age 39, is appointed consul
events.blurb: Future Byzantine emperor Justinian, age 39, is appointed consul. He later becomes Commander-in-chief of the Army of the East.

events.title: Ma`adikarib Ya`fur becomes king, supported by the Aksumites
events.blurb: Ma`adikarib Ya`fur becomes king, supported by the Aksumites; he begins a military campaign against the Arabian tribes.

events.title: Ecclesius becomes a bishop of Ravenna
events.blurb: Ecclesius becomes a bishop of Ravenna.

events.title: Samson of Dol is ordained as bishop in Brittany, on the Feast of the Chair of…
events.blurb: Samson of Dol is ordained as bishop in Brittany, on the Feast of the Chair of Saint Peter.

events.title: Dhū Nuwas moves to Najran, an Aksumite stronghold
events.blurb: Dhū Nuwas moves to Najran, an Aksumite stronghold. After accepting the city's capitulation, he massacres the Christian inhabitants (some sources estimate a death toll up to 20,000).

events.title: Amalaric, age 20, is proclaimed king of the Visigoths
events.blurb: Amalaric, age 20, is proclaimed king of the Visigoths. His kingdom is threatened from the north by the Burgundians.

events.title: Dhu Nuwas seizes the throne of the Himyarite Kingdom in Yemen
events.blurb: Dhu Nuwas seizes the throne of the Himyarite Kingdom in Yemen. He attacks the Aksumite garrison at Zafar, capturing the city and burning the churches.

events.title: Leptis Magna (modern Libya) is sacked by Berber (Moor) raiders
events.blurb: Leptis Magna (modern Libya) is sacked by Berber (Moor) raiders. Gelimer leads a successful expedition in North Africa.

events.title: The Songyue Pagoda is completed during the Northern Wei era
events.blurb: The Songyue Pagoda is completed during the Northern Wei era; the circular-based tower is still 40 m (131 ft) in height.

events.title: Hilderic succeeds his uncle Thrasamund after a 27-year reign, and becomes king…
events.blurb: Hilderic succeeds his uncle Thrasamund after a 27-year reign, and becomes king of the Vandals and Alans. He favours Catholicism and grants the inhabitants religious freedom.

events.title: Seong becomes king of Baekje, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea
events.blurb: Seong becomes king of Baekje, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea.

events.title: Pope Hormisdas dies at Rome after a tenure of 9 years and 17 days, in which he…
events.blurb: Pope Hormisdas dies at Rome after a tenure of 9 years and 17 days, in which he has been instrumental in ending the Acacian Schism. He is succeeded by John I as the 53rd pope.

events.title: Date unknown
events.blurb: Date unknown – Queen Guntheuc, widow of Chlodomer, is forced into marrying his brother, Chlothar I. Her two children are murdered by him, but the eldest son Clodoald survives by escaping to Provence.

events.title: Venantius Opilio is appointed by Byzantium's Emperor Justin to administer the…
events.blurb: Venantius Opilio is appointed by Byzantium's Emperor Justin to administer the Western Roman Empire as the Roman consul, replacing Anicius Maximus.

events.title: King Sigismund of Burgundy is executed at Orléans after an 8-year reign, and…
events.blurb: King Sigismund of Burgundy is executed at Orléans after an 8-year reign, and is succeeded by his brother Godomar. He rallies the Burgundian army and begins plundering Frankish territory.

events.title: Battle of Vézeronce
events.blurb: Battle of Vézeronce: The Franks under Chlodomer, Childebert I and Chlothar I are defeated by the Burgundians and allied Ostrogoths near Isère (France), averting the Frankish advance into Burgundy. During the fighting Chlodomer is killed.

events.title: Anicius Manlius Boethius, one of Rome's most prolific writers and…
events.blurb: Anicius Manlius Boethius, one of Rome's most prolific writers and philosophers, is beaten to death at the prison at Pavia, where he has been imprisoned for treason.

events.title: Dionysius Exiguus, Scythian theologian-mathematician, inaugurates the practice…
events.blurb: Dionysius Exiguus, Scythian theologian-mathematician, inaugurates the practice of using A.D. (Anno Domini) in Rome for calendar dates after the birth of Jesus Christ, a system which has been supported by subsequent studies.

events.title: The Daisan river, tributary of the Euphrates, floods Edessa, and within a…
events.blurb: The Daisan river, tributary of the Euphrates, floods Edessa, and within a couple of hours fills the entire city except for the highest parts. Eventually the pent-up waters break through the city walls.

events.title: Cosmas Indicopleustes, Alexandrian explorer-geographer, travels up the Nile
events.blurb: Cosmas Indicopleustes, Alexandrian explorer-geographer, travels up the Nile. He will venture as far to the east as Ceylon, become a monk, and write "Topographia Christiana" to vindicate the biblical account of the world (see 550).

events.title: Bernicia (North East England) is settled by the Angles (approximate date)
events.blurb: Bernicia (North East England) is settled by the Angles (approximate date).

events.title: Kaleb, king of Aksum, collects a fleet and crosses from Africa to conquer Yemen
events.blurb: Kaleb, king of Aksum, collects a fleet and crosses from Africa to conquer Yemen. He establishes better trade ports on the Red Sea.

events.title: Pope John I returns to Ravenna from Constantinople
events.blurb: Pope John I returns to Ravenna from Constantinople. Theodoric the Great finds that he has been only partly successful in persuading the Byzantine emperor Justin I to withdraw his edict against Arian Christianity,

events.title: Probably between May 20 and May 29 – 526 Antioch earthquake
events.blurb: Probably between May 20 and May 29 – 526 Antioch earthquake: A great earthquake kills approximately 250,000 people in Syria and Antioch.

events.title: Amalasuintha rules the Ostrogothic Kingdom that extends throughout the Italian…
events.blurb: Amalasuintha rules the Ostrogothic Kingdom that extends throughout the Italian Peninsula, Dalmatia, Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica.

events.title: King Theodoric the Great dies of dysentery at Ravenna
events.blurb: King Theodoric the Great dies of dysentery at Ravenna; his daughter Amalasuintha takes power as regent for her 10-year-old son Athalaric.

events.title: Justinian I reorganises the command structure of the Byzantine army, and…
events.blurb: Justinian I reorganises the command structure of the Byzantine army, and fields a small but highly trained army.

events.title: The Kingdom of Essex is founded by the Saxons, who land north of the Thames
events.blurb: The Kingdom of Essex is founded by the Saxons, who land north of the Thames. They take control of the land between what is now London and St Albans, ceding from the Kingdom of Kent

events.title: Justinian I appoints Belisarius to command the Eastern army in Armenia and on…
events.blurb: Justinian I appoints Belisarius to command the Eastern army in Armenia and on the Byzantine-Persian frontier.

events.title: The Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem is rebuilt until 565, restoring the…
events.blurb: The Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem is rebuilt until 565, restoring the architectural tone of the basilica.

events.title: Æscwine becomes the first king of Essex (approximate date), defeating Octa in…
events.blurb: Æscwine becomes the first king of Essex (approximate date), defeating Octa in battle at Hackney, west of the River Lea.

events.title: Silla, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, formally adopts Buddhism as a state…
events.blurb: Silla, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, formally adopts Buddhism as a state religion (approximate date).

events.title: Justinian I outlaws pagan religious practices in Egypt, and dispatches…
events.blurb: Justinian I outlaws pagan religious practices in Egypt, and dispatches Byzantine missionaries to southern territories (approximate date).

events.title: Iwai Rebellion
events.blurb: Iwai Rebellion: A revolt against the Yamato court breaks out in Tsukushi Province (according to Nihon Shoki).

events.title: Emperor Justin I names his nephew Justinian I as co-ruler, as an incurable…
events.blurb: Emperor Justin I names his nephew Justinian I as co-ruler, as an incurable wound saps his strength.

events.title: Justin, Byzantine general (magister militum), dies in battle against the…
events.blurb: Justin, Byzantine general (magister militum), dies in battle against the Bulgars on the frontier of the Danubian limes in Moesia. He is succeeded by Constantiolus.

events.title: Bulguksa, a Buddhist temple, is built in South Korea
events.blurb: Bulguksa, a Buddhist temple, is built in South Korea.

events.title: Emperor Justinian I appoints a commission (including the jurist Tribonian) to…
events.blurb: Emperor Justinian I appoints a commission (including the jurist Tribonian) to codify all laws of the Roman Empire that are still in force from Hadrian to the current date; this becomes the Corpus Juris Civilis.

events.title: Emperor Xiaoming of Northern Wei, emperor of Northern Wei, is poisoned by…
events.blurb: Emperor Xiaoming of Northern Wei, emperor of Northern Wei, is poisoned by order of his mother, the regent Empress Dowager Hu.

events.title: Xiaoming's daughter is replaced by the 2- or 3-year-old Yuan Zhao as emperor…
events.blurb: Xiaoming's daughter is replaced by the 2- or 3-year-old Yuan Zhao as emperor of Northern Wei, by order of Empress Dowager Hu

events.title: Empress Dowager Hu, regent of Northern Wei, having resorted to an old…
events.blurb: Empress Dowager Hu, regent of Northern Wei, having resorted to an old monarchist tool and executed lovers who have displeased her, is drowned in the Yellow River along with the nominal emperor, the baby Yuan Zhao,

events.title: Natural disaster
events.blurb: Natural disaster: A second earthquake strikes Antioch, killing thousands.

events.title: The Samaritans revolt and are defeated
events.blurb: The Samaritans revolt and are defeated; the Church of the Nativity is burnt down during the Rebellion.

events.title: Al-Harith ibn Jabalah becomes the fifth king of the Ghassanids
events.blurb: Al-Harith ibn Jabalah becomes the fifth king of the Ghassanids. He helps the Byzantines to suppress the wide-scale Samaritan Revolt.

events.title: Kʼan Joy Chitam I becomes the new ruler of the Mayan city-state of Palenque…
events.blurb: Kʼan Joy Chitam I becomes the new ruler of the Mayan city-state of Palenque what is now the state of Chiapas in southern Mexico, ending an interregnum of a little over four years, and reigns until his death in 565.

events.title: Xiao Tong, eldest son of emperor Wu Di, compiles the Wen Xuan (Literary…
events.blurb: Xiao Tong, eldest son of emperor Wu Di, compiles the Wen Xuan (Literary Selections), a famous anthology of works dating from the Han to the Liang dynasty (approximate date).

events.title: Emperor Xiao Zhuang Di is arrested and imprisoned in a Buddhist temple at…
events.blurb: Emperor Xiao Zhuang Di is arrested and imprisoned in a Buddhist temple at Jinyang (Shanxi). He is succeeded by Chang Guang Wang, who becomes the new ruler of Northern Wei.

events.title: The Vishnu Temple at Deogarh, Uttar Pradesh (India) is built
events.blurb: The Vishnu Temple at Deogarh, Uttar Pradesh (India) is built.

events.title: Summer – Battle of Satala
events.blurb: Summer – Battle of Satala: A Byzantine cavalry force (30,000 men) under command of Sittas defeats a major Persian invasion into Roman Armenia.

events.title: Brendan, Irish abbot, allegedly climbs to the top of Mount Brandon to look for…
events.blurb: Brendan, Irish abbot, allegedly climbs to the top of Mount Brandon to look for the Americas (approximate date).

events.title: Tribonian becomes quaestor sacri palatii and chief editor of the compilation…
events.blurb: Tribonian becomes quaestor sacri palatii and chief editor of the compilation of the old Roman lawyers' writings.

events.title: Spring – Battle of Dara
events.blurb: Spring – Battle of Dara: Belisarius and Hermogenes (magister officiorum) defeat a combined Persian-Arab army of 50,000 men at Dara (modern Turkey), by entrenching his infantry in a refused position in the centre line,

events.title: Pope Felix IV dies at Rome after a tenure of four years, two months and 13…
events.blurb: Pope Felix IV dies at Rome after a tenure of four years, two months and 13 days, in which he has condemned semi-pelagianism. He is succeeded by Boniface II, who becomes the 55th pope.

events.title: Dioscorus is elected as antipope in the Lateran Palace, but he dies within a…
events.blurb: Dioscorus is elected as antipope in the Lateran Palace, but he dies within a month, thus ending the schism.

events.title: King Childebert I receives pleas from his sister Clotilde, wife of King…
events.blurb: King Childebert I receives pleas from his sister Clotilde, wife of King Amalaric, claiming that she is abused by her husband. Childebert invades Septimania (Gaul).

events.title: Ankan, age 66, succeeds his father Keitai as the 27th emperor of Japan
events.blurb: Ankan, age 66, succeeds his father Keitai as the 27th emperor of Japan.

events.title: King Kavad I, age 82, dies after a 43-year reign
events.blurb: King Kavad I, age 82, dies after a 43-year reign. Khosrau I, his favourite son, is proclaimed successor over his elder brothers.

events.title: The reign of Chang Guang Wang, ruler of Northern Wei, ends
events.blurb: The reign of Chang Guang Wang, ruler of Northern Wei, ends. Gao Huan, Chinese general, begins a rebellion and declares another member of the imperial clan, An Ding Wang, emperor.

events.title: Anwon becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo
events.blurb: Anwon becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

events.title: Theudis, sword-bearer of former king Theodoric the Great, succeeds Amalaric as…
events.blurb: Theudis, sword-bearer of former king Theodoric the Great, succeeds Amalaric as new ruler of the Visigoths.

events.title: Battle of Callinicum
events.blurb: Battle of Callinicum: A Byzantine army (20,000 men), commanded by Belisarius, is defeated by the Persians at Raqqa (northern Syria). Emperor Justinian I negotiates an end to the hostilities, and Belisarius is hailed as a hero.

events.title: First year in which the Anno Domini calendar is used for numbering the years
events.blurb: First year in which the Anno Domini calendar is used for numbering the years.

events.title: An Ding Wang commits suicide, and is succeeded by Xiao Wu Di as Chinese…
events.blurb: An Ding Wang commits suicide, and is succeeded by Xiao Wu Di as Chinese emperor of Northern Wei.

events.title: Battle of Autun (532)
events.blurb: Battle of Autun - The Franks, under command of King Childebert I and his brother Chlothar I, invade the Kingdom of Burgundy. They defeat the Burgundians under King Godomar near Autun (modern France).

events.title: Nika riots in Constantinople
events.blurb: Nika riots in Constantinople: Anger among the supporters of the most important chariot teams—the Blues and the Greens—escalates into violence towards the emperor. For the next five days the capital is in chaos.

events.title: Pope Boniface II dies in Rome after a tenure of two years, four months and six…
events.blurb: Pope Boniface II dies in Rome after a tenure of two years, four months and six days.

events.title: Spring – Vandalic War
events.blurb: Spring – Vandalic War: Anti-Vandal revolt in Tripolitania and Sardinia; Gelimer, king of the Vandals, dispatches the bulk of the Vandal fleet (120 ships and 5,000 men) under his brother Tzazo to Sardinia.

events.title: Theudebert I succeeds his father Theuderic I and becomes king of Austrasia
events.blurb: Theudebert I succeeds his father Theuderic I and becomes king of Austrasia.

events.title: After an interregnum of 2 months and 15 days, Pope John II becomes the 56th…
events.blurb: After an interregnum of 2 months and 15 days, Pope John II becomes the 56th pope of Rome, and the first to adopt a regnal name upon elevation to the papacy (his birth name, Mercurius, being of pagan origin).

events.title: The Byzantine army lands at Caput Vada (modern Tunisia)
events.blurb: The Byzantine army lands at Caput Vada (modern Tunisia). Belisarius marches his army northwards, towards Carthage (over 140 miles), following the coast, accompanied by the fleet and shadowed by Gelimer.

events.title: Battle of Ad Decimum
events.blurb: Battle of Ad Decimum: Gelimer attempts to ambush the Byzantines in a defile at the "10th milestone" from Carthage;

events.title: Battle of Tricamarum
events.blurb: Battle of Tricamarum: Gelimer assembles an army of about 50,000 men at Bulla Regia (Numidia), and advances towards Carthage. Belisarius moves out to meet the Vandals; he leads the Byzantine cavalry (5,000 men) into battle.

events.title: Toledo becomes the capital of the Visigothic Kingdom that controls the Iberian…
events.blurb: Toledo becomes the capital of the Visigothic Kingdom that controls the Iberian Peninsula. King Theudis expands Visigoth rule in the southern regions (Hispania Baetica).

events.title: Decius Paulinus enters the office of consul (the last to hold this office in…
events.blurb: Decius Paulinus enters the office of consul (the last to hold this office in the West).

events.title: King Gelimer surrenders to Belisarius, after spending a winter in the…
events.blurb: King Gelimer surrenders to Belisarius, after spending a winter in the mountains of Numidia. He and large numbers of captured Vandals are transported to Constantinople.

events.title: Belisarius leaves a small force in Africa under the Byzantine general Solomon,…
events.blurb: Belisarius leaves a small force in Africa under the Byzantine general Solomon, to continue the subjugation of the province. He is appointed governor (Exarch) and pacifies the Moorish tribes with success.

events.title: King Athalaric dies of tuberculosis, age 18, having dissipated his youth in…
events.blurb: King Athalaric dies of tuberculosis, age 18, having dissipated his youth in drink and debauchery.

events.title: A second and final revision of the Codex Justinianus is published
events.blurb: A second and final revision of the Codex Justinianus is published.

events.title: Justinian I issues the Lex Julia and declares that a wife has no right to…
events.blurb: Justinian I issues the Lex Julia and declares that a wife has no right to bring criminal charges of adultery against a husband. This makes divorce almost impossible in the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Sicily
events.blurb: Summer – Belisarius lands in Sicily and meets little opposition, save for the Gothic garrison of Palermo. Laying siege to the citadel, he blockades the harbour with his ships. Mundus invades Dalmatia and captures its capital, Salona.

events.title: The Byzantine city of Justiniana Prima is founded, and later becomes a…
events.blurb: The Byzantine city of Justiniana Prima is founded, and later becomes a bishop's seat of the Central Balkans.

events.title: Byzantine troops drive the extremist Monophysite party out of Alexandria, and…
events.blurb: Byzantine troops drive the extremist Monophysite party out of Alexandria, and establish Theodosius I as patriarch of the Eastern Orthodox Church.

events.title: Justinian I reorganises the province as an African prefecture, centered in…
events.blurb: Justinian I reorganises the province as an African prefecture, centered in Carthage. He restores frontier defences, and returns property to the Catholic Church.

events.title: King Theodahad revenges himself upon Queen Amalasuintha
events.blurb: King Theodahad revenges himself upon Queen Amalasuintha. He has her taken from the capital of Ravenna to a small island on Lake Bolsena, where she is strangled in her bath.

events.title: The Little Hagia Sophia in Constantinople (begun in 527) is completed as the…
events.blurb: The Little Hagia Sophia in Constantinople (begun in 527) is completed as the Church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

events.title: Before March 13
events.blurb: Before March 13 – Anthimus I is deposed as patriarch of Constantinople in favour of Menas.

events.title: Pincian Hill
events.blurb: Winter – Belisarius sets up his headquarters on the Pincian Hill, and repairs the neglected city walls of Rome. He stations a 5,000-man garrison, of whom half are his personal bodyguard (bucellarii).

events.title: Early in 536 (possible) – Volcanic winter of 536
events.blurb: Early in 536 (possible) – Volcanic winter of 536: Famine is described in the Annals of Ulster.

events.title: Constantinianus
events.blurb: Summer – Constantinianus, magister militum per Illyricum, retakes Dalmatia. The Goths abandon Salona and withdraw to the north. The Byzantines rebuild its walls and reclaim the province.

events.title: Battle of the River Bagradas
events.blurb: Battle of the River Bagradas: Belisarius defeats the mutineers, and hurries back to Sicily.

events.title: Senka succeeds his brother Ankan as the 28th emperor of Japan
events.blurb: Senka succeeds his brother Ankan as the 28th emperor of Japan.

events.title: Pope Agapetus I dies in Constantinople, after a reign of just ten months
events.blurb: Pope Agapetus I dies in Constantinople, after a reign of just ten months. He is succeeded by Silverius as the 58th pope.

events.title: Council of Constantinople
events.blurb: Council of Constantinople.

events.title: Siege of Naples
events.blurb: Siege of Naples: Belisarius captures Naples after a month's siege, by sending troops into the city through an abandoned Roman aqueduct.

events.title: Vitiges deposes his rival Theodahad at Ravenna, and marries Mataswintha…
events.blurb: Vitiges deposes his rival Theodahad at Ravenna, and marries Mataswintha (daughter of queen Amalasuintha). He becomes king of the Ostrogoths and assembles an army to fight against Belisarius.

events.title: Belisarius enters Rome through the Porta Asinaria, and the Gothic garrison of…
events.blurb: Belisarius enters Rome through the Porta Asinaria, and the Gothic garrison of 4,000 men flees the city.

events.title: Vitiges sets up seven camps, overlooking the main gates and access routes to…
events.blurb: Vitiges sets up seven camps, overlooking the main gates and access routes to the city, in order to starve it out.

events.title: John Cottistis starts a short-lived rebellion against Justinian I
events.blurb: John Cottistis starts a short-lived rebellion against Justinian I. He is declared emperor at Dara, but is killed four days later by conspiring soldiers.

events.title: Eastern Wei sends an advance guard of three army columns through the Tong…
events.blurb: Eastern Wei sends an advance guard of three army columns through the Tong Pass, to attack Western Wei. The Western army under Yu-Wen Tai defeats one of the columns while the others retreat.

events.title: The Aqua Virgo aqueduct is destroyed by the Goths
events.blurb: The Aqua Virgo aqueduct is destroyed by the Goths; they try to use the underground channel as a secret route to invade Rome.

events.title: Yaxchilan captures the ajaws of Bonampak, Lakamtuun, and Calakmul, at the…
events.blurb: Yaxchilan captures the ajaws of Bonampak, Lakamtuun, and Calakmul, at the outset of the First Tikal-Calakmul War.

events.title: Battle of Camlann
events.blurb: Battle of Camlann: King Arthur fights his last battle against the forces of his rebellious son (or nephew) Mordred, and is mortally wounded (traditional date)

events.title: Siege of Rome
events.blurb: Siege of Rome: The Ostrogothic army (45,000 men) under King Vitiges begins the siege of the city. Belisarius conducts a delaying action outside the Flaminian Gate; he and a detachment of his bucellarii are almost cut off.

events.title: Vitiges attempts to assault the northern and eastern city walls with four…
events.blurb: Vitiges attempts to assault the northern and eastern city walls with four siege towers, but is repulsed at the Praenestine Gate, known as the Vivarium, by the defenders under the Byzantine generals Bessas and Peranius.

events.title: Pope Vigilius succeeds Silverius as the 59th pope, when the latter is deposed…
events.blurb: Pope Vigilius succeeds Silverius as the 59th pope, when the latter is deposed by Belisarius at the order of Justinian I.

events.title: The Goths capture the Portus Claudii at Ostia
events.blurb: The Goths capture the Portus Claudii at Ostia; the harbor is left unguarded by the Romans. Belisarius is forced to unload his supplies at Antium; he sends urgent messages for reinforcements to Constantinople.

events.title: Belisarius receives his promised reinforcements
events.blurb: Belisarius receives his promised reinforcements: 1,600 cavalry, mostly of Hunnic or Slavic origin and expert bowmen. Despite shortages, he starts raids against the Gothic camps and Vitiges is forced into a stalemate.

events.title: Belisarius sends John "the Sanguinary" with a force of 2,000 men towards…
events.blurb: Belisarius sends John "the Sanguinary" with a force of 2,000 men towards Picenum, to plunder the east coast of Italy. He arrives at Ariminum (Rimini), where he is welcomed by the local population.

events.title: The construction of the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople (begun in 532) is completed
events.blurb: The construction of the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople (begun in 532) is completed.

events.title: Gabrán mac Domangairt becomes king of Dál Riata (Scotland)
events.blurb: Gabrán mac Domangairt becomes king of Dál Riata (Scotland).

events.title: The Kofun period ends and the Asuka period, the second part of the Yamato…
events.blurb: The Kofun period ends and the Asuka period, the second part of the Yamato period in Japan, begins.

events.title: The Third Council of Orléans takes place, and prohibits rural labor on Sunday
events.blurb: The Third Council of Orléans takes place, and prohibits rural labor on Sunday.

events.title: Sittas, Byzantine general, suppresses a revolt in Armenia in protest against…
events.blurb: Sittas, Byzantine general, suppresses a revolt in Armenia in protest against heavy taxation. During the campaign he is killed by Artabanes, leader of the revolt.

events.title: Belisarius secures Liguria, Mediolanum (modern Milan) and Ariminum, but…
events.blurb: Belisarius secures Liguria, Mediolanum (modern Milan) and Ariminum, but disagreements, especially with Narses, leads to disunity in the Byzantine army.

events.title: Kinmei succeeds his brother Senka, and ascends as 29th emperor to the throne…
events.blurb: Kinmei succeeds his brother Senka, and ascends as 29th emperor to the throne of Japan.

events.title: Walthari murders his uncle Wacho and becomes king of the Lombards
events.blurb: Walthari murders his uncle Wacho and becomes king of the Lombards.

events.title: Antioch is struck by an earthquake
events.blurb: Antioch is struck by an earthquake.

events.title: Global environmental cooling occurs, due either to a comet impact or volcanic…
events.blurb: Global environmental cooling occurs, due either to a comet impact or volcanic eruption in Central America, evidenced by global tree ring growth diminution. Recent evidence from Swiss ice core points to volcanic eruptions in Iceland.

events.title: King Custennin ap Cado is deposed, and returns to Dumnonia in the south-west…
events.blurb: King Custennin ap Cado is deposed, and returns to Dumnonia in the south-west of Great Britain.

events.title: Cassiodorus, former Roman statesman, establishes a monastery at his estate in…
events.blurb: Cassiodorus, former Roman statesman, establishes a monastery at his estate in Italy.

events.title: King Khosrow I breaks the "Eternal Peace" treaty with the Byzantine Empire…
events.blurb: King Khosrow I breaks the "Eternal Peace" treaty with the Byzantine Empire after eight years.

events.title: Ildibad succeeds Vitiges as king of the Ostrogoths, and installs his nephew…
events.blurb: Ildibad succeeds Vitiges as king of the Ostrogoths, and installs his nephew Totila as commander of the Gothic army. He recaptures Venetia and Liguria in Northern Italy.

events.title: Belisarius consolidates Italy and begins mopping-up operations, capturing the…
events.blurb: Belisarius consolidates Italy and begins mopping-up operations, capturing the Gothic fortifications. The cities Ticinum and Verona north of River Po remain in Gothic hands.

events.title: Benedict of Nursia writes his monastic rules, containing precepts for his…
events.blurb: Benedict of Nursia writes his monastic rules, containing precepts for his monks (approximate date).

events.title: Jinheung becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla
events.blurb: Jinheung becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla.

events.title: Totila
events.blurb: Autumn – Totila is elected king by the Ostrogothic nobles after the death of his uncle Ildibad. He wins the support of the lower classes by liberating slaves and distributing land to the peasants.

events.title: Lazic War
events.blurb: Lazic War: King Khosrau I intervenes in Lazica (modern Georgia), and supports the weakened king Gubazes II against a full-scale uprising.

events.title: Winter – Siege of Verona
events.blurb: Winter – Siege of Verona: Totila defends the city of Verona against a numerically superior Byzantine army. He gains control over the Po Valley and prepares a Gothic offensive in Central Italy.

events.title: John the Cappadocian, praetorian prefect of the East, is dismissed by the…
events.blurb: John the Cappadocian, praetorian prefect of the East, is dismissed by the Byzantine empress Theodora for treason. He is banished to Cyzicus, and his estates are confiscated.

events.title: Jacob Baradaeus becomes bishop of Edessa (approximate date)
events.blurb: Jacob Baradaeus becomes bishop of Edessa (approximate date).

events.title: Plague of Justinian
events.blurb: Plague of Justinian: Bubonic plague appears suddenly in the Egyptian port of Pelusium, spreading to Alexandria and, the following year, to Constantinople.

events.title: Anicius Faustus Albinus Basilius is appointed as consul in Constantinople, the…
events.blurb: Anicius Faustus Albinus Basilius is appointed as consul in Constantinople, the last person to hold this office.

events.title: Spring – Battle of Faventia
events.blurb: Spring – Battle of Faventia: King Totila scatters the Byzantine forces near Faventia (modern Faenza) with 5,000 men, beginning the resurgence of Gothic resistance to the reconquest of Italy.

events.title: Battle of Mucellium
events.blurb: Battle of Mucellium: Totila marches down into Tuscany and defeats the Byzantines at Florence, in the valley of Mugello. He treats his prisoners well, and many are induced to join his banner.

events.title: Gildas, British monk, writes his work "De Excidio et Conquestu Britanniae"…
events.blurb: Gildas, British monk, writes his work "De Excidio et Conquestu Britanniae" (approximate date).

events.title: Siege of Naples
events.blurb: Siege of Naples: Totila besieges the city of Naples in Campania. A Byzantine relief force from Sicily is intercepted and almost destroyed by Gothic warships.

events.title: Approximate date
events.blurb: Approximate date – The Yupian (玉篇) Chinese dictionary is edited by Gu Yewang.

events.title: Barsanuphius, a famous hermit close to Gaza, retreats fully from the world…
events.blurb: Barsanuphius, a famous hermit close to Gaza, retreats fully from the world after the death of Seridus, abbot of the nearby monastery,

events.title: The fortress city of Old Dongola (modern Sudan) along the River Nile becomes…
events.blurb: The fortress city of Old Dongola (modern Sudan) along the River Nile becomes the capital of the Kingdom of Makuria. Several churches are built, including the "Old Church" (approximate date).

events.title: King Pulakeshin I establishes the Chalukya dynasty in India
events.blurb: King Pulakeshin I establishes the Chalukya dynasty in India. He extends his kingdom by conquering Vakataka and the west coast of Karnataka, giving him access to the valuable Arabian Sea trade routes.

events.title: Justinian I issues a new edict condemning the Three Chapters
events.blurb: Justinian I issues a new edict condemning the Three Chapters. In Western Europe, Pope Vigilius refuses to acknowledge the imperial edict and is ordered to summon to Constantinople.

events.title: Battle of Cillium
events.blurb: Battle of Cillium: A medium-sized Byzantine army under Solomon is defeated by the Moors on the border of Numidia. Solomon and his bodyguard are forced to retreat and are later killed.

events.title: The Liang dynasty retaliates against Van Xuân, and sends an imperial army…
events.blurb: The Liang dynasty retaliates against Van Xuân, and sends an imperial army (120,000 men) under Chen Baxian to re-occupy the region.

events.title: Yangwon becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo
events.blurb: Yangwon becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

events.title: The Synod of Brefi is held at Llanddewi Brefi, to condemn the Pelagian heresy
events.blurb: The Synod of Brefi is held at Llanddewi Brefi, to condemn the Pelagian heresy. Dubricius, archbishop of South Wales, resigns his position in favour of David (approximate date).

events.title: Audoin murders and succeeds Walthari as king of the Lombards
events.blurb: Audoin murders and succeeds Walthari as king of the Lombards.

events.title: Approximate date
events.blurb: Approximate date – The Diocese of Bangor is established in the Welsh kingdom of Gwynedd, with Deiniol consecrated as first bishop.

events.title: Sack of Rome
events.blurb: Sack of Rome: After almost a year's siege, the capture of a grain fleet sent by the exiled Pope Vigilius near the mouth of the Tiber, and failure of troops of the Byzantine Empire under Belisarius to relieve the city,

events.title: Battle of Marta
events.blurb: Battle of Marta: The Byzantine army under John Troglita is defeated by Moorish tribes in Tripolitania. He flees to Lunci (9 km south of Mahares), and is forced to withdraw north to the fortress of Laribus (near modern El Kef).

events.title: Theudebald, age 13, succeeds his father Theudebert I after a reign of 14…
events.blurb: Theudebald, age 13, succeeds his father Theudebert I after a reign of 14 years, and becomes king of Austrasia (or 548).

events.title: King Ida establishes the kingdom of Bernicia
events.blurb: King Ida establishes the kingdom of Bernicia. He builds Bamburgh Castle (northeast England) as a fortress that will become the seat of Anglo-Saxon kings (according to the Historia Brittonum).

events.title: The Tonkin revolt (Vietnam), led by Lý Nam Đế, is suppressed by the Chinese…
events.blurb: The Tonkin revolt (Vietnam), led by Lý Nam Đế, is suppressed by the Chinese Liang dynasty.

events.title: Gubazes II besieges the fortress of Petra, located on the Black Sea
events.blurb: Gubazes II besieges the fortress of Petra, located on the Black Sea. The Persian army under Mermeroes defeats a small Byzantine force guarding the mountain passes, and relieves Petra.

events.title: Saint Catherine's Monastery is established in the Sinai Peninsula
events.blurb: Saint Catherine's Monastery is established in the Sinai Peninsula.

events.title: Theudigisel, Visigothic general, proclaims himself ruler over the Visigothic…
events.blurb: Theudigisel, Visigothic general, proclaims himself ruler over the Visigothic Kingdom, after King Theudis is assassinated.

events.title: Emperor Lý Nam Đế of Vietnam is killed by Laotian tribesmen, while on retreat…
events.blurb: Emperor Lý Nam Đế of Vietnam is killed by Laotian tribesmen, while on retreat from the Hong River Plain. He is succeeded by his elder brother Lý Thiên Bảo.

events.title: Empress Theodora I dies at age 48, probably of breast cancer (according to…
events.blurb: Empress Theodora I dies at age 48, probably of breast cancer (according to Bishop Victor of Tunnuna). Her body is buried in the Church of the Holy Apostles (Constantinople).

events.title: Jianwen Di succeeds his father Wu Di as emperor of the Liang Dynasty (China)
events.blurb: Jianwen Di succeeds his father Wu Di as emperor of the Liang Dynasty (China).

events.title: Bishop Maximianus of Ravenna consecrates the Basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe
events.blurb: Bishop Maximianus of Ravenna consecrates the Basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe.

events.title: Siege of Petra (549)
events.blurb: The Romans unsuccessfully besiege Petra, Lazica.

events.title: In the Circus Maximus, first and largest circus in Rome, the last chariot…
events.blurb: In the Circus Maximus, first and largest circus in Rome, the last chariot races are held.

events.title: Jesus
events.blurb: c. 549–564 – Transfiguration of Christ, mosaic in the apse, Church of the Virgin, Saint Catherine's Monastery in Egypt, is made.

events.title: Agila I succeeds Theudigisel as king of the Visigoths, after he is murdered by…
events.blurb: Agila I succeeds Theudigisel as king of the Visigoths, after he is murdered by a group of conspirators during a banquet in Seville.

events.title: Totila conquers the city of Perugia (Central Italy) and stations a Gothic garrison
events.blurb: Totila conquers the city of Perugia (Central Italy) and stations a Gothic garrison. He takes bishop Herculanus prisoner, and orders him to be completely flayed.

events.title: Fifth Council of Orléans
events.blurb: Fifth Council of Orléans: Nine archbishops and forty-one bishops pronounce an anathema against the errors of Nestorius and Eutyches.

events.title: The Roman Catholic Diocese of Ossory (which still exists) is founded in Ireland
events.blurb: The Roman Catholic Diocese of Ossory (which still exists) is founded in Ireland.

events.title: Battle of Ciiil Conaire, Ireland
events.blurb: Battle of Ciiil Conaire, Ireland: Ailill Inbanda and his brother are defeated and killed.

events.title: The Gupta Empire falls
events.blurb: The Gupta Empire falls; India is again ruled by regional kingdoms (approximate date).

events.title: The churches of Lazica (Georgia) and Armenia split
events.blurb: The churches of Lazica (Georgia) and Armenia split. While the Armenian Church remains independent, the Georgian church unites with the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Procopius writes the Secret History (approximate date)
events.blurb: Procopius writes the Secret History (approximate date).

events.title: Construction of Quiriguá (Guatemala) begins (approximate date)
events.blurb: Construction of Quiriguá (Guatemala) begins (approximate date).

events.title: The main redaction of the Babylonian Talmud is completed under Rabbis Ravina…
events.blurb: The main redaction of the Babylonian Talmud is completed under Rabbis Ravina and Ashi (approximate date).

events.title: Gothic War
events.blurb: Gothic War: The Ostrogoths under king Totila recapture Rome after a long siege, by bribing the Isaurian garrison.

events.title: Xiao Dong
events.blurb: Autumn – Xiao Dong, great-nephew of the rebellious general Hou Jing, succeeds Jianwen Di as emperor of the Liang Dynasty. Xiao Dong has no real power and Hou Jing controls the imperial government at the capital Jiankang.

events.title: Jordanes, Roman bureaucrat, publishes "The Origin and Deeds of the Goths"…
events.blurb: Jordanes, Roman bureaucrat, publishes "The Origin and Deeds of the Goths" (approximate date).

events.title: Autumn – Battle of Sena Gallica
events.blurb: Autumn – Battle of Sena Gallica: The Byzantine fleet (50 warships) destroys the Gothic naval force under Indulf near Sena Gallica (Senigallia), some 17 miles (27 km) north of Ancona.

events.title: Bumin Qaghan, chieftain of the Göktürks, founds the Turkic Khaganate
events.blurb: Bumin Qaghan, chieftain of the Göktürks, founds the Turkic Khaganate. He unites the local Turkic tribes and throws off the yoke of Rouran domination.

events.title: Athanagild revolts against the Visigothic king Agila
events.blurb: Athanagild revolts against the Visigothic king Agila. Their armies meet at Seville (Andalusia), and Agila is defeated.

events.title: After the death of his cousin Germanus, Justinian I appoints Narses new…
events.blurb: After the death of his cousin Germanus, Justinian I appoints Narses new supreme commander, and returns to Italy.

events.title: Beirut is destroyed by an earthquake and tsunami
events.blurb: Beirut is destroyed by an earthquake and tsunami. Its epicenter has an estimated magnitude of about 7.2 or 7.6, and according to reports of Antoninus of Piacenza, Christian pilgrim, some 30,000 people are killed.

events.title: Yuan Di succeeds Xiao Dong as emperor of the Liang dynasty
events.blurb: Yuan Di succeeds Xiao Dong as emperor of the Liang dynasty.

events.title: Battle of Asfeld
events.blurb: Battle of Asfeld: The Lombards under King Audoin defeat the Gepids.

events.title: Teia becomes the last king of the Ostrogoths in Italy
events.blurb: Teia becomes the last king of the Ostrogoths in Italy.

events.title: Buddhism in Japan is introduced, according to the Nihon Shoki
events.blurb: Buddhism in Japan is introduced, according to the Nihon Shoki.

events.title: The Roman Catholic Diocese of Meath is established in Ireland
events.blurb: The Roman Catholic Diocese of Meath is established in Ireland.

events.title: Battle of Taginae
events.blurb: Battle of Taginae: Narses crosses the Apennines with a Byzantine army (25,000 men). He is blocked by a Gothic force under King Totila near Taginae (Central Italy).

events.title: The Armenian calendar is introduced
events.blurb: The Armenian calendar is introduced.

events.title: Battle of Mons Lactarius
events.blurb: Battle of Mons Lactarius: King Teia secretly marches to join forces with his brother Aligern in Campania, to relieve the siege of Cumae. Meanwhile at Mons Lactarius (modern Monti Lattari), Narses lays an ambush.

events.title: In the Turkic Khaganate Istemi is appointed governor (yabgu) in the west of…
events.blurb: In the Turkic Khaganate Istemi is appointed governor (yabgu) in the west of the empire (modern Turkestan), and Muqan Qaghan succeeds his brother Issik Qaghan as emperor (khagan) of the Göktürks.

events.title: The Fifth Ecumenical Council is held in Constantinople
events.blurb: The Fifth Ecumenical Council is held in Constantinople. In an edict, Emperor Justinian I condemns the Three Chapters, causing further schisms and heresies of monoenergism and monothelitism.

events.title: Muqan Qaghan succeeds his brother Issik Qaghan as emperor (khagan) of the Göktürks
events.blurb: Muqan Qaghan succeeds his brother Issik Qaghan as emperor (khagan) of the Göktürks.

events.title: Wei Shou completes compilation of the Book of Wei
events.blurb: Wei Shou completes compilation of the Book of Wei.

events.title: Gong Di succeeds his brother Fei Di as emperor of Western Wei
events.blurb: Gong Di succeeds his brother Fei Di as emperor of Western Wei. He is deposed by general Yuwen Tai who puts him to death.

events.title: Wideok becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje
events.blurb: Wideok becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

events.title: 554 Anatolia earthquake
events.blurb: The 554 Anatolia earthquake takes place in the southwest coasts of Anatolia (Asia Minor). It affects the Güllük Gulf (Mandalya Gulf), and the island of Kos.

events.title: Battle of the Volturnus
events.blurb: Battle of the Volturnus: During the spring Butilinus (Buccelin) has marched north; the Frankish army (infected by an epidemic of dysentery which kills their leader Leutharis (Lothair)) is reduced to about 30,000 men.

events.title: King Gubazes II is invited to observe the siege of a Persian-held fortress,…
events.blurb: King Gubazes II is invited to observe the siege of a Persian-held fortress, and is murdered by the Byzantine military staff after accusing them of incompetence.

events.title: Cybi Felyn, abbot of Holyhead, dies at his monastery in Caer Gybi (approximate…
events.blurb: Cybi Felyn, abbot of Holyhead, dies at his monastery in Caer Gybi (approximate date).

events.title: Taliesin, British poet, becomes court bard to King Brochwel of Powys…
events.blurb: Taliesin, British poet, becomes court bard to King Brochwel of Powys (approximate date).

events.title: King Erb of Gwent (in Southern Wales) dies
events.blurb: King Erb of Gwent (in Southern Wales) dies; his kingdom is divided into Gwent and Ergyng (approximate date).

events.title: Siege of Phasis
events.blurb: Siege of Phasis: The Persians are defeated at the besieged town of Phasis in Lazica, held by the Byzantines.

events.title: The diplomatic representative (apocrisiarius) to Constantinople is elected as…
events.blurb: The diplomatic representative (apocrisiarius) to Constantinople is elected as Pope Pelagius I, succeeding Vigilius as the 60th pope of Rome.

events.title: The Western Wei Dynasty ends
events.blurb: The Western Wei Dynasty ends: Yuwen Hu deposes emperor Gong Di, and places Yuwen Tai's son Xiaomin on the throne. Yuwen Hu becomes regent and establishes the Northern Zhou dynasty in China.

events.title: Ming Di is made emperor, after his younger brother Xiao Min Di is arrested…
events.blurb: Ming Di is made emperor, after his younger brother Xiao Min Di is arrested while trying to assume power. Xiao Min Di is deposed and executed by Yuwen Hu.

events.title: The Jiming Temple in Nanjing is built
events.blurb: The Jiming Temple in Nanjing is built; the Buddhist pagoda is located near Xuanwu Lake.

events.title: The Avars arrive in the northern region of the Caucasus, between the Black Sea…
events.blurb: The Avars arrive in the northern region of the Caucasus, between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea. They send envoys to the Byzantines in Lazica (modern Georgia).

events.title: 557 Constantinople earthquake
events.blurb: The 557 Constantinople earthquake occurs.

events.title: The Bangor Abbey is founded by the Irish abbot Comgall in Northern Ireland…
events.blurb: The Bangor Abbey is founded by the Irish abbot Comgall in Northern Ireland (approximate date).

events.title: Istämi, ruler of the Western Turkic Khaganate, establishes diplomatic…
events.blurb: Istämi, ruler of the Western Turkic Khaganate, establishes diplomatic relations with the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: The Avars and the Slavs occupy the Hungarian Plain on the Balkans
events.blurb: The Avars and the Slavs occupy the Hungarian Plain on the Balkans. The threat of Avar domination prompts the Lombards to migrate to Italy.

events.title: Conall mac Comgaill becomes king of Dál Riata, a Gaelic overkingdom on the…
events.blurb: Conall mac Comgaill becomes king of Dál Riata, a Gaelic overkingdom on the western coast of Scotland.

events.title: King Chlothar I reunites the Frankish Kingdom after his brother Childebert I…
events.blurb: King Chlothar I reunites the Frankish Kingdom after his brother Childebert I dies, becoming sole ruler of the Franks.

events.title: Battle of Melantias
events.blurb: Battle of Melantias: Outside the city walls of Constantinople, Belisarius defeats the combined "barbarians" with his veteran cavalry (bucellarii), and a few thousand hastily raised levies.

events.title: Pyeongwon becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo
events.blurb: Pyeongwon becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

events.title: Wen Di, age 37, succeeds his uncle Chen Wu Di as emperor of the Chen dynasty
events.blurb: Wen Di, age 37, succeeds his uncle Chen Wu Di as emperor of the Chen dynasty. During his reign, he consolidates the state against the rebellious warlords.

events.title: Glappa succeeds his father Ida as king of Bernicia (North East England)
events.blurb: Glappa succeeds his father Ida as king of Bernicia (North East England). During his rule, Anglian settlers expand their territory in what is now southeastern Scotland.

events.title: Kutrigurs
events.blurb: Winter – The Kutrigurs and Huns under Zabergan cross the frozen Danube River, and invade the Balkans. They raid Thracia and Macedonia, but are driven back near Constantinople by a Byzantine force under Belisarius.

events.title: The city-state Ara Gaya, a member of the Gaya confederacy, surrenders to Silla…
events.blurb: The city-state Ara Gaya, a member of the Gaya confederacy, surrenders to Silla in the Korean peninsula.

events.title: Elidyr of Strathclyde invades Gwynedd (Wales) and tries to expel his…
events.blurb: Elidyr of Strathclyde invades Gwynedd (Wales) and tries to expel his brother-in-law, King Rhun ap Maelgwn.

events.title: Ælla becomes king of Deira (this according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle)
events.blurb: Ælla becomes king of Deira (this according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle).

events.title: Adda succeeds his brother Glappa as king of Bernicia (approximate date)
events.blurb: Adda succeeds his brother Glappa as king of Bernicia (approximate date).

events.title: Ceawlin succeeds his father Cynric as king of Wessex (approximate date)
events.blurb: Ceawlin succeeds his father Cynric as king of Wessex (approximate date).

events.title: The First Council of Braga is held
events.blurb: The First Council of Braga is held. The council condemns the doctrine of Priscillianism.

events.title: Emperor Wucheng of Northern Qi
events.blurb: Winter – Wu Cheng Di succeeds his brother Xiao Zhao Di, who dies from injuries suffered while hunting, as Chinese emperor of Northern Qi.

events.title: Sky Witness is crowned as leader of Calakmul
events.blurb: Sky Witness is crowned as leader of Calakmul.

events.title: Pope Pelagius I dies in Rome after a five-year reign, and is succeeded by John…
events.blurb: Pope Pelagius I dies in Rome after a five-year reign, and is succeeded by John III as the 61st pope.

events.title: King Sigebert I repels an attack on Austrasia by the Avars at Regensburg (Germany)
events.blurb: King Sigebert I repels an attack on Austrasia by the Avars at Regensburg (Germany). He moves his capital from Reims to Metz (approximate date).

events.title: The secondary capital Taiyuan in Northern Qi is rebuilt and becomes a center…
events.blurb: The secondary capital Taiyuan in Northern Qi is rebuilt and becomes a center of Buddhism.

events.title: Tauredunum event
events.blurb: Tauredunum event: A mountain landslide into the Rhone river destroys a fort and two villages, and creates a tsunami in Lake Geneva. The wave which reaches Lausanne is thirteen metres high, and eight metres high by the time it hits Geneva.

events.title: Cadoc, abbot of Llancarfan (Wales), settles in Weedon and is made bishop…
events.blurb: Cadoc, abbot of Llancarfan (Wales), settles in Weedon and is made bishop (approximate date).

events.title: Tulum, Maya walled city, on the Yucatán Peninsula (modern Mexico) is first…
events.blurb: Tulum, Maya walled city, on the Yucatán Peninsula (modern Mexico) is first mentioned on a stele inscription.

events.title: Columba reports seeing the Loch Ness Monster at the River Ness (according to…
events.blurb: Columba reports seeing the Loch Ness Monster at the River Ness (according to the "Life of St. Columba").

events.title: The Madaba Map is made in the Byzantine church of Saint George
events.blurb: The Madaba Map is made in the Byzantine church of Saint George. The floor mosaic contains the depiction of the Holy Land (approximate date).

events.title: Agathias begins to write a history, beginning where Procopius finished his work
events.blurb: Agathias begins to write a history, beginning where Procopius finished his work.

events.title: Justin II sends his son-in-law Baduarius (magister militum) with a Byzantine…
events.blurb: Justin II sends his son-in-law Baduarius (magister militum) with a Byzantine army, to support the Gepids in their war against the Lombards.

events.title: Justin II recalls his cousin Justin (pretender to the throne) to Constantinople
events.blurb: Justin II recalls his cousin Justin (pretender to the throne) to Constantinople; after accusations against him, he is placed under house arrest.

events.title: Gao Wei succeeds his father Wu Cheng Di as ruler of the Chinese Northern Qi…
events.blurb: Gao Wei succeeds his father Wu Cheng Di as ruler of the Chinese Northern Qi Dynasty. Wu Cheng Di becomes a regent and Grand Emperor.

events.title: Patriarch Eutychius of Constantinople is deposed as Ecumenical Patriarch of…
events.blurb: Patriarch Eutychius of Constantinople is deposed as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople by Justinian I after he refuses the Byzantine Emperor's order to adopt the tenets of the Aphthartodocetae, a sect of Monophysites.

events.title: Ahkal Moʼ Nahb II becomes the new ruler of Palenque and reigns until his death…
events.blurb: Ahkal Moʼ Nahb II becomes the new ruler of Palenque and reigns until his death in 570.

events.title: Justin II succeeds his uncle Justinian I as emperor of the Byzantine Empire
events.blurb: Justin II succeeds his uncle Justinian I as emperor of the Byzantine Empire. He begins his reign by refusing subsidies to the Avars, who conduct several large-scale raids through the Balkan Peninsula.

events.title: Ainmuire mac Sétnai becomes High King of Ireland, and rules from 566–569 (this…
events.blurb: Ainmuire mac Sétnai becomes High King of Ireland, and rules from 566–569 (this according to the Book of Leinster).

events.title: A poet from Italy named Venantius Fortunatus arrives at the Merovingian court…
events.blurb: A poet from Italy named Venantius Fortunatus arrives at the Merovingian court at Metz. With a strong grasp of traditional Roman poetry, Fortunatus impresses and entertains the Frankish royalty and aristocracy.

events.title: Fei Di, age 12, succeeds his father Wen Di, as emperor of the Chinese Chen dynasty
events.blurb: Fei Di, age 12, succeeds his father Wen Di, as emperor of the Chinese Chen dynasty. He honors his grand-aunt Zhang Yao'er with the title of Grand Empress, and she becomes his regent.

events.title: John III, patriarch of Constantinople, organizes a compromise between the…
events.blurb: John III, patriarch of Constantinople, organizes a compromise between the Chalcedonians and Monophysites.

events.title: King Charibert I dies without an heir
events.blurb: King Charibert I dies without an heir; his realm (region Neustria and Aquitaine) is divided between his brothers Guntram, Sigebert I and Chilperic I.

events.title: Lombard–Gepid War (567)
events.blurb: The Lombard–Gepid War (567) ends with a Lombard-Avar victory, and the annihilation of the Gepids.

events.title: Liuva I succeeds his predecessor Athanagild, after an interregnum of five…
events.blurb: Liuva I succeeds his predecessor Athanagild, after an interregnum of five months, and becomes king of the Visigoths.

events.title: Lombards
events.blurb: Spring – The Lombards, led by King Alboin, cross the Julian Alps. Their invasion of Northern Italy is almost unopposed;

events.title: A Turkish khan sends emissaries to the Byzantine Empire (approximate date)
events.blurb: A Turkish khan sends emissaries to the Byzantine Empire (approximate date).

events.title: Æthelric succeeds his brother Adda as king of Bernicia (modern Scotland)
events.blurb: Æthelric succeeds his brother Adda as king of Bernicia (modern Scotland). He rules from 568–572 (approximate date).

events.title: Mummolus, Gallo-Roman prefect, defeats the Lombards at Embrun and expels them…
events.blurb: Mummolus, Gallo-Roman prefect, defeats the Lombards at Embrun and expels them from Provence (Southern Gaul).

events.title: Paulinus I, patriarch of Aquileia, flees with the treasures of his church and…
events.blurb: Paulinus I, patriarch of Aquileia, flees with the treasures of his church and transfers them to the island of Grado.

events.title: The Turks and Sassanids succeed in destroying the Hepthalites on the eastern…
events.blurb: The Turks and Sassanids succeed in destroying the Hepthalites on the eastern frontier (approximate date).

events.title: The Nubian kingdom of Alodia is converted to Christianity by Byzantine…
events.blurb: The Nubian kingdom of Alodia is converted to Christianity by Byzantine missionaries (according to John of Ephesus).

events.title: Al-Mundhir III succeeds his father Al-Harith V and becomes king of the Ghassanids
events.blurb: Al-Mundhir III succeeds his father Al-Harith V and becomes king of the Ghassanids.

events.title: Gisulf I, nephew of Alboin, is appointed as the first duke of Friuli…
events.blurb: Gisulf I, nephew of Alboin, is appointed as the first duke of Friuli (approximate date).

events.title: The Garamantian Kingdom (modern Libya) signs a peace treaty with the Byzantine…
events.blurb: The Garamantian Kingdom (modern Libya) signs a peace treaty with the Byzantine Empire. The capital city of Garama is converted to Christianity.

events.title: Year of the Elephant, according to Islamic tradition
events.blurb: Year of the Elephant, according to Islamic tradition.

events.title: Leutfred becomes duke of Alemannia (modern Germany)
events.blurb: Leutfred becomes duke of Alemannia (modern Germany).

events.title: Ctesiphon, capital of the Sassanid Empire, becomes the largest city in the…
events.blurb: Ctesiphon, capital of the Sassanid Empire, becomes the largest city in the world, taking the lead from Constantinople, capital of the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Spoleto becomes the capital of an independent duchy, under the Lombard…
events.blurb: Spoleto becomes the capital of an independent duchy, under the Lombard chieftain Faroald (approximate date).

events.title: Abraha, Christian ruler of coastal Yemen, who was acting as a general for the…
events.blurb: Abraha, Christian ruler of coastal Yemen, who was acting as a general for the Christian kingdom in Abyssinia, begins a military expedition in Arabia against the predominantly pagan Quraysh of Mecca, known as the Year of the Elephant.

events.title: The first mention is made of the Spear of Destiny (approximate date)
events.blurb: The first mention is made of the Spear of Destiny (approximate date).

events.title: The anonymous Pilgrim of Piacenza travels the Holy Sites of Christianity in…
events.blurb: The anonymous Pilgrim of Piacenza travels the Holy Sites of Christianity in Syria, Palestine and Sinai, an experience that he later writes down as a travel report (approximate date).

events.title: Benevento becomes the capital of an independent duchy, under the Lombard…
events.blurb: Benevento becomes the capital of an independent duchy, under the Lombard chieftain Zotto (approximate date).

events.title: Wuffa becomes the first king of East Anglia, as recorded in the Anglo-Saxon…
events.blurb: Wuffa becomes the first king of East Anglia, as recorded in the Anglo-Saxon royal genealogies (approximate date).

events.title: Taspar Qaghan succeeds his brother Muqan Qaghan as ruler (khagan) of the…
events.blurb: Taspar Qaghan succeeds his brother Muqan Qaghan as ruler (khagan) of the Turkic Khaganate (Central Asia).

events.title: Calakmul defeats Tikal, bringing an end to the First Tikal-Calakmul War
events.blurb: Calakmul defeats Tikal, bringing an end to the First Tikal-Calakmul War.

events.title: Theodric succeeds his brother Æthelric as king of Bernicia (southeastern Scotland)
events.blurb: Theodric succeeds his brother Æthelric as king of Bernicia (southeastern Scotland). He rules until 579.

events.title: Alboin, king of the Lombards, is murdered at Verona in his palace, at the…
events.blurb: Alboin, king of the Lombards, is murdered at Verona in his palace, at the instigation of his wife Rosamund (daughter of the Gepid king Cunimund), and her henchman, Helmechis (the king's squire);

events.title: Battle of Arfderydd
events.blurb: Battle of Arfderydd: Leading his warband, Gwenddoleu ap Ceidio is slain by the sons of Eliffer, Gwrgi and Peredur. Myrddin Wyllt goes mad watching this defeat (according to the Annales Cambriae).

events.title: King Cleph completes the Lombard conquest of Tuscany (Central Italy) and…
events.blurb: King Cleph completes the Lombard conquest of Tuscany (Central Italy) and extends his dominion to the gates of Ravenna.

events.title: Sigibert I appoints Gregory to succeed his mother's cousin, Eufronius, as…
events.blurb: Sigibert I appoints Gregory to succeed his mother's cousin, Eufronius, as bishop of Tours (approximate date).

events.title: Sophia (empress)
events.blurb: Winter – Empress Sophia and Tiberius agree to a one year truce with the Persians, at the cost of 45,000 solidi. The truce applies only to the Mesopotamian front; in the Caucasus, war continues.

events.title: Áedán mac Gabráin becomes king of Dál Riata (Scotland) (approximate Date)
events.blurb: Áedán mac Gabráin becomes king of Dál Riata (Scotland) (approximate Date).

events.title: Marius Aventicensis is made bishop of Aventicum (modern Avenches)
events.blurb: Marius Aventicensis is made bishop of Aventicum (modern Avenches).

events.title: Pope John III dies at Rome after a 13-year tenure
events.blurb: Pope John III dies at Rome after a 13-year tenure. The Holy See becomes sede vacante until June of the following year.

events.title: Tardu succeeds his father Istämi, as governor (yabgu) of the Western Turkic…
events.blurb: Tardu succeeds his father Istämi, as governor (yabgu) of the Western Turkic Khaganate (Central Asia).

events.title: Zhiyi, Chinese monk, travels to Mount Tiantai for intensive study and practice
