events.blurb: Zhiyi, Chinese monk, travels to Mount Tiantai for intensive study and practice. He works with a group of disciples on the Indian meditation of śamatha and vipaśyanā.

events.title: Alexander of Tralles, Greek physician, writes "Libri duodecim de re Medica"…
events.blurb: Alexander of Tralles, Greek physician, writes "Libri duodecim de re Medica" (approximate date).

events.title: Pope Benedict I succeeds Pope John III as the 62nd pope
events.blurb: Pope Benedict I succeeds Pope John III as the 62nd pope.

events.title: Jinji becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla
events.blurb: Jinji becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla.

events.title: Northern Qi
events.blurb: Winter – Northern Qi, one of the Northern Dynasties, is conquered by Northern Zhou under Emperor Wu Di. He orders the last ruler (Gao Wei) and other members of the Gao clan to commit suicide.

events.title: Reccopolis (modern Zorita de los Canes) in Hispania is founded by King…
events.blurb: Reccopolis (modern Zorita de los Canes) in Hispania is founded by King Liuvigild, in honour of his son Reccared.

events.title: Battle of Deorham
events.blurb: Battle of Deorham: The Anglo-Saxons under Ceawlin of Wessex invade the lower Severn Valley, and defeat the British Celts at Dyrham (South West England).

events.title: Maurice (emperor)
events.blurb: Winter – Maurice is appointed commander-in-chief of the Byzantine army in the East. He succeeds Justinian, despite complete lack of military experience.

events.title: The Temple of Dendur, dedicated to the Egyptian gods Isis, Harpocrates (Horus)…
events.blurb: The Temple of Dendur, dedicated to the Egyptian gods Isis, Harpocrates (Horus) and Osiris, is converted for use as a Christian church (approximate date).

events.title: Wu Di, age 35, dies from an illness, and is succeeded by his eldest son Xuan…
events.blurb: Wu Di, age 35, dies from an illness, and is succeeded by his eldest son Xuan Di as emperor of Northern Zhou.

events.title: Summer – Emperor Wu Di engages in military campaigns on two fronts
events.blurb: Summer – Emperor Wu Di engages in military campaigns on two fronts: against the invading Göktürks to the north and against the Chen dynasty in the south.

events.title: Kongō Gumi, the world's oldest construction company (578–2006), is founded in…
events.blurb: Kongō Gumi, the world's oldest construction company (578–2006), is founded in Osaka (Japan).

events.title: Hermenegild, son of Visigothic king Liuvigild, marries Ingund
events.blurb: Hermenegild, son of Visigothic king Liuvigild, marries Ingund. He rebels against his father, starting in Seville (Southern Spain), and declares himself Catholic.

events.title: Jinpyeong becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla
events.blurb: Jinpyeong becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Silla.

events.title: Leander, Catholic bishop of Seville, is exiled by Liuvigild and withdraws to…
events.blurb: Leander, Catholic bishop of Seville, is exiled by Liuvigild and withdraws to Constantinople. At the Byzantine court he composes works against Arianism (approximate date).

events.title: Khosrau I dies after a 48-year reign, during which he has extended his realm…
events.blurb: Khosrau I dies after a 48-year reign, during which he has extended his realm from the River Oxus to the Red Sea. He is succeeded by his son Hormizd IV, who becomes king of the Persian Empire.

events.title: Frithuwald succeeds his brother Theodoric as king of Bernicia (Scotland)
events.blurb: Frithuwald succeeds his brother Theodoric as king of Bernicia (Scotland). He rules from 579–585 (approximate date).

events.title: Uneh Chan becomes the ruler of the Mayan city state of Calakmul in southern…
events.blurb: Uneh Chan becomes the ruler of the Mayan city state of Calakmul in southern Mexico and reigns until 611.

events.title: The Northern Zhou dynasty, strategically based in the basin of the Wei River,…
events.blurb: The Northern Zhou dynasty, strategically based in the basin of the Wei River, is supreme in Northern China. In the south only the Chen dynasty remains a rival.

events.title: Siege of Sirmium
events.blurb: Siege of Sirmium: The Avars march to the right bank of the River Sava, and besiege the Byzantine stronghold of Sirmium (Pannonia).

events.title: Palace coup in Austrasia
events.blurb: Palace coup in Austrasia: New advisors break the peace treaty with King Guntram, and make a new alliance with his half brother Chilperic I, in which Childebert II, age 11, is recognized as Chilperic's heir.

events.title: The "Great City of Helu", situated on the shores of Taihu Lake, is renamed…
events.blurb: The "Great City of Helu", situated on the shores of Taihu Lake, is renamed Suzhou during the Sui dynasty (approximate date).

events.title: Maurice writes an encyclopedic work on the science of war (the Strategikon),…
events.blurb: Maurice writes an encyclopedic work on the science of war (the Strategikon), which exercises a major influence on the military system.

events.title: Byzantine–Sasanian War
events.blurb: Byzantine–Sasanian War: A Byzantine army commanded by Maurice, and supported by Ghassanid forces under King Al-Mundhir III, fails to capture the Persian capital, Ctesiphon, along the Euphrates.

events.title: Al-Nu'man VI, son (de facto) of Mundhir III, revolts with the Ghassanids…
events.blurb: Al-Nu'man VI, son (de facto) of Mundhir III, revolts with the Ghassanids against the Byzantine Empire, after his father is treacherously arrested.

events.title: Emperor Xuan of Chen
events.blurb: Spring – Emperor Xuan of Chen, age 52, dies after a 13-year reign and is succeeded by his incompetent son Chen Shubao (Houzhu), who becomes the new ruler of the Chen dynasty.

events.title: John Mystacon
events.blurb: Autumn – Maurice elevates John Mystacon to magister militum per Orientem. He sends a Byzantine expeditionary force to Arzanene (Armenia), where they fight a pitched battle at the river Nymphius (Batman River).

events.title: Gundoald, illegitimate son of Clotaire I, arrives with the financial support…
events.blurb: Gundoald, illegitimate son of Clotaire I, arrives with the financial support of Constantinople in southern Gaul. He claims as usurper king the cities Poitiers and Toulouse, part of the Frankish Kingdom (approximate date).

events.title: Emperor Tiberius II Constantine, age 47, dies (possibly from deliberately…
events.blurb: Emperor Tiberius II Constantine, age 47, dies (possibly from deliberately poisoned food) at Constantinople, after a 4-year reign during which Thrace and Greece have been inundated by the Slavs.

events.title: Yohl Ikʼnal succeeds Kan Bahlam I as queen of the Maya city of Palenque (Mexico)
events.blurb: Yohl Ikʼnal succeeds Kan Bahlam I as queen of the Maya city of Palenque (Mexico).

events.title: Smallpox begins spreading from China to Japan and Korea (approximate date)
events.blurb: Smallpox begins spreading from China to Japan and Korea (approximate date).

events.title: The city of Monemvasia (Peloponnese) is founded by people seeking refuge from…
events.blurb: The city of Monemvasia (Peloponnese) is founded by people seeking refuge from the Slavs and Avars.

events.title: Eboric (also called Euric) succeeds his father Miro as king of the Suevi…
events.blurb: Eboric (also called Euric) succeeds his father Miro as king of the Suevi (Hispania Gallaecia).

events.title: The Slavs push south on the Balkan Peninsula
events.blurb: The Slavs push south on the Balkan Peninsula – partly in conjunction with the Avars under their ruler (khagan) Bayan I – ravaging the cities Athens and Corinth, and threatening the Long Walls of Constantinople.

events.title: The Exarchate of Ravenna is founded, and organised into a group of duchies,…
events.blurb: The Exarchate of Ravenna is founded, and organised into a group of duchies, mainly coastal cities on the Italian Peninsula. The civil and military head of these Byzantine territories is the exarch (governor) in Ravenna.

events.title: King Chilperic I is stabbed to death while returning from a hunt near Chelles,…
events.blurb: King Chilperic I is stabbed to death while returning from a hunt near Chelles, after a 23-year reign over a territory extending from Aquitaine, to the northern seacoast of what later will be France.

events.title: King Childebert II, age 15, takes up his sole rule of Austrasia
events.blurb: King Childebert II, age 15, takes up his sole rule of Austrasia. A Frankish army under King Guntram marches to Comminges (Pyrenees), and besieges the citadel of Saint-Bertrand.

events.title: Columbanus, Irish missionary, gathers 12 companions for his journey to…
events.blurb: Columbanus, Irish missionary, gathers 12 companions for his journey to Britain, probably to the Scottish coast. After a short time, he crosses the English Channel and lands in Brittany (France).

events.title: Hussa succeeds his brother Frithuwald as king of Bernicia (approximate date)
events.blurb: Hussa succeeds his brother Frithuwald as king of Bernicia (approximate date).

events.title: Creoda becomes king of Mercia (according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle)
events.blurb: Creoda becomes king of Mercia (according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle).

events.title: Emperor Bidatsu, age 47, dies of smallpox after a 13-year reign, and is…
events.blurb: Emperor Bidatsu, age 47, dies of smallpox after a 13-year reign, and is succeeded by his brother Yōmei as the 31st emperor of Japan.

events.title: Saint Comgall founds an abbey in Bangor, Northern Ireland
events.blurb: Saint Comgall founds an abbey in Bangor, Northern Ireland.

events.title: Battle of Solachon
events.blurb: Battle of Solachon: A Byzantine army under command of Philippicus defeats the Sassanid Persians, near Dara.

events.title: The Vlachs are first mentioned in a Byzantine chronicle (approximate date)
events.blurb: The Vlachs are first mentioned in a Byzantine chronicle (approximate date).

events.title: The Page with the Crucifixion, from the "Rabbula Gospels", at the Monastery of St
events.blurb: The Page with the Crucifixion, from the "Rabbula Gospels", at the Monastery of St. John in Beth Zagba (Syria), is completed. It is now kept at the Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Florence, Italy.

events.title: King Liuvigild dies at Toledo after an 18-year reign, and is succeeded by his…
events.blurb: King Liuvigild dies at Toledo after an 18-year reign, and is succeeded by his second son Reccared I.

events.title: Bagha Qaghan becomes the seventh ruler (khagan) of the Turkic Kaganate
events.blurb: Bagha Qaghan becomes the seventh ruler (khagan) of the Turkic Kaganate.

events.title: King Reccared I renounces Arianism and adopts Catholicism
events.blurb: King Reccared I renounces Arianism and adopts Catholicism. Many Visigothic nobles follow his example, but in Septimania (Southern Gaul) there are Arian uprisings.

events.title: Uncelen
events.blurb: Winter – Childebert II appoints Uncelen as the Duke of Alemannia (approximate date).

events.title: Sledd succeeds his father Æscwine as king of Essex (approximate date)
events.blurb: Sledd succeeds his father Æscwine as king of Essex (approximate date).

events.title: Comentiolus, Byzantine general (magister militum), assembles an army of 10,000…
events.blurb: Comentiolus, Byzantine general (magister militum), assembles an army of 10,000 men at Anchialus (modern Bulgaria). He prepares an ambush for the Avars in the Haemus Mountains.

events.title: Treaty of Andelot
events.blurb: Treaty of Andelot: Guntram recognizes King Childebert II of Austrasia as heir. He signs a treaty with Queen Brunhilda at Andelot-Blancheville.

events.title: Guaram I
events.blurb: Summer – Guaram I of Iberia, Georgian prince in exile, is sent by Emperor Maurice to the city of Mtskheta (Georgia). He restores the monarchy and is bestowed with the Byzantine court title of curopalates.

events.title: The Guanghua Temple in Putian (China) is built during the Chen dynasty, under…
events.blurb: The Guanghua Temple in Putian (China) is built during the Chen dynasty, under Emperor Chen Wu Di.

events.title: The Skellig Michael monastery is founded on a steep rocky island off the coast…
events.blurb: The Skellig Michael monastery is founded on a steep rocky island off the coast of Ireland (approximate date).

events.title: Æthelric succeeds his father Ælla as king of Deira in Northern England
events.blurb: Æthelric succeeds his father Ælla as king of Deira in Northern England.

events.title: The Lombard Kingdom (Italy) is converted to Roman Catholicism under the rule…
events.blurb: The Lombard Kingdom (Italy) is converted to Roman Catholicism under the rule of King Authari (approximate date).

events.title: The Third Council of Toledo, called by King Reccared I of the Visigoths,…
events.blurb: The Third Council of Toledo, called by King Reccared I of the Visigoths, renounces Arianism and embraces Catholicism.

events.title: Yan Zhitui, scholar-official, makes the first reference to the use of toilet…
events.blurb: Yan Zhitui, scholar-official, makes the first reference to the use of toilet paper in human history. It is used in the Chinese imperial court and amongst the other wealthy citizens.

events.title: Tulan Qaghan, son of Ishbara Qaghan, becomes the seventh ruler (khagan) of the…
events.blurb: Tulan Qaghan, son of Ishbara Qaghan, becomes the seventh ruler (khagan) of the Turkic Khaganate.

events.title: Bubonic plague
events.blurb: The plague hits Rome, and its victims include Pope Pelagius II.

events.title: Claudius, duke (dux) of Lusitania, defeats the Franks and Burgundians at…
events.blurb: Claudius, duke (dux) of Lusitania, defeats the Franks and Burgundians at Carcassonne (Languedoc) on the Aude River.

events.title: The Chinese Empire is reunited under the leadership of Emperor Wéndi (Sui…
events.blurb: The Chinese Empire is reunited under the leadership of Emperor Wéndi (Sui dynasty), who defeats the Chen forces at Jiankang (modern Nanjing), ending the Chen dynasty (the last of the Southern dynasties) that has ruled since 557.

events.title: King Authari marries Theodelinda, daughter of the Bavarian duke Garibald I
events.blurb: King Authari marries Theodelinda, daughter of the Bavarian duke Garibald I. A Catholic, she has great influence at court and among the Lombard nobility.

events.title: Breach at Cucca
events.blurb: Breach at Cucca. The Adige River overflows its banks, flooding the church of St. Zeno and damaging the walls of Verona.

events.title: Stephen I succeeds his father Guaram I as king of Iberia (Georgia)…
events.blurb: Stephen I succeeds his father Guaram I as king of Iberia (Georgia) (approximate date).

events.title: Owain mab Urien succeeds his father Urien, as Brythonic king of Rheged in…
events.blurb: Owain mab Urien succeeds his father Urien, as Brythonic king of Rheged in Northern England (approximate date).

events.title: Egidius, bishop of Reims, is tried at Metz before a council of bishops for a…
events.blurb: Egidius, bishop of Reims, is tried at Metz before a council of bishops for a conspiracy against King Childebert II; he is found guilty and exiled to Strasbourg.

events.title: Siege of Lindisfarne
events.blurb: Siege of Lindisfarne: A Brythonic coalition lays siege to King Hussa of Bernicia at Lindisfarne Castle (Holy Island).

events.title: Maurice establishes the Exarchate of Carthage in Africa
events.blurb: Maurice establishes the Exarchate of Carthage in Africa. He combines the civil authority of a praetorian prefect and the military authority, based at Carthage.

events.title: The Franks again invade Italy
events.blurb: The Franks again invade Italy; they capture Modena and Mantua. Several Lombard dukes defect: Gisulf I, duke of Friuli, is defeated and replaced by his son Gisulf II.

events.title: Hormizd IV
events.blurb: Spring – King Hormizd IV dismisses Bahrām Chobin as commander (Eran spahbed). He revolts and marches with the support of the Persian army towards Ctesiphon.

events.title: Yeongyang becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo
events.blurb: Yeongyang becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

events.title: John of Biclaro, Visigoth chronicler, finishes his "Chronicle" before he is…
events.blurb: John of Biclaro, Visigoth chronicler, finishes his "Chronicle" before he is appointed bishop of Girona (Catalonia, Spain).

events.title: Pope Pelagius II falls victim to the plague that devastated Rome
events.blurb: Pope Pelagius II falls victim to the plague that devastated Rome. He is succeeded by Gregory I, age 50, as the 64th pope, and the first from a monastic background.

events.title: Hormizd IV is deposed and assassinated by Persian nobles
events.blurb: Hormizd IV is deposed and assassinated by Persian nobles. Having ruled since 579, he is succeeded by his son Khosrau II as king of the Persian Empire.

events.title: Theodosius, eldest son of Maurice, is proclaimed as co-emperor
events.blurb: Theodosius, eldest son of Maurice, is proclaimed as co-emperor. He becomes his father's heir to the Byzantine throne.

events.title: Battle of Blarathon
events.blurb: Battle of Blarathon: A Persian army of about 40,000 men under King Bahrām VI is defeated, in the lowlands near Ganzak (northwestern Iran), by the Byzantines.

events.title: Agilulf, cousin of Authari (called "the Thuringian"), is raised on the shield…
events.blurb: Agilulf, cousin of Authari (called "the Thuringian"), is raised on the shield (a ceremonial investment) by Lombard warriors in Milan. He becomes king of the Lombards, on advice of the Lombard dukes (dux).

events.title: Arechis I succeeds his uncle Zotto as the second Duke of Benevento
events.blurb: Arechis I succeeds his uncle Zotto as the second Duke of Benevento.

events.title: The first city wall of Hangzhou (Eastern China) is constructed
events.blurb: The first city wall of Hangzhou (Eastern China) is constructed.

events.title: A Mesoamerican ballgame court is dedicated at the Mayan city of Chinkultic…
events.blurb: A Mesoamerican ballgame court is dedicated at the Mayan city of Chinkultic (Mexico).

events.title: Battle of Woden's Burg
events.blurb: Battle of Woden's Burg: After the mass killing at Woden's Burg, near Marlborough (South West England), Ceawlin is deposed as king of the West Saxons. His son Cuthwine is taken prisoner and goes into exile.

events.title: Ceol succeeds his uncle Ceawlin after his defeat at Woden's Burg
events.blurb: Ceol succeeds his uncle Ceawlin after his defeat at Woden's Burg. He becomes king of Wessex (according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle).

events.title: Ariulf becomes the second Duke of Spoleto (Central Italy)
events.blurb: Ariulf becomes the second Duke of Spoleto (Central Italy).

events.title: King Guntram, age 59, dies after a 31-year reign, and is succeeded by his…
events.blurb: King Guntram, age 59, dies after a 31-year reign, and is succeeded by his nephew Childebert II, who becomes ruler of Burgundy. He is buried at Saint Marcellus of Chalons Church, in Chalon-sur-Saône (Eastern France).

events.title: Emperor Sushun of Japan is murdered after 5 years on the throne by agents of…
events.blurb: Emperor Sushun of Japan is murdered after 5 years on the throne by agents of his rival Umako Soga, who is jealous of the emperor's power. He is succeeded by Suiko, widow of the late emperor Bidatsu.

events.title: Priscus (magister militum)
events.blurb: Spring – Priscus, commander-in-chief in Thrace, defeats the Slavic tribes and Gepids on Byzantine territory south of the Danube. He crosses the river to fight in the uncharted swamps and forests of modern-day Wallachia.

events.title: The Altar to Amitābha Buddha is made during the Sui dynasty
events.blurb: The Altar to Amitābha Buddha is made during the Sui dynasty. It is now kept at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

events.title: Anastasius I is restored as patriarch of Antioch, after Gregory dies
events.blurb: Anastasius I is restored as patriarch of Antioch, after Gregory dies.

events.title: Suiko appoints her 21-year-old nephew Shōtoku as regent, with strongman Umako Soga
events.blurb: Suiko appoints her 21-year-old nephew Shōtoku as regent, with strongman Umako Soga. He holds shared power for nearly 30 years, creating the nation's first constitution (Seventeen-article constitution).

events.title: The Shitennō-ji monastery is founded at Osaka (Japan) by Shōtoku
events.blurb: The Shitennō-ji monastery is founded at Osaka (Japan) by Shōtoku.

events.title: Pybba succeeds his father Creoda as king of Mercia (approximate date)
events.blurb: Pybba succeeds his father Creoda as king of Mercia (approximate date).

events.title: Supratisthitavarman succeeds his father Susthitavarman, as king of the Varman…
events.blurb: Supratisthitavarman succeeds his father Susthitavarman, as king of the Varman dynasty in Assam (Northeast India).

events.title: King Dynod Bwr of the Pennines (Northern England) dies fighting off a…
events.blurb: King Dynod Bwr of the Pennines (Northern England) dies fighting off a Bernician invasion. His kingdom Hen Ogledd ("The Old North") is overrun, and his family flees to Powys (approximate date).

events.title: Construction begins on the Zhaozhou Bridge ("Safe crossing bridge") in Hebei…
events.blurb: Construction begins on the Zhaozhou Bridge ("Safe crossing bridge") in Hebei Province, during the Sui dynasty (China).

events.title: After the death of Euin, Gaidoald becomes the Duke of Trent (Northern Italy)
events.blurb: After the death of Euin, Gaidoald becomes the Duke of Trent (Northern Italy).

events.title: Battle of Raith
events.blurb: Battle of Raith: An invading force of Angles lands on the Fife coast near Raith (Kirkcaldy) and defeats an alliance of Scots, Britons and Picts, under King Áedán mac Gabráin of Dál Riata (Scotland).

events.title: Chlothar II, age 13, becomes sole ruler of Neustria, and continues his…
events.blurb: Chlothar II, age 13, becomes sole ruler of Neustria, and continues his mother's feud with Brunhilda. He is advised to prepare for war against Austrasia, the eastern part of the Frankish Kingdom.

events.title: Mangalesha becomes king of the Chalukya dynasty, after his brother Kirtivarman…
events.blurb: Mangalesha becomes king of the Chalukya dynasty, after his brother Kirtivarman I dies. He rules as regent of Kirtivarman's son Pulakeshin II, and invades the territory of Khandesh and Gujarat (northwestern India).

events.title: Queen Fredegund defeats her old rival Brunhilda of Austrasia, who supports the…
events.blurb: Queen Fredegund defeats her old rival Brunhilda of Austrasia, who supports the claims of her grandsons Theudebert II and Theuderic II to the Frankish throne, against those of Fredegund's son Chlothar II.

events.title: The King's School is founded by Augustine in Canterbury
events.blurb: The King's School is founded by Augustine in Canterbury. He builds an abbey where the Benedictine teaching takes place.

events.title: Ceolwulf succeeds his brother Ceol as king of Wessex
events.blurb: Ceolwulf succeeds his brother Ceol as king of Wessex. He becomes regent of Ceol's son Cynegils who is too young to inherit the throne.

events.title: Missionaries begin to convert the Anglo-Saxons to Christianity throughout much…
events.blurb: Missionaries begin to convert the Anglo-Saxons to Christianity throughout much of what will later be the British Isles (approximate date).

events.title: The Guoqing Temple is built on Mount Tiantai (Zhejiang), and becomes the site…
events.blurb: The Guoqing Temple is built on Mount Tiantai (Zhejiang), and becomes the site for the teachings of Chinese Buddhism.

events.title: Battle of Catraeth
events.blurb: Battle of Catraeth: The Gododdin under Mynyddog Mwynfawr, Brythonic king of Hen Ogledd ("The Old North"), defeat the Angles of Bernicia and Deira, at the stronghold of Catraeth in Northern England (approximate date).

events.title: The Avars rout the Byzantine forces of Comentiolus (south of Haemus Mons), and…
events.blurb: The Avars rout the Byzantine forces of Comentiolus (south of Haemus Mons), and capture Drizipera (Thrace). A large part of their troops are killed by the plague, after many cities are devastated in the Balkan Peninsula.

events.title: Hye becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje
events.blurb: Hye becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

events.title: The Chinese fleet engages in battle against the Goguryeo fleet (50,000 men)…
events.blurb: The Chinese fleet engages in battle against the Goguryeo fleet (50,000 men) under Admiral Kang I-sik, and is destroyed in the Bohai Sea. During the invasion the Sui forces are all defeated, and Yang Liang is forced to retreat.

events.title: Priscus pursues the fleeing Avar tribes and invades their homeland in Pannonia
events.blurb: Priscus pursues the fleeing Avar tribes and invades their homeland in Pannonia. He devastates the land east of the Tisza River, deciding the war for the Byzantines and ending the Avar and Slavic incursions across the Danube.

events.title: Gate of Trajan
events.blurb: Autumn – Comentiolus reopens the Gate of Trajan pass, near Ihtiman (Bulgaria). This strategic mountain pass, whose fortress "Stipon" defends the border between the provinces Thrace and Macedonia, is not used for decades.

events.title: Rædwald becomes king (bretwalda) of East Anglia (East of England), under the…
events.blurb: Rædwald becomes king (bretwalda) of East Anglia (East of England), under the overlordship of Æthelberht of Kent (according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle).

events.title: Callinicus, governor (exarch) of Ravenna, repulses attacks of the South Slavs…
events.blurb: Callinicus, governor (exarch) of Ravenna, repulses attacks of the South Slavs in Istria (Croatia). The region is pillaged, but the Byzantines drive them all out.

events.title: The Hopewell tradition (North America) ceases to be the dominant culture…
events.blurb: The Hopewell tradition (North America) ceases to be the dominant culture (approximate date).

events.title: The oldest inscription in Mon language dated from 600 AD
events.blurb: The oldest inscription in Mon language dated from 600 AD. later found at Wat Phorang, Thailand.

events.title: The first of the Japanese embassies to Imperial China is sent (approximate date)
events.blurb: The first of the Japanese embassies to Imperial China is sent (approximate date).

events.title: 600-750 - Maguey Bloodletting Ritual, fragment of a fresco from Teotihuacan,…
events.blurb: 600-750 - Maguey Bloodletting Ritual, fragment of a fresco from Teotihuacan, Mexico, is made. Teotihuacan culture. It is now kept at the Cleveland Museum of Art.

events.title: Early settlers from the Marquesas build the Alakoko fishpond and taro fields…
events.blurb: Early settlers from the Marquesas build the Alakoko fishpond and taro fields on Kauai, Hawaii.

events.title: The population of the Earth rises to about 208 million people (approximate date)
events.blurb: The population of the Earth rises to about 208 million people (approximate date).

events.title: Moche culture ends in the Andes (approximate date)
events.blurb: Moche culture ends in the Andes (approximate date).

events.title: Nazca culture ends in the Andes (approximate date)
events.blurb: Nazca culture ends in the Andes (approximate date).

events.title: Namri Songtsen becomes the new king of Tibet (approximate date)
events.blurb: Namri Songtsen becomes the new king of Tibet (approximate date).

events.title: 600-900 - Palace and Temple of the Inscriptions (tomb-pyramid of K'inich…
events.blurb: 600-900 - Palace and Temple of the Inscriptions (tomb-pyramid of K'inich Janaab' Pakal), Palenque, Mexico, are built. Maya culture.

events.title: 600-900 - Cylindrical vessel is made
events.blurb: 600-900 - Cylindrical vessel is made. Maya culture. It is now kept at the Princeton University Art Museum, New Jersey.

events.title: Sumatra, Java, and the surrounding islands are converted to Buddhism
events.blurb: Sumatra, Java, and the surrounding islands are converted to Buddhism.

events.title: Mu becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje
events.blurb: Mu becomes king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

events.title: According to the Ynglinga saga, king Ingvar Harra of Sweden invades Adalsysla…
events.blurb: According to the Ynglinga saga, king Ingvar Harra of Sweden invades Adalsysla (present day Lääne County in Estonia), but is killed by the locals (approximate date).

events.title: Dorestad, lying in a fork between two branches of the Rhine, is established by…
events.blurb: Dorestad, lying in a fork between two branches of the Rhine, is established by the Franks as a trade center.

events.title: The Wari Empire is established in The Andes (approximate date)
events.blurb: The Wari Empire is established in The Andes (approximate date)

events.title: Food production increases in northern and Western Europe as a result of…
events.blurb: Food production increases in northern and Western Europe as a result of agricultural technology introduced by the Slavs, who employ a lightweight plow with a knife blade (coulter), that cuts deep into the soil at grassroots level,

events.title: The Qieyun, a Chinese character rhyme dictionary, is published
events.blurb: The Qieyun, a Chinese character rhyme dictionary, is published.

events.title: The future Archbishops of Canterbury (Mellitus, Justus, and Honorius), and the…
events.blurb: The future Archbishops of Canterbury (Mellitus, Justus, and Honorius), and the future Archbishop of York Paulinus, are sent to England by Pope Gregory I to aid Augustine in his missionary work.

events.title: Liuva II, age 18, succeeds his father Reccared I as king of the Visigoths
events.blurb: Liuva II, age 18, succeeds his father Reccared I as king of the Visigoths. Reccared dies a natural death at the capital in Toledo after a 15-year reign.

events.title: Witteric
events.blurb: Spring – Witteric is appointed commander-in-chief of the Visigoth army, and receives orders from King Liuva II to expel the Byzantines from Hispania.

events.title: 602 Surb Karapet Monastery earthquake
events.blurb: 602 Surb Karapet Monastery earthquake. It affected the Surb Karapet Monastery, located in the district of Taron.

events.title: Khosrau II annexes the Lakhmid kingdom (Southern Iraq), and puts king Nu'man…
events.blurb: Khosrau II annexes the Lakhmid kingdom (Southern Iraq), and puts king Nu'man III to death.

events.title: The future Pope Boniface III is appointed papal legate to Constantinople
events.blurb: The future Pope Boniface III is appointed papal legate to Constantinople.

events.title: Agilulf, under the influence of his wife Theodelinda, abandons Arianism for…
events.blurb: Agilulf, under the influence of his wife Theodelinda, abandons Arianism for Catholicism, and is (with his son Adaloald) baptised in the Cathedral of Monza, where later the Iron Crown of Lombardy is installed.

events.title: Battle of Degsastan
events.blurb: Battle of Degsastan: King Æthelfrith of Northumbria defeats the combined forces of the Strathclyde Britons and Scots under Áedán mac Gabráin,

events.title: Schuttern Abbey (Germany) is founded by the wandering Irish monk Offo
events.blurb: Schuttern Abbey (Germany) is founded by the wandering Irish monk Offo.

events.title: The last mention of the Roman Senate on the Italian mainland is made…
events.blurb: The last mention of the Roman Senate on the Italian mainland is made (according to the Gregorian register). It mentions that the Senate has acclaimed new statues of Emperor Phocas and Empress Leontia.

events.title: Æthelberht of Kent founds St
events.blurb: Æthelberht of Kent founds St. Paul's Cathedral. Mellitus is appointed the first Saxon bishop of London (and Essex).

events.title: Queen Brunhilda of Austrasia conspires to have Berthoald, Mayor of the Palace,…
events.blurb: Queen Brunhilda of Austrasia conspires to have Berthoald, Mayor of the Palace, assassinated. She convinces King Theuderic II to send him to inspect the royal villae along the Seine.

events.title: The See of Rochester is established, and Justus is appointed as bishop
events.blurb: The See of Rochester is established, and Justus is appointed as bishop. He founds Rochester Cathedral (Kent).

events.title: Pope Gregory I (the Great) dies at Rome, after a 14-year tenure
events.blurb: Pope Gregory I (the Great) dies at Rome, after a 14-year tenure. He has laid the foundations which claim papal absolutism,

events.title: Augustine, Archbishop of Canterbury, is succeeded by Laurence
events.blurb: Augustine, Archbishop of Canterbury, is succeeded by Laurence. He is a member of the Gregorian mission (see 596).

events.title: Emperor Wéndi dies, age 63, presumably assassinated by his son Yángdi, after a…
events.blurb: Emperor Wéndi dies, age 63, presumably assassinated by his son Yángdi, after a 23-year reign in which he has attacked hereditary privilege and reduced the power of the military aristocracy.

events.title: Battle of Ėtampes
events.blurb: Battle of Ėtampes: Theuderic II, with the aid of Berthoald, defeats the Frankish forces under King Chlothar II of Neustria, at Étampes (near Paris).

events.title: Emperor Phocas recognizes Agilulf as king of the Lombards, and signs a peace…
events.blurb: Emperor Phocas recognizes Agilulf as king of the Lombards, and signs a peace treaty. He pays a tribute and cedes Orvieto (Central Italy), among other towns. The Byzantine army is withdrawn from the Balkan Peninsula.

events.title: Phocas has Constantina, empress consort of Maurice, and her three daughters…
events.blurb: Phocas has Constantina, empress consort of Maurice, and her three daughters arrested. He accuses her of conspiracy, and has them executed at Chalcedon (Bithynia).

events.title: Emperor Yángdi orders the capital to be transferred from Chang'an to Luoyang
events.blurb: Emperor Yángdi orders the capital to be transferred from Chang'an to Luoyang. He begins the construction of the Grand Canal, that will link existing waterways to the new Chinese capital; it will be built by a million laborers.

events.title: King Harsha of Thanesar establishes a northern Indian Empire, and unites the…
events.blurb: King Harsha of Thanesar establishes a northern Indian Empire, and unites the small monarchical states, from Punjab to the Indus Valley (modern Pakistan).

events.title: Shashanka is the first recorded independent king of Bengal
events.blurb: Shashanka is the first recorded independent king of Bengal. He establishes his capital in modern-day Murshidabad (approximate date).

events.title: Cearl succeeds Pybba as king of Mercia (English Midlands)
events.blurb: Cearl succeeds Pybba as king of Mercia (English Midlands).

events.title: Sabinian dies at Rome after a two-year reign, and will not be replaced until 607
events.blurb: Sabinian dies at Rome after a two-year reign, and will not be replaced until 607.

events.title: The Hōryū-ji Buddhist temple in Ikaruga, near Nara (Japan), is constructed
events.blurb: The Hōryū-ji Buddhist temple in Ikaruga, near Nara (Japan), is constructed.

events.title: Yángdi is offended by his general Gao Jiong, who makes several comments…
events.blurb: Yángdi is offended by his general Gao Jiong, who makes several comments critical of the emperor's policies, against Tujue submissive Yami Qaghan. He is executed (beheaded), and Gao's sons are exiled to the border provinces (Northern China).

events.title: Empress Suiko appoints Ono no Imoko as official envoy to the Sui Court…
events.blurb: Empress Suiko appoints Ono no Imoko as official envoy to the Sui Court (Japanese missions to Imperial China).

events.title: The observance of Halloween in the Roman Catholic Church is first recorded
events.blurb: The observance of Halloween in the Roman Catholic Church is first recorded.

events.title: Heraclius proclaims himself and his son as consuls, claiming the imperial…
events.blurb: Heraclius proclaims himself and his son as consuls, claiming the imperial title—and mint coins with the two wearing the consular robes. Syria and Palaestina Prima revolt.

events.title: Eochaid Buide succeeds his father Áedán mac Gabráin as king of Dál Riata…
events.blurb: Eochaid Buide succeeds his father Áedán mac Gabráin as king of Dál Riata (modern Scotland).

events.title: Heraclian revolt
events.blurb: Heraclian revolt: Heraclius the Elder, exarch of Africa, and his son (also named Heraclius) revolt against Emperor Phocas, whose regime in Constantinople has become unpopular and violent.

events.title: The Column of Phocas at Rome is dedicated in honour of Phocas
events.blurb: The Column of Phocas at Rome is dedicated in honour of Phocas. The Corinthian column has a height of 13.6 m (44 ft).

events.title: Pope Boniface IV succeeds Boniface III, as the 67th pope of Rome
events.blurb: Pope Boniface IV succeeds Boniface III, as the 67th pope of Rome.

events.title: Nicetas, cousin of future emperor Heraclius, launches an overland invasion in…
events.blurb: Nicetas, cousin of future emperor Heraclius, launches an overland invasion in Egypt. He defeats a Byzantine army under Bonus (comes Orientis) outside Alexandria, sent from Constantinople.

events.title: The Pantheon in Rome is consecrated as "St
events.blurb: The Pantheon in Rome is consecrated as "St. Mary and the Martyrs" (informally known as "Santa Maria Rotonda") by Pope Boniface IV (or 610).

events.title: Muhammad claims to have received what was to become the first wahy of Islam
events.blurb: Muhammad claims to have received what was to become the first wahy of Islam.

events.title: Paper technology is imported into Japan from China by the Korean Buddhist…
events.blurb: Paper technology is imported into Japan from China by the Korean Buddhist priest, Dam Jing (approximate date).

events.title: The Volga Bulgaria arises on the territory of modern Russia, being the first…
events.blurb: The Volga Bulgaria arises on the territory of modern Russia, being the first civilization in the region to arise from the Early Slavs (approximate date).

events.title: Selyf ap Cynan succeeds his father Cynan Garwyn as king of Powys (Wales)
events.blurb: Selyf ap Cynan succeeds his father Cynan Garwyn as king of Powys (Wales).

events.title: King Theuderic II loses Alsace, Champagne and Thurgau to his elder brother…
events.blurb: King Theuderic II loses Alsace, Champagne and Thurgau to his elder brother Theudebert II of Austrasia. His Burgundian army is defeated east of the Jura Mountains against the Alemanni.

events.title: John V (the Merciful) becomes patriarch of Alexandria (approximate date)
events.blurb: John V (the Merciful) becomes patriarch of Alexandria (approximate date).

events.title: The Four Gates Pagoda, located in central Shandong Province (East China), is…
events.blurb: The Four Gates Pagoda, located in central Shandong Province (East China), is completed.

events.title: Gallus founds the monastery of St
events.blurb: Gallus founds the monastery of St. Gallen (Switzerland).

events.title: Battle of Salsu
events.blurb: Battle of Salsu: A Sui force of 305,000 men is defeated by the Korean general Ŭlchi Mundŏk at the Yalu River; only 2,700 troops survive.

events.title: The Holy Sponge is brought to Constantinople from Palestine
events.blurb: The Holy Sponge is brought to Constantinople from Palestine.

events.title: King Theudebert II is defeated by his brother Theuderic II at Toul…
events.blurb: King Theudebert II is defeated by his brother Theuderic II at Toul (northeastern France). He is captured in battle and, after having his royal paraphernalia taken, is handed over to his grandmother Brunhilda.

events.title: Arnulf, counselor of Theudebert II, becomes bishop of Metz
events.blurb: Arnulf, counselor of Theudebert II, becomes bishop of Metz.

events.title: Sisebut succeeds Gundemar as king of the Visigoths
events.blurb: Sisebut succeeds Gundemar as king of the Visigoths. He begins a campaign against the remains of Byzantine power in Spania.

events.title: Goguryeo–Sui War
events.blurb: Goguryeo–Sui War: Emperor Yángdi invades Goguryeo (Korea) with an expeditionary force of over one million men, named the "24 Armies".

events.title: Empress Eudokia, wife of Heraclius, dies of epilepsy
events.blurb: Empress Eudokia, wife of Heraclius, dies of epilepsy. She leaves two children, and is buried in the Church of the Holy Apostles in Constantinople.

events.title: Sak Kʼukʼ succeeds her father Ajen Yohl Mat, as queen of the Maya state of…
events.blurb: Sak Kʼukʼ succeeds her father Ajen Yohl Mat, as queen of the Maya state of Palenque (modern Mexico).

events.title: Chlothar II reunites the Frankish Kingdom by ordering the murder of Sigebert II
events.blurb: Chlothar II reunites the Frankish Kingdom by ordering the murder of Sigebert II. He accuses Brunhilda, age 70, of killing ten kings of the Franks (according to the Liber Historiae Francorum).

events.title: Battle of Chester
events.blurb: Battle of Chester: King Æthelfrith of Northumbria invades Gwynedd (northwest Wales), in order to route out his old enemy, Edwin of Deira. A united Brythonic force (Gwynedd, Powys, Pengwern and Dumnonian warriors) is defeated near Chester.

events.title: Isanapura becomes the capital of the Cambodian kingdom of Chenla (approximate…
events.blurb: Isanapura becomes the capital of the Cambodian kingdom of Chenla (approximate date).

events.title: Battle of Antioch
events.blurb: Battle of Antioch: Heraclius mobilises a Byzantine expeditionary force to Antioch (Syria), but is completely defeated outside the city by the Persians. Shahin Vahmanzadegan makes further inroads into Central and Western Anatolia.

events.title: Constantine is crowned co-emperor (Caesar) by his father Heraclius and shortly…
events.blurb: Constantine is crowned co-emperor (Caesar) by his father Heraclius and shortly after betrothed to his cousin, Gregoria, daughter of Nicetas. Only 8 months old, Constantine has no real power and his dynastic title is purely ceremonial.

events.title: The Sudarium of Oviedo is taken from Palestine, after the invasion of the…
events.blurb: The Sudarium of Oviedo is taken from Palestine, after the invasion of the Sassanid Persians.

events.title: Byzantine–Sasanian War of 602–628
events.blurb: Byzantine–Sasanian War of 602–628:

events.title: Sasanian conquest of Jerusalem
events.blurb: Sasanian conquest of Jerusalem: A Persian–Judaean army (26,000 men) commanded by Shahrbaraz captures and sacks Jerusalem, after a 20-day siege against the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: The Levantine cities of Caesarea Maritima, Arsuf, and Tiberias surrender on…
events.blurb: The Levantine cities of Caesarea Maritima, Arsuf, and Tiberias surrender on terms to the Sasanians.

events.title: The Palace of Diocletian in Split (Croatia) is damaged by the Avars, who sack…
events.blurb: The Palace of Diocletian in Split (Croatia) is damaged by the Avars, who sack the nearby city of Salona. The population flees to the walled palace, which is able to hold out.

events.title: The Persians destroy the Ghassanid Kingdom (Arabia), a vassal state of the…
events.blurb: The Persians destroy the Ghassanid Kingdom (Arabia), a vassal state of the Byzantine Empire (approximate date).

events.title: King Chlothar II promulgates the Edict of Paris (Edictum Chlotacharii), a sort…
events.blurb: King Chlothar II promulgates the Edict of Paris (Edictum Chlotacharii), a sort of Frankish Magna Carta that defends the rights of the Frankish nobles and the church,

events.title: The Balkans are freely overrun by the Slavs, who settle in large numbers in…
events.blurb: The Balkans are freely overrun by the Slavs, who settle in large numbers in what is now Bulgaria, Serbia, North Macedonia and parts of Greece.

events.title: The city of Epidaurus (Dalmatia) is destroyed by the Avars and Slavic invaders
events.blurb: The city of Epidaurus (Dalmatia) is destroyed by the Avars and Slavic invaders. The Illyrian refugees flee to the nearby island Laus, where they found Dubrovnik (Ragusa).

events.title: Bangor Massacre
events.blurb: Bangor Massacre: The Anglo-Saxons, under King Æthelfrith of Northumbria, after defeating the Kingdom of Powys, finally reach the Irish Sea and massacre 1,200 Christian monks at their monastery, in Bangor (Wales).

events.title: Eleutherius succeeds John I as exarch of Ravenna
events.blurb: Eleutherius succeeds John I as exarch of Ravenna. He persecutes those implicated in the murder of John and the judges of the State.

events.title: The Slavs under Chatzon attack in longboats along the coasts of Thessaly,…
events.blurb: The Slavs under Chatzon attack in longboats along the coasts of Thessaly, western Anatolia, and various Greek islands. They besiege the Byzantine city of Thessaloniki in a combined land and sea attack.

events.title: The Persian army under Shahin Vahmanzadegan destroys the city of Sardis,…
events.blurb: The Persian army under Shahin Vahmanzadegan destroys the city of Sardis, including its synagogue. Its importance is due to a highway, leading from the interior to the Aegean coast.

events.title: Adaloald, age 14, succeeds his father Agilulf as Lombard king of Italy
events.blurb: Adaloald, age 14, succeeds his father Agilulf as Lombard king of Italy. He reigns under his mother Theodelinda as regent.

events.title: Mellitus, bishop of London, is exiled by Sexred and his pagan brothers (Sæward…
events.blurb: Mellitus, bishop of London, is exiled by Sexred and his pagan brothers (Sæward and Sigeberht). He is forced to take refuge in Gaul, and returns to England the following year.

events.title: King Sæberht of Essex dies after a 12-year reign, and is succeeded by his son…
events.blurb: King Sæberht of Essex dies after a 12-year reign, and is succeeded by his son Sexred. He rules conjointly with his two brothers Sæward and Sigeberht; they throw out the Christian missionaries and return to paganism.

events.title: Æthelberht, the first Christian Anglo-Saxon king, dies in Kent after a 26-year…
events.blurb: Æthelberht, the first Christian Anglo-Saxon king, dies in Kent after a 26-year reign. He is succeeded by his pagan son, Eadbald, who promptly marries his stepmother Emma, in accordance with pre-Christian custom.

events.title: Battle of Bu'ath
events.blurb: Battle of Bu'ath: A pre-Islamic Arabian conflict between the Aws and Khazraj, two major Arabian tribes of Medina.

events.title: Heathens revolt in Kent under King Eadbald
events.blurb: Heathens revolt in Kent under King Eadbald. During the uprising Justus, bishop of Rochester, flees to Gaul.

events.title: Sigeberht becomes king of Essex, after his father Sæward and uncle Sexred are…
events.blurb: Sigeberht becomes king of Essex, after his father Sæward and uncle Sexred are killed in battle against the West Saxons.

events.title: Battle of Huoyi
events.blurb: Battle of Huoyi: Rebel forces under Li Yuān defeat the Sui troops near the Fen River, and capture the Chinese capital, Chang'an.

events.title: Yeongnyu becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo
events.blurb: Yeongnyu becomes ruler of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

events.title: The Persians besiege Alexandria
events.blurb: The Persians besiege Alexandria; the defence of the city is led by Nicetas (cousin of emperor Heraclius). The Byzantine resistance is undermined by a blockade of the harbor; the usual grain supplies are cut off from Egypt to Constantinople.

events.title: The Sui dynasty ends
events.blurb: The Sui dynasty ends: Rebel leader Li Yuan captures Luoyang, and has Emperor Yángdi murdered.

events.title: Battle of Yanshi
events.blurb: Battle of Yanshi: Wang Shichong decisively defeats Li Mi, during the transition from Sui to Tang civil war.

events.title: Pope Adeodatus I dies in Rome after a 3-year reign, in which he has reversed…
events.blurb: Pope Adeodatus I dies in Rome after a 3-year reign, in which he has reversed the policies of his predecessors, Boniface IV and Gregory I, who favored monks over the secular clergy. Adeodatus will not be replaced until next year.

events.title: Battle of Qianshuiyuan
events.blurb: Battle of Qianshuiyuan: The Tang dynasty scores a decisive victory over their rival Xue Rengao.

events.title: The calculation of the Chinese calendar begins to use true motions of the sun…
events.blurb: The calculation of the Chinese calendar begins to use true motions of the sun and moon, modeled using two offset opposing parabolas.

events.title: Kubrat, ruler of the Bulgars, is baptised in Constantinople
events.blurb: Kubrat, ruler of the Bulgars, is baptised in Constantinople.

events.title: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks
events.blurb: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks: A khagan of the Western Turkic Khaganate is assassinated in a Chinese palace by Eastern Turkic rivals, with the approval of Emperor Gaozu of Tang.

events.title: Pope Boniface V succeeds Adeodatus I as the 69th pope of Rome
events.blurb: Pope Boniface V succeeds Adeodatus I as the 69th pope of Rome.

events.title: The town of Cholula is founded in central Mexico (later said to be the oldest…
events.blurb: The town of Cholula is founded in central Mexico (later said to be the oldest continuously occupied town in all of North America).

events.title: The Angles under King Edwin of Northumbria invade Rheged ("Old North") in…
events.blurb: The Angles under King Edwin of Northumbria invade Rheged ("Old North") in Northern England, and expel King Llywarch Hen. He flees to Powys, and becomes a famous bard. Edwin's armies fight against Gododdin and Strathclyde.

events.title: Weltenburg Abbey in Bavaria (Germany) is founded by Benedictine monks
events.blurb: Weltenburg Abbey in Bavaria (Germany) is founded by Benedictine monks.

events.title: King Pulakeshin II defeats the Harsha army on the banks of the Narmada River
events.blurb: King Pulakeshin II defeats the Harsha army on the banks of the Narmada River. Harsha loses a major part of his elephant force and retreats. A truce establishes Narmada as the northern boundary of the Chalukya Kingdom (India).

events.title: The Chinese establish an imperial bureau for the manufacture of porcelain
events.blurb: The Chinese establish an imperial bureau for the manufacture of porcelain. Their technology will advance further under the Tang dynasty (approximate date).

events.title: The city of Málaga, in southern Spain in the province of Spania, is conquered…
events.blurb: The city of Málaga, in southern Spain in the province of Spania, is conquered by the Visigoths.

events.title: Battle of Hulao
events.blurb: Battle of Hulao: Li Shimin defeats the numerically superior army of Dou Jiande near the Hulao Pass.

events.title: Wang Shichong, self-declared emperor, surrenders to Li Shimin at Luoyang…
events.blurb: Wang Shichong, self-declared emperor, surrenders to Li Shimin at Luoyang following Dou Jiande's defeat. Gaozu spares his life, but he is later assassinated.

events.title: Xuanzang is fully ordained as a Buddhist monk at the age of 20
events.blurb: Xuanzang is fully ordained as a Buddhist monk at the age of 20.

events.title: The Western Turks conquer the Oxus valley and cooperate with Heraclius against…
events.blurb: The Western Turks conquer the Oxus valley and cooperate with Heraclius against Persia, taking Khorasan (modern Afghanistan).

events.title: Tajoom Ukʼab Kʼahkʼ becomes the ruler of the Mayan city state of Calakmul in…
events.blurb: Tajoom Ukʼab Kʼahkʼ becomes the ruler of the Mayan city state of Calakmul in southern Mexico and reigns until 630.

events.title: or June 17
events.blurb: or June 17 – The Islamic prophet Muhammad secretly leaves his home in Mecca to make the Hijrah (emigrate) to Yathrib (later renamed by him Medina), along with his companion Abu Bakr.

events.title: or June 28
events.blurb: or June 28 – Muhammad does not enter Yathrib directly, but stops at its outlying environs of Quba. He establishes the Quba Mosque here, the first mosque of Islam.

events.title: or July 13
events.blurb: or July 13 – After a fourteen days' stay in Quba, Muhammad finally moves from Quba to Yathrib, and is greeted cordially by its people.

events.title: Tuyuhun invasion of Gansu
events.blurb: Tuyuhun invasion of Gansu: Tang forces under Chai Shao defeat the Tuyuhun, and prevent further incursions into Gansu (China).

events.title: Tori Busshi makes "Shaka Triad", in the kon-dō of Hōryū-ji, during the Asuka…
events.blurb: Tori Busshi makes "Shaka Triad", in the kon-dō of Hōryū-ji, during the Asuka period (approximate date).

events.title: Samo, reputedly a Frankish merchant, is elected king of the Slavs in Moravia,…
events.blurb: Samo, reputedly a Frankish merchant, is elected king of the Slavs in Moravia, Slovakia and Lower Austria.

events.title: Khosrow II
events.blurb: Winter – King Khosrow II withdraws most of his troops from Chalcedon (Anatolia); he assembles three armies to trap and destroy Heraclius' forces.

events.title: The Yiwen Leiju encyclopedia is completed during the Tang dynasty, by the…
events.blurb: The Yiwen Leiju encyclopedia is completed during the Tang dynasty, by the Chinese calligrapher Ouyang Xun.

events.title: Eorpwald succeeds his father Rædwald, as king (bretwalda) of the independent…
events.blurb: Eorpwald succeeds his father Rædwald, as king (bretwalda) of the independent Kingdom of East Anglia (approximate date). Raedwald is regarded as the most likely occupant of the Sutton Hoo ship-burial which contains the Sutton Hoo helmet.

events.title: The Raid on Nakhla, the first successful raid the Muslims of Medina, against…
events.blurb: (29 Rajab 2 AH) The Raid on Nakhla, the first successful raid the Muslims of Medina, against the Quraysh tribe in Mecca, is carried out by Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, who leads the plunder of a caravan of supplies.

events.title: Chinese General Li Daliang leads an army to retake the Yu prefecture, near…
events.blurb: Chinese General Li Daliang leads an army to retake the Yu prefecture, near Xuancheng in what is now the Anhui province, from the rebel leader Fu Gongshi.

events.title: While praying in the Masjid al-Qiblatayn in Medina, the Islamic prophet…
events.blurb: While praying in the Masjid al-Qiblatayn in Medina, the Islamic prophet Muhammad receives revelations from God on the qibla, the direction of prayer, that he should be facing Mecca rather than Jerusalem during prayer,

events.title: Battle of Badr
events.blurb: (17 Ramadah 2 AH) The Battle of Badr takes place in what is now Saudi Arabia as Muhammad and some 300 of his followers from Medina surprise a reinforced Meccan caravan at Badr (modern-day Saudi Arabia) returning from Syria,

events.title: Heraclius, Emperor of Byzantium, departs from his capital at Constantinople…
events.blurb: Heraclius, Emperor of Byzantium, departs from his capital at Constantinople (now Istanbul in Turkey) with his wife, the Empress Martina, and two of his children, and does not return for more than four years.

events.title: Siege of Banu Qaynuqa
events.blurb: (15 Shawwal 2 AH) The Siege of Banu Qaynuqa is started by the Muslims in what is now Yathrib in Saudi Arabia, four days after Ghalib ibn Abd Allah al-Laythi is dispatched by Muhammad.

events.title: Emperor Haraclius celebrates Easter at Nicomedia (now İzmit) then travels to…
events.blurb: Emperor Haraclius celebrates Easter at Nicomedia (now İzmit) then travels to Caesarea (now Kayseri), proceeding during April to Theodosiopolis. He leads troops into Armenia and sacks its capital, Dvin.

events.title: Du Fuwei, a Chinese prince who rebelled against Sui dynasty China and then was…
events.blurb: (27th day of the 3rd month of the 6th year of the Wu'de era) Du Fuwei, a Chinese prince who rebelled against Sui dynasty China and then was rewarded with the title "Prince of Wu" by Emperor Gaozu of Tang, dies suddenly of poisoning,

events.title: Justus
events.blurb: St. Justus is appointed as the new Archbishop of Canterbury by Pope Boniface V upon the death of Archbishop Mellitus., receiving the pallium — symbol of the jurisdiction entrusted to archbishops.

events.title: While at Ganzak at what is now northwest Iran, the Sassanid Emperor Khosrow II…
events.blurb: While at Ganzak at what is now northwest Iran, the Sassanid Emperor Khosrow II (Chosroes) is informed by soldiers who had escaped capture that Emperor Heraclius of Byzantium is preparing a surprise attack.

events.title: Upon the death of Khunays ibn Hudhafa, a companion of Muhammad, Khunays's…
events.blurb: Upon the death of Khunays ibn Hudhafa, a companion of Muhammad, Khunays's widow Hafsa bint Umar becomes eligible to marry Muhammad.

events.title: The Army of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, led by Illig Qaghan, clashes with…
events.blurb: The Army of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, led by Illig Qaghan, clashes with the army of Tang dynasty China, led by Taizong, Prince of Qin and son of Emperor Gaozu,

events.title: A group of 1,000 Muslims from Mecca, led by Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, sets out from…
events.blurb: A group of 1,000 Muslims from Mecca, led by Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, sets out from Mecca to capture Medina, defended by the Banu Khazraj tribe, led by Abd Allah ibn Ubayy.

events.title: Battle of Sarus
events.blurb: Battle of Sarus: Heraclius is victorious in a Byzantine assault river crossing. The reinforced Persians under Shahrbaraz are defeated along the Sarus River, near Adana (modern Turkey).

events.title: Battle of Uhud
events.blurb: Battle of Uhud: Muhammad retreats against the inhabitants of Mecca (Saudi Arabia), which they consider a victory.

events.title: Heraclius invites the Croats, a Slavic tribe living in Galicia, Silesia, and…
events.blurb: Heraclius invites the Croats, a Slavic tribe living in Galicia, Silesia, and Bohemia, to settle in Illyricum. They are given the land between the Drava River and the Adriatic Sea for ridding of Avars.

events.title: Edinburgh (Scotland) is founded by Edwin of Northumbria (approximate date)
events.blurb: Edinburgh (Scotland) is founded by Edwin of Northumbria (approximate date).

events.title: Siege of Constantinople
events.blurb: Siege of Constantinople: A horde of Avars, consisting of about 80,000 men (including large contingents of Slavs, Bulgars, and other "barbarians"), attack the walls of Constantinople.

events.title: Arioald succeeds his brother-in-law Adaloald as king of the Lombards, and…
events.blurb: Arioald succeeds his brother-in-law Adaloald as king of the Lombards, and afterwards goes insane. Arioald has his wife locked up in a monastery, accusing her of plotting against him with Grasulf II, duke of Friuli (northern Italy).

events.title: Eanflæd, daughter of Edwin of Northumbria, is born at a royal residence by the…
events.blurb: Eanflæd, daughter of Edwin of Northumbria, is born at a royal residence by the River Derwent. She is baptised by Paulinus, bishop of York.

events.title: Li Shimin travels to the Tang capital Chang'an to bid farewell to his younger…
events.blurb: Li Shimin travels to the Tang capital Chang'an to bid farewell to his younger brother Li Yuanji, who has been given command of a Chinese expedition against the Eastern Turkic Khaganate.

events.title: The Avars and Persian allies under Shahrbaraz launch an attack along the…
events.blurb: The Avars and Persian allies under Shahrbaraz launch an attack along the entire length of the Theodosian Walls (about 5.7 kilometres); the main effort is concentrated against the central section, particularly the low-lying mesoteichion.

events.title: In the waters of the Golden Horn, the Persian fleet is destroyed while…
events.blurb: In the waters of the Golden Horn, the Persian fleet is destroyed while ferrying reinforcements. The Avars, having suffered terrible losses, running short of food and supplies, burn their siege engines.

events.title: Emperor Gao Zu abdicates in favor of his son Li Shimin after an 8-year reign
events.blurb: Emperor Gao Zu abdicates in favor of his son Li Shimin after an 8-year reign. He passes the throne to him (as Emperor Tai Zong).

events.title: St Peter's School, York, is founded by Paulinus
events.blurb: St Peter's School, York, is founded by Paulinus.

events.title: Dastgerd
events.blurb: Winter – Heraclius plunders the city palace of Dastgerd (Iran) and gains tremendous riches (also recovering 300 captured Byzantine flags). He turns northeastward to Caucasian Albania to rest his army.

events.title: Cunibert is elected bishop of Cologne
events.blurb: Cunibert is elected bishop of Cologne. Throughout his episcopacy, monasticism flourishes in Austrasia (approximate date).

events.title: Battle of the Trench
events.blurb: Battle of the Trench: Muhammad successfully withstands a siege for 27 days at Medina, by Meccan forces (10,000 men) under Abu Sufyan, whose allies, the Jewish tribe of Banu Qurayza, ultimately surrender to Muhammad.

events.title: King Edwin of Northumbria is converted to Christianity by Bishop Paulinus of…
events.blurb: King Edwin of Northumbria is converted to Christianity by Bishop Paulinus of York, who previously saved his life.

events.title: Paulinus, last of the missionaries sent by Pope Gregory I, builds a wooden…
events.blurb: Paulinus, last of the missionaries sent by Pope Gregory I, builds a wooden church in the old Roman legionary headquarters in York, and baptises Edwin of Northumbria as the first Christian king in northern England.

events.title: Battle of Nineveh
events.blurb: Battle of Nineveh: Heraclius crosses the Great Zab river and, in a feigned retreat, defeats the Persian army (12,000 men) under Rhahzadh, near the ruins of Nineveh (Iraq).

events.title: Muhammad's letters to world leaders explain the principles of the new…
events.blurb: Muhammad's letters to world leaders explain the principles of the new monotheistic Muslim faith, as they will be contained in his book, the Quran.

events.title: Brahmagupta writes the Brāmasphuțasiddhānta, an early, yet very advanced, math…
events.blurb: Brahmagupta writes the Brāmasphuțasiddhānta, an early, yet very advanced, math book.

events.title: The Shariah enjoins women as well as men to obtain secular and religious…
events.blurb: The Shariah enjoins women as well as men to obtain secular and religious educations. It forbids eating pork, domesticated donkey, and other flesh denied to Jews by Mosaic law (approximate date).

events.title: Battle of Cirencester
events.blurb: Battle of Cirencester: King Penda of Mercia defeats the West Saxons at Cirencester (South West England) in what later will be Gloucestershire.

events.title: Ardashir III, age 7, succeeds his father Kavadh II as the twenty-fourth king…
events.blurb: Ardashir III, age 7, succeeds his father Kavadh II as the twenty-fourth king of the Sasanian Empire on the latter's death from plague.

events.title: Muhammad meets Al-Khansa', Arabic poet, and converts her to Islam
events.blurb: Muhammad meets Al-Khansa', Arabic poet, and converts her to Islam.

events.title: Battle of Fid Eoin
events.blurb: Battle of Fid Eoin: King Connad Cerr of Dál Riata is killed by the Dál nAraidi of the over-kingdom of Ulaid in north-eastern Ireland (approximate date).

events.title: Heraclius styles himself as Basileus, Greek word for "sovereign", and takes…
events.blurb: Heraclius styles himself as Basileus, Greek word for "sovereign", and takes the ancient title of "King of Kings", after his victory over Persia.

events.title: June – Battle of Khaybar
events.blurb: June – Battle of Khaybar: Muhammad and his followers defeat the Jews living in the fortified oasis at Khaybar, located 150 kilometers from Medina.

events.title: Jerusalem is reconquered by the Byzantines (after 15 years of occupation),…
events.blurb: Jerusalem is reconquered by the Byzantines (after 15 years of occupation), from the Persian Empire.

events.title: Battle of Mu'tah
events.blurb: Battle of Mu'tah: The Muslims fail to take the lands east of the Jordan River, and are pushed back near Mu'tah by the Ghassanids.

events.title: Illig Qaghan, ruler (khagan) of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, is captured by…
events.blurb: Illig Qaghan, ruler (khagan) of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, is captured by Li Jing during the Tang campaign against the Eastern Turks.

events.title: King Penda of Mercia besieges Exeter in southwest England
events.blurb: King Penda of Mercia besieges Exeter in southwest England. King Cadwallon ap Cadfan of Gwynedd lands with a force nearby, and negotiates an alliance with Penda.

events.title: Chorpan Tarkhan, general of the Khazars, invades and devastates Roman Armenia
events.blurb: Chorpan Tarkhan, general of the Khazars, invades and devastates Roman Armenia. He defeats a Persian cavalry force (10,000 men) sent by Shahrbaraz to repel the invasion.

events.title: Eanswith, daughter of King Eadbald of Kent, founds the Benedictine Folkestone…
events.blurb: Eanswith, daughter of King Eadbald of Kent, founds the Benedictine Folkestone Priory, the first nunnery in England.

events.title: King Ricberht of East Anglia dies and is succeeded by Sigeberht, who returns…
events.blurb: King Ricberht of East Anglia dies and is succeeded by Sigeberht, who returns from exile in France. He rules together with his kinsman Ecgric, re-establishing Christianity.

events.title: Yngling King Olof Trätälja founds a colony in Värmland
events.blurb: Yngling King Olof Trätälja founds a colony in Värmland. He is expelled from his native Västergötland (in modern-day Sweden) (according to the Ynglingatal).

events.title: Battle of Hunayn
events.blurb: Battle of Hunayn: Muhammad defeats the Bedouin tribe of Hawazin (12,000 men) in a valley, on one of the roads leading to Ta'if (Western Arabia).

events.title: Siege of Ta'if
events.blurb: Siege of Ta'if: Muhammad begins to besiege Ta'if and brings battering rams and catapults to suppress the fortress city, but is unable to penetrate it.

events.title: Conquest of Mecca
events.blurb: Conquest of Mecca: A Muslim army (10,000 men) marches on Mecca, which surrenders. Muhammad takes the city from the Quraysh

events.title: The Saxons (Northern Germany) appeal to Dagobert I, against the yearly tribute…
events.blurb: The Saxons (Northern Germany) appeal to Dagobert I, against the yearly tribute (500 cows) which they still pay (approximate date).

events.title: Battle of Wogastisburg
events.blurb: Battle of Wogastisburg: The Slavs under King Samo defeat the Austrasian Franks, in a three-day battle. King Dagobert I is forced to retreat; the Franks with their allies are slaughtered. Samo invades Thuringia and undertakes looting raids.

events.title: Benjamin I, Coptic patriarch of Alexandria, escapes during the persecutions of…
events.blurb: Benjamin I, Coptic patriarch of Alexandria, escapes during the persecutions of his fellow Christians and hides in the monastery of St. Macarius (Upper Egypt).

events.title: Azarmidokht (daughter of king Khosrau II) succeeds her sister Borandukht, as…
events.blurb: Azarmidokht (daughter of king Khosrau II) succeeds her sister Borandukht, as monarch of the Persian Empire.

events.title: King Suintila is overthrown after a 10-year reign by his son Sisenand, with…
events.blurb: King Suintila is overthrown after a 10-year reign by his son Sisenand, with the aid of Dagobert I. The Visigothic nobles offer him a 500-pound plate made of pure gold.

events.title: Hormizd VI proclaims himself king in Nisibis (Turkey)
events.blurb: Hormizd VI proclaims himself king in Nisibis (Turkey). He seizes the throne and will reign until 632.

events.title: Tai Zong establishes a new Daoist abbey, out of gratitude for Daoist priests…
events.blurb: Tai Zong establishes a new Daoist abbey, out of gratitude for Daoist priests who had apparently cured the crown prince of an illness.

events.title: Ridda Wars
events.blurb: Ridda Wars: Abu Bakr launches a series of military campaigns against rebel Arabian tribes, to re-establish the power of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and to secure Muhammad's legacy.

events.title: Seondeok is crowned queen of Silla (Korea)
events.blurb: Seondeok is crowned queen of Silla (Korea).

events.title: 632 Armenia earthquake
events.blurb: The 632 Armenia earthquake affects the region of the Armenian Highlands.

events.title: Farewell Sermon
events.blurb: (Friday, 9 Zulhijja, 10 AH) – The Farewell Sermon (Khuṭbatu l-Wadāʿ) is delivered by Muhammad, Islamic prophet, in the Uranah valley of Mount Arafat, to the Muslims who have accompanied him for the Hajj (pilgrimage).

events.title: King Charibert II is assassinated at Blaye (Gironde), (possibly on orders of…
events.blurb: King Charibert II is assassinated at Blaye (Gironde), (possibly on orders of his half-brother Dagobert I), along with his infant son. Dagobert I claims Aquitaine and Gascony, becoming the most powerful Merovingian king in the West.

events.title: Muhammad dies in Medina, at the age of 62, and is succeeded by Abu Bakr who…
events.blurb: Muhammad dies in Medina, at the age of 62, and is succeeded by Abu Bakr who becomes the first caliph (vicegerent of the messenger of God). He establishes the Rashidun Caliphate until 661.

events.title: Yazdegerd III, age 8, ascends to the throne as king (shah) of the Persian Empire
events.blurb: Yazdegerd III, age 8, ascends to the throne as king (shah) of the Persian Empire. He becomes the last ruler of the Sassanid Dynasty (modern Iran).

events.title: Battle of Buzakha
events.blurb: Battle of Buzakha: An Islamic column (6,000 men) under Khalid ibn al-Walid defeats the Apostate rebels under Tulayha, near Ha'il (Saudi Arabia).

events.title: Introduction of elective monarchy in The Visigothic Kingdom
events.blurb: Introduction of elective monarchy in The Visigothic Kingdom.

events.title: Siege
events.blurb: Winter – Cadwallon is besieged by King Osric at York; he successfully breaks out of the city with all his forces, by surprise, and destroys Osric's army.

events.title: Battle of Ullais
events.blurb: Battle of Ullais: Forces of the Rashidun Caliphate under Khalid defeat an entire Persian army (70,000 men) near the river Euphrates. Khalid besieges the city of Hira.

events.title: Battle of Ein ut Tamr
events.blurb: Battle of Ein ut Tamr: The Muslim army attacks a Persian frontier post located south of Anbar. The Arab Christian auxiliaries are overrun and surrender.

events.title: Siege of Hira
events.blurb: Siege of Hira: The Muslim Arabs (15,000 men) under Khalid attack the fortress city of Hira. After a brief fight the citizens surrender, and bring gifts to Khalid.

events.title: Li Chungfeng builds an armillary sphere (approximate date)
events.blurb: Li Chungfeng builds an armillary sphere (approximate date).

events.title: Osric succeeds his uncle Edwin as king of Deira
events.blurb: Osric succeeds his uncle Edwin as king of Deira. Prince Eanfrith returns from Pictland to claim his rightful crown of Bernicia (Northern England). Both revert to paganism.

events.title: The Arabian Peninsula is united under the central authority of Abu Bakr
events.blurb: The Arabian Peninsula is united under the central authority of Abu Bakr. This sets the stage for the Islamic conquest of Persia and the fall of the Sassanid dynasty.

events.title: Battle of Chains (Kuwait) and Battle of River (Iraq)
events.blurb: Battle of Chains (Kuwait) and Battle of River (Iraq): A Muslim army (18,000 men) under Khalid ibn al-Walid invades Mesopotamia, and wins decisive victories.

events.title: Battle of Walaja
events.blurb: Battle of Walaja: The Rashidun Caliphate army under Khalid defeats the Persians and their Arab Christian allies. The Persian army is at least three times the size.

events.title: Battle of Dumat Al-Jandal
events.blurb: Battle of Dumat Al-Jandal: A Muslim army (10,000 men) under Khalid defeats the rebel Arab Christians at Dumat Al-Jandal (Saudi Arabia).

events.title: Battle of Hatfield Chase
events.blurb: Battle of Hatfield Chase: King Edwin of Northumbria is defeated and killed by Penda of Mercia and Cadwallon of Gwynedd, at Hatfield Chase (South Yorkshire).

events.title: Battle of Muzayyah, Battle of Saniyy, and Battle of Zumail
events.blurb: Battle of Muzayyah, Battle of Saniyy, and Battle of Zumail: Khalid coordinates successful night attacks against the Arab Christians.

events.title: Fourth Council of Toledo
events.blurb: Fourth Council of Toledo: King Sisenand orders a meeting in the church of St. Leocadia; the bishops accept a decree that all Visigoths must take an oath to preserve the stability of the Gothic nation.

events.title: Tai Zong orders the construction of the Daming Palace in Chang'an
events.blurb: Tai Zong orders the construction of the Daming Palace in Chang'an. He builds the summer palace for his retired father, Emperor Gao Zu, as an act of filial piety.

events.title: The Rashidun Caliphate starts the Islamic conquest of the Byzantine Empire,…
events.blurb: The Rashidun Caliphate starts the Islamic conquest of the Byzantine Empire, when Muslim forces under Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah invade the Levant. Khalid sets out for Syria from Al-Hirah, taking with him half his army, about 8,000 strong.

events.title: Aidan of Lindisfarne, Irish missionary, is summoned by King Oswald from Iona…
events.blurb: Aidan of Lindisfarne, Irish missionary, is summoned by King Oswald from Iona (Inner Hebrides) to establish a bishopric on the holy island of Lindisfarne, and reestablish Christianity in Northumbria (approximate date).

events.title: Battle of Marj Rahit
events.blurb: Battle of Marj Rahit: A Muslim Arab army under Khalid defeats the Byzantine forces (15,000 men) and their Ghassanid allies. After the battle he sends a mounted column to the outskirts of Damascus, to plunder the region.

events.title: Battle of the Bridge
events.blurb: Battle of the Bridge: Persian forces (10,000 men) under Bahman Jadhuyih defeat the Muslim Arabs at the Euphrates (near Kufa). The sight of elephants panics the Muslims, and many are killed. Bahman does not pursue the fleeing Arab army.

events.title: Battle of al-Qaryatayn
events.blurb: Battle of al-Qaryatayn: The Muslim Arabs under Khalid defeat the Ghassanids at Al-Qaryatayn, after the inhabitants resist his proposals. His army conquers and plunders the city, before proceeding to capture other towns in the area.

events.title: Battle of Bosra
events.blurb: Battle of Bosra: Muslim forces under Khalid besiege the Byzantine and Christian Arab garrison (12,000 men) at Bosra. After a few days the fortress city surrenders; Khalid imposes a payment of tribute on the inhabitants.

events.title: Sophronius becomes patriarch of Jerusalem
events.blurb: Sophronius becomes patriarch of Jerusalem. He sends synodical letters to Pope Honorius I and the Eastern patriarchs, explaining the Orthodox belief, by renouncing Monothelitism.

events.title: Battle of Firaz
events.blurb: Battle of Firaz: The Rashidun Arabs (15,000 men) under Khalid ibn al-Walid defeat the combined forces of the Byzantine Empire, Persian Empire and Arab Christians (at least 10 times larger than Khalid's army) in Mesopotamia (Iraq).

events.title: Birinus, Frankish missionary, lands at the port of "Hamwic" (now in the St
events.blurb: Birinus, Frankish missionary, lands at the port of "Hamwic" (now in the St. Mary's area of Southampton), on his mission to reconvert the West Saxons in England. About this time, the St Mary's Church is founded.

events.title: Eanfrith of Bernicia and his bodyguard are killed by King Cadwallon of…
events.blurb: Eanfrith of Bernicia and his bodyguard are killed by King Cadwallon of Gwynedd, in an attempt to negotiate peace. Eanfrith's brother Oswald returns from 18 years exile in Dál Riata (modern Scotland), to claim the crown of Northumbria.

events.title: Battle of Heavenfield
events.blurb: Battle of Heavenfield: Oswald, possibly accompanied by a force of Scots (or Picts), defeats and kills Cadwallon with a Welsh army near Hexham (northern England). He reunites Deira with Bernicia, and becomes king of Northumbria.

events.title: Battle of Dathin
events.blurb: Battle of Dathin: Rashidun forces under Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan defeat the Christian Arabs around Gaza. The Muslim victory is celebrated by the local Jews, who have been a persecuted minority within the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Battle of Ajnadayn
events.blurb: Battle of Ajnadayn: Byzantine forces (90,000 men according to Muslim sources) under Theodore are defeated by the Rashidun Caliphate near Beit Shemesh (modern-day Israel).

events.title: Abu Bakr dies at Medina and is succeeded by Umar I, who becomes the second…
events.blurb: Abu Bakr dies at Medina and is succeeded by Umar I, who becomes the second caliph (khalifah) of the Rashidun Caliphate. During his rule, Umar conquers Syria, Persia, and Egypt in a "Holy War".

events.title: Siege of Damascus
events.blurb: Siege of Damascus: Muslim Arabs under Khalid conquer Damascus as the first major city of the Byzantine Empire. Damascan refugees are given a guarantee of safety to retreat to Antioch.

events.title: Yao Silian, Chinese historian, completes his Book of Liang
events.blurb: Yao Silian, Chinese historian, completes his Book of Liang. It contains the history of the Liang dynasty.

events.title: King Gartnait III dies after a 4-year reign, and is succeeded by his brother…
events.blurb: King Gartnait III dies after a 4-year reign, and is succeeded by his brother Bridei II, as ruler of the Picts.

events.title: King Meurig of Glywysing and Gwent invades Ergyng (Archenfield), and reunites…
events.blurb: King Meurig of Glywysing and Gwent invades Ergyng (Archenfield), and reunites the two Welsh kingdoms (approximate date).

events.title: Gaza is conquered by the Muslim Arabs under 'Amr ibn al-'As
events.blurb: Gaza is conquered by the Muslim Arabs under 'Amr ibn al-'As. It becomes the first city in Palestine developed into a centre of Islamic law.

events.title: Christian missionaries arrive in China
events.blurb: Christian missionaries arrive in China: Alopen, bishop of the Assyrian Church of the East, preaches Nestorian Christianity in the Tang dynasty capital, Chang'an.

events.title: Battle of Fahl
events.blurb: Battle of Fahl: The Rashidun army, (30,000 men) under Khalid ibn al-Walid (known as the "Drawn Sword of God"), defeats the Byzantine forces led by Theodore Trithyrius, at Pella in the Jordan Valley (Jordan).

events.title: The historical texts of the Book of Northern Qi, Book of Chen, and Book of Sui…
events.blurb: The historical texts of the Book of Northern Qi, Book of Chen, and Book of Sui are compiled in China, during the Tang dynasty.

events.title: Rothari (formerly duke of Brescia) marries widowed Queen Gundeberga, and…
events.blurb: Rothari (formerly duke of Brescia) marries widowed Queen Gundeberga, and succeeds Arioald as king of the Lombards. During his reign, he puts many insubordinate nobles to death.

events.title: Chintila is elected by a convention of bishops and nobles (in accordance with…
events.blurb: Chintila is elected by a convention of bishops and nobles (in accordance with the 75th canon of the Fourth Council of Toledo) as ruler of the Visigoths, after the death of King Sisenand.

events.title: The city of Basra (modern Iraq) is founded on the Shatt al-Arab, at the head…
events.blurb: The city of Basra (modern Iraq) is founded on the Shatt al-Arab, at the head of the Persian Gulf. The port will become a major trading center for commodities from Arabia, India, and Persia.

events.title: The Xumi Pagoda of Zhengding (China) is built, during the reign of Emperor…
events.blurb: The Xumi Pagoda of Zhengding (China) is built, during the reign of Emperor Taizong of Tang.

events.title: Yuknoom Chʼeen II becomes the ruler of the Mayan city state of Calakmul in…
