events.blurb: Yuknoom Chʼeen II becomes the ruler of the Mayan city state of Calakmul in southern Mexico and reigns for 50 years until his death in 686.

events.title: Fifth Council of Toledo
events.blurb: Fifth Council of Toledo: Chintila orders a meeting in the church of St. Leocadia; the bishops accept a decree that only Gothic nobility (with military functions) may be king of the Visigothic Kingdom.

events.title: Battle of Hazir
events.blurb: Battle of Hazir: Muslim Arab forces (17,000 men) under Khalid ibn al-Walid defeat the Byzantine army near Qinnasrin (Northern Syria). The cities of Beirut and Tyre are captured by Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan after a short siege.

events.title: Battle of Jalula
events.blurb: Battle of Jalula: Muslim Arabs defeat the Persian forces (20,000 men) under Farrukhzad at the Diyala River. The cities Tikrit and Mosul are captured, completing the conquest of Mesopotamia.

events.title: Chang'an, capital of the Tang dynasty (China), becomes the largest city of the…
events.blurb: Chang'an, capital of the Tang dynasty (China), becomes the largest city of the world, taking the lead from Ctesiphon, capital of Persia.

events.title: Battle of the Iron Bridge
events.blurb: Battle of the Iron Bridge: Rashidun forces under Khalid ibn al-Walid defeat the Byzantine army and Christian Arabs near Antioch, at the Orontes River. It marks the complete annexation of Syria into the Rashidun Caliphate.

events.title: Siege of Ctesiphon
events.blurb: Siege of Ctesiphon: The Rashidun army (15,000 men) under Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas occupies the Persian capital of Ctesiphon, after a two-month siege. King Yazdegerd III flees with the imperial treasure eastward into Media.

events.title: Battle of Mag Rath
events.blurb: Battle of Mag Rath: King Oswald of Northumbria sends troops to Ireland, to assist Domnall Brecc King of Dál Riata in his alliance with King Congal Cáech of Ulaid against Domnall mac Áedo High King of Ireland,

events.title: Siege of Aleppo
events.blurb: Siege of Aleppo: Muslim Arabs under Khalid ibn al-Walid conquer the Byzantine stronghold Aleppo; the large walled city surrenders after a four-month siege. A column of troops under Malik al-Ashtar is sent to take Azaz.

events.title: The Tibetan Empire, seeking an alliance through marriage with Tang dynasty…
events.blurb: The Tibetan Empire, seeking an alliance through marriage with Tang dynasty China, launches an attack on Songzhou that is repelled by Chinese forces,

events.title: Heraclius issues his Ekthesis, espousing the Monothelete doctrine (that there…
events.blurb: Heraclius issues his Ekthesis, espousing the Monothelete doctrine (that there is only one will in Christ), and setting it forth as the official doctrine of the Eastern Orthodox Church.

events.title: The Islamic calendar is introduced by Abu Musa al-Asha'ari
events.blurb: The Islamic calendar is introduced by Abu Musa al-Asha'ari. He convinces Umar I to make notes of an era for Muslims.

events.title: King Oswald and his Northumbrian army besiege and conquer Edinburgh (Scotland)
events.blurb: King Oswald and his Northumbrian army besiege and conquer Edinburgh (Scotland). His half-brother, Oswiu of Bernicia, marries Princess Rhiainfelt, heiress of North Rheged ("Old North").

events.title: Plague of Amwas
events.blurb: The Plague of Amwas breaks out.

events.title: Year 0 of the Burmese calendar, based on the Chula Sakarat, is also used in…
events.blurb: Year 0 of the Burmese calendar, based on the Chula Sakarat, is also used in the mainland of Southeast Asia.

events.title: Pope Honorius I dies at Rome after a 13-year reign, and is succeeded by…
events.blurb: Pope Honorius I dies at Rome after a 13-year reign, and is succeeded by Severinus, but the Byzantine emperor Heraclius will delay the new pope's consecration until May 640.

events.title: The First Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta is founded by the exarch Isaac of…
events.blurb: The First Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta is founded by the exarch Isaac of Ravenna on Torcello, confirming the island's importance as a centre of population in Venice at this date.

events.title: The Xueyantuo assaults the Chinese-conquered vassal of Eastern Tujue
events.blurb: The Xueyantuo assaults the Chinese-conquered vassal of Eastern Tujue. Although simultaneously fighting in Korea against Goguryeo,

events.title: Eligius succeeds Acarius as bishop of Doornik and Noyon
events.blurb: Eligius succeeds Acarius as bishop of Doornik and Noyon. He becomes constituted guardian of the towns of Vermandois, which also include Ghent and Kortrijk (Flanders).

events.title: Hormuzan, Persian satrap of Susiana (vassal of the Rashidun Caliphate),…
events.blurb: Hormuzan, Persian satrap of Susiana (vassal of the Rashidun Caliphate), revolts against the Muslims and raids Mesopotamia. Arab forces under Abu Musa al-Asha'ari destroy Susa in the lower Zagros Mountains.

events.title: An unsuccessful revolt of Prince Kürşat (of the Eastern Turks) breaks out in China
events.blurb: An unsuccessful revolt of Prince Kürşat (of the Eastern Turks) breaks out in China.

events.title: Dagobert I dies after a 10-year reign as king of all the Franks, in which his…
events.blurb: Dagobert I dies after a 10-year reign as king of all the Franks, in which his realm has prospered.

events.title: At the request of Porga of Croatia, one of the first dukes or princes…
events.blurb: At the request of Porga of Croatia, one of the first dukes or princes (Croatian: knez) of Dalmatian Croatia, the Byzantine emperor Heraclius sends Christian missionaries to the Croatian Provinces (approximate date).

events.title: Hartlepool Abbey in Northumbria (northern England) is founded
events.blurb: Hartlepool Abbey in Northumbria (northern England) is founded. Wooden huts surrounding a church are built in Saxon style.

events.title: King Eadbald of Kent dies after a 24-year reign
events.blurb: King Eadbald of Kent dies after a 24-year reign. He is succeeded by his sons, Eorcenberht and Eormenred, who jointly rule the Kingdom of Kent (now south east England).

events.title: Disibod, Irish monk and hermit, arrives as a missionary in Francia
events.blurb: Disibod, Irish monk and hermit, arrives as a missionary in Francia. He begins his religious work in the Vosges and Ardennes.

events.title: The French city of Lille (according to the legend) is founded by Lydéric
events.blurb: The French city of Lille (according to the legend) is founded by Lydéric. He kills Phinaert in a duel to avenge his parents' deaths (approximate date).

events.title: Pepin the Elder, Mayor of the Palace of Austrasia, dies and is succeeded by…
events.blurb: Pepin the Elder, Mayor of the Palace of Austrasia, dies and is succeeded by his son Grimoald. He becomes the head of the Frankish household, and the most powerful man in the Frankish Kingdom (approximate date).

events.title: Siege of Babylon Fortress
events.blurb: Siege of Babylon Fortress: The Rashidun army lays siege to Babylon Fortress in the Nile Delta (near Cairo). The next two months' fighting remain inconclusive, the Byzantines having the upper hand by repulsing every Muslim assault.

events.title: Pope Severinus succeeds Honorius I as the 71st pope
events.blurb: Pope Severinus succeeds Honorius I as the 71st pope. He dies in Rome only two months after being consecrated.

events.title: Battle of Heliopolis
events.blurb: Battle of Heliopolis: The Muslim Arab army (15,000 men) under Amr ibn al-As defeats the Byzantine forces near Heliopolis (Egypt). Amr divides his troops into three parts, surrounding the Byzantines.

events.title: On orders of the Saracen leader, Amar, the Serapeum of Alexandria, containing…
events.blurb: On orders of the Saracen leader, Amar, the Serapeum of Alexandria, containing works that had survived the destruction of the Library of Alexandria, is burned down, along with its collection of 500,000 manuscripts.

events.title: Pope John IV succeeds Severinus as the 72nd pope
events.blurb: Pope John IV succeeds Severinus as the 72nd pope. His election is accepted by the Exarchate of Ravenna.

events.title: Constans II establishes a new civil-military defensive organisation, based…
events.blurb: Constans II establishes a new civil-military defensive organisation, based upon geographical military districts. Byzantine forces maintain the frontier, along the line of the Taurus Mountains (Southern Turkey).

events.title: Aega, Mayor of the Palace and regent (alongside of queen mother Nanthild) of…
events.blurb: Aega, Mayor of the Palace and regent (alongside of queen mother Nanthild) of Neustria and Burgundy, dies during the reign of King Clovis II. He is replaced by Erchinoald, a relative of Dagobert I's mother.

events.title: Prince Oswiu of Bernicia conquers Gododdin (or "The Old North") as far north…
events.blurb: Prince Oswiu of Bernicia conquers Gododdin (or "The Old North") as far north as Manau (modern Scotland), on behalf of his half-brother, King Oswald (approximate date).

events.title: Uija becomes the last king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje
events.blurb: Uija becomes the last king of the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

events.title: The city of Fustat (later Cairo) is founded in Egypt
events.blurb: The city of Fustat (later Cairo) is founded in Egypt. It becomes the first capital of Egypt under Muslim rule.

events.title: King Bridei II dies after a 5-year reign, and is succeeded by his brother…
events.blurb: King Bridei II dies after a 5-year reign, and is succeeded by his brother Talorc III as ruler of the Picts.

events.title: Siege of Alexandria
events.blurb: Siege of Alexandria: Muslim Arabs under 'Amr ibn al-'As capture Alexandria after a six-month siege. Byzantine officials formally capitulate to Amr, turning the city over to Arab hands.

events.title: Emperor Jomei of Japan, age 48, dies after a 12-year reign
events.blurb: Emperor Jomei of Japan, age 48, dies after a 12-year reign.

events.title: A monastic settlement is founded in Hampshire (England) which later becomes…
events.blurb: A monastic settlement is founded in Hampshire (England) which later becomes Winchester Cathedral.

events.title: Radulf, a Frankish aristocrat, revolts against King Sigebert III of Austrasia…
events.blurb: Radulf, a Frankish aristocrat, revolts against King Sigebert III of Austrasia and defeats his army, taking the title of rex or king of Thuringia.

events.title: Empress Kōgyoku ascends to the throne of Japan, after her husband (and uncle)…
events.blurb: Empress Kōgyoku ascends to the throne of Japan, after her husband (and uncle) Emperor Jomei's death in 641.

events.title: Emperor Constans II marries Fausta
events.blurb: Emperor Constans II marries Fausta.

events.title: Yŏn Kaesomun
events.blurb: Winter – Yŏn Kaesomun seizes power over Goguryeo (Korea), and places King Bojang on the throne.

events.title: Chindasuinth, a Gothic warlord (already 79 years old), commences a rebellion…
events.blurb: Chindasuinth, a Gothic warlord (already 79 years old), commences a rebellion and deposes King Tulga in Toledo, Spain. He is proclaimed king by the Visigothic nobility and anointed by the bishops.

events.title: Battle of Maserfield
events.blurb: Battle of Maserfield: King Penda of Mercia defeats and kills King Oswald of Northumbria, age 38, at Oswestry (West Midlands).

events.title: Peroz III, son of Yazdegerd III, the last Sassanid king of Persia, flees to…
events.blurb: Peroz III, son of Yazdegerd III, the last Sassanid king of Persia, flees to territory under the control of the Tang dynasty in China (approximate date).

events.title: Duke Leuthari II has Otto, mayor of the palace of Austrasia, murdered
events.blurb: Duke Leuthari II has Otto, mayor of the palace of Austrasia, murdered. He is succeeded by Grimoald the Elder, the eldest son of Pepin of Landen.

events.title: Maurikios names himself dux of Rome, and revolts against exarch Isaac…
events.blurb: Maurikios names himself dux of Rome, and revolts against exarch Isaac (Exarchate of Ravenna). He declares Rome's independence from the Exarchate and from the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Æbbe establishes a monastery at Ebchester, known as Kirk Hill at St Abb's Head…
events.blurb: Æbbe establishes a monastery at Ebchester, known as Kirk Hill at St Abb's Head near Coldingham (Scotland).

events.title: Chinese prefectural government officials travel to the capital of Chang'an, to…
events.blurb: Chinese prefectural government officials travel to the capital of Chang'an, to give the annual report of the affairs in their districts.

events.title: Taizong commissions artist Yan Liben to paint the life-size portraits of 24…
events.blurb: Taizong commissions artist Yan Liben to paint the life-size portraits of 24 government officials in the Lingyan Pavilion, to commemorate their service and contributions to the founding of the Tang dynasty.

events.title: Oswine, son of the late king Osric of Deira, manages to establish himself as…
events.blurb: Oswine, son of the late king Osric of Deira, manages to establish himself as king of Deira (Northern England) despite armed objections from King Oswiu of Bernicia.

events.title: Valentinus, Byzantine general, attempts to usurp the throne of his son-in-law…
events.blurb: Valentinus, Byzantine general, attempts to usurp the throne of his son-in-law Constans II. He appears at the gates of Constantinople with a contingent of Byzantine troops, and demands to be crowned emperor.

events.title: The second caliph Umar, , dies of wounds inflicted by the Persian slave Abu…
events.blurb: The second caliph Umar, , dies of wounds inflicted by the Persian slave Abu Lu'lu'a Firuz at Medina. On his death bed he appoints a committee to determine his successor.

events.title: The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda at Ci'en Temple, Xi'an (Shanxi) is first erected…
events.blurb: The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda at Ci'en Temple, Xi'an (Shanxi) is first erected during the Tang dynasty (approximate date).

events.title: Plato, exarch (imperial governor) of Ravenna, invades the southern Po Valley
events.blurb: Plato, exarch (imperial governor) of Ravenna, invades the southern Po Valley. The Lombards under King Rothari defeat him on the banks of the Panaro River (near Modena); 8,000 imperial troops are killed.

events.title: The first nengō, derived from the Chinese system of eras (nianhao) begins with…
events.blurb: The first nengō, derived from the Chinese system of eras (nianhao) begins with the Taika era. (Unclear significance. Needs more explanation as to why this belongs in the list of major events of the year)

events.title: Kōtoku creates a new city at Naniwa, and moves the capital from Yamato Province
events.blurb: Kōtoku creates a new city at Naniwa, and moves the capital from Yamato Province. The capital has a sea port, establishing foreign trade and diplomatic relations.

events.title: King Cenwalh of Wessex is driven from his kingdom by his brother-in-law, King…
events.blurb: King Cenwalh of Wessex is driven from his kingdom by his brother-in-law, King Penda of Mercia (according to Bede). He flees to the court of king Anna of East Anglia, and is baptised while in exile. Penda overruns Wessex.

events.title: Emperor Kōtoku establishes the Taika Reform
events.blurb: Emperor Kōtoku establishes the Taika Reform: a land reform based on Confucian ideas and philosophies from China (approximate date)

events.title: Gwynedd and much of Wales is in the grasp of famine
events.blurb: Gwynedd and much of Wales is in the grasp of famine. Would-be king Cadwaladr Fendigaid flees to Brittany. Civil war continues in his kingdom (approximate date).

events.title: First conflict of the Goguryeo–Tang War
events.blurb: First conflict of the Goguryeo–Tang War: A Chinese expeditionary army under Emperor Taizong of Tang crosses the Liao River into Goguryeo (one of the Three kingdoms of Korea).

events.title: Tang forces under Li Shiji heading southeast toward the Yalu River put the…
events.blurb: Tang forces under Li Shiji heading southeast toward the Yalu River put the strategic fortress of Ansi City (in the province of Liaoning) under siege.

events.title: Taizong is unable to capture the Ansi fortress defended by Korean general Yang…
events.blurb: Taizong is unable to capture the Ansi fortress defended by Korean general Yang Manch'un. Food supplies running low, he withdraws his forces, ending the Siege of Ansi.

events.title: Battle of Nikiou
events.blurb: Battle of Nikiou: The Rashidun army (15,000 men) under Amr ibn al-'As defeats a smaller Byzantine force, near the fortified town of Nikiou (Egypt).

events.title: Emperor Kōtoku makes a decree about the policies of building tombs
events.blurb: Emperor Kōtoku makes a decree about the policies of building tombs. He discontinues the old customs of sacrificing people in honor of a dead man, and forbids ill-considered rituals about purgation.

events.title: Gregory the Patrician, Byzantine exarch of Africa, begins a rebellion against…
events.blurb: Gregory the Patrician, Byzantine exarch of Africa, begins a rebellion against Constans II, and proclaims himself emperor; the revolt finds broad support among the populace.

events.title: Hilda of Whitby, age 33, is persuaded by Aidan, bishop of Lindisfarne, to…
events.blurb: Hilda of Whitby, age 33, is persuaded by Aidan, bishop of Lindisfarne, to enter the monastic life at Hartlepool Abbey (Northumbria).

events.title: A stone tower astronomical observatory (named Cheomseongdae) at Gyeongju is…
events.blurb: A stone tower astronomical observatory (named Cheomseongdae) at Gyeongju is constructed in Silla (South Korea) around this time.

events.title: Taizong establishes a Chinese military government to pacify the former…
events.blurb: Taizong establishes a Chinese military government to pacify the former territory of Xueyantuo, which extends to the Altai Mountains in the west.

events.title: Jindeok becomes queen of the Korean kingdom of Silla after the death of Queen…
events.blurb: Jindeok becomes queen of the Korean kingdom of Silla after the death of Queen Seondeok.

events.title: Approximate date
events.blurb: Approximate date – Opizzo Fieschi, Latin patriarch of Antioch, is exiled, being displaced because of the East–West Schism of 1054.

events.title: King Ottokar II of Bohemia inherits Carinthia and part of Carniola, making him…
events.blurb: King Ottokar II of Bohemia inherits Carinthia and part of Carniola, making him the most powerful German prince within the Holy Roman Empire; the empire lacking an emperor during the ongoing “Great Interregnum”.

events.title: Petrus Peregrinus de Maricourt, French mathematician and writer, performs a…
events.blurb: Petrus Peregrinus de Maricourt, French mathematician and writer, performs a series of experiments with magnetic poles and proposes that a machine can be run forever in perpetual motion using the properties of magnets.

events.title: Ode de Pougy, French Abbess of Notre Dame aux Nonnains, and several associates…
events.blurb: Ode de Pougy, French Abbess of Notre Dame aux Nonnains, and several associates who assist her, are excommunicated.

events.title: Battle of Colle Val d'Elsa
events.blurb: Battle of Colle Val d'Elsa: Guelph forces (2,200 men) led by King Charles I of Anjou defeat the Ghibellines at Tuscany.

events.title: King Louis IX of France ("the Saint") orders all Jews found in public without…
events.blurb: King Louis IX of France ("the Saint") orders all Jews found in public without an identifying yellow badge to be fined ten livres of silver. He also confiscates goods from the Jewish population to fund the Eighth Crusade.

events.title: An Aragonese contingent under King James I ("the Conqueror") sails from…
events.blurb: An Aragonese contingent under King James I ("the Conqueror") sails from Barcelona to the Holy Land but is caught in a storm and badly damaged. One squadron reaches Acre, but later returns to Catalonia.

events.title: The ancient city of Ascalon is captured from the Crusader States, and utterly…
events.blurb: The ancient city of Ascalon is captured from the Crusader States, and utterly destroyed by the Mamluk sultan Baibars, who goes so far as to fill in its important harbor, leaving the site desolate, and the city never to be rebuilt.

events.title: The Sanskrit fables known as the Panchatantra, dating from as early as 200…
events.blurb: The Sanskrit fables known as the Panchatantra, dating from as early as 200 BCE, are translated into Latin, from a Hebrew version by John of Capua.

events.title: Before August
events.blurb: Before August – King Louis IX of France launches the Eighth Crusade, in an attempt to recapture the Crusader States from the Mamluk sultan Baibars; the opening engagement is a siege of Tunis.

events.title: The independent state of Kutch is founded, in present-day India
events.blurb: The independent state of Kutch is founded, in present-day India.

events.title: The Chronicle of Melrose is ended
events.blurb: The Chronicle of Melrose is ended.

events.title: Edmund, 2nd Earl of Cornwall, donates to the Cistercian Hailes Abbey in…
events.blurb: Edmund, 2nd Earl of Cornwall, donates to the Cistercian Hailes Abbey in England (his father's foundation) a phial held to contain the Blood of Christ, acquired in the Holy Roman Empire;

events.title: Construction of the Old New Synagogue in Prague is completed
events.blurb: Construction of the Old New Synagogue in Prague is completed.

events.title: Sambyeolcho Rebellion
events.blurb: In Korea, the Sambyeolcho Rebellion begins against the Goryeo dynasty, a vassal state of the Yuan dynasty.

events.title: A census of the Chinese city of Hangzhou establishes that some 186,330…
events.blurb: A census of the Chinese city of Hangzhou establishes that some 186,330 families reside within it, not including visitors and soldiers (Historian Jacques Gernet argues that this means a population of over 1 million inhabitants,

events.title: The Summa Theologica, a work by Thomas Aquinas that is considered within the…
events.blurb: The Summa Theologica, a work by Thomas Aquinas that is considered within the Roman Catholic Church to be the paramount expression of its theology, is completed (year uncertain).

events.title: Livonian Crusade - Battle of Karuse
events.blurb: Livonian Crusade - Battle of Karuse: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeats the Livonian Order decisively, on the frozen surface of the Baltic Sea.

events.title: Yekuno Amlak
events.blurb: (10 Nehasé 1262) – Yekuno Amlak overthrows the Ethiopian Zagwe dynasty, claims the imperial throne and establishes the Solomonic Dynasty, which will last until 1974.

events.title: King Stephen V of Hungary writes his walk to the antiquum castellum near…
events.blurb: King Stephen V of Hungary writes his walk to the antiquum castellum near Miholjanec, where the Sword of Attila has been recently discovered.

events.title: Crucial aspects of the philosophy of Averroism (itself based on Aristotle's…
events.blurb: Crucial aspects of the philosophy of Averroism (itself based on Aristotle's works) are banned by the Roman Catholic Church, in a condemnation enacted by papal authority at the University of Paris.

events.title: The Nizari Ismaili garrison of Gerdkuh, Persia surrender after 17 years to the…
events.blurb: The Nizari Ismaili garrison of Gerdkuh, Persia surrender after 17 years to the Mongols.

events.title: Construction of the Tower of Kamyenyets (or the White Tower) in Belarus begins
events.blurb: Construction of the Tower of Kamyenyets (or the White Tower) in Belarus begins. Later, it becomes a frontier stronghold on the northern border of Volhynia.

events.title: The Nakhi Kingdom, of the northern Himalayan foothills, is annexed by the Yuan…
events.blurb: The Nakhi Kingdom, of the northern Himalayan foothills, is annexed by the Yuan dynasty (approximate date).

events.title: The 17-year-old Marco Polo departs from Venice with his father and uncle…
events.blurb: The 17-year-old Marco Polo departs from Venice with his father and uncle Niccolò and Maffeo Polo, to set off for Asia to meet the Mongolian emperor Kublai Khan (the grandson of Genghis Khan) at his court in Beijing, China.

events.title: Siege of Krak des Chevaliers
events.blurb: Siege of Krak des Chevaliers: Mamluk forces under Baibars capture the strategically important castle Krak des Chevaliers from the Knights Hospitaller.

events.title: Peace of Pressburg
events.blurb: Peace of Pressburg: Kings Ottokar II and Stephen V sign a peace agreement at Pressburg, settling territorial claims, following the failed invasion of Hungary by Ottokar in April.

events.title: The counties of Poitou and Toulouse are absorbed into the French domains…
events.blurb: The counties of Poitou and Toulouse are absorbed into the French domains following the death of Alphonse, Count of Poitiers, son of the late King Louis VIII of France.

events.title: Pope Gregory X succeeds the late Clement IV as the 184th pope of the Catholic…
events.blurb: Pope Gregory X succeeds the late Clement IV as the 184th pope of the Catholic Church, as the compromise candidate between French and Italian cardinals, ending a three-year conclave, the longest ever.

events.title: Nichiren, Japanese Buddhist priest, is arrested by a band of soldiers and…
events.blurb: Nichiren, Japanese Buddhist priest, is arrested by a band of soldiers and nearly beheaded.

events.title: Abaqa Khan, Mongol ruler of the Ilkhanate, detaches some 10,000 horsemen from…
events.blurb: Abaqa Khan, Mongol ruler of the Ilkhanate, detaches some 10,000 horsemen from Anatolia to support the Lord Edward in his war against Baibars. They invade Syria and defeat Mamluk forces who protect the region around Aleppo.

events.title: Kublai Khan renames his empire "Great Yuan" (大元
events.blurb: Kublai Khan renames his empire "Great Yuan" (大元; dà yuán), officially marking the start of the Yuan dynasty in China.

events.title: The Worshipful Company of Cordwainers and Curriers are granted rights to…
events.blurb: The Worshipful Company of Cordwainers and Curriers are granted rights to regulate the leather trade in the City of London. The Fishmongers Company receive its first Royal Charter.

events.title: Charles signs a treaty and is proclaimed King of Albania
events.blurb: Charles signs a treaty and is proclaimed King of Albania. He promises to protect the nobles and to honor the privileges they have from the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: King Hugh III of Cyprus ("the Great") signs a peace with Sultan Baibars,…
events.blurb: King Hugh III of Cyprus ("the Great") signs a peace with Sultan Baibars, Mamluk ruler of Egypt, at Caesarea.

events.title: The Lord Edward, heir to the English throne, prevents an assassination attempt…
events.blurb: The Lord Edward, heir to the English throne, prevents an assassination attempt on himself at Acre. A Syrian Nizari (or Assassin) supposedly sent by Baibars penetrates into the prince's chamber and stabs him with a poisoned dagger.

events.title: Nubian forces sack the Egyptian Red Sea outpost of Aydhab and raid the…
events.blurb: Nubian forces sack the Egyptian Red Sea outpost of Aydhab and raid the southern frontier city of Aswan. In return, Baibars invades the kingdom of Makuria.

events.title: Battle of Heiloo
events.blurb: Battle of Heiloo: Floris V, count of Holland, makes an unsuccessful attack on Frisia in an attempt to recover the body of his father, William II, who was killed (16 years ago) by the Frisians near Hoogwoud (modern Netherlands).

events.title: Charles I orders his officials to take all Genoese prisoner within his…
events.blurb: Charles I orders his officials to take all Genoese prisoner within his territories, except for the Guelphs and to seize their property. The Sicilian fleet occupies Ajaccio on Corsica.

events.title: King Henry III of England dies at the Palace of Westminster after a 56-year reign
events.blurb: King Henry III of England dies at the Palace of Westminster after a 56-year reign. He is succeeded by his son Edward I, who slowly returns from the Holy Land via Gascony.

events.title: In Korea, the Sambyeolcho Rebellion against the Goryeo dynasty (a vassal state…
events.blurb: In Korea, the Sambyeolcho Rebellion against the Goryeo dynasty (a vassal state of the Yuan dynasty) ends as rebel forces are defeated.

events.title: Alfonso X creates and grants privileges to the Mesta to promote the wool…
events.blurb: Alfonso X creates and grants privileges to the Mesta to promote the wool industry, protecting livestock owners and their animals in the Crown of Castile.

events.title: Sultan Muhammad I (or Ibn al-Ahmar) suffers fatal injuries after falling from…
events.blurb: Sultan Muhammad I (or Ibn al-Ahmar) suffers fatal injuries after falling from his horse near the city of Granada during a minor military expedition. He is succeeded by his son Muhammad II, who becomes ruler of the Emirate of Granada.

events.title: Battle of Xiangyang
events.blurb: Battle of Xiangyang: Chinese forces surrender to Kublai Khan's general Aju (or Achu) after a 6-year siege. The battle is the first in which firearms are used in combat.

events.title: Mongol forces surround the castle of Al-Bira
events.blurb: Mongol forces surround the castle of Al-Bira. Baibars skirts around the enemy with camels and wagons. He launches a devastating attack and routes the Mongols.

events.title: Rudolf I is elected King of Germany over the rival candidate Ottokar II, king…
events.blurb: Rudolf I is elected King of Germany over the rival candidate Ottokar II, king of Bohemia, ending the Great Interregnum. He is the first of many Habsburgs to hold the throne and is crowned in Aachen Cathedral, on October 24.

events.title: Thomas Aquinas, Italian priest and theologian, writes Summa Theologica, a…
events.blurb: Thomas Aquinas, Italian priest and theologian, writes Summa Theologica, a master work of Catholic theology, leaving it unfinished, after having a mystical experience during Mass.

events.title: Followers of Persian poet and mystic Rumi establish the Mevlevi Order…
events.blurb: Followers of Persian poet and mystic Rumi establish the Mevlevi Order ("whirling dervishes") in the city of Konya (approximate date).

events.title: Bonvesin da la Riva, Italian poet, writes the didactic-allegoric poem Liber di…
events.blurb: Bonvesin da la Riva, Italian poet, writes the didactic-allegoric poem Liber di Tre Scricciur ("Book of the Three Scriptures"). The text is in the Western Lombard language (similar to other Gallo-Italic languages).

events.title: Gregory X obtains the region of Romagna from Rudolf I, in exchange for…
events.blurb: Gregory X obtains the region of Romagna from Rudolf I, in exchange for acknowledging him as Holy Roman Emperor. With this important acquisition, the Papal States become the second-largest power block in Italy after the Kingdom of Sicily.

events.title: The first main survey of the Hundred Rolls, an English census seen as a…
events.blurb: The first main survey of the Hundred Rolls, an English census seen as a follow-up to the Domesday Book (completed in 1086), is begun; it lasts until 1275.

events.title: In Florence, the 9-year-old Dante first sees the 8-year-old Beatrice, his…
events.blurb: In Florence, the 9-year-old Dante first sees the 8-year-old Beatrice, his lifelong muse. She appears later as one of his guides in the Divine Comedy, Paradiso and Purgatorio.

events.title: Second Council of Lyon
events.blurb: Second Council of Lyon: Pope Gregory X convenes a council at Lyon, after Byzantine Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos gives assurances that the Orthodox Church is prepared to reunite with Rome.

events.title: Walter de Merton, English chancellor and regent, retires from royal service,…
events.blurb: Walter de Merton, English chancellor and regent, retires from royal service, in favour of Robert Burnell, who becomes a strong ally of the Edwardian regime.

events.title: Battle of Bun'ei
events.blurb: Battle of Bun'ei: Forces of the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty of China invade Japan. After conquering the Japanese settlements on Tsushima and Iki islands, Kublai Khan's fleet moves on to Japan and lands at Hakata Bay.

events.title: Ramon Llull, Spanish scholar and theologian, establishes a school in Majorca…
events.blurb: Ramon Llull, Spanish scholar and theologian, establishes a school in Majorca to teach Arabic to preachers, in an attempt to aid proselytizing to Moors. He also discovers diethyl ether.

events.title: Battle of Demetrias
events.blurb: Battle of Demetrias: Michael VIII Palaiologos sends a Byzantine fleet led by Alexios Philanthropenos to harass the Latin coasts.

events.title: Battle of Neopatras
events.blurb: Battle of Neopatras: Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos assembles a Byzantine expeditionary force (some 30,000 men), mostly mercenaries from Bulgaria, Serbia and the Sultanate of Rum.

events.title: Marinid forces take the city of Algiers, at this time independent
events.blurb: Marinid forces take the city of Algiers, at this time independent.

events.title: The mountain fortress Alamut Castle ("Eagle's Nest") is temporarily recaptured…
events.blurb: The mountain fortress Alamut Castle ("Eagle's Nest") is temporarily recaptured from the Mongols by a Nizari force under Shams al-Din Muhammad.

events.title: Jean de Meun completes the French allegorical work of fiction, Roman de la…
events.blurb: Jean de Meun completes the French allegorical work of fiction, Roman de la Rose, with a second section (the first section was written by Guillaume de Lorris in 1230).

events.title: Rabban Bar Sauma, Chinese Nestorian monk, embarks on a pilgrimage from China…
events.blurb: Rabban Bar Sauma, Chinese Nestorian monk, embarks on a pilgrimage from China to Jerusalem. He travels to Hotan, Kashgar, Taraz and Khorasan (modern Afghanistan).

events.title: Mongol forces (some 200,000 men) under Bayan of the Baarin ("Hundred Eyes")…
events.blurb: Mongol forces (some 200,000 men) under Bayan of the Baarin ("Hundred Eyes") defeat a Chinese army of 130,000 men led by the Song chancellor Jia Sidao on the Yangtze River.

events.title: The Japanese era Bun'ei ends and the Kenji era begins during the reign of the…
events.blurb: The Japanese era Bun'ei ends and the Kenji era begins during the reign of the 8-year-old Emperor Go-Uda (until 1278).

events.title: The first Statute of Westminster, drawn up between Parliament and Edward I,…
events.blurb: The first Statute of Westminster, drawn up between Parliament and Edward I, defines the legal privileges that landowners are allowed. These are based on the investigations carried out in 1274 into the landowner's rights to own their land.

events.title: Marinid forces led by Sultan Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq land in Spain…
events.blurb: Marinid forces led by Sultan Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq land in Spain upon a call from Muhammad II, ruler of Granada.

events.title: Battle of Hova
events.blurb: Battle of Hova: King Valdemar Birgersson of Sweden is defeated by his brother Magnus in the forest of Tiveden.

events.title: Battle of Écija
events.blurb: Battle of Écija: A Castilian army led by Nuño González de Lara is defeated by Marinid forces.

events.title: 1275 British earthquake
events.blurb: 1275 British earthquake: An earthquake strikes the south of Great Britain. The epicentre is unknown, although it may have been in the Portsmouth-Chichester area on the south coast of England or in Glamorgan, Wales.

events.title: Battle of Ronaldsway
events.blurb: Battle of Ronaldsway: Scottish forces under John de Vesci defeat the Manx people of the Isle of Man in a decisive battle, firmly establishing Scottish rule of the island.

events.title: Battle of Martos
events.blurb: Battle of Martos: A Castilian army under Sancho of Aragon (archbishop of Toledo) is defeated by the Moors at Martos.

events.title: Floris V, count of Holland, grants the city of Amsterdam freedom from taxes…
events.blurb: Floris V, count of Holland, grants the city of Amsterdam freedom from taxes (called a road toll).

events.title: Battle of Roccavione
events.blurb: Battle of Roccavione: Ghibelline forces defeat a Neapolitan army at Roccavione (Piedmont).

events.title: Battle of Dongola
events.blurb: Battle of Dongola: Mamluk forces led by Sultan Baibars gain a decisive victory against the Kingdom of Makuria. They capture the Makurian capital of Dongola and force King David of Makuria to flee upstream on the Nile.

events.title: The foundation stone of the Minoritenkirche in Vienna is laid by Ottokar II
events.blurb: The foundation stone of the Minoritenkirche in Vienna is laid by Ottokar II.

events.title: Henry of Ghent (or Henricus) becomes the last major theologian openly to…
events.blurb: Henry of Ghent (or Henricus) becomes the last major theologian openly to consider annuities as a usurious contract.

events.title: Merton College, Oxford, is first recorded as having a collection of books,…
events.blurb: Merton College, Oxford, is first recorded as having a collection of books, making its Library the world's oldest in continuous daily use.

events.title: Augsburg is granted the status of a free imperial city
events.blurb: Augsburg is granted the status of a free imperial city. Later this year, Ravensburg also receives the status.

events.title: Remnants of the Chinese Song court in Fuzhou province conduct the coronation…
events.blurb: Remnants of the Chinese Song court in Fuzhou province conduct the coronation ceremony for Prince Zhao Shi to become Emperor Emperor Duanzong (until 1278).

events.title: Adrian V (Hadrian) dies after a 2-month reign at Viterbo
events.blurb: Adrian V (Hadrian) dies after a 2-month reign at Viterbo. He is succeeded by John XXI as the 187th pope of Rome (until 1277).

events.title: Roger Bacon, Franciscan friar and University of Oxford lecturer, is arrested…
events.blurb: Roger Bacon, Franciscan friar and University of Oxford lecturer, is arrested for spreading anti-Church views; specifically, the Church's stance on Greek philosopher Galen.

events.title: Battle of Ngasaunggyan
events.blurb: Battle of Ngasaunggyan: A Burmese army (some 80,000 men) led by King Narathihapate (or Sithu IV) invades Mongol territory in Yunnan.

events.title: Summer – Uprising of Ivaylo
events.blurb: Summer – Uprising of Ivaylo: An uprising under Ivaylo breaks out in northeastern Bulgaria against the failure of Emperor Konstantin Tih to cope with the constant Mongol invasions which have devastated the country for years.

events.title: Late – Battle of Pharsalus
events.blurb: Late – Battle of Pharsalus: Michael VIII sends a Byzantine expeditionary army under John Synadenos to invade Thessaly.

events.title: Migration of the (Southern) Song dynasty
events.blurb: Migration of the (Southern) Song dynasty: Some 50,000 citizens of the Song dynasty in China become the first recorded inhabitants of Macau, as they seek refuge from the invading armies of the Yuan dynasty.

events.title: Battle of Desio
events.blurb: Battle of Desio: Lombard forces under Archbishop Ottone Visconti defeat the Della Torre family troops for the rule of Milan.

events.title: Siger of Brabant, Dutch teacher and philosopher, is condemned by the French…
events.blurb: Siger of Brabant, Dutch teacher and philosopher, is condemned by the French Inquisition for his advocacy of the Averroist doctrine that reason is separate from Christian faith.

events.title: Charles I, king of Sicily, buys the title to the Kingdom of Jerusalem from…
events.blurb: Charles I, king of Sicily, buys the title to the Kingdom of Jerusalem from Maria of Antioch, for 1,000 bezants and an annual payment of 4,000 livres tournois.

events.title: Byzantine–Venetian Treaty
events.blurb: Byzantine–Venetian Treaty: Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos concludes an agreement with the Republic of Venice. Stipulating a two-year truce, and renewing Venetian commercial privileges in the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Battle of Elbistan
events.blurb: Battle of Elbistan: A Mamluk army (some 14,000 men) under Sultan Baibars marches from Syria into the Mongol-dominated Sultanate of Rum and attacks the Mongol occupation force at Elbistan.

events.title: Treaty of Aberconwy
events.blurb: Treaty of Aberconwy: Prince Llywelyn ap Gruffudd and King Edward I of England sign a peace treaty which leaves Llywelyn only with the western part of Gwynedd.

events.title: Giles of Lessines writes his De usuris
events.blurb: Giles of Lessines writes his De usuris. He estimates that some credit contracts need not to be usurious, as "future things are not estimated to be of such value as those collected in the instant".

events.title: The earliest known written copy of the Avesta, a collection of ancient sacred…
events.blurb: The earliest known written copy of the Avesta, a collection of ancient sacred Persian Zoroastrian texts previously passed down orally, is produced.

events.title: Charles I is crowned King of Jerusalem, and is recognized by the kingdom's…
events.blurb: Charles I is crowned King of Jerusalem, and is recognized by the kingdom's barons at Acre. He surrenders the vicariate of Tuscany to Nicholas III.

events.title: William of Villehardouin, prince of Achaea, dies
events.blurb: William of Villehardouin, prince of Achaea, dies. By the terms of the Treaty of Viterbo, his lands passed under the direct control of Charles I, king of Sicily. Charles appoints a bailiff to rule the Latin principality.

events.title: The 7-year-old Emperor Emperor Duanzong (or Zhao Shi) dies of illness
events.blurb: The 7-year-old Emperor Emperor Duanzong (or Zhao Shi) dies of illness. He is succeeded by his brother Zhao Bing who becomes the last ruler of the Song dynasty.

events.title: Reconquista
events.blurb: Reconquista: Siege of Algeciras – Castilian forces (some 30,000 men) led by King Alfonso X ("the Wise") besiege Algeciras (at this time under control of the Marinids).

events.title: Battle on the Marchfeld
events.blurb: Battle on the Marchfeld: German-Hungarian forces (some 9,000 men) led by Kings Rudolf I of Germany in alliance with Ladislaus IV of Hungary ("the Cuman"), defeat and kill Ottokar II, ruler of Bohemia.

events.title: Pere d'Urtx, Catalan bishop of Urgell, becomes the first Episcopal Co-Prince…
events.blurb: Pere d'Urtx, Catalan bishop of Urgell, becomes the first Episcopal Co-Prince of Andorra, when he signs the paréage, establishing joint-sovereignty over the territory with Roger-Bernard III, count of Foix.

events.title: Trần Thánh Tông, second emperor of Vietnam's Trần dynasty, takes up the post…
events.blurb: Trần Thánh Tông, second emperor of Vietnam's Trần dynasty, takes up the post of Retired Emperor, but continues for 11 years to co-rule with his son Trần Khâm.

events.title: The Chola dynasty of South India falls under the rule of Rajendra Chola III,…
events.blurb: The Chola dynasty of South India falls under the rule of Rajendra Chola III, due to attacks by the Hoysala Empire and Pandya kingdom.

events.title: Abu Bakr al-Razi's (or Rhazes') medical writings are translated into Latin by…
events.blurb: Abu Bakr al-Razi's (or Rhazes') medical writings are translated into Latin by Faraj ben Salim, some 350 years after al-Razi's death.

events.title: The town of Haapsalu in Estonia is founded and later becomes the centre of the…
events.blurb: The town of Haapsalu in Estonia is founded and later becomes the centre of the Bishopric of Ösel–Wiek.

events.title: Abu Ishaq, uncle of the Hafsid caliph Abu Ishaq Ibrahim I, sides with the…
events.blurb: Abu Ishaq, uncle of the Hafsid caliph Abu Ishaq Ibrahim I, sides with the Almohad rebels of Béjaïa, and takes Tunis.

events.title: The Royal Mint is moved into the Tower of London
events.blurb: The Royal Mint is moved into the Tower of London. Mints outside London are reduced, with only a few local and episcopal mints continuing to operate.

events.title: Battle of Aizkraukle
events.blurb: Battle of Aizkraukle: Lithuanian forces led by Grand Duke Traidenis defeat an army of Teutonic Knights of the Livonian Order at Aizkraukle.

events.title: Battle of Yamen
events.blurb: Battle of Yamen: Kublai Khan's Mongol Yuan fleet attacks the Chinese Song fleet (some 1,000 ships) under Admiral Zhang Shijie at Yamen.

events.title: Thawun Gyi settles at Taungoo (modern-day Myanmar), and becomes the first…
events.blurb: Thawun Gyi settles at Taungoo (modern-day Myanmar), and becomes the first ruler of the Toungoo dynasty (until 1317).

events.title: Battle of Devina
events.blurb: Battle of Devina: Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos sends a Byzantine expeditionary force (some 10,000 men) to Bulgaria, to impose his ally (and son-in-law) Ivan Asen III on the throne.

events.title: Siege of Algeciras
events.blurb: Siege of Algeciras: Castilian forces led by King Alfonso X ("the Wise") abandon the siege (begun in 1278), after their fleet (some 400 ships) is destroyed by the Marinids led by Sultan Abu Yaqub Yusuf an-Nasr.

events.title: The Diet of Hungary adopts the so-called Cuman laws to regulate the social…
events.blurb: The Diet of Hungary adopts the so-called Cuman laws to regulate the social status and lifestyle of the nomadic and pagan Cumans living in the Kingdom of Hungary.

events.title: Alfonso X ("the Wise") grants the cities of Medina-Sidonia and Alcalá de los…
events.blurb: Alfonso X ("the Wise") grants the cities of Medina-Sidonia and Alcalá de los Gazules to the Order of Saint Mary of Spain. He also donates the town of Morón de la Frontera to the Order of Alcántara.

events.title: The first of the Statutes of Mortmain are passed during the reign of King…
events.blurb: The first of the Statutes of Mortmain are passed during the reign of King Edward I ("Longshanks"), which prevents land from passing into the possession of the Church.

events.title: The final expansion of Lincoln Cathedral in England is completed
events.blurb: The final expansion of Lincoln Cathedral in England is completed.

events.title: Tsar Ivan Asen III of Bulgaria flees from Tarnovo, ending the Asen dynasty in…
events.blurb: Tsar Ivan Asen III of Bulgaria flees from Tarnovo, ending the Asen dynasty in Bulgaria.

events.title: Turin is conquered by Thomas III of Savoy, becoming the capital of the House…
events.blurb: Turin is conquered by Thomas III of Savoy, becoming the capital of the House of Savoy.

events.title: Battle of al-Jassora
events.blurb: Battle of al-Jassora: Syria attempts to secede from the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt, but Al Mansur Qalawun defeats the rebels and keeps Syria within the Egyptian sultanate.

events.title: King Magnus Ladulås of Sweden founds a Swedish nobility by enacting a law…
events.blurb: King Magnus Ladulås of Sweden founds a Swedish nobility by enacting a law accepting a contribution of a cavalry member in lieu of ordinary tax payments.

events.title: Guy of Dampierre, count of Flanders, licenses the first Lombard merchants to…
events.blurb: Guy of Dampierre, count of Flanders, licenses the first Lombard merchants to open a changing business in his realm.

events.title: Spring – Siege of Berat
events.blurb: Spring – Siege of Berat: A Byzantine relief force under Michael Tarchaneiotes arrives at the strategically important citadel of Berat. Tarchaneiotes avoids a confrontation with the Angevines and relies on ambushes and raids instead.

events.title: Osman I, founder of the Ottoman Empire, becomes bey of the Söğüt tribe in…
events.blurb: Osman I, founder of the Ottoman Empire, becomes bey of the Söğüt tribe in central Anatolia after the death of his father, Ertuğrul Ghazi.

events.title: Frenchman Simon de Brion succeeds Nicholas III as Pope Martin IV, becoming the…
events.blurb: Frenchman Simon de Brion succeeds Nicholas III as Pope Martin IV, becoming the 189th pope of the Catholic Church.

events.title: Treaty of Orvieto
events.blurb: Treaty of Orvieto: Charles I, Giovanni Dandolo, doge of Venice, and Philip I, Latin emperor, make an agreement to recover the Latin Empire.

events.title: Battle of Kōan (or Second Battle of Hakata Bay)
events.blurb: Battle of Kōan (or Second Battle of Hakata Bay): A second Mongol invasion of Japan is foiled, as a large typhoon, famously called a kamikaze, or 'divine wind', destroys much of the combined Mongol and Chinese fleet and forces,

events.title: Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos is excommunicated by Pope Martin IV without…
events.blurb: Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos is excommunicated by Pope Martin IV without any warning or provocation. Martin authorizes Charles I, king of Sicily, to make a Crusade against Michael, who has re-established his rule in Constantinople.

events.title: Second Battle of Homs
events.blurb: Second Battle of Homs: In a pitched battle, Mamluk forces (some 30,000 men) led by Qalawun destroy the Mongol center; Möngke Temür is wounded and flees. He orders a retreat, followed by a disorganized army.

events.title: September or October – Battle of Lake Hód
events.blurb: September or October – Battle of Lake Hód: Hungarian forces led by King Ladislaus IV successfully repel and defeat an invading Cuman army. Ladislaus receives the title "the Cuman" for his heroic victory.

events.title: First evidence of the existence of consolidated public debt in Bruges,…
events.blurb: First evidence of the existence of consolidated public debt in Bruges, confirming the expansion of use of annuities, to fund government expenditure to the Low Countries.

events.title: John Peckham, archbishop of Canterbury, orders all the synagogues of London to…
events.blurb: John Peckham, archbishop of Canterbury, orders all the synagogues of London to close, and forbids Jewish doctors from practicing on non-Jews.

events.title: North Africa
events.blurb: Summer – An Aragonese expeditionary army under King Peter III lands in North Africa at Collo, in proclaimed support of a rebellion of the governor of Constantine, Ibn Wazir.

events.title: King Stefan Dragutin breaks his leg while hunting and becomes ill
events.blurb: King Stefan Dragutin breaks his leg while hunting and becomes ill. He abdicates the throne in favor of his younger brother, Stefan Milutin, who becomes ruler of Serbia (until 1321).

events.title: Daniel of Moscow, youngest son of Alexander Nevsky, is mentioned during this…
events.blurb: Daniel of Moscow, youngest son of Alexander Nevsky, is mentioned during this year as an independent Prince of the Grand Duchy of Moscow.

events.title: Trial of the Pyx
events.blurb: The form for the Trial of the Pyx in England, during which it is confirmed that newly minted coins conform to required standards, is established.

events.title: Hertford College is founded, at the University of Oxford
events.blurb: Hertford College is founded, at the University of Oxford.

events.title: Peter III of Aragon obtains the support of Nasrid Granada preparing for the…
events.blurb: Peter III of Aragon obtains the support of Nasrid Granada preparing for the incoming Aragonese Crusade, led by Philip "the Fair" of France.

events.title: Construction of Albi Cathedral in Languedoc begins
events.blurb: Construction of Albi Cathedral in Languedoc begins.

events.title: War of the Sicilian Vespers
events.blurb: War of the Sicilian Vespers: A group of Sicilian conspirators begins an uprising against the rule of King Charles I of Sicily; over the next six weeks, thousands of French are killed.

events.title: Battle of Forlì
events.blurb: Battle of Forlì: A French expeditionary army under Jean d'Eppe launches an assault on Forlì and breaches the outer wall.

events.title: Battle of Llandeilo Fawr
events.blurb: Battle of Llandeilo Fawr: English forces led by Gilbert de Clare are ambushed and defeated by Welsh troops at Llandeilo. English expansion into southern Wales is halted.

events.title: King Denis of Portugal ("the Poet King") marries the 11-year-old Elizabeth of…
events.blurb: King Denis of Portugal ("the Poet King") marries the 11-year-old Elizabeth of Aragon, daughter of Peter III, in Trancoso. Elizabeth receives the towns of Óbidos, Abrantes and Porto de Mós as part of her dowry.

events.title: Peter III of Aragon, traveling with his fleet on a military expedition against…
events.blurb: Peter III of Aragon, traveling with his fleet on a military expedition against Tunis, ends up in the Sicilian town of Trapani, after being asked by the inhabitants of Palermo to help in the fight against Charles I.

events.title: Peter III of Aragon is proclaimed "King of Sicily"
events.blurb: Peter III of Aragon is proclaimed "King of Sicily". Charles is forced to flee across the Strait of Messina, and be content with the Kingdom of Naples (ruling a part of the Italian Peninsula with the Pope).

events.title: Battle of Moel-y-don
events.blurb: Battle of Moel-y-don: English forces led by Luke de Tany are ambushed and defeated by Welsh troops, while crossing over a floating bridge to the island of Anglesey.

events.title: Battle of Orewin Bridge
events.blurb: Battle of Orewin Bridge: English forces (some 6,000 men) under Edward I of England defeat a Welsh army near Cilmeri. Llywelyn ap Gruffudd is killed.

events.title: 1283 Samtskhe earthquake
events.blurb: An earthquake destroys two thirds of the cave city of Vardzia, Georgia.

events.title: King Philip III of France ("the Bold") outlaws Jews from residence in the…
events.blurb: King Philip III of France ("the Bold") outlaws Jews from residence in the small villages and rural localities of France, causing a mass migration.

events.title: The first regulated Catalan Courts are reunited by King Peter III, for the…
events.blurb: The first regulated Catalan Courts are reunited by King Peter III, for the whole Principality of Catalonia. It became one of the first medieval parliaments that bans the royal power to create legislation unilaterally.

events.title: Mongol forces invade the Khmer Empire (modern Cambodia)
events.blurb: Mongol forces invade the Khmer Empire (modern Cambodia). King Jayavarman VIII decides to pay tribute rather than fight the invasion, buying peace and preserving the empire.

events.title: The Libro de los juegos, an early European treatise on board games (including…
events.blurb: The Libro de los juegos, an early European treatise on board games (including chess, dice, and a version of backgammon), is commissioned by King Alfonso X of Castile ("the Wise") (approximate date).

events.title: The German city of Goslar starts making efforts to redeem its already issued…
events.blurb: The German city of Goslar starts making efforts to redeem its already issued annuities, a sure indication of financial difficulty, and maybe an early sign of the 13th century crisis.

events.title: Mongol invasion of Burma
events.blurb: Mongol invasion of Burma: Mongol forces besiege the fortress at Ngasaunggyan on September 23. The Burmese garrison withstands the siege for two months, but finally falls to the invaders on December 3.

events.title: Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd
events.blurb: Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd: Construction of Caernarfon Castle, Conwy Castle and Harlech Castle in Wales by Edward I of England begins as a system of defenses against possible future Welsh uprisings.

events.title: Most of Dublin, including St
events.blurb: Most of Dublin, including St. Patrick's Cathedral, is burned in a fire.

events.title: Battle of Thị Nại Bay
events.blurb: Battle of Thị Nại Bay: A Mongol-led Yuan expeditionary force (some 5,000 men) lands on the beach, near Champa's capital Vijaya in Vietnam.

events.title: The last independent Welsh stronghold, Castell y Bere, is surrendered by…
events.blurb: The last independent Welsh stronghold, Castell y Bere, is surrendered by Cynfrig ap Madog to the English.

events.title: Treaty of Rheinfelden
events.blurb: Treaty of Rheinfelden: The 11-year-old Rudolf II is forced to relinquish his claim on the Duchies of Austria and Styria to his elder brother, Albert I.

events.title: Battle of Malta
events.blurb: Battle of Malta: An Aragonese fleet (some 20 galleys) under Admiral Roger of Lauria attacks and defeats the Angevin ships in the Grand Harbour, sent to help put down a rebellion on Malta.

events.title: The events giving rise to the story of the Pied Piper of Hamelin take place in…
events.blurb: The events giving rise to the story of the Pied Piper of Hamelin take place in Lower Saxony.

events.title: King Peter III of Aragon takes advantage of the weakness of the Hafsid dynasty…
events.blurb: King Peter III of Aragon takes advantage of the weakness of the Hafsid dynasty and raids the island of Djerba. Aragonese forces massacre the population and occupy the island.

events.title: Hafsid forces under Abu Hafs Umar bin Yahya (half-brother of Abu Ishaq Ibrahim…
events.blurb: Hafsid forces under Abu Hafs Umar bin Yahya (half-brother of Abu Ishaq Ibrahim I) reconquer Tunis and reinstall the Hafsid dynasty as the dominating power in Ifriqiya. This ends the Bedouin rebellion started in 1283.

events.title: Construction of Beauvais Cathedral is interrupted by a partial collapse of the…
events.blurb: Construction of Beauvais Cathedral is interrupted by a partial collapse of the choir; the event unnerves French masons working in the Gothic style.

events.title: Aragonese Crusade
events.blurb: Aragonese Crusade: The first French armies under King Philip III ("the Bold") and his 14-year-old son Charles of Valois enter Roussillon.

events.title: Peterhouse, oldest collegiate foundation of the University of Cambridge in…
events.blurb: Peterhouse, oldest collegiate foundation of the University of Cambridge in England, is established by Bishop Hugh de Balsham.

events.title: Statute of Rhuddlan
events.blurb: Statute of Rhuddlan: King Edward I of England brings Wales under direct rule after the Welsh Wars (1277–1283).

events.title: King Alfonso X of Castile ("the Wise") falls ill and dies after a 32-year…
events.blurb: King Alfonso X of Castile ("the Wise") falls ill and dies after a 32-year reign at Seville. He is succeeded by his 25-year-old son Sancho IV ("the Brave") who becomes ruler of Castile and León.

events.title: Jönköping in Sweden is granted town privileges by King Magnus Ladulås
events.blurb: Jönköping in Sweden is granted town privileges by King Magnus Ladulås.

events.title: Battle of the Gulf of Naples
events.blurb: Battle of the Gulf of Naples: An Aragonese-Sicilian fleet (some 30 galleys) led by Admiral Roger of Lauria surrounds and defeats the Neapolitan ships in the Gulf of Naples.

events.title: Battle of Meloria
events.blurb: Battle of Meloria: A Genoese fleet (some 90 galleys) led by Admiral Oberto Doria defeats the Pisan ships in the Ligurian Sea. This marks the decline of the maritime power of Pisa in the Mediterranean.

events.title: The Mor Bar Sauma Monastery, one of the most important monasteries of the…
events.blurb: The Mor Bar Sauma Monastery, one of the most important monasteries of the Syriac Orthodox Church, is destroyed. Though a monastic community remains, the patriarchal seat is moved to Sis.

events.title: The writ Circumspecte Agatis, issued by King Edward I (Longshanks), defines…
events.blurb: The writ Circumspecte Agatis, issued by King Edward I (Longshanks), defines the jurisdictions of church and state, thereby limiting the church's judicial powers to ecclesiastical cases only.

events.title: The County of Champagne is integrated into the kingdom of France
events.blurb: The County of Champagne is integrated into the kingdom of France; the region loses its haven characteristics for foreign merchants, and the Fairs of Troyes quickly dwindle into economic insignificance.

events.title: The English romantic poem The Lay of Havelok the Dane is written (approximate…
events.blurb: The English romantic poem The Lay of Havelok the Dane is written (approximate date).

events.title: The Second Statute of Westminster is accepted in parliament, reforming various…
events.blurb: The Second Statute of Westminster is accepted in parliament, reforming various laws; it includes the clause de donis conditionalibus, considered one of the fundamental institutes of medieval law.

events.title: Golden Horde
events.blurb: Winter – The Mongol Golden Horde led by Nogai Khan and Talabuga attacks Hungary for the second time. They successfully subdue Slovakia and sack territory north of the Carpathian Mountains.

events.title: Archbishop Jakub Świnka organizes a synod in Łęczyca
events.blurb: Archbishop Jakub Świnka organizes a synod in Łęczyca. During the meeting, he orders all priests who are subject to his bishopric to deliver their sermons in Polish rather than German.

events.title: Pope Martin IV dies after a 4-year pontificate in Perugia
events.blurb: Pope Martin IV dies after a 4-year pontificate in Perugia. He is succeeded by Honorius IV, who becomes the 190th pope of the Catholic Church.

events.title: Mamluk forces under Sultan Qalawun (the Victorious) appear with specially…
events.blurb: Mamluk forces under Sultan Qalawun (the Victorious) appear with specially built war engines before the Crusader fortress of Margat and begin a siege.

events.title: Marinid forces under Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq prolong their siege at…
events.blurb: Marinid forces under Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq prolong their siege at Jerez de la Frontera.

events.title: Battle of Chương Dương
events.blurb: Battle of Chương Dương: Joint forces of Champa and Đại Việt defeat the Mongol-led Yuan fleet on the Red River. Most of the Yuan warships are burned during the battle, and the Mongol army retreats to China in late June.

events.title: Castilian forces led by Sancho IV (the Brave) march against the Marinids at…
events.blurb: Castilian forces led by Sancho IV (the Brave) march against the Marinids at Jerez de la Frontera.

events.title: Battle of Les Formigues
events.blurb: Battle of Les Formigues: An Aragonese-Sicilian fleet (some 40 galleys) under Admiral Roger of Lauria defeats French and Genoese ships near the Formigues Islands.

events.title: Battle of the Col de Panissars
events.blurb: Battle of the Col de Panissars: Aragonese forces under King Peter III (the Great) ambush and defeat a French expeditionary army while it was retreating over the Pyrenees.

events.title: Peter III (the Great) dies after a 9-year reign at Vilafranca del Penedès
events.blurb: Peter III (the Great) dies after a 9-year reign at Vilafranca del Penedès. He is succeeded by his 20-year-old son Alfonso III (the Liberal), who becomes king of Aragon. Peter's other son James II (the Just), is crowned ruler of Sicily.

events.title: Old Prussians resettle in Samland and start an uprising against Teutonic rule…
events.blurb: Old Prussians resettle in Samland and start an uprising against Teutonic rule (supported by the Principality of Rügen). The Prussians are defeated by the Teutonic Knights and forced to submit.

events.title: War of the Donkey
events.blurb: The War of the Donkey is fought between the rival noble families of the Ghisi and the Sanudo, in the Duchy of the Archipelago in the Aegean Sea.

events.title: In the Lao kingdom of Muang Sua, King Panya Leng is overthrown in a coup…
events.blurb: In the Lao kingdom of Muang Sua, King Panya Leng is overthrown in a coup d'état led by his son, Prince Panya Khamphong, which is likely to have been supported by the Mongol-led Yuan Dynasty in China.

events.title: The 17-year-old Philip IV (the Fair) is crowned king of France at Reims
events.blurb: The 17-year-old Philip IV (the Fair) is crowned king of France at Reims. He settles the Aragonese conflict, and intensifies his predecessors' efforts to reform and rationalize the administration of the realm.

events.title: The Catholicon, a religious Latin dictionary, is completed by John of Genoa
events.blurb: The Catholicon, a religious Latin dictionary, is completed by John of Genoa.

events.title: King Alexander III dies in a fall from his horse at Kinghorn in Fife, leaving…
events.blurb: King Alexander III dies in a fall from his horse at Kinghorn in Fife, leaving Queen Yolande of Dreux's unborn child and the 3-year-old Margaret (Maid of Norway) as heirs to the throne.

events.title: The 15-year-old Henry II sails from Cyprus and lands in Acre, but is refused…
events.blurb: The 15-year-old Henry II sails from Cyprus and lands in Acre, but is refused entry into the citadel. There, he stays for six weeks in the palace to negotiate an agreement to take over the city from the Angevins.

events.title: Henry II is crowned king of Jerusalem at Tyre
events.blurb: Henry II is crowned king of Jerusalem at Tyre. After the ceremony, he returns to Acre for the festivities. A few weeks later, Henry returns to Cyprus and appoints his uncle Philip of Ibelin as regent (bailiff).

events.title: Winter – Mongol invasion of Poland
events.blurb: Winter – Mongol invasion of Poland: Mongol forces (some 30,000 men) under Talabuga Khan and Nogai Khan, attack Poland for the third time. The cities of Lublin, Sandomierz and Sieradz are devastated by the invaders.

events.title: Gloucester
events.blurb: Summer – Edward I (Longshanks) replies to the Welsh rebellion by raising an army at Gloucester commanded by Edmund of Almain.

events.title: Arghun
events.blurb: Spring – Arghun Khan, Mongol ruler of the Ilkhanate, sends an embassy under Rabban Bar Sauma with the mission of contracting a military alliance against the Mamluk Sultanate and take the city of Jerusalem.

events.title: The Altar of St
events.blurb: The Altar of St. James in Pistoia Cathedral, Italy – a masterwork of the silversmithing trade containing nearly a ton of silver – is begun; it will not be completed for nearly 200 years.

events.title: Union of Aragon
events.blurb: Alfonso III (the Liberal) is forced to make concessions to the nobility after an aristocratic uprising (called the Union of Aragon). In particular, he grants his barons a "Bill of Rights", known as the Privilegium Generale.

events.title: The Italian city of Siena exacts a forced loan from its taxpayers for the…
events.blurb: The Italian city of Siena exacts a forced loan from its taxpayers for the first time, a common feature of medieval public finance.

events.title: An Aragonese fleet raids the Tunisian Kerkennah Islands in the Gulf of Gabès
events.blurb: An Aragonese fleet raids the Tunisian Kerkennah Islands in the Gulf of Gabès.

events.title: Construction of Uppsala Cathedral in Sweden begins (it lasts until 1435)
events.blurb: Construction of Uppsala Cathedral in Sweden begins (it lasts until 1435).

events.title: Aragonese forces led by King Alfonso III (the Liberal) conquer the island of…
events.blurb: Aragonese forces led by King Alfonso III (the Liberal) conquer the island of Menorca. He signs the "Treaty of San Agayz" with Sultan Abû 'Umar ibn Sa'îd on January 21.

events.title: Wareru creates the Hanthawaddy kingdom (modern Myanmar) following the collapse…
events.blurb: Wareru creates the Hanthawaddy kingdom (modern Myanmar) following the collapse of the Pagan Kingdom. He is crowned king on April 5 and declares himself independent of Pagan.

events.title: South England flood
events.blurb: South England flood: A large storm hits the south coast, this has a powerful effect on the Cinque Ports, two of which are hit (Hastings and New Romney). The storm destroys Old Winchelsea on Romney Marsh and nearby Broomhill.

events.title: Pope Honorius IV dies after a 2-year pontificate at Rome
events.blurb: Pope Honorius IV dies after a 2-year pontificate at Rome. During his reign, he tries to restore Sicily to papal vassalage, but Honorius clashes with King Peter III (the Great), who supports Sicilian independence.

events.title: Nayan, Mongol prince of the Borjigin clan, revolts against the rule of Kublai Khan
events.blurb: Nayan, Mongol prince of the Borjigin clan, revolts against the rule of Kublai Khan. Kublai leads a punitive expedition against Nayan in Manchuria and defeats his forces on July 16.

events.title: Welsh forces led by Rhys ap Maredudd revolt in Wales against King Edward I…
events.blurb: Welsh forces led by Rhys ap Maredudd revolt in Wales against King Edward I (Longshanks). Although Maredudd has assisted the English in the past, he accuses Edward of treating him unfairly over taxes.

events.title: Battle of the Counts
events.blurb: Battle of the Counts: An Aragonese-Sicilian fleet (some 50 galleys) under Admiral Roger of Lauria defeat a larger Angevin fleet of 70 galleys near Naples. After a feigned retreat, Roger attacks the Angevin galleys from all sides.

events.title: Bohemond VII, ruler of Tripoli, dies childless
events.blurb: Bohemond VII, ruler of Tripoli, dies childless. He is succeeded by his sister Lucia, who is married to Charles I of Naples' former Grand Admiral, Narjot de Toucy.

events.title: Parts of Norfolk are flooded, the port of Dunwich in Suffolk is further…
events.blurb: Parts of Norfolk are flooded, the port of Dunwich in Suffolk is further devastated, and in The Fens through the storm and the violence of the sea,

events.title: Battle of Pagan
events.blurb: Battle of Pagan: Mongol-led Yuan forces (some 7,000 cavalry) led by Temür Khan defeat King Thihathu of the Pagan Kingdom. The kingdom disintegrates and anarchy ensues.

events.title: A huge storm and associated storm tide in the North Sea and English Channel,…
events.blurb: A huge storm and associated storm tide in the North Sea and English Channel, known as St. Lucia's flood in the Netherlands, kills thousands and reshapes the coastline of the Netherlands and England.

events.title: The Parliament of Scotland creates a law allowing women to propose marriage to…
events.blurb: The Parliament of Scotland creates a law allowing women to propose marriage to men during leap years; men who refuse such proposals are required to pay a fine to the spurned bride-to-be.

events.title: Work is begun on the construction of Mob Quad in Merton College, Oxford
events.blurb: Work is begun on the construction of Mob Quad in Merton College, Oxford.

events.title: Muhammad II of Granada
events.blurb: Summer – Sultan Muhammad II drives the rebellious Banu Ashqilula from one stronghold to the next, where they are finally expelled from Granadan territory in Al-Andalus (modern Spain).

events.title: Newcastle Emlyn Castle in West Wales is recaptured by the English forces after…
events.blurb: Newcastle Emlyn Castle in West Wales is recaptured by the English forces after a ten-day siege, bringing Rhys ap Maredudd's revolt to an end. Rhys is exiled to Ireland.

events.title: The Japanese era Kōan ends and the Shōō era begins during the reign of the…
events.blurb: The Japanese era Kōan ends and the Shōō era begins during the reign of the 22-year-old Emperor Fushimi (until 1293).

events.title: Battle of Bạch Đằng
events.blurb: Battle of Bạch Đằng: Đại Việt (Vietnamese) general Trần Hưng Đạo sinks the fleet of an invading Mongol-led Yuan expeditionary army (some 94,000 men).

events.title: War of the Limburg Succession – Battle of Worringen
events.blurb: War of the Limburg Succession – Battle of Worringen: Brabantian forces under Duke John I defeat the coalition army of Cologne, Luxemburg, and Nassau at Worringen (in a struggle to conquer the Duchy of Limburg).

events.title: Petrus, bishop of Västerås, buys 1/8 of the Stora Kopparberg copper mine in…
events.blurb: Petrus, bishop of Västerås, buys 1/8 of the Stora Kopparberg copper mine in Falun, Sweden. During the reign of King Magnus Ladulås, nobles and foreign merchants from Lübeck take interests in the mining area.

events.title: Pope Nicholas IV proclaims a crusade against the 26-year-old King Ladislaus…
events.blurb: Pope Nicholas IV proclaims a crusade against the 26-year-old King Ladislaus IV, who had lost credibility by favoring his semi-pagan Cuman subjects in Hungary, and in general refusing to conform to the social standards of Western Europe.

events.title: Treaty of Canfranc
events.blurb: Treaty of Canfranc: King Edward I signs an agreement with Alfonso III at Canfranc, about the release of Charles II, who has been captured by Admiral Roger of Lauria in the Battle of the Gulf of Naples (see 1284).

events.title: Construction of Conwy Castle in Wales, ordered by Edward I (Longshanks), is…
events.blurb: Construction of Conwy Castle in Wales, ordered by Edward I (Longshanks), is completed.

events.title: Siege of Tripoli
events.blurb: Siege of Tripoli: Mamluk forces under Qalawun (the Victorious) capture Tripoli after a month-long siege, thus extinguishing the County of Tripoli.

events.title: Battle of Campaldino
events.blurb: Battle of Campaldino: Pro-papal Guelph forces of Florence and their allies, Lucca, Pistoia, Prato and Siena under Viscount Aimery IV defeat the Ghibelline army (some 10,000 men) in Tuscany.

events.title: Battle of Copenhagen
events.blurb: Battle of Copenhagen: A Norwegian expeditionary force under King Eric II, supported by Danish outlaws, sets sail to Copenhagen and attacks the city. But they are repelled and forced to withdraw to Zealand.

events.title: The Dnyaneshwari is written in India
events.blurb: The Dnyaneshwari is written in India. This holy book is a commentary on the Bhagvad Gita and is narrated by Dnyaneshwar.

events.title: Quia Emptores, a statute passed by Edward I, puts an end to the practice of…
events.blurb: Quia Emptores, a statute passed by Edward I, puts an end to the practice of subinfeudations. The statute allows land to be sold according to royal approval, as long as the new owner answers directly to his lord or the king.

events.title: The University of Coimbra is founded in Lisbon by Denis I ("the Poet King")
events.blurb: The University of Coimbra is founded in Lisbon by Denis I ("the Poet King"). He decrees that Portuguese is the official language of Portugal, replacing classical Latin in that capacity.

events.title: Beatrice Portinari, muse of the Italian poet Dante Alighieri, dies in Florence
events.blurb: Beatrice Portinari, muse of the Italian poet Dante Alighieri, dies in Florence. In his Divine Comedy (La Divina Commedia), he transforms his memory of Beatrice into an allegory of divine love.

events.title: Shamsuddin Kayumars, Mamluk ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, is murdered and…
events.blurb: Shamsuddin Kayumars, Mamluk ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, is murdered and succeeded by Jalal-ud-din Khalji (or Firuz Shah I), founder of the Khalji dynasty, ending Mamluk rule and instigating the Khalji Revolution.

events.title: King Ladislaus IV of Hungary ("the Cuman") is assassinated at the castle of…
events.blurb: King Ladislaus IV of Hungary ("the Cuman") is assassinated at the castle of Körösszeg (modern Romania).

events.title: Edict of Expulsion
events.blurb: Edict of Expulsion: King Edward I of England ("Longshanks") orders all Jews (at this time probably numbering around 2,000) to leave the country by November 1 (All Saints' Day).

events.title: Italian Crusaders massacre Muslim merchants and peasants, and some local…
events.blurb: Italian Crusaders massacre Muslim merchants and peasants, and some local Christians in Acre. Some claim it began at a drunken party – others that a European husband found his wife making love to a Muslim.

events.title: The 7-year-old Margaret, Maid of Norway, queen-designate and heir to the crown…
events.blurb: The 7-year-old Margaret, Maid of Norway, queen-designate and heir to the crown of Scotland, dies en route to the British Isles in Orkney, leading to thirteen competitors for the crown of Scotland, a succession crisis.

events.title: 1290 Zhili earthquake
events.blurb: The 6.8 Zhili earthquake affects the province of Zhili in China, with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), killing 7,270–100,000 people.

events.title: Qalawun ("the Victorious") dies as the Egyptian Mamluk army sets out for Acre
events.blurb: Qalawun ("the Victorious") dies as the Egyptian Mamluk army sets out for Acre. He is succeeded by his eldest son Al-Ashraf Khalil as ruler of the Mamluk Sultanate.

events.title: Eleanor of Castile, wife of Edward I, dies while traveling in the North
events.blurb: Eleanor of Castile, wife of Edward I, dies while traveling in the North. She has been suffering from illness for some time, and the cold and dampness of the winter months probably aggravate her condition.

events.title: Edward I travels with the body of Queen Eleanor from Lincoln to London
events.blurb: Edward I travels with the body of Queen Eleanor from Lincoln to London. Remembering his wife, Edward erects a series of crosses at each location that the body rests overnight. These are known as the twelve Eleanor crosses.

events.title: Klenová Castle is constructed in southern Bohemia near the town of Klatovy…
events.blurb: Klenová Castle is constructed in southern Bohemia near the town of Klatovy (modern Czech Republic) as part of a frontier defense system.

events.title: Late September
events.blurb: Late September – Abu Yaqub Yusuf an-Nasr crosses the Strait of Gibraltar from Alcácer Seguir to Tarifa. During the next three months, Marinid forces besiege Vejer de la Frontera, and carry out daily raids around Ferez.

events.title: King Andrew III of Hungary ("the Venetian") gives royal town privileges to…
events.blurb: King Andrew III of Hungary ("the Venetian") gives royal town privileges to Bratislava, modern-day capital of Slovakia.

events.title: Venetian glass manufacture is concentrated on the island of Murano (located in…
events.blurb: Venetian glass manufacture is concentrated on the island of Murano (located in the Venetian Lagoon), to prevent fires in Venice itself.

events.title: Guo Shoujing, Chinese engineer and astronomer, constructs the artificial…
events.blurb: Guo Shoujing, Chinese engineer and astronomer, constructs the artificial Kunming Lake, which is developed into a reservoir with summer gardens for Khanbaliq (or Dadu of Yuan), Mongol capital of Emperor Kublai Khan.

events.title: Vandino and Ugolino Vivaldi
events.blurb: Spring – The brothers Vandino and Ugolino Vivaldi, Italian explorers and merchants from Genoa, embark with two galleys intending to reach India and establish a trade route to Italy.

events.title: Four towns of the County of Holland (Dordrecht, Haarlem, Leiden and Alkmaar)…
events.blurb: Four towns of the County of Holland (Dordrecht, Haarlem, Leiden and Alkmaar) and two of the County of Zeeland (Middelburg and Zierikzee) agree collectively to secure a loan by their sovereign, Count Floris V.

events.title: Edward I meets the claimants for the Scottish crown at Norham Castle and…
events.blurb: Edward I meets the claimants for the Scottish crown at Norham Castle and informs them that he will judge the various claims to the throne, but they must acknowledge him as overlord of Scotland and, to ensure peace,

events.title: Siege of Acre
events.blurb: Siege of Acre: Mamluk forces under Sultan Al-Ashraf Khalil capture Acre after a six-week siege. The Mamluks take the outer wall of the city after fierce fighting.

events.title: Al-Ashraf Khalil enters Damascus in triumph with Crusaders chained at their…
events.blurb: Al-Ashraf Khalil enters Damascus in triumph with Crusaders chained at their feet and the captured Crusader standards, which are carried upside-down as a sign of their defeat.

events.title: Thibaud Gaudin arrives with the surviving knights, with the treasure of the…
events.blurb: Thibaud Gaudin arrives with the surviving knights, with the treasure of the Order, in Sidon. There, he is elected as Grand Master of the Knights Templar, to succeed Guillaume de Beaujeu (who was mortally wounded during the siege of Acre).

events.title: Federal Charter of 1291
