events.blurb: Federal Charter of 1291: The "three forest cantons" (Waldstätte) of Switzerland (Schwyz, Uri and Unterwalden) form a defensive alliance to protect themselves from the House of Habsburg;

events.title: A combined Genoese-Sevillian fleet led by Admiral Benedetto Zaccaria wins a…
events.blurb: A combined Genoese-Sevillian fleet led by Admiral Benedetto Zaccaria wins a victory over 27 Marinid galleys at Alcácer Seguir –12 galleys are taken and the rest put to flight.

events.title: Mamluk forces conquer the last Crusader outpost in Syria, the Templar fortress…
events.blurb: Mamluk forces conquer the last Crusader outpost in Syria, the Templar fortress of Atlit south of Acre. All that now is left to the Knights Templar is the island fortress of Ruad.

events.title: December
events.blurb: December – The kings Sancho IV of Castile ("the Brave") and James II of Aragon ("the Just") agree to join the war against the Marinids and conclude a treaty of friendship.

events.title: Shanghai County is established
events.blurb: Shanghai County is established.

events.title: Taxatio Ecclesiastica
events.blurb: Spring – The Taxatio Ecclesiastica, compiled in 1291–1292, is completed under the order of Pope Nicholas IV. It is a detailed database valuation for ecclesiastical taxation of English, Welsh and Irish churches.

events.title: The Vaghela dynasty in Gujarat (located along the western coast of India) is…
events.blurb: The Vaghela dynasty in Gujarat (located along the western coast of India) is subjugated by the Deccan Seuna (Yadava) dynasty of Daulatabad.

events.title: Al-Ashraf Khalil returns to Damascus and assembles an army to attack Sis, the…
events.blurb: Al-Ashraf Khalil returns to Damascus and assembles an army to attack Sis, the capital of the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia. An Armenian embassy arrives in Damascus, and reaches a settlement with Khalil.

events.title: The College of Electors select Adolf, count of Nassau, as the new King of the…
events.blurb: The College of Electors select Adolf, count of Nassau, as the new King of the Romans and successor of Habsburg Rudolf I who had died the previous year. Adolf is forced to make wide-ranging concessions to the Electors to get elected.

events.title: Castilian forces led by King Sancho IV ("the Brave") begin the siege of…
events.blurb: Castilian forces led by King Sancho IV ("the Brave") begin the siege of Tarifa: eleven newly built engines bombard the city constantly by land and sea.

events.title: Michael II becomes Syriac Orthodox patriarch of Antioch (until 1312)
events.blurb: Michael II becomes Syriac Orthodox patriarch of Antioch (until 1312).

events.title: John Balliol is selected by King Edward I of England as ruler of Scotland at…
events.blurb: John Balliol is selected by King Edward I of England as ruler of Scotland at Berwick from among 13 competitors for the Crown of Scotland.

events.title: Dante Alighieri completes the book of verse La Vita Nuova
events.blurb: Dante Alighieri completes the book of verse La Vita Nuova.

events.title: Torkel Knutsson leads Sweden in beginning the Third Swedish Crusade, against…
events.blurb: Torkel Knutsson leads Sweden in beginning the Third Swedish Crusade, against unchristianized Finnish Karelia. In the same year, the construction of Vyborg Castle begins, by orders of Knutsson.

events.title: The Ordinances of Justice are enacted in the Commune of Florence
events.blurb: The Ordinances of Justice are enacted in the Commune of Florence.

events.title: The Isle of Wight is sold to King Edward I of England by Isabella de Forz,…
events.blurb: The Isle of Wight is sold to King Edward I of England by Isabella de Forz, Countess of Devon, on her deathbed, for 6,000 marks.

events.title: Ignatius bar Wahib becomes Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Mardin
events.blurb: Ignatius bar Wahib becomes Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Mardin.

events.title: 1293 Kamakura earthquake
events.blurb: An earthquake in Kamakura, Japan kills an estimated 23,000.

events.title: The forces of Raden Wijaya win a major victory in the Mongol invasion of Java,…
events.blurb: The forces of Raden Wijaya win a major victory in the Mongol invasion of Java, which is considered to be the founding date of the city of Surabaya.

events.title: Madog ap Llywelyn
events.blurb: Autumn – In response to the actions of new royal administrators in north and west Wales, Madog ap Llywelyn leads a revolt against his English overlords.

events.title: Korela Fortress
events.blurb: Spring – Following the arrival of a fleet from Sweden, an offensive takes place in which Sweden captures Kexholm after an assault.

events.title: Strata Florida Abbey is rebuilt
events.blurb: Strata Florida Abbey is rebuilt; it had been destroyed some years earlier, during King Edward I's conquest of Wales.

events.title: Architect Arnolfo di Cambio designs Florence Cathedral (Cattedrale di Santa…
events.blurb: Architect Arnolfo di Cambio designs Florence Cathedral (Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Fiore, better known simply as Il Duomo); he also begins work on the Basilica of Santa Croce, Florence.

events.title: Kublai Khan dies
events.blurb: Kublai Khan dies; by this time the separation of the four khanates of the Mongol Empire (the Chagatai Khanate in Central Asia, the Golden Horde in Russia, the Ilkhanate in Persia, and the Yuan Dynasty in China) has deepened.

events.title: Third Swedish Crusade
events.blurb: Third Swedish Crusade: a Novgorodian army led by Prince Roman Glebovich attempts a storm of Vyborg, but the attack fails.

events.title: Pope Boniface VIII succeeds Pope Celestine V, becoming the 193rd pope, after…
events.blurb: Pope Boniface VIII succeeds Pope Celestine V, becoming the 193rd pope, after Celestine V abdicates the papacy on December 13, only five months after reluctantly accepting his surprise election on July 5,

events.title: Construction begins on Beaumaris Castle in Anglesey under the direction of…
events.blurb: Construction begins on Beaumaris Castle in Anglesey under the direction of James of Saint George as part of the conquest of Wales by Edward I.

events.title: King Jayavarman VIII is overthrown after a 52-year reign
events.blurb: King Jayavarman VIII is overthrown after a 52-year reign. He is succeeded by his son-in-law Indravarman III as ruler of the Khmer Empire (modern Cambodia).

events.title: Battle of Maes Moydog
events.blurb: Battle of Maes Moydog: English forces led by William de Beauchamp, 9th Earl of Warwick defeat the Welsh rebels (some 700 men), near the modern-day town of Llanfair Caereinion in Wales.

events.title: Treaty of Anagni
events.blurb: Treaty of Anagni: Pope Boniface VIII arranges a peace treaty between King Philip IV of France ("the Fair"), Charles II of Naples ("the Lame"), and James II of Majorca.

events.title: Przemysł II is crowned king of Poland at Gniezno, the first coronation of a…
events.blurb: Przemysł II is crowned king of Poland at Gniezno, the first coronation of a Polish ruler in 219 years. Przemysł travels to Pomerelia where he confirms the privileges of the monasteries in Oliwa and Żarnowiec.

events.title: War of Curzola
events.blurb: War of Curzola: Genoese raids on the Venetian quarter in Constantinople lead to a formal declaration of war with the Republic of Venice. A Venetian fleet (some 40 war galleys) attacks Galata, the quarter of the Genoese merchants.

events.title: Mongol leader Baydu Khan is executed after a 7-month reign at Tabriz
events.blurb: Mongol leader Baydu Khan is executed after a 7-month reign at Tabriz. He is succeeded by Ghazan, who becomes ruler of the Ilkhanate. He converts to Islam, ending a line of Vajrayana (Tantric Buddhist) leaders.

events.title: The first treaty forming the Auld Alliance ("Old Alliance"), between Scotland…
events.blurb: The first treaty forming the Auld Alliance ("Old Alliance"), between Scotland and France against England, is signed in Paris by Kings John Balliol and Philip IV.

events.title: Chinese diplomat Zhou Daguan spends a year at the court of Khmer King…
events.blurb: Chinese diplomat Zhou Daguan spends a year at the court of Khmer King Indravarman III at Angkor, and pens a journal setting forth his observations.

events.title: Boniface of Verona expels the Byzantines from their last remaining strongholds…
events.blurb: Boniface of Verona expels the Byzantines from their last remaining strongholds on Euboea.

events.title: approximate date
events.blurb: approximate date – Tarabya, self-proclaimed king of Pegu, is defeated in single combat on war elephants by Wareru.

events.title: King Mangrai the Great of Ngoenyang establishes a new capital by founding…
events.blurb: King Mangrai the Great of Ngoenyang establishes a new capital by founding Chiangmai, and founds the Mangrai Dynasty,

events.title: Battle of Dunbar
events.blurb: Battle of Dunbar: John Balliol's Scottish army is defeated by an English army commanded by John de Warenne, 6th Earl of Surrey.

events.title: The formal coronation of Alauddin Khalji as Sultan of Delhi takes place, and…
events.blurb: The formal coronation of Alauddin Khalji as Sultan of Delhi takes place, and he takes the regnal name Muhammad Shah I.

events.title: Treaty of Alcañices
events.blurb: Treaty of Alcañices: Kings Denis of Portugal ("the Poet King") and 11-year-old Ferdinand IV of Castile ("the Summoned") (under the guidance of his mother, Queen-Regent Maria de Molina) sign a treaty between Portugal and Castile,

events.title: Roxburgh
events.blurb: Summer – Edward I of England orders a punitive expedition against the rebellious Scots. At Roxburgh, an army of some 9,000 men (including 2,000 cavalry) led by John de Warenne is assembled.

events.title: A Portuguese Water Dog is first described in a monk's report of a drowning…
events.blurb: A Portuguese Water Dog is first described in a monk's report of a drowning sailor, who has been pulled from the sea by a dog.

events.title: Guelph forces, led by the Genoese leader François Grimaldi (il Malizia), storm…
events.blurb: Guelph forces, led by the Genoese leader François Grimaldi (il Malizia), storm and capture the Rock of Monaco. François, disguised as a Franciscan friar, gains entry to the city, and opens the gates for his soldiers.

events.title: William Wallace, Scottish rebel leader, leads an uprising against the English…
events.blurb: William Wallace, Scottish rebel leader, leads an uprising against the English at Lanark and kills Sheriff William Hesselrig.

events.title: Stefano Colonna, Italian chief magistrate and papal official, captures the…
events.blurb: Stefano Colonna, Italian chief magistrate and papal official, captures the treasure of the tomb of Caecilia Metella near Rome, which is sent by the rival Caetani family to Pope Boniface VIII.

events.title: Battle of Furnes
events.blurb: Battle of Furnes: French forces under Robert II defeat the Flemings at Veurne. During the battle, Robert's son Philip of Artois is gravely wounded and dies a year later of his wounds.

events.title: English expedition to Flanders (1297–1298)
events.blurb: Edward I of England leads an expedition to Flanders. He moves with an army (some 8,000 men) supported by 800 knights to Ghent and makes the city his base of operations in Flanders.

events.title: Battle of Stirling Bridge
events.blurb: Battle of Stirling Bridge: Scottish forces (some 6,000 men) led by Andrew Moray and William Wallace defeat an English army under John de Warenne at Stirling on the Forth.

events.title: November
events.blurb: November – Scottish forces led by William Wallace begin raids in Northumberland and Cumberland. During a ceremony at Selkirk, Wallace is knighted and appointed Guardian of Scotland.

events.title: Englishman Andrew Harclay, 1st Earl of Carlisle, who had recently defeated…
events.blurb: Englishman Andrew Harclay, 1st Earl of Carlisle, who had recently defeated rebel Thomas, 2nd Earl of Lancaster at the Battle of Boroughbridge, commits treason by signing a peace treaty with Scotland's King Robert the Bruce.

events.title: On behalf of the Fraticelli order of Spiritual Franciscans, Italian lawyer…
events.blurb: On behalf of the Fraticelli order of Spiritual Franciscans, Italian lawyer Bonagrazia of Bergamo issues a protest to Pope John XXII of the December 8 papal bull Ad conditorem canonum.

events.title: Vilnius, now the capital of Lithuania is first mentioned as a city, when the…
events.blurb: Vilnius, now the capital of Lithuania is first mentioned as a city, when the second of the Letters of Grand Duke Gediminas of the Duchy of Lithuania are sent to German cities inviting German Jews and other Germans to resettle in the city…

events.title: Norway's regency council takes a stand against Ingeborg Haakonsdater, mother…
events.blurb: Norway's regency council takes a stand against Ingeborg Haakonsdater, mother of and regent for the 7-year-old King Magnus VII. Ingeborg is removed from her position as chief regent on charges of misuse of her power.

events.title: Treaty of Paris
events.blurb: Treaty of Paris: Count Louis I relinquishes Flemish claims over the County of Zeeland. He acknowledges William II the Good as count of Avesnes, Holland, and Zeeland as a state within the Holy Roman Empire.

events.title: Siege of Warangal
events.blurb: Siege of Warangal: Sultan Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq sends an expeditionary army led by his son, Muhammad bin Tughluq, to the Kakatiya capital Warangal – after ruler Prataparudra has refused to make tribute payments.

events.title: Hugh II, the self-styled King of Arborea (on the Italian island of Sardinia,…
events.blurb: Hugh II, the self-styled King of Arborea (on the Italian island of Sardinia, with a capital at Oristano, becomes a vassal of Spain's King James II of Aragon in exchange for maintenance of the dynastic rights over his Judicate,

events.title: Elizabeth of Carinthia marries Peter, Crown Prince of Sicily, co-ruler (with…
events.blurb: Elizabeth of Carinthia marries Peter, Crown Prince of Sicily, co-ruler (with his father Frederick II) of the Kingdom of Sicily.

events.title: Nicolò Pistorino becomes the new Grand Chancellor of the Republic of Venice,…
events.blurb: Nicolò Pistorino becomes the new Grand Chancellor of the Republic of Venice, succeeding Jacopo Bertoldi, who held the office for almost nine years.

events.title: Marie of Luxembourg is formally crowned as Queen consort of France at…
events.blurb: Marie of Luxembourg is formally crowned as Queen consort of France at Sainte-Chapelle after her September 21 marriage to King Charles IV.

events.title: Gediminas, Grand Duke of Lithuania, sends his third, fourth and fifth letters…
events.blurb: Gediminas, Grand Duke of Lithuania, sends his third, fourth and fifth letters to German cities to advocate that residents relocate to his the Duchy of Lithuania.

events.title: King Edward II of England makes a 13-year truce with Scotland at York
events.blurb: King Edward II of England makes a 13-year truce with Scotland at York. Despite the truce, Edward refuses to accept Robert the Bruce as ruler of an independent Scottish kingdom.

events.title: Zhao Xian, who had been the Song dynasty Emperor of China from 1274 to 1276,…
events.blurb: Zhao Xian, who had been the Song dynasty Emperor of China from 1274 to 1276, commits suicide as an alternative to being executed, after being viewed as a threat by the Yuan dynasty Mongol Emperor Yingzong.

events.title: Bertrand du Pouget, French papal legate, commanding a military campaign…
events.blurb: Bertrand du Pouget, French papal legate, commanding a military campaign against the Ghibellines besieges Milan – but abandons the siege when Louis IV of Bavaria, King of the Romans,

events.title: Siege of Villa di Chiesa
events.blurb: Siege of Villa di Chiesa: Aragonese forces under Prince Alfonso IV the Kind begin the siege at Villa di Chiesa. The fortified town is founded by Count Ugolino della Gherardesca, but is now under the control of the Republic of Pisa.

events.title: Treaty of Nöteborg
events.blurb: Treaty of Nöteborg: Sweden signs a peace treaty with the Novgorod Republic, regulating the border (known as Finland today) for the first time.

events.title: Gegeen Khan, the Mongol Emperor Yingzong of China is assassinated in a coup…
events.blurb: Gegeen Khan, the Mongol Emperor Yingzong of China is assassinated in a coup d'etat on orders of Yesün Temür, who becomes the new Emperor

events.title: In southern Burma (now Myanmar), Saw Zein becomes the new monarch of the…
events.blurb: In southern Burma (now Myanmar), Saw Zein becomes the new monarch of the Hanthawaddy kingdom (or Martaban) upon the death of his older brother, Saw O.

events.title: John XXII claims the right to confirm imperial elections and demands that…
events.blurb: John XXII claims the right to confirm imperial elections and demands that Louis IV of Bavarian surrender his claim to be King of the Romans.

events.title: War of Saint-Sardos
events.blurb: Hostilities that will lead to the War of Saint-Sardos between England and France begin when King Charles IV of France has a royal sergeant place a stake claiming to claim the French town of Saint-Sardos,

events.title: Lord Raymond-Bernard, of the Aquitaine town of Montpezat, burns the village of…
events.blurb: Lord Raymond-Bernard, of the Aquitaine town of Montpezat, burns the village of Saint-Sardos to the ground and hangs the French royal sergeant who acted as agent for King Charles IV.

events.title: Flemish Revolt
events.blurb: Flemish Revolt: A uprising in Flanders is caused by both excessive taxation levied by Louis I, and by his pro-French policies. The revolt is led by landowning farmers under Nicolaas Zannekin.

events.title: Pope John XXII issues the papal bull Cum inter nonnullos as an addendum to the…
events.blurb: Pope John XXII issues the papal bull Cum inter nonnullos as an addendum to the December 8 bull Ad conditorem canonum,

events.title: In further retaliation by the King Charles of France against King Edward of…
events.blurb: In further retaliation by the King Charles of France against King Edward of England for the Saint-Sardos incident, Edward's chief advocate in France's parliament, Pons Tournemire, is arrested and imprisoned in the Grand Châtelet.

events.title: Marsilius of Padua writes Defensor pacis ("The Defender of Peace"), a…
events.blurb: Marsilius of Padua writes Defensor pacis ("The Defender of Peace"), a theological treatise arguing against the power of the clergy and in favor of a secular state.

events.title: King Charles IV of France issues an order declaring the Duchy of Aquitaine,…
events.blurb: King Charles IV of France issues an order declaring the Duchy of Aquitaine, French territory ruled by King Edward II of England, forfeited to the crown.

events.title: The Taiding Era begins in China three months after Borjigin Yesün Temür…
events.blurb: The Taiding Era begins in China three months after Borjigin Yesün Temür ascends the throne.

events.title: England's envoy to France, Ralph Basset, and Raymond-Bernard de Montpezat,…
events.blurb: England's envoy to France, Ralph Basset, and Raymond-Bernard de Montpezat, decline to obey an order to appear before King Charles IV of France to answer for the October 16 burning of Saint-Sardos.

events.title: Battle of Lucocisterna
events.blurb: Battle of Lucocisterna: Aragonese forces led by Prince Alfonso defeat a Pisan army, which is disembarked near the area of Capoterra. During the battle, Alfonso loses some 150 knights.

events.title: Hugh IV becomes the new King of Cyprus upon the death of his father, King Henry II
events.blurb: Hugh IV becomes the new King of Cyprus upon the death of his father, King Henry II. Hugh also inherits Henry's nominal title of "King of Jerusalem".

events.title: Boleslaw III, Duke of Wroclaw, declares his Polish duchy to be a vassal of the…
events.blurb: Boleslaw III, Duke of Wroclaw, declares his Polish duchy to be a vassal of the Holy Roman Empire as part of a defense agreement made with Louis IV, King of the Romans.

events.title: France's Consistori del Gay Saber holds its first annual contest to determine…
events.blurb: France's Consistori del Gay Saber holds its first annual contest to determine the best poet in the Kingdom. Arnaut Vidal de Castelnou d'Ari wins the first prize, the violeta d'aur. The contest continues for 160 years, ceasing in 1484.

events.title: King Edward II of England dispatches his envoy, Aymer de Valence, 2nd Earl of…
events.blurb: King Edward II of England dispatches his envoy, Aymer de Valence, 2nd Earl of Pembroke to France in an attempt to negotiate a peaceful end to the Saint-Sardos incident.

events.title: A royal wedding takes place in France as King Charles IV marries his cousin…
events.blurb: A royal wedding takes place in France as King Charles IV marries his cousin Joan of Évreux, the 14-year-old daughter of his uncle, Louis, Count of Évreux.

events.title: Mansa Musa, the extraordinarily-wealthy Emperor of Africa's Mali Empire,…
events.blurb: (26 Rajab 724 AH) Mansa Musa, the extraordinarily-wealthy Emperor of Africa's Mali Empire, arrives in Cairo after three days of camping by the pyramids of Giza,

events.title: Basarab I, ruler of Wallachia (part of modern-day Romania) is designated by…
events.blurb: Basarab I, ruler of Wallachia (part of modern-day Romania) is designated by King Charles I of Hungary (Károly Róbert) as a subject of the Hungarian crown.

events.title: The Blitar Regency is established on the island of Java (part of modern-day…
events.blurb: The Blitar Regency is established on the island of Java (part of modern-day Indonesia) by Java's King Jayanegara of Majapahit.

events.title: The coronation of King Christopher II of Denmark (who has ruled since 1320)…
events.blurb: The coronation of King Christopher II of Denmark (who has ruled since 1320) takes place at Vordingborg, with his son Prince Erik Christoffersen being crowned alongside him as the samkonge, a junior co-monarch.

events.title: In Italy, Pagano della Torre, Patriarch of Aquileia, is defeated in battle at…
events.blurb: In Italy, Pagano della Torre, Patriarch of Aquileia, is defeated in battle at Vaprio d'Agogna in Piedmont in his attempt to reclaim Milan from the Visconti family, and abandons further crusades.

events.title: War of Metz
events.blurb: War of Metz: In Western Europe, the "Four Lords", King John of Bohemia ("the Blind"), his uncle Baldwin, Archbishop of Trier, Count Edward I, Count of Bar and Frederick IV,

events.title: James III of Majorca ("the Unfortunate") becomes the new King of Majorca, a…
events.blurb: James III of Majorca ("the Unfortunate") becomes the new King of Majorca, a set of islands in the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Spain, upon the death of his uncle, King Sancho ("the Peaceful").

events.title: When the body of King Sancho of Majorca arrives in the French city of…
events.blurb: When the body of King Sancho of Majorca arrives in the French city of Perpignan for interment at the Perpignan Cathedral, a mob attacks the funeral procession and steals valuables that had accompanied the corpse.

events.title: After he and his entourage of Muslim pilgrims have stayed in Cairo for three…
events.blurb: (28 Shawwal 724 AH) After he and his entourage of Muslim pilgrims have stayed in Cairo for three months, the Emperor Mansa Musa of Africa's Mali Empire resumes the group's pilgrimage to Mecca

events.title: At Kilkenny in Ireland, Petronilla de Meath, the maidservant of Dame Alice…
events.blurb: At Kilkenny in Ireland, Petronilla de Meath, the maidservant of Dame Alice Kyteler, becomes the first person in the British Isles to be burned at the stake as a witch. Dame Alice had been able to escape before capture.

events.title: In Italy, Marsilio da Carrara becomes the new Lord of Padua upon the death of…
events.blurb: In Italy, Marsilio da Carrara becomes the new Lord of Padua upon the death of his uncle, Jacopo I da Carrara.

events.title: The Shōchū era begins in Japan during the reign of the Emperor Go-Daigo
events.blurb: The Shōchū era begins in Japan during the reign of the Emperor Go-Daigo.

events.title: Treaty of Trausnitz
events.blurb: The Treaty of Trausnitz is signed between the Duchy of Austria and the Kingdom of Bavaria.

events.title: Afonso IV becomes the new King of Portugal upon the death of his father, King…
events.blurb: Afonso IV becomes the new King of Portugal upon the death of his father, King Denis I.

events.title: Sultan Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq is murdered after a 5-year reign at Kara-Manikpur
events.blurb: Sultan Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq is murdered after a 5-year reign at Kara-Manikpur. He is succeeded by his son Muhammad bin Tughluq (Juna Khan) as ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.

events.title: Queen Isabella of England, wife of King Edward II of England and sister of…
events.blurb: Queen Isabella of England, wife of King Edward II of England and sister of King Charles IV of France, departs from England on a mission to Paris to mediate an end to the war between the two kingdoms.

events.title: At the age of 11, Valdemar III becomes the new ruler of the Duchy of Schleswig…
events.blurb: At the age of 11, Valdemar III becomes the new ruler of the Duchy of Schleswig upon the death of his father, Eric II, Duke of Schleswig.

events.title: Elizabeth de Comyn, daughter of the late Guardian of Scotland, John Comyn III…
events.blurb: Elizabeth de Comyn, daughter of the late Guardian of Scotland, John Comyn III of Badenoch,

events.title: The Istrian Demarcation, setting out the boundaries of disputed Italian…
events.blurb: The Istrian Demarcation, setting out the boundaries of disputed Italian territories in the Adriatic Sea peninsula of Istria (part of the modern-day Republic of Croatia),

events.title: Led by Michael of Cesena, the Michaelites, a French branch of the Spiritual…
events.blurb: Led by Michael of Cesena, the Michaelites, a French branch of the Spiritual Franciscans who have been accused of heresy within the Roman Catholic Church in a disagreement over the issue of a vow of poverty,

events.title: At Stuttgart in Germany, Ulrich III becomes the new Count of Württemberg upon…
events.blurb: At Stuttgart in Germany, Ulrich III becomes the new Count of Württemberg upon the death of his father, Eberhard I.

events.title: Ibn Battuta, Moroccan scholar and explorer, sets off from his hometown of…
events.blurb: (2 Rajab 725 AH) Ibn Battuta, Moroccan scholar and explorer, sets off from his hometown of Tangier on a hajj, or pilgrimage, to Mecca. En route, he travels to Tlemcen, Béjaïa and Tunis, where he stays for two months.

events.title: Ismail, Sultan of Granada, begins the siege of Martos in the Spanish Kingdom…
events.blurb: Ismail, Sultan of Granada, begins the siege of Martos in the Spanish Kingdom of Castile, but loses control of his troops, who pillage the city after two weeks.

events.title: Battle of Varey
events.blurb: Battle of Varey: The 16-year-old Guigues VIII, local ruler (dauphin) of Vienne, defeats the Savoyard forces at Saint-Jean-le-Vieux. During the battle, a Burgundian cavalry charge is repulsed and is forced back to the Savoyard camp.

events.title: At Valladolid, Alfonso XI reaches the age of 14 and is proclaimed by the…
events.blurb: At Valladolid, Alfonso XI reaches the age of 14 and is proclaimed by the Cortes to have full power as the King of Castile.

events.title: Edward II is persuaded not to go to France by Hugh Despenser the Elder, his…
events.blurb: Edward II is persuaded not to go to France by Hugh Despenser the Elder, his chief adviser. He decides to send his 12-year-old son, Prince Edward of Windsor, to go to Paris and to pay homage instead.

events.title: Isabella of France conspires with the exiled Roger Mortimer to have Edward II…
events.blurb: Isabella of France conspires with the exiled Roger Mortimer to have Edward II deposed. To build up diplomatic and military support, Isabella has Edward of Windsor engaged to the 12-year-old Philippa of Hainault.

events.title: Edward, Prince of Wales pays homage to King Charles IV of France on behalf of…
events.blurb: Edward, Prince of Wales pays homage to King Charles IV of France on behalf of his father, King Edward II of England.

events.title: King Edward II sends a letter to Pope John XXII (who is in Avignon in France),…
events.blurb: King Edward II sends a letter to Pope John XXII (who is in Avignon in France), expressing deep concern for Queen Isabella's failure to return home from Paris.

events.title: War of the Bucket
events.blurb: War of the Bucket: At the Battle of Zappolino in northern Italy, the 7,000-man Ghibelline forces backed by the Holy Roman Empire defeat the much stronger (32,000-men) Guelph army under sent by Pope John XXII near Bologna.

events.title: Yuri III Danilovich, Grand Duke of Moscow, is assassinated by Dmitry of Tver,…
events.blurb: Yuri III Danilovich, Grand Duke of Moscow, is assassinated by Dmitry of Tver, Grand Duke of Vladimir, nicknamed "the Terrible Eyes".

events.title: Charles, Count of Valois, uncle of King Charles IV of France and heir apparent…
events.blurb: Charles, Count of Valois, uncle of King Charles IV of France and heir apparent to the throne, dies at the age of 55 at Nogent-le-Roi, leaving his son Philip as heir to the throne.

events.title: The foundation of Oriel College (as King's College), the University of…
events.blurb: The foundation of Oriel College (as King's College), the University of Oxford's fifth oldest (still surviving) college, is confirmed by royal charter.

events.title: The Raid on Brandenburg begins as Polish-Lithuanian forces led by Władysław I…
events.blurb: The Raid on Brandenburg begins as Polish-Lithuanian forces led by Władysław I Łokietek, "the elbow-high", King of Poland, and of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Gediminas,

events.title: The foundation of Clare College (as University Hall), the University of…
events.blurb: The foundation of Clare College (as University Hall), the University of Cambridge's second oldest (still surviving) college, by royal charter.

events.title: Frederick the Fair becomes the sole Duke of Austria upon the death of his…
events.blurb: Frederick the Fair becomes the sole Duke of Austria upon the death of his younger brother, Leopold I of the House of Habsburg.

events.title: At Dagnum (a former city in modern-day Albania), a peace treaty is signed…
events.blurb: At Dagnum (a former city in modern-day Albania), a peace treaty is signed between Venetian merchants of Ragusa and King Stefan Dečanski of Serbia.

events.title: Siege of Bursa
events.blurb: Siege of Bursa: Ottoman forces (some 10,000 men) led by Sultan Orhan I capture the Byzantine city of Bursa. Orhan makes Bursa the first official Ottoman capital.

events.title: The Peace of Arques, brokered by King Charles IV of France, ends the Flemish…
events.blurb: The Peace of Arques, brokered by King Charles IV of France, ends the Flemish Revolt, but the treaty is not supported by rebel districts in Flanders.

events.title: Treaty of Novgorod (1326)
events.blurb: The Treaty of Novgorod, a 10-year armistice, ends decades of border skirmishes between Norway and Novgorod in the far-northern region of Finnmark.

events.title: Wartislaw IV, Duke of Pomerania, makes an alliance with Gerhard III, Count of…
events.blurb: Wartislaw IV, Duke of Pomerania, makes an alliance with Gerhard III, Count of Holstein-Rendsburg, who has taken control of Denmark after the overthrow of King Christopher II. Wartislaw becomes ill and dies 18 days later.

events.title: The Scottish Parliament meets at Cambuskenneth and votes to restore…
events.blurb: The Scottish Parliament meets at Cambuskenneth and votes to restore 10-year-old Robert Stewart, grandson of Robert the Bruce, to the line of succession to the throne of Scotland.

events.title: Dmitry, Grand Prince of Tver, is executed for the murder of Grand Duke Yuri of…
events.blurb: Dmitry, Grand Prince of Tver, is executed for the murder of Grand Duke Yuri of Moscow at Sarai on orders of Özbeg Khan, ruler of the Golden Horde that controls much of modern-day Asian Russia.

events.title: Invasion of England
events.blurb: Invasion of England: Isabella of France and her supporters (including Roger Mortimer) land at the River Orwell in Suffolk. Their aim is to remove King Edward II from his throne and place Prince Edward there as the new ruler.

events.title: Siege of Bristol (1326)
events.blurb: Isabella of France begins the Siege of Bristol, which is defended by Hugh Despenser the Elder.

events.title: After eight days, the castle of Bristol is captured by Queen Isabella, and…
events.blurb: After eight days, the castle of Bristol is captured by Queen Isabella, and Hugh Despenser the elder is taken captive. With Bristol secured, Isabella moves her base of operations to Hereford, near the Welsh border.

events.title: King Edward II of England is captured at Neath Abbey in Wales and brought to…
events.blurb: King Edward II of England is captured at Neath Abbey in Wales and brought to England, where he is imprisoned at Kenilworth Castle in Warwickshire.

events.title: In Bavaria, a large fire breaks out in Munich and is not brought under control…
events.blurb: In Bavaria, a large fire breaks out in Munich and is not brought under control for two days. One-third of the buildings in the city are destroyed.

events.title: Richard of Wallingford, English cleric and abbot, describes the construction…
events.blurb: Richard of Wallingford, English cleric and abbot, describes the construction of an astronomical clock in his Tractatus Horologii Astronomici.

events.title: King Charles I of Hungary and King John of Bohemia sign an alliance agreement…
events.blurb: King Charles I of Hungary and King John of Bohemia sign an alliance agreement at Nagyszombat in Bohemia (modern Trnava in the Republic of Slovakia), to proceed against the Austrian Habsburgs who occupy Pressburg (modern Bratislava,

events.title: In Spain, Marinid Prince Uthman ibn Abi al-Ula, who started an uprising the…
events.blurb: In Spain, Marinid Prince Uthman ibn Abi al-Ula, who started an uprising the year before against the Emirate of Granada and its ruler Muhammad IV, arrives at Almería and proceeds to enlist Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Abi Sa'id,

events.title: At Opava (in the modern-day Czech Republic), the Polish Silesian noble Casimir…
events.blurb: At Opava (in the modern-day Czech Republic), the Polish Silesian noble Casimir I, Duke of Cieszyn swears homage to King John of Bohemia, "the Blind". In return, Casimir is granted Oświęcim (Auschwitz) as a fiefdom on February 23.

events.title: Other Silesian nobles follow the example of Casimir of Cieszyn at Opava and…
events.blurb: Other Silesian nobles follow the example of Casimir of Cieszyn at Opava and swear homage to King John of Bohemia, including the Piast nobles Leszek of Racibórz, Siemowit of Bytom and George of Bytom.

events.title: Good Friday
events.blurb: (Good Friday) – Francesco Petrarca, Italian scholar and poet, sees a woman he names Laura (possibly Laura de Noves) in the church of Sainte-Claire d'Avignon, which awakes in him a lasting passion.

events.title: In Milan, Louis IV ("Ludwig the Bavarian"), King of the Romans, becomes the…
events.blurb: In Milan, Louis IV ("Ludwig the Bavarian"), King of the Romans, becomes the first King of Italy since 1313, when Henry VII, Holy Roman Emperor died.

events.title: During a banquet given by Galeazzo I Visconti in Milan, an attempt is…
events.blurb: During a banquet given by Galeazzo I Visconti in Milan, an attempt is apparently made to poison the guest of honor, Louis IV, newly crowned as King of Italy.

events.title: Demasq Kaja, Viceroy of Azerbaijan and of Iraq in the Ilkhanate, the Mongol…
events.blurb: Demasq Kaja, Viceroy of Azerbaijan and of Iraq in the Ilkhanate, the Mongol Empire's area of control in the Middle East, is killed in Soltaniyeh after trying to escape arrest on orders of the Ilkhan, Abu Sa'id Bahadur Khan.

events.title: Less than a year after his arrest, the former King of England, Edward II, is…
events.blurb: Less than a year after his arrest, the former King of England, Edward II, is brutally murdered in Berkeley Castle in Gloucestershire.

events.title: Elizabeth de Burgh, Queen consort of Scotland as the wife of King Robert the…
events.blurb: Elizabeth de Burgh, Queen consort of Scotland as the wife of King Robert the Bruce, is fatally injured when she falls from her horse while traveling with her entourage to Cullen Castle in Banffshire.

events.title: In Barcelona, Prince Alfonso "the Kind" becomes the new King of Aragon upon…
events.blurb: In Barcelona, Prince Alfonso "the Kind" becomes the new King of Aragon upon the death of his father, King Jaime II, and is enthroned as King Alfonso IV.

events.title: Simon Mepeham is elected as England's new Archbishop of Canterbury as the…
events.blurb: Simon Mepeham is elected as England's new Archbishop of Canterbury as the candidate of the Earl of Lancaster, leader of the regency council.

events.title: The late King Edward II of England is buried in the Gloucester Cathedral in…
events.blurb: The late King Edward II of England is buried in the Gloucester Cathedral in Gloucestershire, three months after his death.

events.title: Ala ud-Din Timurtash, the Viceroy for Anatolia within the Ilkhanate of the…
events.blurb: Ala ud-Din Timurtash, the Viceroy for Anatolia within the Ilkhanate of the Middle East, and the brother of Demasq Kaja, learns that the Ilkhan Abu Sa'id had arranged for the execution of Demasq.

events.title: Augustiner-Bräu
events.blurb: Undated – The Augustiner-Bräu is first recorded as the brewery of an Augustinian monastery at Munich.

events.title: Louis IV, "the Bavarian", is crowned Holy Roman Emperor at St
events.blurb: Louis IV, "the Bavarian", is crowned Holy Roman Emperor at St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. Because of conflict with the Avignon Papacy, the ceremony is carried out by a senator and three Italian bishops.

events.title: Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton
events.blurb: Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton: England recognises Scotland as an independent nation, after the Wars of Scottish Independence.

events.title: Antipope Nicholas V is consecrated at St
events.blurb: Antipope Nicholas V is consecrated at St. Peter's Basilica in Rome by the bishop of Venice.

events.title: William of Ockham secretly leaves Avignon, under threat from Pope John XXII
events.blurb: William of Ockham secretly leaves Avignon, under threat from Pope John XXII.

events.title: King Philip VI of France is crowned, founding the House of Valois, after the…
events.blurb: King Philip VI of France is crowned, founding the House of Valois, after the death of King Charles IV of France, who has no sons to inherit.

events.title: Battle of Cassel
events.blurb: Battle of Cassel: French troops stop an uprising of Flemish farmers.

events.title: Wiesbaden is granted the right of coinage by Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor
events.blurb: Wiesbaden is granted the right of coinage by Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor.

events.title: King John of Bohemia (of the Teutonic Order) captures Medvėgalis, an important…
events.blurb: King John of Bohemia (of the Teutonic Order) captures Medvėgalis, an important fortress of the pagan Grand Duchy of Lithuania, and baptizes 6,000 of its defenders.

events.title: Amda Seyon I, Emperor of Ethiopia, begins his campaigns in the southern Muslim…
events.blurb: Amda Seyon I, Emperor of Ethiopia, begins his campaigns in the southern Muslim provinces (possibly in 1332).

events.title: David II becomes King of Scots at age 5
events.blurb: David II becomes King of Scots at age 5; he will rule Scotland for nearly 42 years.

events.title: Battle of Maltepe (Pelekanon)
events.blurb: Battle of Maltepe (Pelekanon): Ottoman Turks defeat the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Treaty of Pavia (1329)
events.blurb: Wittelsbach possessions are divided by the Treaty of Pavia into those of the Bavarian line and those of Palatinate line. Both lines will be reunited in 1777.

events.title: Ivan Alexander becomes the despot of Lovech
events.blurb: Ivan Alexander becomes the despot of Lovech.

events.title: Odoric of Pordenone narrates the story of his 10 years of missionary travel to…
events.blurb: Odoric of Pordenone narrates the story of his 10 years of missionary travel to China, from which he is newly returned, to Friar William of Solagna in Padua, who records it as the Relatio.

events.title: Battle of Velbazhd
events.blurb: Battle of Velbazhd: The Bulgarians under Tsar Michael Shishman (who is mortally wounded) are beaten by the Serbs.

events.title: Battle of Posada
events.blurb: Battle of Posada: The Wallachians, under Basarab I, defeat the Hungarians, though heavily outnumbered, thus making a firm statement towards the independence of Wallachia.

events.title: The British Isles are hit by a great storm, creating large areas of sand dunes…
events.blurb: The British Isles are hit by a great storm, creating large areas of sand dunes on Anglesey.

events.title: Genkō War
events.blurb: The Genkō War begins in Japan.

events.title: The first recorded outbreak of the Black Death occurs, in the Chinese province…
events.blurb: The first recorded outbreak of the Black Death occurs, in the Chinese province of Hebei.

events.title: The Sieges of Cividale del Friuli and Alicante begin
events.blurb: The Sieges of Cividale del Friuli and Alicante begin.

events.title: Stefan Dušan declares himself king of Serbia
events.blurb: Stefan Dušan declares himself king of Serbia.

events.title: Battle of Płowce
events.blurb: Battle of Płowce: The German Teutonic Knights and the Poles battle to a draw.

events.title: Battle of Dupplin Moor
events.blurb: Battle of Dupplin Moor: Edward Balliol rebels, and the English defeat the loyalists of David II in Scotland.

events.title: Lucerne joins the Swiss Confederation with Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden
events.blurb: Lucerne joins the Swiss Confederation with Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden.

events.title: Battle of Annan
events.blurb: Battle of Annan: The loyalists of David II defeat Edward Balliol in Scotland.

events.title: Jan IV of Dražic, Bishop of Prague, founds a friary and builds a stone bridge…
events.blurb: Jan IV of Dražic, Bishop of Prague, founds a friary and builds a stone bridge at Roudnice in Bohemia.

events.title: The Kapellbrücke wooden bridge over the Reuss in Lucerne (Switzerland) is built
events.blurb: The Kapellbrücke wooden bridge over the Reuss in Lucerne (Switzerland) is built; by the 20th century it will be the world's oldest truss bridge and Europe's oldest covered bridge.

events.title: A great famine takes place in Southern Europe
events.blurb: A great famine takes place in Southern Europe. It is known to historians of Catalonia as ', "the First Bad Year" (equivalent to the Great Famine of 1315–1317 further north),

events.title: Chinese famine of 1333–1337
events.blurb: A famine (lasting until 1337) breaks out in China, killing six million.

events.title: Siege of Kamakura in Japan
events.blurb: Siege of Kamakura in Japan: Forces loyal to Emperor Go-Daigo, led by Nitta Yoshisada, enter and destroy the city, breaking the power of the Hōjō clan over the Kamakura shogunate.

events.title: William Donn de Burgh, 3rd Earl of Ulster, is murdered as part of the Burke…
events.blurb: William Donn de Burgh, 3rd Earl of Ulster, is murdered as part of the Burke Civil War in Ireland.

events.title: Ashikaga Takauji leads his army into Kyoto as part of the Kenmu Restoration
events.blurb: Ashikaga Takauji leads his army into Kyoto as part of the Kenmu Restoration.

events.title: The reign of Emperor Kōgon of Japan, first of the Northern Court (Ashikaga)…
events.blurb: The reign of Emperor Kōgon of Japan, first of the Northern Court (Ashikaga) Pretenders, ends.

events.title: Wars of Scottish Independence - Battle of Halidon Hill
events.blurb: Wars of Scottish Independence - Battle of Halidon Hill: Edward III of England decisively defeats Sir Archibald Douglas. Berwick-upon-Tweed returns to English control.

events.title: The River Arno floods, causing massive damage in Florence, as recorded by…
events.blurb: The River Arno floods, causing massive damage in Florence, as recorded by Giovanni Villani.

events.title: Autumn – Battle of Adramyttion
events.blurb: Autumn – Battle of Adramyttion: A Christian league defeats the fleet of the Turkish Beylik of Karasi.

events.title: Pope Benedict XII succeeds Pope John XXII, as the 197th pope
events.blurb: Pope Benedict XII succeeds Pope John XXII, as the 197th pope.

events.title: The School of Arts in Zaragoza, Spain is founded (later known as the…
events.blurb: The School of Arts in Zaragoza, Spain is founded (later known as the University of Zaragoza in the 16th Century).

events.title: Congress of Visegrád
events.blurb: Congress of Visegrád: The monarchs of Bohemia, Hungary, and Poland form an anti-Habsburg alliance.

events.title: Georgians under King George V (the Brilliant) finally defeat the Mongolians in…
events.blurb: Georgians under King George V (the Brilliant) finally defeat the Mongolians in a decisive battle. After that George V returns the Grave of Christ from the Muslims.

events.title: Otto the Merry, Duke of Austria, becomes Duke of Carinthia
events.blurb: Otto the Merry, Duke of Austria, becomes Duke of Carinthia.

events.title: Battle of Boroughmuir
events.blurb: Battle of Boroughmuir: John Randolph, 3rd Earl of Moray defeats Guy, Count of Namur in Scotland.

events.title: Battle of Culblean
events.blurb: Battle of Culblean: David Bruce defeats Edward Balliol in Scotland.

events.title: Abu Sa'id Bahadur Khan dies, a victim of the plague that ravages the Ilkhanate
events.blurb: Abu Sa'id Bahadur Khan dies, a victim of the plague that ravages the Ilkhanate. This is an early outbreak of the Black Death. His death without a clear heir causes the Ilkhanate to disintegrate.

events.title: The Kenmu Restoration ends and the Muromachi period begins in Japan
events.blurb: The Kenmu Restoration ends and the Muromachi period begins in Japan; start of the Nanboku-chō period.

events.title: Vijayanagara Empire
events.blurb: (unconfirmed) – Brothers Harihara and Bukka Raya found the Vijayanagara Empire on the southern part of the Deccan Plateau in South India.

events.title: The governor of Baghdad, Oirat 'Ali Padsah, defeats Arpa Ke'un near Maraga,…
events.blurb: The governor of Baghdad, Oirat 'Ali Padsah, defeats Arpa Ke'un near Maraga, contributing to the disintegration of the Ilkhanate.

events.title: Battle of Minatogawa
events.blurb: Battle of Minatogawa: Ashikaga Takauji defeats Japanese Imperial forces, under Kusunoki Masashige and Nitta Yoshisada.

events.title: Second War of Scottish Independence
events.blurb: Second War of Scottish Independence: Aberdeen, Scotland is burned by the English.

events.title: The reign of Emperor Kōmyō, second of the Ashikaga Pretenders to the Northern…
events.blurb: The reign of Emperor Kōmyō, second of the Ashikaga Pretenders to the Northern Court of Japan, begins.

events.title: The Despotate of Epirus is conquered by the Byzantine Empire
events.blurb: The Despotate of Epirus is conquered by the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Siege of Nicomedia
events.blurb: Siege of Nicomedia: After its foundation by Osman I in about 1299, the Ottoman Empire expanded across Bithynia in north-west Anatolia by capturing territory from the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: The Sofia Psalter is produced in Bulgaria
events.blurb: The Sofia Psalter is produced in Bulgaria.

events.title: Edward the Black Prince establishes the Duchy of Cornwall, becoming the first…
events.blurb: Edward the Black Prince establishes the Duchy of Cornwall, becoming the first English Duke.

events.title: Battle of Cadzand
events.blurb: Battle of Cadzand: English troops raid the Flemish island of Cadzand.

events.title: Hundred Years' War, English Channel naval campaign
events.blurb: Hundred Years' War, English Channel naval campaign: Southampton is destroyed.

events.title: Shams-ud-Din Shah Mir, having defeated Kota Rani, Hindu queen regnant of…
events.blurb: Shams-ud-Din Shah Mir, having defeated Kota Rani, Hindu queen regnant of Kashmir, in battle at Jayapur (modern Sumbal), asks her to marry him, but she commits suicide rather than do so;

events.title: Battle of Laupen
events.blurb: Battle of Laupen: The Canton of Bern defeats the forces of Fribourg.

events.title: Emperor Go-Murakami accedes to the throne of Japan
events.blurb: Emperor Go-Murakami accedes to the throne of Japan.

events.title: Simone Boccanegra
events.blurb: (or 28) – Simone Boccanegra is elected, as the first Doge of Genoa.

events.title: Valdemar IV of Denmark, son of deceased King Christopher II, is elected to the…
events.blurb: Valdemar IV of Denmark, son of deceased King Christopher II, is elected to the throne, following 8 years of interregnum.

events.title: An epidemic in northern Italy is recorded by Augustine of Trent, in his…
events.blurb: An epidemic in northern Italy is recorded by Augustine of Trent, in his Epistola astrologica.

events.title: Europe has about 74 million inhabitants
events.blurb: Europe has about 74 million inhabitants.

events.title: Bohemian Crusade
events.blurb: Bohemian Crusade: The Church authorizes a military expedition against heretics.

events.title: July – Trapezuntine Civil War
events.blurb: July – Trapezuntine Civil War: An abortive uprising occurs against Irene Palaiologina of Trebizond, the first of a number of coups, revolts, and succession disputes.

events.title: Rotterdam is officially declared a city
events.blurb: Rotterdam is officially declared a city.

events.title: Hundred Years' War – Battle of Saint-Omer
events.blurb: Hundred Years' War – Battle of Saint-Omer: The French defeat the English.

events.title: Hundred Years' War
events.blurb: Hundred Years' War: The temporary Truce of Espléchin is signed between England and France.

events.title: Battle of Río Salado in Spain
events.blurb: Battle of Río Salado in Spain: The kings of Castile and Portugal defeat the Nasrid ruler of Granada and his Moroccan allies.

events.title: Saluzzo is sacked by Manfred V of Saluzzo
events.blurb: Saluzzo is sacked by Manfred V of Saluzzo.

events.title: Saint Bridget of Sweden and her husband Ulf Gudmarsson went on pilgrimage to…
events.blurb: Saint Bridget of Sweden and her husband Ulf Gudmarsson went on pilgrimage to Santiago de Compostela.

events.title: Approximate date
events.blurb: Approximate date – Magnus Erikssons landslag (the Country Law of Magnus IV of Sweden) is promulgated.

events.title: The Queen's College, a constituent college of the University of Oxford in…
events.blurb: The Queen's College, a constituent college of the University of Oxford in England, is founded.

events.title: Petrarch is crowned poet laureate in Rome, the first man since antiquity to be…
events.blurb: Petrarch is crowned poet laureate in Rome, the first man since antiquity to be given this honor.

events.title: October
events.blurb: October – The Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347 (between John VI Kantakouzenos and the regency for the infant John V Palaiologos) breaks out.

events.title: The Greek Orthodox patriarch of Antioch is transferred to Damascus, under…
events.blurb: The Greek Orthodox patriarch of Antioch is transferred to Damascus, under Ignatius II.

events.title: Kitzbühel becomes part of Tyrol
events.blurb: Kitzbühel becomes part of Tyrol.

events.title: Pope Clement VI succeeds Pope Benedict XII, as the 198th Pope
events.blurb: Pope Clement VI succeeds Pope Benedict XII, as the 198th Pope.

events.title: Louis I becomes king of Hungary
events.blurb: Louis I becomes king of Hungary.

events.title: Battle of Zava
events.blurb: Battle of Zava: Mu'izz al-Din Husayn defeats the Sarbadars.

events.title: St. Mary Magdalene's flood
events.blurb: St. Mary Magdalene's flood is the worst such event on record for central Europe.

events.title: Louis "the Child", age 4, succeeds his father, Peter II, as king of Sicily and…
events.blurb: Louis "the Child", age 4, succeeds his father, Peter II, as king of Sicily and duke of Athens; he is crowned on September 15 in Palermo Cathedral.

events.title: John III of Trebizond (John III Comnenus) becomes emperor of Trebizond
events.blurb: John III of Trebizond (John III Comnenus) becomes emperor of Trebizond.

events.title: Arnošt of Pardubice becomes the last bishop of Prague and, subsequently, the…
events.blurb: Arnošt of Pardubice becomes the last bishop of Prague and, subsequently, the first Archbishop of Prague.

events.title: A naval league is formed between the Pope, the Republic of Venice, the Knights…
events.blurb: A naval league is formed between the Pope, the Republic of Venice, the Knights Hospitaller and the Kingdom of Cyprus, to prepare the Smyrniote Crusades.

events.title: King Peter IV of Aragon defeats and deposes his cousin, James III of Majorca,…
events.blurb: King Peter IV of Aragon defeats and deposes his cousin, James III of Majorca, thereby absorbing the Balearic Kingdom of Majorca into the Crown of Aragon.

events.title: The Compagnia dei Bardi in Florence goes bankrupt, along with the Peruzzi Bank…
events.blurb: The Compagnia dei Bardi in Florence goes bankrupt, along with the Peruzzi Bank and the Acciaiuoli Bank.

events.title: Bablake School is founded in Coventry, England by the dowager Queen Isabella
events.blurb: Bablake School is founded in Coventry, England by the dowager Queen Isabella.

events.title: A large public dial clock is installed in the tower of the Palazzo…
events.blurb: A large public dial clock is installed in the tower of the Palazzo Capitaniato, Padua, commissioned by Prince Ubertino I da Carrara and supervised by Jacopo Dondi dell'Orologio.

events.title: Newaya Krestos succeeds his father Amda Seyon I as Emperor of Ethiopia
events.blurb: Newaya Krestos succeeds his father Amda Seyon I as Emperor of Ethiopia

events.title: Constantine II, King of Armenia, is killed in an uprising and succeeded by a…
events.blurb: Constantine II, King of Armenia, is killed in an uprising and succeeded by a distant cousin, Constantine III.

events.title: Battle of Pallene
events.blurb: Battle of Pallene: A Christian fleet defeats a Turkish fleet at Pallene, Chalcidice.

events.title: Guy de Chauliac observes the planets Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars conjoined in…
events.blurb: Guy de Chauliac observes the planets Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars conjoined in the sky, under the sign of Aquarius, and a solar eclipse on the same day.

events.title: Battle of Gamenario
events.blurb: Battle of Gamenario: The Lombards defeat the Angevins in the northwest region of present-day Italy, just southeast of Turin.

events.title: Battle of Peritheorion
events.blurb: Battle of Peritheorion: the forces of Momchil, autonomous ruler of the Rhodope, are defeated by the Turkish allies of John VI Kantakouzenos.

events.title: Gascon campaign of 1345 - Battle of Bergerac, Gascony
events.blurb: Gascon campaign of 1345 - Battle of Bergerac, Gascony: English troops are victorious over the French.

events.title: Holland, Hainaut and Zeeland are inherited by Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor,…
events.blurb: Holland, Hainaut and Zeeland are inherited by Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor, and remain part of the imperial crown domain until 1347.

events.title: Andrew, Duke of Calabria, is assassinated in Naples (d
events.blurb: Andrew, Duke of Calabria, is assassinated in Naples (d. in Aversa).

events.title: Battle of Auberoche in Gascony
events.blurb: Battle of Auberoche in Gascony: The English defeat the French.

events.title: The English take La Réole in Gascony
events.blurb: The English take La Réole in Gascony.

events.title: The English take Aiguillon in Gascony
events.blurb: The English take Aiguillon in Gascony.

events.title: The French prepare to defend the channel coasts
events.blurb: The French prepare to defend the channel coasts.

events.title: Siege of Aiguillon
events.blurb: Siege of Aiguillon: The French fail to take Aiguillon from its English defenders.

events.title: The Serbian Empire is proclaimed in Skopje by Dusan Silni, occupying much of…
events.blurb: The Serbian Empire is proclaimed in Skopje by Dusan Silni, occupying much of Southeast Europe.

events.title: June
events.blurb: June – An English invasion fleet assembles at Portsmouth.

events.title: Genoese forces led by Simone Vignoso land on the Mediterranean island of Chios…
events.blurb: Genoese forces led by Simone Vignoso land on the Mediterranean island of Chios and capture it from local Greek control within a week, apart from the Castle of Chios, which resists until 12 September.

events.title: The English win a small victory at La Roche-Derrien in Brittany
events.blurb: The English win a small victory at La Roche-Derrien in Brittany.

events.title: The leaders of Ghent, Bruges and Ypres agree to support Edward III
events.blurb: The leaders of Ghent, Bruges and Ypres agree to support Edward III.

events.title: The English fleet attempts to sail from Portsmouth to Normandy, but is forced…
events.blurb: The English fleet attempts to sail from Portsmouth to Normandy, but is forced back by contrary winds.

events.title: Charles IV, Count of Luxembourg and King of Bohemia, is elected King of the Romans
events.blurb: Charles IV, Count of Luxembourg and King of Bohemia, is elected King of the Romans.

events.title: The English raid and burn neighbouring towns and villages in the Cotentin…
events.blurb: The English raid and burn neighbouring towns and villages in the Cotentin Peninsula.

events.title: Battle of Caen (1346)
events.blurb: Battle of Caen (1346): An English army captures and sacks the French city of Caen.

events.title: Jaume Ferrer sets out from Mallorca for the "River of Gold", the Senegal River
events.blurb: Jaume Ferrer sets out from Mallorca for the "River of Gold", the Senegal River.

events.title: Battle of Blanchetaque
events.blurb: Battle of Blanchetaque: The English defeat the French.

events.title: Battle of Crécy
events.blurb: Battle of Crécy: The English defeat the French, in the first European battle where gunpowder is used.

events.title: The English begin the siege of Calais
events.blurb: The English begin the siege of Calais.

events.title: November
events.blurb: November – Several Mongol towns in the Crimea are cleared of inhabitants by the Black Death.

events.title: Battle of Neville's Cross
events.blurb: Battle of Neville's Cross: The English army defeats the Scots.

events.title: King Phillip of France meets with the Estates General to ask for funds to…
events.blurb: King Phillip of France meets with the Estates General to ask for funds to further the war effort against the English.

events.title: The agreement reorganizing the Byzantine Empire's affairs is finalized, as…
events.blurb: The agreement reorganizing the Byzantine Empire's affairs is finalized, as Anna of Savoy's son John V Palaiologos marries Kantakouzenos' 15-year-old daughter Helena.

events.title: Charles University in Prague is founded by a bull issued by Pope Clement VI,…
events.blurb: Charles University in Prague is founded by a bull issued by Pope Clement VI, at the request of Charles I, King of Bohemia.

events.title: Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347
events.blurb: The Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347 between John VI Kantakouzenos and the regency for John V Palaiologos ends with Kantakouzenos entering Constantinople.

events.title: The Maona of Chios and Phocaea is formed to manage the overseas possessions of…
events.blurb: The Maona of Chios and Phocaea is formed to manage the overseas possessions of the Republic of Genoa.

events.title: Cola di Rienzo, a Roman commoner, declares himself Emperor of Rome, in…
events.blurb: Cola di Rienzo, a Roman commoner, declares himself Emperor of Rome, in response to years of baronial power struggles.

events.title: The Islamic Bahmani Kingdom is established on the Indian subcontinent
events.blurb: The Islamic Bahmani Kingdom is established on the Indian subcontinent.

events.title: The Black Death reaches the French port city of Marseille
events.blurb: The Black Death reaches the French port city of Marseille.

events.title: The Black Death spreads to Aix-en-Provence in France
events.blurb: The Black Death spreads to Aix-en-Provence in France.

events.title: Plague hits the island of Mallorca
events.blurb: Plague hits the island of Mallorca.

events.title: Pembroke College in the University of Cambridge, England, is founded by Marie…
events.blurb: Pembroke College in the University of Cambridge, England, is founded by Marie de St Pol, Countess of Pembroke, as the Hall of Valence Marie.

events.title: By June 24
events.blurb: By June 24 – The Black Death pandemic reaches England, having probably been brought across the English Channel by fleas on rats aboard a ship from Gascony to the south coast port of Melcombe (modern-day Weymouth, Dorset);

events.title: The Pskov Republic gains independence from the Novgorod Republic with the…
events.blurb: The Pskov Republic gains independence from the Novgorod Republic with the treaty of Bolotovo.

events.title: Gonville Hall, the forerunner of Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge,…
events.blurb: Gonville Hall, the forerunner of Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge, England, is founded.

events.title: Battle of Strėva
events.blurb: Battle of Strėva: the Teutonic Order secure a victory over the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. Sources tell of a blow to Lithuanian leadership, one that the Teutonic Order could not fully make use of due to the Black Death.

events.title: Union of Valencia
events.blurb: The anti-royalist Union of Valencia attacks the Jews of Murviedro because they are serfs of the King of Valencia and thus "royalists".

events.title: The Black Death in England spreads to the north and a ship from England…
events.blurb: The Black Death in England spreads to the north and a ship from England carries it to Askøy and Bjørgvin (modern-day Bergen) in Norway. The disease also breaks out in Mecca and is prevalent in the Île-de-France and the Kingdom of Navarre.

events.title: An earthquake affects L'Aquila in southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli…
events.blurb: An earthquake affects L'Aquila in southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), causing severe damage, and leaving 2,000 dead.

events.title: Günther von Schwarzburg is elected Holy Roman Emperor
events.blurb: Günther von Schwarzburg is elected Holy Roman Emperor

events.title: Jewish persecutions during the Black Death
events.blurb: Jewish persecutions during the Black Death: Erfurt massacre – The Jewish community of Erfurt (Germany) is murdered and expelled in a pogrom.

events.title: An earthquake in England strikes Meaux Abbey
events.blurb: An earthquake in England strikes Meaux Abbey.

events.title: The Black Death ceases in Ireland

events.title: The region of Vantaa in Finland is first mentioned (as Helsinge)

events.title: Wiener Neustadt, the last town in Lower Austria to resist Hungary's King…

events.title: Choe Bu (1454-1504), the Korean Commissioner of Registers for the island of…
events.blurb: Choe Bu (1454-1504), the Korean Commissioner of Registers for the island of Cheju, shipwrecks on the south east coast of China in Taizhou, Zhejiang.

events.blurb: Hadım Ali Pasha, the Ottoman beylerbey of Karaman, recaptures Adana and Tarsus from the Mamluks.
