events.blurb: In Morocco, Portugal's fortress at Graciosa falls to the troops of the Moroccan Sultan Muhammad al-Wattasi after a six week siege.

events.title: King Ferdinand I of Naples is excommunicated from the Roman Catholic Church…
events.blurb: King Ferdinand I of Naples is excommunicated from the Roman Catholic Church and declared deposed from office by a bull issued by Pope Innocent VIII.

events.title: The Rorschacher Klosterbruch, a civil war in Switzerland, comes to an end…
events.blurb: The Rorschacher Klosterbruch, a civil war in Switzerland, comes to an end after three months when the Abbey of Saint Gall (in the canton of St. Gallen) signs a peace with the canton of Appenzell.

events.title: Arthur Tudor, heir apparent to the throne of England as the son of King Henry…
events.blurb: Arthur Tudor, heir apparent to the throne of England as the son of King Henry VII, is named Prince of Wales.

events.title: Jeannetto de Tassis is appointed Chief Master of Postal Services in Innsbruck
events.blurb: Jeannetto de Tassis is appointed Chief Master of Postal Services in Innsbruck; his descendants, the Thurn und Taxis Family, later run much of the postal system of Europe.

events.title: Aldus Manutius moves to Venice
events.blurb: Aldus Manutius moves to Venice.

events.title: Battle of Glendale (Skye)
events.blurb: Traditional date of the Battle of Glendale (Skye) between the Scottish clans MacDonald and MacLeod.

events.title: Battle of Chocontá
events.blurb: Battle of Chocontá: The northern (zaque) tribes of the pre-Columbian Muisca Confederation (central Colombia) are beaten by the southern (zipa) tribes.

events.title: All Saints' Church, the Schlosskirche in Wittenberg, is begun
events.blurb: All Saints' Church, the Schlosskirche in Wittenberg, is begun.

events.title: John Colet receives his M
events.blurb: John Colet receives his M.A. from Magdalen College, Oxford.

events.title: Catholic missionaries arrive in the African Kingdom of Kongo
events.blurb: Catholic missionaries arrive in the African Kingdom of Kongo.

events.title: The Scottish Parliament opens in Edinburgh to address matters of lands…
events.blurb: The Scottish Parliament opens in Edinburgh to address matters of lands confiscated in the year before.

events.title: Robert Lyle, 2nd Lord Lyle, is restored by Scotland's King James IV to his…
events.blurb: Robert Lyle, 2nd Lord Lyle, is restored by Scotland's King James IV to his previous title of Scottish nobility that had been forfeited on July 4,

events.title: Carlo Giovanni Amedeo becomes Duke of Savoy at nine months old upon the death…
events.blurb: Carlo Giovanni Amedeo becomes Duke of Savoy at nine months old upon the death of his father, Carlo I di Savoia. his mother, Bianca di Monferrato, serves as regent.

events.title: At Junnar in what is now India's Maharashtra state, the Ahmadnagar Sultanate…
events.blurb: At Junnar in what is now India's Maharashtra state, the Ahmadnagar Sultanate is established by Ahmad Nizam Shah, who leads a secession of his land from the Bahmani Kingdom and defeats the Bahmani General Jahangir Khan.

events.title: English printer William Caxton prints his English language translation of the…
events.blurb: English printer William Caxton prints his English language translation of the French book, Ars moriendi, which he renders as The art and crafte to knowe well to dye.

events.title: John Corvinus, son of the late King Matthias Corvinus of Hungary and a…
events.blurb: John Corvinus, son of the late King Matthias Corvinus of Hungary and a claimant to the throne, is defeated by the Kingdom of Hungary at the Battle of Bonefield.

events.title: John of Kastav finishes a cycle of frescoes in the Holy Trinity Church,…
events.blurb: John of Kastav finishes a cycle of frescoes in the Holy Trinity Church, Hrastovlje (modern-day southwestern Slovenia).

events.title: King Vladislaus of Bohemia is proclaimed as the new King of Hungary by a…
events.blurb: King Vladislaus of Bohemia is proclaimed as the new King of Hungary by a majority of the Hungarian nobility, prompting the Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian to plan an invasion and conquest of the Hungarian Kingddom.

events.title: At Heian-kyō, in Japan, now Kyoto, Ashikaga Yoshitane becomes the 10th…
events.blurb: (5th day of 7th month of Entoku 2) At Heian-kyō, in Japan, now Kyoto, Ashikaga Yoshitane becomes the 10th Muromachi shōgun of Japan, more than a year after the death of his cousin, Ashikaga Yoshihisa.

events.title: The Scottish Admiral Sir Andrew Wood of Largo, commanding the warships Flower…
events.blurb: The Scottish Admiral Sir Andrew Wood of Largo, commanding the warships Flower and Yellow Carrel, successfully repels an attempted ambush by three armed English merchant ships at the Firth of Forth.

events.title: The coronation of Vladislaus II as King of Hungary takes place at Székesfehérvár
events.blurb: The coronation of Vladislaus II as King of Hungary takes place at Székesfehérvár.

events.title: Massacre of Monzievaird
events.blurb: The Massacre of Monzievaird takes place in Scotland at the county Perthshire, with 20 members of Clan Murray being killed when members of Clan Drummond and Clan Campbell set fire to the church where the Murrays have assembled.

events.title: The first edition of the chivalric romance Tirant lo Blanch, by Joanot…
events.blurb: The first edition of the chivalric romance Tirant lo Blanch, by Joanot Martorell, is printed in Valencia.

events.title: In the Russian territory of Komi (the modern-day Komi Republic), annexed by…
events.blurb: In the Russian territory of Komi (the modern-day Komi Republic), annexed by Russia in 1478, copper and silver ores are discovered, and the territory gains importance as a mining and metallurgical center.

events.title: The Bread and Cheese Revolt breaks out in West Frisia, North Holland, caused…
events.blurb: The Bread and Cheese Revolt breaks out in West Frisia, North Holland, caused by a famine among the peasants due to bad weather conditions.

events.title: Jan I Olbracht, son of King Casimir IV or Poland and, like his older brother…
events.blurb: Jan I Olbracht, son of King Casimir IV or Poland and, like his older brother Vladislaus, a claimant to the throne of the Kingdom of Hungary, renounces all of his claims in return for the Duchy of Głogów.

events.title: Having defected to France, Alain I of Albret captures the Château des ducs de…
events.blurb: Having defected to France, Alain I of Albret captures the Château des ducs de Bretagne, the royal palace of Brittany's capital, Nantes, after the Breton regent, the Marshal Jean IV de Rieux, leads the evacuation of Breton officials.

events.title: King Charles VIII makes a triumphant entry to the city of Nantes, facing no…
events.blurb: King Charles VIII makes a triumphant entry to the city of Nantes, facing no resistance and marking the conquest of the Duchy of Brittany by France.

events.title: The city of Granada, capital of the Muslim Emirate of Granada in Spain, is…
events.blurb: The city of Granada, capital of the Muslim Emirate of Granada in Spain, is besieged by the armies of Castile and Aragon, ruled by the Catholic Monarchs of Spain, Ferdinand and Isabella.

events.title: Ottoman–Mamluk War (1485–1491)
events.blurb: The Ottoman–Mamluk War (1485–1491) between the Ottoman Empire and the Egyptian Mamluks ends.

events.title: The ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo, Nkuwu Nzinga, is baptised by Portuguese…
events.blurb: The ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo, Nkuwu Nzinga, is baptised by Portuguese missionaries, adopting the baptismal name of João I.

events.title: A solar eclipse observed in Metz
events.blurb: A solar eclipse observed in Metz.

events.title: King João I of Kongo, who had recently converted to Christianity, completes…
events.blurb: King João I of Kongo, who had recently converted to Christianity, completes the construction of the first Christian church in sub-Saharan Africa, the Cathedral of the Holy Saviour of Congo (Kulumbimbi),

events.title: In what is now Tibet in the People's Republic of China, Tsokye Dorje becomes…
events.blurb: In what is now Tibet in the People's Republic of China, Tsokye Dorje becomes the new ruler of the Buddhist Kingdom of Ü-Tsang upon the death of King Ngagi Wangpo.

events.title: Prince Alfonso, the only legitimate son of King João II of Portugal, and heir…
events.blurb: Prince Alfonso, the only legitimate son of King João II of Portugal, and heir apparent to the throne, is killed in an accident when the horse he is riding falls and crushes him.

events.title: The first Feria de Agosto takes place in the Spanish city of Málaga in…
events.blurb: The first Feria de Agosto takes place in the Spanish city of Málaga in celebration of the 1487 conquest of the Granadan city by the Kingdom of Castile. The festival is still celebrated in Spain more than 500 years later.

events.title: King Charles VIII of France and the Duchess Anne of Brittany conclude a treaty…
events.blurb: King Charles VIII of France and the Duchess Anne of Brittany conclude a treaty at Rennes, leading to the breaking of Anne's engagement to Archduke Maximilian of Austria,

events.title: The English Parliament assembles at Westminster, and Richard Empson is elected…
events.blurb: The English Parliament assembles at Westminster, and Richard Empson is elected as Speaker of the House of Commons.

events.title: King Charles VIII of France convenes the Estates of Brittany in Vannes, to…
events.blurb: King Charles VIII of France convenes the Estates of Brittany in Vannes, to counsel Anne of Brittany of France's conditions for keeping her as Duchess, including the occupation of the Duchy of Brittany by the French army,

events.title: The Truce of Coldstream secures a five-year peace between Scotland and England
events.blurb: The Truce of Coldstream secures a five-year peace between Scotland and England.

events.title: The Black Army of Hungary and its Bohemian Czech allies, commanded by Stephen…
events.blurb: The Black Army of Hungary and its Bohemian Czech allies, commanded by Stephen Zápolya, defeats Duke Jan II Olbracht at the Battle of Presov in what is now Slovakia.

events.title: Russians build the Ivangorod Fortress, on the eastern banks of the Narva River
events.blurb: Russians build the Ivangorod Fortress, on the eastern banks of the Narva River.

events.title: Marsilio Ficino publishes his translation and commentary of Plotinus
events.blurb: Marsilio Ficino publishes his translation and commentary of Plotinus.

events.title: Martin Behaim constructs the first surviving globe of Earth, the Erdapfel
events.blurb: Martin Behaim constructs the first surviving globe of Earth, the Erdapfel. As Columbus would only return from his voyage in 1493, this globe does not show the New World yet.

events.title: Ermysted's Grammar School, Skipton, North Yorkshire, is founded
events.blurb: Ermysted's Grammar School, Skipton, North Yorkshire, is founded.

events.title: Antonio de Nebrija publishes Gramática de la lengua castellana, the first…
events.blurb: Antonio de Nebrija publishes Gramática de la lengua castellana, the first grammar text for the Castilian Spanish language, in Salamanca, which he introduces to the Catholic Monarchs, Isabella I of Castile and Ferdinand II of Aragon,

events.title: The Soncino Bible, which includes the Pentateuch, Song of Songs, Ruth,…
events.blurb: The Soncino Bible, which includes the Pentateuch, Song of Songs, Ruth, Lamentations, Ecclesiastes, and Esther is printed.

events.title: The Titulus Crucis relic is discovered, during the renovation of Santa Croce…
events.blurb: The Titulus Crucis relic is discovered, during the renovation of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme Church in Rome.

events.title: Alhambra Decree
events.blurb: Ferdinand and Isabella sign the Alhambra Decree, expelling all Jews from Spain unless they convert to Roman Catholicism.

events.title: The Capitulations of Santa Fe are signed between Christopher Columbus and the…
events.blurb: The Capitulations of Santa Fe are signed between Christopher Columbus and the Crown of Castile, agreeing on arrangements for his forthcoming voyage.

events.title: In the Canary Islands, the Spanish conquistador Alonso Fernandez de Lugo…
events.blurb: In the Canary Islands, the Spanish conquistador Alonso Fernandez de Lugo finishes the conquest of the island of La Palma by capturing Tanausu, King of the native Guanches.

events.title: At the shipbuilding town of Palos de la Frontera in Spain, an April 30 decree…
events.blurb: At the shipbuilding town of Palos de la Frontera in Spain, an April 30 decree of Queen Isabella of Castile and King Ferdinand of Aragon is read aloud to the residents,

events.title: Pope Innocent VIII and members of the College of Cardinals meet at the church…
events.blurb: Pope Innocent VIII and members of the College of Cardinals meet at the church of Santa Maria del Popolo in Rome with diplomatic envoys sent by the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid II.

events.title: Casimir IV Jagiellon, of the Jagiellon Royal House, dies, ending his reign…
events.blurb: Casimir IV Jagiellon, of the Jagiellon Royal House, dies, ending his reign over Poland and Lithuania.

events.title: Elizabeth Woodville, the last living Yorkist queen consort, dies in England
events.blurb: Elizabeth Woodville, the last living Yorkist queen consort, dies in England.

events.title: Alexander Jagiellon is crowned as Grand Duke of Lithuania
events.blurb: Alexander Jagiellon is crowned as Grand Duke of Lithuania.

events.title: The Jews are expelled from Spain on the Tisha B'Av fast day, pursuant to the…
events.blurb: The Jews are expelled from Spain on the Tisha B'Av fast day, pursuant to the Alhambra Decree. More than 40,000 and perhaps as many as 200,000 leave.

events.title: The Genoese navigator Christopher Columbus sails with three ships (Niña, Pinta…
events.blurb: The Genoese navigator Christopher Columbus sails with three ships (Niña, Pinta and Santa María) from Palos de la Frontera, in the service of the Crown of Castile, on his first voyage across the Atlantic Ocean, intending to reach Asia.

events.title: The papal conclave, the first to be held in the Sistine Chapel, begins…
events.blurb: The papal conclave, the first to be held in the Sistine Chapel, begins balloting with 23 of the 27 members of the College of Cardinals in attendance.

events.title: The English army besieges Boulogne
events.blurb: The English army besieges Boulogne.

events.title: Believing he has reached the East Indies, Christopher Columbus and his…
events.blurb: Believing he has reached the East Indies, Christopher Columbus and his expedition of three ships make landfall in the Caribbean and land on the island of Guanahani, now part of the Bahamas. He names the island "San Salvador".

events.title: Christopher Columbus lands in what is now the Holguín Province of the island…
events.blurb: Christopher Columbus lands in what is now the Holguín Province of the island of Cuba.

events.title: Peace of Étaples
events.blurb: The Peace of Étaples is signed between England and France, ending French support for Perkin Warbeck, the pretender to the English throne. All English-held territory in France (with the exception of Calais) is returned to France.

events.title: In what is now the West African nation of Mali, Sonni Baru becomes the new…
events.blurb: In what is now the West African nation of Mali, Sonni Baru becomes the new monarch of the Songhai Empire following death of his father, the Emperor Sonni Ali.

events.title: Christopher Columbus becomes the first European to set foot on the island of…
events.blurb: Christopher Columbus becomes the first European to set foot on the island of Hispaniola in present day northwestern Haiti.

events.title: Columbus' ship Santa María runs aground off Cap-Haïtien in present day Haiti,…
events.blurb: Columbus' ship Santa María runs aground off Cap-Haïtien in present day Haiti, and is abandoned. The local chief, Guacanagaríx, allows 39 men of Columbus' crew to remain on the island after his departure.

events.title: Huayna Capac becomes emperor of the Inca Empire
events.blurb: Huayna Capac becomes emperor of the Inca Empire.

events.title: Columbus's letter on the first voyage
events.blurb: Columbus begins writing his first account of his voyage to the New World, titled "Letter of Columbus, on the islands of India beyond the Ganges recently discovered", an account later printed and sold throughout Europe.

events.title: Martín Alonso Pinzón returns in the Pinta to the city of Bayona in Spain from…
events.blurb: Martín Alonso Pinzón returns in the Pinta to the city of Bayona in Spain from Christopher Columbus's voyage of discovery, sending the first notice about the discovery to the Catholic Monarchs.

events.title: Battle of Anfao
events.blurb: Battle of Anfao: Askia Mohammad I defeats Sonni Baru in what becomes the African nation of Mali, and usurps the throne of the Songhai Empire.

events.title: Treaty of Senlis
events.blurb: The Treaty of Senlis is signed in France at the city of Senlis (in the modern Oise département) between King Charles VIII of France and Maximilian I, King of the Romans,

events.title: In the most well-documented surgical procedures in the 15th century, the left…
events.blurb: In the most well-documented surgical procedures in the 15th century, the left leg of the Holy Roman Emperor Frederick III is amputated. The surgery is performed at the Linz castle under the direction of the surgeon Hans Seyff.

events.title: Friar Bernardo Buil, a Catalan monk in Spain, is appointed by Pope Alexander…
events.blurb: Friar Bernardo Buil, a Catalan monk in Spain, is appointed by Pope Alexander VI as the first Christian "Vicar Apostolic of the New World".

events.title: The Nuremberg Chronicle, written in Latin by Hartmann Schedel as Liber…
events.blurb: The Nuremberg Chronicle, written in Latin by Hartmann Schedel as Liber Chronicarum and described as "a history of the world from the Creation to the year 1493", with woodcut illustrations by Michael Wohlgemut and Wilhelm Pleydenwurff,

events.title: Battle of Krbava Field
events.blurb: At the Battle of Krbava Field in southern Croatia, forces of the Ottoman Empire defeat those of the Kingdom of Croatia.

events.title: Christopher Columbus lands on the coast of the island of Borinquen, which he…
events.blurb: Christopher Columbus lands on the coast of the island of Borinquen, which he renames San Juan (modern-day Puerto Rico).

events.title: The first Roman Catholic Mass in the New World is celebrated, with Friar Juan…
events.blurb: The first Roman Catholic Mass in the New World is celebrated, with Friar Juan Pérez of the Order of Friars Minor conducting the services at Point Concepcion on the island of Hispaniola.

events.title: In a battle fought at the village of Igris (now part of western Romania) in…
events.blurb: In a battle fought at the village of Igris (now part of western Romania) in territory claimed by Hungary and the Ottoman state of Wallachia,

events.title: The Cetinje Octoechos (Цетињски октоих, an Eastern Orthodox octoechos…
events.blurb: The Cetinje Octoechos (Цетињски октоих, an Eastern Orthodox octoechos (liturgy), first tone), the first incunabulum written in the Serbian recension of Church Slavonic, and the first book printed in Cyrillic in Southeast Europe,

events.title: Alfonso II becomes King of Naples
events.blurb: Alfonso II becomes King of Naples.

events.title: Lithuanian–Muscovite War (1487–1494)
events.blurb: The war between the Grand Duchy of Moscow and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania ends after almost seven years, with the Tsar Ivan III signing a "treaty of Eternal Peace" with Lithuania's Grand Duke Alexander Jagiellon.

events.title: An earthquake estimated centuries later at 5
events.blurb: An earthquake estimated centuries later at 5.5 magnitude, strikes the Chinese city of Qujing, destroying 200 homes.

events.title: The infant Amda Seyon II succeeds his father Eskender as Emperor of Ethiopia
events.blurb: The infant Amda Seyon II succeeds his father Eskender as Emperor of Ethiopia.

events.title: First Battle of Acentejo
events.blurb: First Battle of Acentejo: Natives of the island of Tenerife, known as Guanches, defeat the invading Spanish forces.

events.title: Treaty of Tordesillas
events.blurb: Treaty of Tordesillas: Spain and Portugal divide the New World between themselves.

events.title: Jan V Zatorski, ruler of the Duchy of Zator, sells the Duchy to King Jan I…
events.blurb: Jan V Zatorski, ruler of the Duchy of Zator, sells the Duchy to King Jan I Olbracht of Poland for 80,000 florins, on condition that he retains his title and the right to continue to live in his castle for the rest of his life.

events.title: Battle of Rapallo
events.blurb: The three day Battle of Rapallo, fought as part of the Italian War of 1494–1495 between the Kingdom of France and the Kingdom of Naples, is won by the French naval fleet, which then captures and loots Rapallo, near Genoa,

events.title: King Charles VIII of France and Ludovico Sforza, regent for the Duke of Milan,…
events.blurb: King Charles VIII of France and Ludovico Sforza, regent for the Duke of Milan, meet in Asti and conclude an alliance against King Alfonso II of Naples.

events.title: The British administrator assigned to Ireland, Sir Edward Poynings, arrives at…
events.blurb: The British administrator assigned to Ireland, Sir Edward Poynings, arrives at Ireland with about 1,000 men and lands at Howth.

events.title: France and Milan, with at least 14,000 troops, capture the town of Mordano,…
events.blurb: France and Milan, with at least 14,000 troops, capture the town of Mordano, part of the Lordship of Imola, an ally of Naples.

events.title: Ludovico Sforza becomes Duke of Milan upon the death of his nephew, the Duke…
events.blurb: Ludovico Sforza becomes Duke of Milan upon the death of his nephew, the Duke Gian Galeazzo Sforza, and invites Charles VIII of France to invade Italy in support of his claim, beginning the First Italian War in the Italian Wars.

events.title: Facing little opposition in his march across Italy, King Charles VIII of…
events.blurb: Facing little opposition in his march across Italy, King Charles VIII of France captures Pisa.

events.title: The Medici Bank becomes insolvent and the House of Medici is expelled from…
events.blurb: The Medici Bank becomes insolvent and the House of Medici is expelled from Florence.

events.title: Fra Luca Pacioli's Summa de arithmetica, geometria, proportioni et…
events.blurb: Fra Luca Pacioli's Summa de arithmetica, geometria, proportioni et proportionalità is published in Venice, containing the first printed account of algebra in the vernacular,

events.title: The Irish Parliament opens at Drogheda on the first Monday after Saint…
events.blurb: The Irish Parliament opens at Drogheda on the first Monday after Saint Andrew's Day as summoned by Sir Edward Poynings, to pass the two "Poynings' Laws" restricting Irish self-government.

events.title: Second Battle of Acentejo
events.blurb: Second Battle of Acentejo: The Spanish crush the native forces of the island of Tenerife, leading to the subjugation of this last bastion of resistance in the Canary Islands.

events.title: Piero Pacini da Pescia publishes Epistles, Gospels, and Popular Readings in…
events.blurb: Piero Pacini da Pescia publishes Epistles, Gospels, and Popular Readings in the Tuscan Language

events.title: Poynings' Law comes into effect, placing the Parliament of Ireland under the…
events.blurb: Poynings' Law comes into effect, placing the Parliament of Ireland under the authority of the Parliament of England.

events.title: The Reichskammergericht of the Holy Roman Empire is founded in Frankfurt
events.blurb: The Reichskammergericht of the Holy Roman Empire is founded in Frankfurt.

events.title: Prince Cem Sultan, brother of the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid II, imprisoned since…
events.blurb: Prince Cem Sultan, brother of the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid II, imprisoned since 1482 after being captured by the Knights Hospitaller, and held captive in Rome since 1489,

events.title: King's College, Aberdeen, predecessor of the University of Aberdeen in…
events.blurb: King's College, Aberdeen, predecessor of the University of Aberdeen in Scotland, is founded with the issuance of the papal bull Primo Erectio Universitatis by Pope Alexander VI on the petition of William Elphinstone, Bishop of Aberdeen.

events.title: The first military combat between the Old World and the New World takes place…
events.blurb: The first military combat between the Old World and the New World takes place at the Battle of Vega Real.

events.title: The inaugural session of the Diet of Worms (Wormser Reichstag), a gathering of…
events.blurb: The inaugural session of the Diet of Worms (Wormser Reichstag), a gathering of the electors and princes of the Holy Roman Empire to discuss reforms of the government, is opened at Worms, Germany, by Maximilian I,

events.title: Vaishakha
events.blurb: (10th waxing of Vaishakha 857 ME The two-day coronation of King Binnya Ran II as ruler of the Hanthawaddy kingdom, in what is now southern Myanmar, begins at the Shwemawdaw Pagoda at the capital, Pegu (now Bago in Myanmar).

events.title: Battle of Rapallo (1495)
events.blurb: At the Battle of Rapallo, 11 ships of the Republic of Genoa Navy commanded by Francesco Spinola and Fabrizio Giustiniani, defeat a French 11-ship force led by Louis de Miolans,

events.title: A Spanish army under Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba lands in Calabria, with the…
events.blurb: A Spanish army under Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba lands in Calabria, with the purpose of ousting the French and restoring Ferdinand II of Naples to the throne.

events.title: Gribshunden, the flagship of King Hans Oldenburg of Denmark sinks off the…
events.blurb: Gribshunden, the flagship of King Hans Oldenburg of Denmark sinks off the coast of Ronneby in Sweden while King Hans is ashore to negotiate with Sten Sture the Elder to restore the power of the Kalmar Union.

events.title: Brother John Cor of Lindores Abbey pays duty on 8 bolls of malt to the…
events.blurb: Brother John Cor of Lindores Abbey pays duty on 8 bolls of malt to the Exchequer in Scotland to make aqua vitae for King James IV; the record in the Exchequer Rolls is the first written reference to Scotch whisky.

events.title: Battle of Seminara
events.blurb: Battle of Seminara: The deposed King Ferdinand II of Naples and the reigning Spanish King Ferdinand II of Aragon, with forces commanded by Gonzalo Fernandez, are defeated by a French army commanded by Bernard Stewart, Lord of Aubigny.

events.title: Battle of Deal
events.blurb: At the Battle of Deal, Perkin Warbeck's troops land in Kent, in support of his claim to the English crown, backed by Margaret of York, Duchess of Burgundy.

events.title: Battle of Fornovo
events.blurb: Winning the Battle of Fornovo, the French army under King Charles secures its retreat from Italy, by defeating a combined Milanese-Venetian force of the League of Venice, commanded by [[Francesco II Gonzaga, Marquis of Mantua|

events.title: After failing at the Battle of Deal, Perkin Warbeck and his troops land with…
events.blurb: After failing at the Battle of Deal, Perkin Warbeck and his troops land with 11 ships at the Ireland port of Waterford to gain a foothold in his attempt to invade England.

events.title: Siege of Waterford (1495)
events.blurb: After the sinking of two of his ships, Perkin Warbeck ends this siege of Waterford and retreats from Ireland along with his remaining fleet and warriors.

events.title: The Diet of Worms is adjourned in the Holy Roman Empire after more than four…
events.blurb: The Diet of Worms is adjourned in the Holy Roman Empire after more than four months, with an agreement among the constituent states to enact the Ewiger Landfriede (Eternal Peace),

events.title: The League of Venice, with troops commanded by Beatrice d'Este, Duchess of…
events.blurb: The League of Venice, with troops commanded by Beatrice d'Este, Duchess of Milan and Ludovico Sforza, Duke of Milan, succeeeds after more than three months in liberating the Milanese city of Novara from French control,

events.title: Manuel, Duke of Beja and Visieu takes the throne of Portugal as King Manuel I,…
events.blurb: Manuel, Duke of Beja and Visieu takes the throne of Portugal as King Manuel I, following the death of his cousin, King João II.

events.title: An explosion at Vyborg Castle deters the Russian forces, who have invaded…
events.blurb: An explosion at Vyborg Castle deters the Russian forces, who have invaded Sweden through Karelia.

events.title: Pietro Bembo's Petri Bembi de Aetna Angelum Chalabrilem liber, a description…
events.blurb: Pietro Bembo's Petri Bembi de Aetna Angelum Chalabrilem liber, a description of a journey to Mount Etna, is published in Venice by Aldus Manutius,

events.title: Henry VII of England issues letters patent to Italian-born adventurer John…
events.blurb: Henry VII of England issues letters patent to Italian-born adventurer John Cabot and his sons, authorizing them to discover unknown lands.

events.title: In the Marquisate of Mantua on the Italian peninsula, Francesco II Gonzaga,…
events.blurb: In the Marquisate of Mantua on the Italian peninsula, Francesco II Gonzaga, Marquis of Mantua decrees that all Jews in Mantua are to wear a yellow badge to distinguish themselves from the Christian residents of Mantua.

events.title: Jesus College, Cambridge, is founded
events.blurb: Jesus College, Cambridge, is founded.

events.title: Bartholomew Columbus, brother of Christopher Columbus, formally founds the…
events.blurb: Bartholomew Columbus, brother of Christopher Columbus, formally founds the city of Santo Domingo (first settled in March) on Hispaniola (in the modern-day Dominican Republic),

events.title: Federico of Aragon becomes the King of Naples upon the death of his nephew,…
events.blurb: Federico of Aragon becomes the King of Naples upon the death of his nephew, King Ferdinando II.

events.title: Joanna of Castile, second daughter of Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of…
events.blurb: Joanna of Castile, second daughter of Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile, heiress to Castile, marries the archduke Philip, heir through his mother to the Burgundian Netherlands, and through his father to the Holy Roman Empire.

events.title: Led by Prince Prataparudra Deva, son of the Emperor Purushottama Deva, the…
events.blurb: Led by Prince Prataparudra Deva, son of the Emperor Purushottama Deva, the Gajapati Empire (now India's state of Odisha) invades the Vijayanagara Empire (now the Karnataka state) and its armies advance as far as the Penna River,

events.title: King Manuel I of Portugal issues a decree ordering the expulsion of "heretics"…
events.blurb: King Manuel I of Portugal issues a decree ordering the expulsion of "heretics" from the country.

events.title: Philibert II of Savoy (Filiberto II) becomes the new Duke of Savoy upon the…
events.blurb: Philibert II of Savoy (Filiberto II) becomes the new Duke of Savoy upon the death of his father, Philip II (Filippo II), who had reigned for only 19 months.

events.title: The Ottomans give Russian merchants freedom of trade within the empire
events.blurb: The Ottomans give Russian merchants freedom of trade within the empire.

events.title: Iamblichus' De mysteriis Aegyptorum edited by Marsilio Ficino is published
events.blurb: Iamblichus' De mysteriis Aegyptorum edited by Marsilio Ficino is published.

events.title: Benefit of Clergy Act 1496
events.blurb: Benefit of Clergy Act 1496, requiring that charges against a church official for treason must be tried in a government court of law.

events.title: Weights and Measures Act 1496, standardizing units of weight and of volume…
events.blurb: Weights and Measures Act 1496, standardizing units of weight and of volume throughout England. Specifically, the smallest unit, the "sterling" is set at the weight of 32 corns of wheat, 20 sterlings are an ounce, 12 ounces are a pound.

events.title: At Westminster, King Henry VII opens his sixth English Parliament for a…
events.blurb: At Westminster, King Henry VII opens his sixth English Parliament for a two-month session. The House of Commons elects Sir Thomas Englefield as its speaker.

events.title: Russo-Swedish War (1495–1497)
events.blurb: The Russo-Swedish War (1495–1497) ends with a six year truce signed in Russia at Novgorod. Due to gathering unrest at home, the Swedish leader Sten Sture the Elder is forced to offer a peace to Ivan III of Moscow.

events.title: Persecution of Jews and Muslims by Manuel I of Portugal
events.blurb: Persecution of Jews and Muslims by Manuel I of Portugal: Forced conversion of Jews in Portugal begins.

events.title: Captain Andrea Loredan of the Republic of Venice departs southward on the…
events.blurb: Captain Andrea Loredan of the Republic of Venice departs southward on the Adriatic Sea on a large, heavily-armed warship with a crew of 450, with a mission of locating the Spanish Navarrese pirate Pedro Navarro.

events.title: Amerigo Vespucci allegedly leaves Cádiz, for his first voyage to the New World
events.blurb: Amerigo Vespucci allegedly leaves Cádiz, for his first voyage to the New World. The account of a voyage (lasting until October 15, 1498) is doubted because the only mention of it is in a letter written six years later,

events.title: At what is supposed to be a meeting at Nysa about a united front by the…
events.blurb: At what is supposed to be a meeting at Nysa about a united front by the nobility of Poland against the Ottoman Empire, Nicholas II of Niemodlin (Mikołaj II Niemodlińsk),

events.title: Vasco da Gama's fleet departs from Lisbon, beginning his expedition to India
events.blurb: Vasco da Gama's fleet departs from Lisbon, beginning his expedition to India.

events.title: Battle of Rotebro
events.blurb: At the Battle of Rotebro, Hans, King of Denmark, defeats Sten Sture the Elder.

events.title: Sten Sture the Elder agrees to recognize Hans, King of Denmark and of Norway…
events.blurb: Sten Sture the Elder agrees to recognize Hans, King of Denmark and of Norway as the rightful King of Sweden and ends his 27-year term as the Swedish Regent.

events.title: Kalmar Union
events.blurb: The nobles of Sweden's estates formally elect King Hans of Denmark and Norway as King of Sweden, restoring the power of the Kalmar Union.

events.title: The Vasco da Gama expedition discovers the first sea route from Europe to…
events.blurb: The Vasco da Gama expedition discovers the first sea route from Europe to India as he and his crew, on four ships, round the Cape of Good Hope.

events.title: The coronation of Hans of Denmark as King of Sweden takes place at Stockholm,…
events.blurb: The coronation of Hans of Denmark as King of Sweden takes place at Stockholm, as he adopts the regnal name of King Johann II of Sweden.

events.title: The Vasco da Gama expedition travels past the Great Fish River on South…
events.blurb: The Vasco da Gama expedition travels past the Great Fish River on South Africa's Eastern Cape and sails into previously unexplored waters in the Indian Ocean.

events.title: During the summer, the final Welsh revolt of the medieval era breaks out in…
events.blurb: During the summer, the final Welsh revolt of the medieval era breaks out in Meirionnydd, North Wales; Harlech Castle is captured by the rebels before the revolt is suppressed.

events.title: João Fernandes Lavrador and Pedro de Barcelos journey to Greenland
events.blurb: João Fernandes Lavrador and Pedro de Barcelos journey to Greenland; during their voyage, they discover the land which they name Labrador.

events.title: Gun barrel rifling is invented in Augsburg, Bavaria
events.blurb: Gun barrel rifling is invented in Augsburg, Bavaria.

events.title: Leonardo da Vinci completes his painting The Last Supper, on the refectory…
events.blurb: Leonardo da Vinci completes his painting The Last Supper, on the refectory wall of Milan's Santa Maria delle Grazie Convent.

events.title: In Friesland, in the Netherlands, during the ongoing civil war between the…
events.blurb: In Friesland, in the Netherlands, during the ongoing civil war between the Vetkopers and Schieringers, the Schieringers seek out the help of Albrecht III, Duke of Saxony at the cost of losing Frisian independence.

events.title: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama reaches Malindi, in modern-day Kenya
events.blurb: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama reaches Malindi, in modern-day Kenya.

events.title: In England, the members of the Company of Merchant Adventurers of London are…
events.blurb: In England, the members of the Company of Merchant Adventurers of London are granted a trade monopoly with the Netherlands by King Henry VII "in return for the payment of £5,000" to the royal coffers.

events.title: Girolamo Savonarola, ruler of Florence, is executed for criticizing the Pope
events.blurb: Girolamo Savonarola, ruler of Florence, is executed for criticizing the Pope.

events.title: The formal coronation of King Louis XII in France takes place at the Reims…
events.blurb: The formal coronation of King Louis XII in France takes place at the Reims Cathedral.

events.title: Niccolò Machiavelli, who will later be the author of the influential political…
events.blurb: Niccolò Machiavelli, who will later be the author of the influential political theory guide The Prince, is elected by the Great Council of Florence as the Secretary of the Second Chancellery of the Republic of Florence.

events.title: The Wiener Hofmusikkapelle, a forerunner of the Vienna Boys' Choir, is founded…
events.blurb: The Wiener Hofmusikkapelle, a forerunner of the Vienna Boys' Choir, is founded by order of Maximilian I, Holy Roman Emperor, instructing officials of the imperial court at Vienna to employ a vocal teacher (singing master),

events.title: Columbus becomes the first European to visit the island of Trinidad
events.blurb: Columbus becomes the first European to visit the island of Trinidad.

events.title: Columbus discovers the mouth of the Orinoco at what is now Venezuela on the…
events.blurb: Columbus discovers the mouth of the Orinoco at what is now Venezuela on the continent of South America, but does not enter.

events.title: Columbus begins eight days of exploring the Gulf of Paria between Trinidad and…
events.blurb: Columbus begins eight days of exploring the Gulf of Paria between Trinidad and Venezuela.

events.title: Columbus lands on the Paria Peninsula, in what is now Venezuela in the first…
events.blurb: Columbus lands on the Paria Peninsula, in what is now Venezuela in the first definitely recorded landing of Europeans on the mainland Americas.

events.title: A massive earthquake, estimated centuries later as having been 8
events.blurb: (Meiō 7, 2nd day of the 7th month) A massive earthquake, estimated centuries later as having been 8.6 magnitude occurs off of the coast of the Japanese region of Nankaidō at about 8:00 in the morning.

events.title: In the Chinese Empire, two days after being blamed by the Emperor Zhu Youcheng…
events.blurb: In the Chinese Empire, two days after being blamed by the Emperor Zhu Youcheng for bringing misfortunes to the Empire by having built a pavilion in the imperial gardens that disregarded feng shui principles,

events.title: An-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qaitbay, Sultan of Egypt and Syria, is assassinated, and…
events.blurb: An-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qaitbay, Sultan of Egypt and Syria, is assassinated, and is succeeded by his uncle, the Vizier Abu Sa'id Qansuh.

events.title: In the Kingdom of the Catholic Monarchs of Spain, Diego de Deza, Bishop of…
events.blurb: In the Kingdom of the Catholic Monarchs of Spain, Diego de Deza, Bishop of Jaén, is commissioned as the Grand Inquisitor for the Crown of Castile, the Kingdom of León, and for Granada.

events.title: Giggleswick School is founded by Reverend James Carr in England
events.blurb: Giggleswick School is founded by Reverend James Carr in England.

events.title: Johannes Trithemius inadvertently reveals interests in magic by writing a…
events.blurb: Johannes Trithemius inadvertently reveals interests in magic by writing a letter to a Carmelite friar about a treatise he is writing on steganography.

events.title: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa matriculates at Cologne University
events.blurb: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa matriculates at Cologne University.

events.title: Zeta, the last free monarchy in Southeastern Europe, is annexed by the Ottoman…
events.blurb: Zeta, the last free monarchy in Southeastern Europe, is annexed by the Ottoman Empire, as part of the sanjak of Shkodër, and Stefan II Crnojević is removed from office.

events.title: Hans, King of Denmark is formally crowned as King of Sweden and his wife…
events.blurb: Hans, King of Denmark is formally crowned as King of Sweden and his wife Christina of Saxony crowned as Queen Consort.

events.title: Treaty of Blois (1499)
events.blurb: The Treaty of Blois is signed between the Kingdom of France and the Republic of Venice as a secret military alliance between the two nations to attack the Duchy of Milan.

events.title: Battle of Hard
events.blurb: The Battle of Hard is fought near the village of Hard in modern-day western Austria as the Swiss Confederacy defeats the troops of the Holy Roman Empire in the first large-scale confrontation of the Swabian War.

events.title: Battle of Bruderholz
events.blurb: At the Battle of Bruderholz, the Swiss Confederation defeats a larger force of troops from the Swabian League near Basel.

events.title: Battle of Schwaderloh
events.blurb: The Battle of Schwaderloh is won by the Swiss Confederacy over the Swabian League with more than 1,400 of the Swabian troops killed.

events.title: Battle of Frastanz
events.blurb: The Swiss Confederacy defeats the forces of the Holy Roman Empire in the Battle of Frastanz, with more than 2,000 Imperial troops killed.

events.title: The University of Valencia is founded in Spain with the passage of the…
events.blurb: The University of Valencia is founded in Spain with the passage of the University Statutes by the magistrates of Valencia.{{Cite book|first=Abelardo|last=Palanca|title = La Universidad de Valencia en el primer decenio del siglo…

events.title: Catherine of Aragon, the future first wife of Henry VIII, is married by proxy…
events.blurb: Catherine of Aragon, the future first wife of Henry VIII, is married by proxy to his brother, Arthur, Prince of Wales.

events.title: Pedro Alonso Niño, who had accompanied Columbus on his first voyage to the New…
events.blurb: Pedro Alonso Niño, who had accompanied Columbus on his first voyage to the New World in 1492, departs from Palos in Spain toward South America on a 7-month voyage to the New World. Niño sets sail in a small caravel with 33 men

events.title: Battle of Dornach
events.blurb: Battle of Dornach: The Swiss decisively defeat the army of Maximilian I, Holy Roman Emperor.

events.title: Polydore Vergil completes De inventoribus rerum, the first modern history of…
events.blurb: Polydore Vergil completes De inventoribus rerum, the first modern history of inventions.

events.title: Lake Maracaibo is discovered, by Alonso de Ojeda and Amerigo Vespucci
events.blurb: Lake Maracaibo is discovered, by Alonso de Ojeda and Amerigo Vespucci.

events.title: Treaty of Basel
events.blurb: Treaty of Basel: Maximilian is forced to grant the Swiss de facto independence.

events.title: The Pont Notre-Dame in Paris, constructed under Charles VI of France,…
events.blurb: The Pont Notre-Dame in Paris, constructed under Charles VI of France, collapses into the Seine.

events.title: The Catholicon is published in Tréguier (Brittany)
events.blurb: The Catholicon is published in Tréguier (Brittany). This Breton–greek–Latin dictionary had been written in 1464 by Jehan Lagadeuc. It is the first dictionary of either French or Breton.

events.title: Perkin Warbeck, pretender to the throne of England, is hanged for reportedly…
events.blurb: Perkin Warbeck, pretender to the throne of England, is hanged for reportedly attempting to escape from the Tower of London.

events.title: Rebellion of the Alpujarras (1499–1501)
events.blurb: The Rebellion of the Alpujarras (1499–1501) begins in the Kingdom of Granada (Crown of Castile) against the forced conversions of Muslims in Spain.

events.title: Europe's population is estimated at 56
events.blurb: Europe's population is estimated at 56.7 million people. The world's population is estimated to be between 425 million and 540 million.

events.title: Spanish navigator Vicente Yáñez Pinzón reaches the northern coast of Brazil
events.blurb: Spanish navigator Vicente Yáñez Pinzón reaches the northern coast of Brazil.

events.title: Battle of Hemmingstedt
events.blurb: Battle of Hemmingstedt: The Danish army fails to conquer the peasants' republic of Dithmarschen.

events.title: Pedro Álvares Cabral, with a fleet of 13 ships, departs Portugal on a voyage…
events.blurb: Pedro Álvares Cabral, with a fleet of 13 ships, departs Portugal on a voyage to the New World.

events.title: The day after departing the Cape Verde Islands with the rest of Cabral's…
events.blurb: The day after departing the Cape Verde Islands with the rest of Cabral's fleet, Vasco de Ataíde and his 150 crewmates die when their ship goes down in a storm.

events.title: Pero Vaz de Caminha finishes writing his chronicle of the Portuguese discovery…
events.blurb: Pero Vaz de Caminha finishes writing his chronicle of the Portuguese discovery of Brazil while accompanying Cabral.

events.title: Representatives of the English and Spanish royal families sign a treaty at…
events.blurb: Representatives of the English and Spanish royal families sign a treaty at Canterbury for the marriage of 13-year-old Arthur, Prince of Wales (son of King Henry VII and Elizabeth of York) to 14-year-old Princess Catherine of Aragon.

events.title: The first guide to distilling of liquor is published, Liber de arte…
events.blurb: The first guide to distilling of liquor is published, Liber de arte distillandi de simplicibus by Hieronymus Brunschwig.

events.title: A combined force of troops from the Kingdom of France and from the Republic of…
events.blurb: A combined force of troops from the Kingdom of France and from the Republic of Florence lay siege to the city of Pisa.

events.title: Sultan Abu Sa'id Qansuh of Egypt is overthrown and sent into exile
events.blurb: Sultan Abu Sa'id Qansuh of Egypt is overthrown and sent into exile. Al-Ashraf Abu al-Nasir Janbalat is crowned as the new Mamluk sultan, but reigns for less than six months.

events.title: Ottoman–Venetian War
events.blurb: Ottoman–Venetian War: The Turkish fleet of Kemal Reis defeats the Venetians in the Second Battle of Lepanto.

events.title: The Ottoman Empire defeats the Venetians and capture Modon and Coron, the "two…
events.blurb: The Ottoman Empire defeats the Venetians and capture Modon and Coron, the "two eyes of the Republic".

events.title: Diogo Dias discovers an island which he names São Lourenço, since August 10 is…
events.blurb: Diogo Dias discovers an island which he names São Lourenço, since August 10 is the feast day of Saint Lawrence, a Roman Catholic martyr of the 3rd century. The massive island is later known as Madagascar.

events.title: Francisco de Bobadilla, appointed to replace Admiral Christopher Columbus as…
events.blurb: Francisco de Bobadilla, appointed to replace Admiral Christopher Columbus as Spanish Governor-General of the New World, arrives at Santo Domingo on the island of Hispanola.

events.title: George the Bearded begins a reign of more than 38 years as Duke of Saxony at…
events.blurb: George the Bearded begins a reign of more than 38 years as Duke of Saxony at the Saxon capital of Emden, after the death of his father, Albert III, who had ruled 36 years. George also becomes George II, Margrave of Meissen.

events.title: Pedro Cabral's fleet of nine ships arrives in India, more than six months…
events.blurb: Pedro Cabral's fleet of nine ships arrives in India, more than six months after departing from Portugal, and lands at the port of Calicut, which had been visited two years earlier by Vasco da Gama.

events.title: Christopher Columbus and his brothers, arrested and in chains, are deported…
events.blurb: Christopher Columbus and his brothers, arrested and in chains, are deported from Santo Domingo to Spain.

events.title: Treaty of Granada
events.blurb: Treaty of Granada: Louis XII of France and Ferdinand II of Aragon agree to divide the Kingdom of Naples between them.

events.title: Emperor Go-Kashiwabara accedes to the throne of Meiō era Japan
events.blurb: Emperor Go-Kashiwabara accedes to the throne of Meiō era Japan.

events.title: The Swiss cantons of Basel and Schaffhausen join the Old Swiss Confederacy
events.blurb: The Swiss cantons of Basel and Schaffhausen join the Old Swiss Confederacy.

events.title: Leonardo Loredan is elected 75th doge of the Venetian Republic, taking office…
events.blurb: Leonardo Loredan is elected 75th doge of the Venetian Republic, taking office on October 13, and serves for almost 20 years.

events.title: Italic type (cut by Francesco Griffo) is first used by Aldus Manutius at the…
events.blurb: Italic type (cut by Francesco Griffo) is first used by Aldus Manutius at the Aldine Press in Venice, in an edition of Virgil.

events.title: Gaspar Corte-Real, Portuguese navigator, makes the first documented European…
events.blurb: Gaspar Corte-Real, Portuguese navigator, makes the first documented European landing in North America since c. 1000 A.D.

events.title: Rodrigo de Bastidas, sailing westward from Venezuela in search of gold,…
events.blurb: Rodrigo de Bastidas, sailing westward from Venezuela in search of gold, becomes the first European to explore the Isthmus of Panama.

events.title: The Duchy of Bavaria-Dachau, created in Germany in 1467 after Sigismund, Duke…
events.blurb: The Duchy of Bavaria-Dachau, created in Germany in 1467 after Sigismund, Duke of Bavaria was granted his own state following his resignation from the throne of the Duchy of Bavaria-Munich,

events.title: Minkhaung II becomes the sole King of Burma upon the death of his son…
events.blurb: Minkhaung II becomes the sole King of Burma upon the death of his son Thihathura II, with whom he was co-ruler for 15 years. Minkhaung's reign ends five weeks later when he dies on April 7.

events.title: Portuguese navigator João da Nova discovers Ascension Island
events.blurb: Portuguese navigator João da Nova discovers Ascension Island. It is definitely sighted and named on May 20, 1503 (Feast of the Ascension) by Afonso de Albuquerque.

events.title: Shwenankyawshin Narapati begins an almost 26-year reign as King of Burma upon…
events.blurb: Shwenankyawshin Narapati begins an almost 26-year reign as King of Burma upon the death of his father, King Minkhaung II.

events.title: Harmonice Musices Odhecaton, the first printed collection of polyphonic music,…
events.blurb: Harmonice Musices Odhecaton, the first printed collection of polyphonic music, is published by Ottaviano Petrucci in Venice.

events.title: The semi-independent city of Basel joins the Swiss Confederation as the…
events.blurb: The semi-independent city of Basel joins the Swiss Confederation as the eleventh canton of Switzerland.

events.title: Nicolau Coelho, part of Pedro Cabral's Portuguese expedition to India, returns…
events.blurb: Nicolau Coelho, part of Pedro Cabral's Portuguese expedition to India, returns home with one ship, having left ahead of Cabral.

events.title: Cesare Borgia's French troops storm and overtake the fortress at Capua in the…
events.blurb: Cesare Borgia's French troops storm and overtake the fortress at Capua in the Kingdom of Naples, overcoming the defense of Fabrizio Colonna in the occupation of the Spanish Kingdom of Aragon in southern Italy.

events.title: The Kingdom of Naples, led by King Federico I, surrenders to Cesare Borgia's…
events.blurb: The Kingdom of Naples, led by King Federico I, surrenders to Cesare Borgia's French and Aragonese troops.

events.title: Copernicus is formally installed as canon of Frauenberg Cathedral
events.blurb: Copernicus is formally installed as canon of Frauenberg Cathedral.

events.title: Battle of the Siritsa River
events.blurb: Battle of the Siritsa River: The Livonian Order, supporting the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in the Second Muscovite–Lithuanian War, and commanded by Wolter von Plettenberg, defeats an army of the Grand Duchy of Moscow and Pskov Republic.

events.title: The Banquet of Chestnuts is purportedly held by Cesare Borgia, in the Papal…
events.blurb: The Banquet of Chestnuts is purportedly held by Cesare Borgia, in the Papal Palace of Rome (this account is not historical fact, and could be attributed to enemies of Alexander VI).

events.title: All Saints' Day
events.blurb: (All Saints) – Amerigo Vespucci discovers and names Baía de Todos os Santos, in Brazil.

events.title: Ismail I is enthroned as the first Shah of Iran, choosing Tabriz as his…
events.blurb: (1 Jumada al-Thani 907 AH) Ismail I is enthroned as the first Shah of Iran, choosing Tabriz as his capital, founding the Safavid dynasty in northern Iran. He declares Shi'ism the official and compulsory religion, under penalty of death.

events.title: First Battle of Cannanore
events.blurb: First Battle of Cannanore: João da Nova fleet engaged the fleet of the Zamorin in a battle outside of the Cannanore harbor, the first Portuguese naval battle in the Indian Ocean.

events.title: Meñli I Giray defeats the Golden Horde and sacks their capital, Sarai
events.blurb: Meñli I Giray defeats the Golden Horde and sacks their capital, Sarai.

events.title: Wilhelm Bombast moves to Villach with his son, Paracelsus
events.blurb: Wilhelm Bombast moves to Villach with his son, Paracelsus.

events.title: Isabella I issues an edict outlawing Islam in the Crown of Castile, forcing…
events.blurb: Isabella I issues an edict outlawing Islam in the Crown of Castile, forcing virtually all her Muslim subjects to convert to Christianity.

events.title: The new Viceroy of the New World, Nicolás de Ovando, departs Spain with a…
events.blurb: The new Viceroy of the New World, Nicolás de Ovando, departs Spain with a fleet of 30 ships and orders to replace Viceroy Francisco de Bobadilla at Santo Domingo on the island of Hispaniola, and arrives in April.

events.title: The first recorded earthquake in what is now Croatia strikes at Medvednica…
events.blurb: The first recorded earthquake in what is now Croatia strikes at Medvednica with a Mercalli scale intensity estimated at VIII. (2000).

events.title: Dmitry Ivanovich Vnuk, who had been the teenage co-ruler of the Grand Duchy of…
events.blurb: Dmitry Ivanovich Vnuk, who had been the teenage co-ruler of the Grand Duchy of Moscow since 1498 with his grandfather Ivan III, is arrested along with his mother, Elena of Moldavia on suspicion of conspiracy.

events.title: The formal coronation of Ivan the Great as Grand Prince of Moscow…
events.blurb: The formal coronation of Ivan the Great as Grand Prince of Moscow (encompassing most of the Russian people's territory) to reflect that he is the nation's sole ruler.

events.title: Columbus and his men complete the rescue of stranded Portuguese soldiers in…
events.blurb: Columbus and his men complete the rescue of stranded Portuguese soldiers in Morocco, then depart Asilah for a crossing of the Atlantic in 20 days.

events.title: Columbus and his crew land on the island of Martinique and land at Le Carbet
events.blurb: Columbus and his crew land on the island of Martinique and land at Le Carbet.

events.title: The "Cantino planisphere", a precise copy for an Italian spy of Portugal's…
events.blurb: The "Cantino planisphere", a precise copy for an Italian spy of Portugal's secret Padrão Real map of the New World, is acquired by Alberto Cantino, agent for Ercole I d'Este, Duke of Ferrara, at a cost of 12 golden ducats.

events.title: Hieronymus Bosch works on the triptych The Garden of Earthly Delights,…
events.blurb: Hieronymus Bosch works on the triptych The Garden of Earthly Delights, although other sources suggest a 1490-1510 date range for when he worked on it.

events.title: The Spanish explorer Juan de Bermúdez discovered the island Bermuda
events.blurb: The Spanish explorer Juan de Bermúdez discovered the island Bermuda.

events.title: Mariotto Albertinelli paints The Visitation
events.blurb: Mariotto Albertinelli paints The Visitation.

events.title: Seville in Castile is awarded exclusive rights to trade with the New World
events.blurb: Seville in Castile is awarded exclusive rights to trade with the New World.

events.title: Construction of the Henry VII Chapel at Westminster Abbey begins in the…
events.blurb: Construction of the Henry VII Chapel at Westminster Abbey begins in the perpendicular Gothic style, the final stage of English Gothic art.

events.title: Challenge of Barletta
events.blurb: Challenge of Barletta: Thirteen Italian knights defeat thirteen French knights, near Barletta.

events.title: The Kingdom of Cochin (ruled by a Portuguese-installed raja, Unni Ramman Koyil…
events.blurb: The Kingdom of Cochin (ruled by a Portuguese-installed raja, Unni Ramman Koyil II in modern-day India's Kerala state) is invaded by 50,000 Nair troops of the Zamorin of Calicut.

events.title: Naples is captured by the Spanish
events.blurb: Naples is captured by the Spanish.

events.title: Feast of the Ascension
events.blurb: (Feast of the Ascension) – Ascension Island is first definitively sighted, by Portuguese admiral Afonso de Albuquerque.

events.title: The coronation of Moctezuma II as ruler of the Aztec Empire takes place at the…
events.blurb: The coronation of Moctezuma II as ruler of the Aztec Empire takes place at the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan, part of modern-day Mexico City.

events.title: Murad, the last Sultan of Aq Qoyunlu in modern-day eastern Turkey fights the…
events.blurb: Murad, the last Sultan of Aq Qoyunlu in modern-day eastern Turkey fights the Safavid King of Persia, Ismail I in a battle near the city of Hamadan, and suffers 10,000 casualties, including his commander Güzel Ahmad.

events.title: The book The Imitation of Christ by Thomas à Kempis is re-published in an…
events.blurb: The book The Imitation of Christ by Thomas à Kempis is re-published in an English translation.

events.title: Orbital calculations suggest that on this day Pluto moves outside Neptune's…
events.blurb: Orbital calculations suggest that on this day Pluto moves outside Neptune's orbit, remaining there for 233 years.

events.title: Saint Helena is first definitively sighted, by ships of Portuguese navigator…
events.blurb: Saint Helena is first definitively sighted, by ships of Portuguese navigator Estêvão da Gama returning from the East.

events.title: Francesco Todeschini Piccolomini, Archbishop of Siena, is elected as the new…
events.blurb: Francesco Todeschini Piccolomini, Archbishop of Siena, is elected as the new Pope after the voting cardinals cannot decide between Georges d'Amboise of France or Giuliano della Rovere of Italy.

events.title: Fort Emmanuel is christened at Cochin after Afonso de Albuquerque obtained…
events.blurb: Fort Emmanuel is christened at Cochin after Afonso de Albuquerque obtained permission to be able to build it. It is the first European fort in India, in addition to being the first Portuguese fort.

events.title: Pope Julius II, formerly Giuliano della Rovere, adds four new people to the…
events.blurb: Pope Julius II, formerly Giuliano della Rovere, adds four new people to the College of Cardinals, including two members of his family, Clemente della Rovere and Galeotto della Rovere.

events.title: Islamic scholar Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah issues the Oran fatwa for Muslims in…
events.blurb: (approximate date) Islamic scholar Ahmad ibn Abi Jum'ah issues the Oran fatwa for Muslims in Spain (1 Rajab 910 AH in Islamic calendar, Gregorian date is approximate).

events.title: Sheikh Ahmed, the final leader of the Great Horde, is last heard of as a…
events.blurb: Sheikh Ahmed, the final leader of the Great Horde, is last heard of as a Lithuanian prisoner at Vilnius until 1527 when he was released, after which he came to rule over the Astrakhan Khanate.

events.title: Raphael paints The Marriage of the Virgin, which exemplifies some major…
events.blurb: Raphael paints The Marriage of the Virgin, which exemplifies some major principles of High Renaissance art.

events.title: Islamization of the Sudan region
events.blurb: Islamization of the Sudan region: A Funj leader, Amara Dunqas, founds the Sultanate of Sennar.

events.title: King Ferdinand V of Castile contracts with Juan de la Cosa to finance an…
events.blurb: King Ferdinand V of Castile contracts with Juan de la Cosa to finance an independent expedition to the Pearl Islands and the Gulf of Urabá.

events.title: The investiture of Prince Henry of England as Prince of Wales and Earl of…

events.blurb: Lucien Grimaldi takes over as the new Lord of Monaco after stabbing his brother Jean II to death.

events.blurb: In Portuguese India, the King of Cannanore gives permission to Francisco de Almeida to build the Fortaleza de Santo Ângelo in Kannur.

events.blurb: The Swiss Guard arrives at the Vatican, to serve as permanent ceremonial and palace guards under Pope Julius II.

events.blurb: Iye Roy Mackay, Chief of Scotland's Clan Mackay, records his 1504 grant of six lands in what is now the County Sutherland, and starts a feud with Euphemia II, Countess of Ross.

events.title: Malus Intercursus, a treaty between King Henry VII of England and Duke Philip…
events.blurb: Malus Intercursus, a treaty between King Henry VII of England and Duke Philip the Handsome of Burgundy, is signed.

events.blurb: Mahmud Shah II begins a 41-year reign as the Sultan of Kedah, a Muslim kingdom on the Malay Peninsula, on the death of his father, Adilin I.

events.title: Treaty of Villafáfila

events.blurb: Philip the Handsome, Duke of Burgundy, becomes the ruler of the Spanish Kingdom of Castile with his insane wife Joanna, but reigns for only two months before dying of typhoid.

events.blurb: Pope Julius II issues a bull excommunicating Giovanni II Bentivoglio from the Roman Catholic Church, who had dominated the Italian city state of Bologna.

events.blurb: Pedro Mascarenhas discovers Diego Garcia, and reaches Mauritius in the Mascarene Islands.

events.blurb: Svante Nilsson, regent of Sweden since 1504, dies at the age of 51. Eric Trolle is subsequently elected as the new Regent, but will be ousted after only six months.

events.blurb: Neagoe Basarab becomes the new Prince of Wallachia at the capital, Târgoviște, after Prince Prince Vlad V is captured at battle in Bucharest and then decapitated.

events.title: The Fifth Council of the Lateran begins

events.title: Thomas Howard, 2nd Duke of Norfolk, leads an English expedition into France…

events.blurb: Sten Sture the Younger is elected new Regent of Sweden, replacing Eric Trolle.

events.blurb: The Spanish Crown issues the Laws of Burgos, governing the conduct of settlers with regard to native Indians in the New World.

events.blurb: Pope Leo X sends a letter to Scotland's King James IV, threatening him with ecclesiastical censure or excommunication for breaking his peace treaties with England.

events.blurb: Scotland's Earl of Arran departs from the Firth of Forth with 22 ships on a plan to join France in cutting off England's communications with the rest of Europe.

events.blurb: At Edirne, the Ottoman sultan Selim II confirms the renewal of peace treaties with Venice, under terms that are accepted by the Venetian government on December 3.

events.blurb: Gazapati, becomes the new King of Burma as his father, King Raza, abdicates the throne at the capital of Arakan, Mrauk U.

events.blurb: Albrecht Dürer makes his famous engraving Melencolia I.

events.blurb: A great fire breaks out, in the Rialto of Venice.

events.blurb: The Poor Conrad peasant revolt against Ulrich, Duke of Württemberg begins in Beutelsbach.

events.blurb: The Hungarian rebel leader György Dózsa is defeated in battle at Temesvár in Transylvania in Hungary (now Timișoara in Romania, and tortured over a period of six days until his death.

events.title: Hersekzade Ahmed Pasha steps down as Grand vizier of the Ottoman Empire

events.blurb: Ottoman General Dukaginzade Ahmed Pasha is appointed by the Sultan Selim I as the new Grand Vizier, but serves for less than three months before he is removed and executed.

events.blurb: Giovanni Carlo Tramontano, Count of Matera, is assassinated in Matera, the day after demanding that the aristocracy and people of his realm pay 24,000 ducates in taxes to clear up his personal debts.

events.blurb: The Portuguese are the first Europeans to land in Timor island, as the first settlers arrive to the north coast of Madeira Island, there establishing Saint George.

events.title: Bartolomé de las Casas urges Ferdinand II of Aragon to end Amerindian slavery,…
events.blurb: Bartolomé de las Casas urges Ferdinand II of Aragon to end Amerindian slavery, and recommends experimental free towns.

events.title: Dürer's Rhinoceros is cut
events.blurb: Dürer's Rhinoceros is cut.

events.blurb: The Emirate of Oman, ruled by Muhammad bin Ismail, becomes a protectorate of Portugal.

events.blurb: Manchester Grammar School is endowed by Hugh Oldham, the first free grammar school in England.

events.blurb: Isabella of Austria is crowned as Queen consort of Denmark and Norway after her marriage to King Christian II is ratified.

events.title: Conquistador Diego Velázquez de Cuéllar founds Havana, Cuba

events.title: Lopo Soares de Albergaria becomes the new Viceroy of Portuguese India as…

events.title: The fall of the Nantan meteorite is possibly observed near the city of Nantan,…
events.blurb: The fall of the Nantan meteorite is possibly observed near the city of Nantan, Nandan County, Guangxi (China).

events.title: Portuguese soldier Fernão Lopes becomes the first known permanent inhabitant…
events.blurb: Portuguese soldier Fernão Lopes becomes the first known permanent inhabitant of Saint Helena.

events.title: Gillingham School is founded, the oldest in Dorset, England
events.blurb: Gillingham School is founded, the oldest in Dorset, England.

events.blurb: The predecessor of the Royal Mail, known as the Master of the Posts, is established by Henry VIII of England.

events.title: Fuggerei is established in Augsburg (Bavaria), as the world's oldest social…
events.blurb: Fuggerei is established in Augsburg (Bavaria), as the world's oldest social housing complex still in use.

events.blurb: After two months in Bologna, part of the Papal States in Italy, Pope Leo X concludes two months of negotiation with King François I of France.

events.title: In his capacity as Lord of Ireland, Henry VIII opens the first of six…
events.blurb: In his capacity as Lord of Ireland, Henry VIII opens the first of six assemblies of parliament during his reign of the Parliament of Ireland at Dublin. The parliament holds three sessions, ending on October 2, when it is dismissed.

events.title: Desiderius Erasmus publishes a new Greek edition of the New Testament, Novum…
events.blurb: Desiderius Erasmus publishes a new Greek edition of the New Testament, Novum Instrumentum omne, in Basel.

events.blurb: At the age of 9, Louis II of Jagiellon becomes the new King of Hungary, Croatia and Bohemia upon the death of his father, King Vladislaus II.

events.title: The Venetian Ghetto is instituted in the Republic of Venice
events.blurb: The Venetian Ghetto is instituted in the Republic of Venice.

events.title: The Reinheitsgebot is instituted in Ingolstadt, Bavaria, regulating the purity…
events.blurb: The Reinheitsgebot is instituted in Ingolstadt, Bavaria, regulating the purity of beer permissible for sale.

events.title: A Category IX earthquake strikes Ragusa in the Republic of Ragusa
events.blurb: A Category IX earthquake strikes Ragusa in the Republic of Ragusa.

events.title: In what is now Vietnam, Le Tuong Duc, Emperor of Dai Viet, since 1509, is…
events.blurb: In what is now Vietnam, Le Tuong Duc, Emperor of Dai Viet, since 1509, is murdered at his palace at Thang Long (now in Hanoi) by his bodyguards.

events.title: In Spain, King John III of Navarre dies after a reign of 32 years and is…
events.blurb: In Spain, King John III of Navarre dies after a reign of 32 years and is succeeded by his widow, Queen Catherine.

events.title: King James V of Scotland opens the Scottish Parliament at Edinburgh
events.blurb: King James V of Scotland opens the Scottish Parliament at Edinburgh.

events.title: German theologian Andreas Karlstadt completes his series of 151 theses, an…
events.blurb: German theologian Andreas Karlstadt completes his series of 151 theses, an attack against corruption in the Roman Catholic Church.

events.title: Based in Kamaran, an island in the Red Sea, the Mamluk Egyptian Admiral Selman…
events.blurb: Based in Kamaran, an island in the Red Sea, the Mamluk Egyptian Admiral Selman Reis leads of fleet 19 ships in an unsuccessful attempt to take Yemen and Aden.

events.title: The "Treaty of Perpetual Peace" is signed in the city of Fribourg in…
events.blurb: The "Treaty of Perpetual Peace" is signed in the city of Fribourg in Switzerland, between representatives of the Thirteen Cantons of the Old Swiss Confederacy, and King Francis of the Kingdom of France,

events.title: Battle of Ridaniya
events.blurb: Battle of Ridaniya: The Ottoman army of sultan Selim I defeats the Mamluk army in Egypt, commanded by king Tuman Bay II.

events.title: Bernal Díaz del Castillo, a chronicler who documents the conquest of Mexico,…
events.blurb: Bernal Díaz del Castillo, a chronicler who documents the conquest of Mexico, sets out with the Hernández de Córdoba expedition from Jaruco. They arrive at Cape Catoche twenty-one days later, and are met with hostility by the natives.

events.title: At the age of 13, Henry II becomes the King of Navarre, by then limited to the…
events.blurb: At the age of 13, Henry II becomes the King of Navarre, by then limited to the part of the Iberian peninsula north of the Pyrennes, upon the death of his mother, Queen Catherine in the capital, Pamplona.

events.title: The first intentional landing by Europeans on the coast of Mexico takes place…
events.blurb: The first intentional landing by Europeans on the coast of Mexico takes place as the Cordoba Expedition arrives at Cabo Catoche on the Yucatán Peninsula, now in the Mexican state of Quintana Roo.

events.title: Tuman Bey II, the former King of Egypt, is executed along with his aides,…
events.blurb: Tuman Bey II, the former King of Egypt, is executed along with his aides, bringing an end to the Abbasid dynasty.
