events.title: Ottoman–Mamluk War (1516–1517)
events.blurb: The Ottoman–Mamluk War officially ends as the Ottoman Empire annexes the Mamluk Sultanate territories in the Middle East (the Levant), the Arabian Peninsula (Hejaz) and Egypt as provinces.

events.title: In what is now Romania, Stephen IV becomes the new Prince of Moldavia at…
events.blurb: In what is now Romania, Stephen IV becomes the new Prince of Moldavia at Suceava upon the death of his father, Bogdan III the One-Eyed.

events.title: Anticipating a riot in London, the Lord Mayor announces at 8:30 in the evening…
events.blurb: Anticipating a riot in London, the Lord Mayor announces at 8:30 in the evening that a curfew will begin within 30 minutes, at 9:00. An attempt by a local alderman, John Mundy, to enforce the curfew triggers the attack by a mob hours later.

events.title: Evil May Day
events.blurb: Evil May Day: Xenophobic riots break out in London as English citizens attack foreigners, including Flemish shoemakers and French royal courtiers. The Duke of Norfolk leads a private army of 1,300 men to put down the rioting.

events.title: The coronation of Queen Consort Claude of France, wife of King Francis I,…
events.blurb: The coronation of Queen Consort Claude of France, wife of King Francis I, takes place at the Basilica of St Denis with Cardinal Philippe de Luxembourg performing the ceremony.

events.title: Pier Gerlofs Donia, leader of a rebellion of the Frisians minority of the…
events.blurb: Pier Gerlofs Donia, leader of a rebellion of the Frisians minority of the Netherlands, leads 4,000 of his Arumer Zwarte Hoop soldiers on an attack against the Dutch inhabitants of Medemblik,

events.title: Yunus Pasha, the Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire and the Ottoman Governor…
events.blurb: Yunus Pasha, the Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire and the Ottoman Governor of Egypt after leading the Egyptian conquest, is fired by the Ottoman Sultan Selim I and then executed by decapitation.

events.title: In India, Ibrahim Khan Lodi becomes the new Sultan of Delhi upon the death of…
events.blurb: In India, Ibrahim Khan Lodi becomes the new Sultan of Delhi upon the death of his father, Sikandar Khan Lodi. Ibrahim will reign until 1526, when the Sultanate of Delhi is conquered by the Afghan Mughal king, Babur.

events.title: Bona Sforza of Italy, daughter of the late Duke of Milan, Gian Galeazzo…
events.blurb: Bona Sforza of Italy, daughter of the late Duke of Milan, Gian Galeazzo Sforza, marries King Sigismund of Poland by proxy at Naples, then begins a three month journey to Kraków to assume the throne.

events.title: Johann Froben publishes Erasmus's work Colloquies, which was unauthorized, and…
events.blurb: Johann Froben publishes Erasmus's work Colloquies, which was unauthorized, and it took until 1519 that an authorized version would be published.

events.title: The remnants of The Abbasid Caliphate (stationed in Egypt under the Mamluk…
events.blurb: The remnants of The Abbasid Caliphate (stationed in Egypt under the Mamluk Sultanate (Cairo) hands over the title of caliph to the Ottoman Empire that had conquered Constantinople in 1453, 65 years earlier.

events.title: A swarm of stinging ants devastates crops on Hispaniola
events.blurb: A swarm of stinging ants devastates crops on Hispaniola.

events.title: The Rajput Mewar Kingdom under Rana Sanga achieves a major victory over Sultan…
events.blurb: The Rajput Mewar Kingdom under Rana Sanga achieves a major victory over Sultan Ibrahim Lodi of Delhi.

events.title: Henricus Grammateus publishes Ayn neu Kunstlich Buech in Vienna, containing…
events.blurb: Henricus Grammateus publishes Ayn neu Kunstlich Buech in Vienna, containing the earliest printed use of plus and minus signs for arithmetic.

events.title: Piri Mehmed Pasha is appointed as the new Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire…
events.blurb: Piri Mehmed Pasha is appointed as the new Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire by the Sultan Selim I, replacing Yunus Pasha, who was executed four months earlier on September 13.

events.title: Sir John Ernley is selected as the new Chief Justice of the Common Pleas of…
events.blurb: Sir John Ernley is selected as the new Chief Justice of the Common Pleas of England by King King Henry VIII to replace the late Robert Rede, who died on January 8. Emley.

events.title: Spanish conquistador Juan de Grijalva embarks from Cuba on a mission to…
events.blurb: Spanish conquistador Juan de Grijalva embarks from Cuba on a mission to explore and conquer Mexico, departing from Matanzas with four ships and 170 people.

events.title: Grijalva and his crew become the first Europeans to find Cozumel in Mexico
events.blurb: Grijalva and his crew become the first Europeans to find Cozumel in Mexico.

events.title: A fleet of four Portuguese ships, commanded by João da Silveira from…
events.blurb: A fleet of four Portuguese ships, commanded by João da Silveira from Portuguese India, arrived in Chittagong (now part of Bangladesh, but at the time part of the Sultanate of Bengal),

events.title: The Girjalva expedition brings the first Europeans to the Yucatan Peninsula in…
events.blurb: The Girjalva expedition brings the first Europeans to the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico, arriving at what is now the Tabasco state.

events.title: Dancing plague of 1518
events.blurb: Dancing plague of 1518: A case of dancing mania breaks out in Strasbourg as a woman identified as "Frau Troffea" begins constant dancing that lasts for six days, after which fellow residents begin to join in.

events.title: Battle of Brännkyrka
events.blurb: Battle of Brännkyrka: The Kalmar Union, led by King Christian II of Denmark, is defeated by the Swedish regent Sten Sture the Younger.

events.title: Diogo Lopes de Sequeira takes office as the new Governor of Portuguese India,…
events.blurb: Diogo Lopes de Sequeira takes office as the new Governor of Portuguese India, replacing Lopo Soares de Albergaria.

events.title: Treaty of London (1518)
events.blurb: The Treaty of London temporarily ensures peace in Western Europe.

events.title: The Deccan sultanates in southern India of Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bidar, Bijapur,…
events.blurb: The Deccan sultanates in southern India of Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bidar, Bijapur, and Golconda formally declare their independence from the Bahmani Sultanate.

events.title: The first recorded fatal accident involving a gun in England is recorded at…
events.blurb: The first recorded fatal accident involving a gun in England is recorded at Welton, East Riding of Yorkshire.

events.title: The Spanish invade Barbados
events.blurb: The Spanish invade Barbados.

events.title: The first civil revolt in Anatolia takes place, led by Alevi preacher Celâl
events.blurb: The first civil revolt in Anatolia takes place, led by Alevi preacher Celâl.

events.title: St. Olaf's Church, Tallinn
events.blurb: St. Olaf's Church, Tallinn is completed in Estonia.

events.title: The Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés and his conquistadores depart from Cuba…
events.blurb: The Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés and his conquistadores depart from Cuba toward the island of Cozumel in Mexico to begin a mission of conquest.

events.title: Because of the large population of Jews included converts to Christianity…
events.blurb: Because of the large population of Jews included converts to Christianity ("New Christians") in the colony of Portuguese India at Goa,

events.title: Giulio de' Medici, who will later become Pope Clement VII becomes the Duke of…
events.blurb: Giulio de' Medici, who will later become Pope Clement VII becomes the Duke of the Florentine Republic upon the death of his father, Lorenzo de' Medici, Duke of Urbino.

events.title: The Leipzig Debate begins at the Pleissenburg lecture hall in the German city…
events.blurb: The Leipzig Debate begins at the Pleissenburg lecture hall in the German city of Leipzig in Saxony, as Martin Luther defends his ideas on the Protestant Reformation against challenges by Johann Eck,

events.title: Prince of Ning rebellion
events.blurb: The Prince of Ning rebellion begins, after Zhu Chenhao declares the Ming dynasty's Zhengde Emperor a usurper, and leads his army north in an attempt to capture Nanjing.

events.title: King Charles of Spain issues a royal order prohibiting navigator Rui Faleiro…
events.blurb: King Charles of Spain issues a royal order prohibiting navigator Rui Faleiro from participating in the Magellan expedition, after Portugal's ambassador to Spain reports that Faleiro is suffering from a nervous breakdown.

events.title: Magellan expedition
events.blurb: The Magellan expedition departs from Seville in Spain.

events.title: Panama City is founded by Spanish conquistador Pedro Arias Dávila
events.blurb: Panama City is founded by Spanish conquistador Pedro Arias Dávila.

events.title: Ferdinand Magellan departs from Spain with a fleet of five ships and a crew of…
events.blurb: Ferdinand Magellan departs from Spain with a fleet of five ships and a crew of 270 men, to sail westbound to the Spice Islands.

events.title: At Toruń, the members of the Sejm of the Kingdom of Poland vote to approve a…
events.blurb: At Toruń, the members of the Sejm of the Kingdom of Poland vote to approve a war against the Teutonic Knights and to assess new taxes to recruit mercenary troops.

events.title: Massacre in the Great Temple of Tenochtitlan
events.blurb: The Massacre in the Great Temple of Tenochtitlan takes place in Mexico after the Aztec Emperor Moctezuma II is allowed by the Deputy Governor of New Spain, Pedro de Alvarado,

events.blurb: Thomas Howard, 3rd Duke of Norfolk becomes England's new Lord Deputy of Ireland

events.blurb: Juan de Cartagena, formerly captain of the largest ship on the Magellan expedition, San Antonio, escapes captivity from the Victoria and begins a mutiny against Ferdinand Magellan.

events.title: Revolt of the Comuneros
events.blurb: Revolt of the Comuneros: Citizens of Toledo, Castile opposed to the rule of the Flemish-born Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, rise up when the royal government attempts to unseat radical city councilors.

events.title: The semi-independent Duchy of Mecklenburg, in what is now Germany, is…
events.blurb: The semi-independent Duchy of Mecklenburg, in what is now Germany, is partitioned into two duchies, Mecklenburg-Schwerin and Mecklenburg-Strelitz.

events.title: La Noche Triste (Night of Sorrow)
events.blurb: La Noche Triste (Night of Sorrow): The forces of Cuitláhuac, Aztec ruler of Tenochtitlan, gain a major victory against the forces of conquistador Hernán Cortés.

events.title: Otumba near Lake Texcaco
events.blurb: Otumba near Lake Texcaco: The Spaniards defeat the Aztecs.

events.title: After wintering in Patagonia in Argentina, the Magellan expedition resumes its…
events.blurb: After wintering in Patagonia in Argentina, the Magellan expedition resumes its attempt to become the first crew to sail around the world.

events.title: The French warrior René of Savoy departs from Marseille on his flagship,…
events.blurb: The French warrior René of Savoy departs from Marseille on his flagship, Sainte Marie de Bonaventure on a four-month mission to protect the Knights Hospitaller against an attack by the Ottoman Turks.

events.title: Suleiman I succeeds his father Selim I as Sultan of the Ottoman Empire
events.blurb: Suleiman I succeeds his father Selim I as Sultan of the Ottoman Empire. He is officially crowned on September 30 and will rule until 1566.

events.title: (Feast of St
events.blurb: (Feast of St. Ursula) – The islands of Saint Pierre and Miquelon are discovered by Portuguese explorer João Álvares Fagundes, off Newfoundland. He names them Islands of the 11,000 Virgins, in honour of Saint Ursula.

events.title: Christian II is crowned king of Sweden in Nikolai Church
events.blurb: Christian II is crowned king of Sweden in Nikolai Church. The coronation is followed by a three-day feast in Stockholm.

events.title: Stockholm Bloodbath
events.blurb: Stockholm Bloodbath: The execution of 82 Swedish noblemen and clergymen, having been sentenced to death for their involvement in the Swedish resistance against the Danish invasion, is completed after two days of beheading.

events.title: Cuauhtémoc becomes the last Aztec Emperor after the death from smallpox of the…
events.blurb: Cuauhtémoc becomes the last Aztec Emperor after the death from smallpox of the Emperor Cuitláhuac, who reigned for only 80 days.

events.title: After navigating through the strait at the southern end of South America,…
events.blurb: After navigating through the strait at the southern end of South America, three ships under the command of Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan reach the Pacific Ocean.

events.title: Teodosie becomes the new Voivode of Wallachia, at the capital, Targoviste, now…
events.blurb: Teodosie becomes the new Voivode of Wallachia, at the capital, Targoviste, now in Romania.

events.title: Gazi Husrev Bey replaces Bali-beg Jahjapašić as the Ottoman Governor of Bosnia
events.blurb: Gazi Husrev Bey replaces Bali-beg Jahjapašić as the Ottoman Governor of Bosnia.

events.title: Jacopo Berengario da Carpi publishes Commentaria cum amplissimus additionibus…
events.blurb: Jacopo Berengario da Carpi publishes Commentaria cum amplissimus additionibus super anatomiam Mundini in Bologna, including observation of the vermiform appendix.

events.title: The Nydala Abbey Bloodbath takes place at Nydala Abbey, Sweden
events.blurb: The Nydala Abbey Bloodbath takes place at Nydala Abbey, Sweden; the abbot and many monks are murdered by Danes.

events.title: The First Mass in the Philippines is held
events.blurb: The First Mass in the Philippines is held.

events.title: May
events.blurb: or May – Battle of Tunmen in Tuen Mun (present-day Hong Kong): The Ming Dynasty navy defeats the Portuguese navy (arguably the first Sino-European battle in world history).

events.title: Battle of Mactan
events.blurb: Battle of Mactan: Ferdinand Magellan is killed in the Philippines when he confronts Lapulapu, the chief of the island.

events.title: Edward Stafford, 3rd Duke of Buckingham, is executed for treason in Tower Hill
events.blurb: Edward Stafford, 3rd Duke of Buckingham, is executed for treason in Tower Hill.

events.title: Battle of Pampeluna
events.blurb: At the Battle of Pampeluna in Spain, and alliance of forces from French and the Kingdom of Navarre forces defeat those of Spain.

events.title: The Diet of Worms ends when Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor issues the Edict of…
events.blurb: The Diet of Worms ends when Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor issues the Edict of Worms, declaring Martin Luther an outlaw and banning his literature.

events.title: June 30
events.blurb: or 30 – The oldest surviving dateable document written primarily in the Romanian language: Neacșu's letter, written by a trader from Câmpulung, to Johannes Benkner, the mayor of Brașov,

events.title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
events.blurb: Fall of Tenochtitlan: Cuauhtémoc surrenders to Cortés, thus incorporating the Aztec Empire into the Spanish Empire and ending the Late Postclassic period in Mesoamerica.

events.title: Italian War of 1521–1526
events.blurb: The Italian War of 1521–1526 breaks out between Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, and Francis I of France as Henry III of Nassau-Breda leads Imperial troops on an invasion of northeastern France.

events.title: Siege of Belgrade (1521)
events.blurb: Belgrade is captured by the Ottoman army of Suleiman the Magnificent.

events.title: Spanish–German–Papal forces under Prospero Colonna force French Marshal Odet…
events.blurb: Spanish–German–Papal forces under Prospero Colonna force French Marshal Odet de Lautrec to abandon Milan.

events.title: The Zwickau prophets arrive in Wittenberg, disturbing the peace and spreading…
events.blurb: The Zwickau prophets arrive in Wittenberg, disturbing the peace and spreading the idea of rejecting infant baptism.

events.title: Australia is sighted by a Portuguese expedition led by Cristóvão de Mendonça,…
events.blurb: Australia is sighted by a Portuguese expedition led by Cristóvão de Mendonça, who maps the continent and names it Jave la Grande ("The Greater Java"), according to the theory of the Portuguese discovery of Australia.

events.title: The Portuguese, allied with King Ilato of the Goratalo kingdom, construct the…
events.blurb: The Portuguese, allied with King Ilato of the Goratalo kingdom, construct the Otanaha Fortress.

events.title: In Zurich in Switzerland, the Affair of the Sausages begins as Pastor Huldrych…
events.blurb: In Zurich in Switzerland, the Affair of the Sausages begins as Pastor Huldrych Zwingli of Grossmünster publicly speaks out against the food restrictions during the Roman Catholic period of fasting during Lent,

events.title: In Wittenberg, as the first day of Lent arrives, Martin Luther begins…
events.blurb: In Wittenberg, as the first day of Lent arrives, Martin Luther begins preaching the first of his eight "Invocavit sermons", stressing the primacy of core Christian values, such as love, patience, charity, and freedom,

events.title: The Grünwald Conference takes place in the Duchy of Bavaria in Germany, as the…
events.blurb: The Grünwald Conference takes place in the Duchy of Bavaria in Germany, as the co-rulers,

events.title: Daniil of Volotsk is appointed by the Grand Duke of Moscow as the new…
events.blurb: Daniil of Volotsk is appointed by the Grand Duke of Moscow as the new Metropolitan of Moscow, becoming the leader of the Russian Orthodox Church.

events.title: In what is now the Karnataka state of India, Waliullah Shah is installed as…
events.blurb: In what is now the Karnataka state of India, Waliullah Shah is installed as the new ruler of Bahmani by the Sultan of Bidar, Amir Barid I.

events.title: Battle of Bicocca
events.blurb: In the Battle of Bicocca, French and Swiss forces under Odet de Lautrec are defeated by the Spanish in their attempt to retake Milan, and are forced to withdraw into Venetian territory.

events.title: Pope Adrian VI, at the request of Spanish Emperor Carlos V, promulgates the…
events.blurb: Pope Adrian VI, at the request of Spanish Emperor Carlos V, promulgates the papal bull Exponi nobis,

events.title: At Coyoacán in Mexico (at the time, the colony of New Spain) Spanish…
events.blurb: At Coyoacán in Mexico (at the time, the colony of New Spain) Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés sends his third report to the Emperor Carlos V, describing the events of the last two years, including the conquest of Tenochtitlan,

events.title: The Ottoman Empire's siege of Knin in the Kingdom of Croatia is successful as…
events.blurb: The Ottoman Empire's siege of Knin in the Kingdom of Croatia is successful as Mihajlo Vojković surrenders to Gazi Husrev Bey and most of the Croatian inhabitants are allowed to leave. Inhabitants of Bosnia then move in.

events.title: Lord Erskine is appointed by Margaret Tudor, regent of Scotland, to be the…
events.blurb: Lord Erskine is appointed by Margaret Tudor, regent of Scotland, to be the "keeper" of Margaret's 10-year-old son, King James V, who is to remain within the confines of Erskine's home at Stirling Castle.

events.title: Knights' War
events.blurb: The Knights' War erupts within the Holy Roman Empire as Franz von Sickingen leads a revolt against the Prince-Bishop of Trier and to seize the church properties within the Electorate of Trier

events.title: A group of 18 men, commanded by Captain Juan Sebastián Elcano, and including…
events.blurb: A group of 18 men, commanded by Captain Juan Sebastián Elcano, and including Antonio Pigafetta, Maestre Anes and Juan de Zubileta become the first people to have traveled around the world.

events.title: Luther Bible
events.blurb: Luther Bible: Martin Luther's translation of the Bible's New Testament into Early New High German from Greek, Das newe Testament Deutzsch, is published in Germany, selling thousands in the first few weeks.

events.title: 1522 Almería earthquake
events.blurb: A 6.8 magnitude earthquake kills more than 2,500 people in the Spanish city of Almería, near Alhama de Almería.

events.title: The Ottomans finally break into Rhodes, but the Knights continue fierce…
events.blurb: The Ottomans finally break into Rhodes, but the Knights continue fierce resistance in the streets.

events.title: In northern Italy, a French army under Guillaume Gouffier tries to recover…
events.blurb: In northern Italy, a French army under Guillaume Gouffier tries to recover Milan but fails due to an offensive by Spanish, Imperial and English troops and they retreat in mid-November.

events.title: Construction of Fort Kastela by Portuguese invaders, on what is now the island…
events.blurb: Construction of Fort Kastela by Portuguese invaders, on what is now the island of Ternate in Indonesia, is completed as Portugal claims the Spice Islands (now the Maluku Islands).

events.title: Captain Antón Mayor formally claims for Spain what is now Nicaragua, after he…
events.blurb: Captain Antón Mayor formally claims for Spain what is now Nicaragua, after he arrives with Andrés Niño and other Spanish troops on the Central American coast at El Realejo.

events.title: In Spain's Kingdom of Valencia, a rebellion by the Brotherhoods of Mallorca is…
events.blurb: In Spain's Kingdom of Valencia, a rebellion by the Brotherhoods of Mallorca is suppressed after two years, as the rebels surrender their capital, Palma de Mallorca, to Spanish and German troops.

events.title: Frederick I is provisionally declared as King of Denmark by Danish nobles at…
events.blurb: Frederick I is provisionally declared as King of Denmark by Danish nobles at Viborg, although loyalists at Copenhagen refuse to recognize his claim to the throne.

events.title: Under a plan organized by Sister Katharina von Bora and Protestant reformer…
events.blurb: Under a plan organized by Sister Katharina von Bora and Protestant reformer Martin Luther,

events.title: The Spanish conquest of Nicaragua continues as Gil González Dávila and 17…
events.blurb: The Spanish conquest of Nicaragua continues as Gil González Dávila and 17 other soldiers arrive at Lake Nicaragua and claim it for the Spanish crown, calling the freshwater source the Mar Dulce.

events.title: Mirza Shah Hossein, Grand Vizier of Persia since 1514, is assassinated in…
events.blurb: Mirza Shah Hossein, Grand Vizier of Persia since 1514, is assassinated in Qazvin (now in Iran) by Shia nobles of the Qizilbash sect, and replaced by Jalal al-Din Mohammad Tabrizi.

events.title: Sir Thomas More, noted for being a Catholic social philosopher and author of…
events.blurb: Sir Thomas More, noted for being a Catholic social philosopher and author of the 1516 novel Utopia, is appointed by King Henry VIII as the Speaker of the English House of Commons for the first parliamentary session since 1515.

events.title: In Nicaragua, Diriangén, ruler of the Chorotega speakers, stages an attack on…
events.blurb: In Nicaragua, Diriangén, ruler of the Chorotega speakers, stages an attack on the Spanish invaders led by González Dávila.

events.title: The Ningbo incident
events.blurb: The Ningbo incident: Two rival trade delegations from Japan feud in the Chinese city of Ningbo, resulting in the pillage and plunder of the city.

events.title: In the Rhineland in Germany, the Knights' War, led by Franz von Sickingen…
events.blurb: In the Rhineland in Germany, the Knights' War, led by Franz von Sickingen since August 27, is finally put down at Landstuhl by troops of the Holy Roman Empire as the Nanstein Castle falls.

events.title: Andrea Gritti is elected as the new Doge of the Republic of Venice, 13 days…
events.blurb: Andrea Gritti is elected as the new Doge of the Republic of Venice, 13 days after the death of Antonio Grimani.

events.title: Swedish War of Liberation
events.blurb: Swedish War of Liberation: The city of Kalmar in Sweden, occupied by troops of Denmark, falls to a Swedish Army force led by Arvid Västgöte after the city's magistrates agree to leave the northern gate of the city open.

events.title: Battle of Sincouwaan
events.blurb: Following the Battle of Sincouwaan at sea between the ships of the Chinese Empire and the Kingdom of Portugal,

events.title: Franconian War

events.title: The Spanish expedition into Nicaragua ends as the Europeans arrive back in…
events.blurb: The Spanish expedition into Nicaragua ends as the Europeans arrive back in Panama in canoes, having been forced to abandon their ships.

events.title: Jan van Essen and Hendrik Vos become the first Lutheran martyrs, burned at the…
events.blurb: Jan van Essen and Hendrik Vos become the first Lutheran martyrs, burned at the stake in Brussels at the Grote Markt. In response to the executions, Martin Luther composed a hymn called "A New Song Be By Us Begun".

events.title: Wijerd Jelckama, a Frisian warlord and military commander, is executed in…
events.blurb: Wijerd Jelckama, a Frisian warlord and military commander, is executed in Leeuwarden, ending the Frisian rebellion fought by the Arumer Black Heap.

events.title: In what is now Mexico, the conquistador Gonzalo de Sandoval founds the city of…
events.blurb: In what is now Mexico, the conquistador Gonzalo de Sandoval founds the city of Colima.

events.title: Spanish conquest of Nicaragua
events.blurb: Spanish conquest of Nicaragua: An agreement is made for an expedition by conquistadores into Nicaragua organized by Pedrarias Dávila.

events.title: After receiving word from Malaya that Portuguese forces were attacking the…
events.blurb: After receiving word from Malaya that Portuguese forces were attacking the Sultanate of Patani and the Malacca Sultanate on the Malaysian peninsula, the Chinese Emperor Zhengde orders extermination of all persons from Portugal,

events.title: A conclave of 32 cardinals begins deliberations in Rome to elect a successor…
events.blurb: A conclave of 32 cardinals begins deliberations in Rome to elect a successor to the late Pope Adrian VI. Three other cardinals arrive on October 6 and balloting begins for a new Pope.

events.title: Hürrem Pasha, the Ottoman Empire's Governor-General of the Damascus Eyalet…
events.blurb: Hürrem Pasha, the Ottoman Empire's Governor-General of the Damascus Eyalet (which includes parts of what will become Syria, Israel, Jordan and Palestine) begins a punitive expedition through Lebanon against the Druze of Chouf.

events.title: At Santa Maria in Via Lata, Cardinal Marco Cornaro carries out the coronation…
events.blurb: At Santa Maria in Via Lata, Cardinal Marco Cornaro carries out the coronation of Pope Clement at the church of Santa Maria in Via Lata in Rome.

events.title: Setting off from the Mexican Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan with an army of 550…
events.blurb: Setting off from the Mexican Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan with an army of 550 Spanish soldiers and 120 horses, Pedro de Alvarado y Contreras begins the Spanish conquest of Guatemala.

events.title: Tecun Uman, the K'iche' Maya ruler of Guatemala's highlands, is killed in a…
events.blurb: Tecun Uman, the K'iche' Maya ruler of Guatemala's highlands, is killed in a battle near Quetzaltenango between the K'iche' Maya people and the invading Spanish conquistadors led by Pedro Alvarado.

events.title: da Verrazzano's expedition makes landfall at Cape Fear at what is later the U
events.blurb: da Verrazzano's expedition makes landfall at Cape Fear at what is later the U.S. state of North Carolina.

events.title: Battle of the Sesia
events.blurb: Battle of the Sesia: Spanish forces under Charles de Lannoy defeat the French army in Italy, under William de Bonnivet. The French, now commanded by François de St. Pol, withdraw from the Italian Peninsula.

events.title: Tahmasp I becomes the ruler of the Safavid Empire, following the death of his…
events.blurb: Tahmasp I becomes the ruler of the Safavid Empire, following the death of his father, Shah Ismail I.

events.title: Atiquipaque, the most important city of the Xinca people, is conquered by the…
events.blurb: Atiquipaque, the most important city of the Xinca people, is conquered by the Spanish, resulting in a significant reduction in the Xinca population.

events.title: Battle of Acajutla
events.blurb: Battle of Acajutla: Spanish conquistador Pedro de Alvarado defeats a battalion of Pipiles, in the neighborhoods of present day Acajutla, El Salvador.

events.title: German Peasants' War
events.blurb: German Peasants' War: Hans Müller von Bulgenbach gathered peasants in Stühlingen and formed the "Evangelical Brotherhood", pledging to emancipate peasants across Germany. An revolt spread in southwestern Germany.

events.title: Treaty of Malmö
events.blurb: By the Treaty of Malmö signed on Sweden withdraws from the Kalmar Union with Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

events.title: Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro, Hernando de Luque and Diego de Almagro…
events.blurb: Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro, Hernando de Luque and Diego de Almagro all set off on the first of three expeditions to conquer Peru, taking along 80 men and 40 horses, but the venture is halted in Colombia.

events.title: The Bundesbrief is adopted by the members of the Three Leagues of Switzerland…
events.blurb: The Bundesbrief is adopted by the members of the Three Leagues of Switzerland (the League of God's House, the League of the Ten Jurisdictions, and the Grey League) as a common constitution.

events.title: John Fleming, 2nd Lord Fleming, Lord Chancellor of Scotland since 1517, is…
events.blurb: John Fleming, 2nd Lord Fleming, Lord Chancellor of Scotland since 1517, is assassinated by John Tweedie of Drummelzier (chief of Clan Tweedie) and others.

events.title: Treaty of Tordesillas (1524)
events.blurb: The Treaty of Tordesillas is signed between representatives of Honoré I, Lord of Monaco and of King Charles of Spain, and places Monaco under the protection of Spain.

events.title: Francisco Hernandez de Cordoba founds the city of Granada, Nicaragua, the…
events.blurb: Francisco Hernandez de Cordoba founds the city of Granada, Nicaragua, the oldest Hispanic city in the mainland America.

events.title: The ducal palace of Celle is constructed in Germany
events.blurb: The ducal palace of Celle is constructed in Germany.

events.title: Strasbourg joins the Christliches Burgrecht, the Protestant alliance of Swiss…
events.blurb: Strasbourg joins the Christliches Burgrecht, the Protestant alliance of Swiss cities.

events.title: Tangaxuan II, last cazonci of the Purépecha Empire, is executed by…
events.blurb: Tangaxuan II, last cazonci of the Purépecha Empire, is executed by conquistador Nuño de Guzmán, ending the Purépecha Empire's independence from Spain.

events.title: The Tribute of the Maltese Falcon, an agreement by the Grand Master of the…
events.blurb: The Tribute of the Maltese Falcon, an agreement by the Grand Master of the Order of St John of Jerusalem to pay an annual tribute to the Charles V, King of Sicily,

events.title: At the invitation of the Holy Roman Emperor, the members of the Imperial Diet…
events.blurb: At the invitation of the Holy Roman Emperor, the members of the Imperial Diet open their session at Augsburg in Germany to prepare the Augsburg Confession, an official imperial set of rules for Protestantism.

events.title: The Kaqchikel people, a tribe of the Maya people of what is now the…
events.blurb: The Kaqchikel people, a tribe of the Maya people of what is now the Sacatepéquez Department of Guatemala, surrender to the Spanish conquistadors.

events.title: The Augsburg Confession is presented to Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor
events.blurb: The Augsburg Confession is presented to Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor.

events.title: The Tetrapolitan Confession, a Protestant confession of faith, is submitted…
events.blurb: The Tetrapolitan Confession, a Protestant confession of faith, is submitted jointly to Holy Roman Emperor Charles V on behalf of the southern German cities of Konstanz, Lindau, Memmingen and Strasbourg.

events.title: Turkish Ottoman troops attempt to take the Hungarian town of Nagykörű but,…
events.blurb: Turkish Ottoman troops attempt to take the Hungarian town of Nagykörű but, according to local legend, the Turkish soldiers are lost in a marsh protecting the city.

events.title: The transfer of Tripoli, in North Africa, from Spain to the Knights of Malta,…
events.blurb: The transfer of Tripoli, in North Africa, from Spain to the Knights of Malta, is formally accomplished, four months after an agreement was reached with Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, King of Spain and King of Sicily.

events.title: At Neue Augsburg (now Coro in the nation of Venezuela), German explorer…
events.blurb: At Neue Augsburg (now Coro in the nation of Venezuela), German explorer Nikolaus Federmann becomes the acting governor of Klein-Venedig ("Little Venice") Germany's short-lived South American colony as Governor Ambrosius Ehinger takes a…

events.title: Battle of Gavinana
events.blurb: Battle of Gavinana: Florence is captured by Spanish troops under Prince Philibert of Chalon (who is killed in the action).

events.title: The miraculous portrait of Saint Dominic in Soriano appears in Soriano…
events.blurb: The miraculous portrait of Saint Dominic in Soriano appears in Soriano Calabro, Calabria.

events.title: The Knights of Malta are formed, when the Knights Hospitaller are given Malta…
events.blurb: The Knights of Malta are formed, when the Knights Hospitaller are given Malta by Charles V. They transfer the island capital from Mdina to Birgu.

events.title: St. Felix's flood devastates Zeeland
events.blurb: St. Felix's flood devastates Zeeland: a large part of the Verdronken Land van Reimerswaal is lost leading to decline of the city of Reimerswaal.

events.title: Tabinshwehti succeeds his father Mingyi Nyo as king of the Toungoo dynasty,…
events.blurb: Tabinshwehti succeeds his father Mingyi Nyo as king of the Toungoo dynasty, following the latter's death.

events.title: Martim Afonso de Sousa's expedition sets out for Brazil from Portugal
events.blurb: Martim Afonso de Sousa's expedition sets out for Brazil from Portugal.

events.title: Humayun starts to rule the Mughal Empire after Babur's death
events.blurb: Humayun starts to rule the Mughal Empire after Babur's death.

events.title: In present-day Czech Republic, the Zástřizl family held Bohdalice and…
events.blurb: In present-day Czech Republic, the Zástřizl family held Bohdalice and Pavlovice from 1413 until 1531.

events.title: Conquistador Francisco de Montejo claims Chichen Itza as capital of…
events.blurb: Conquistador Francisco de Montejo claims Chichen Itza as capital of Spanish-ruled Yucatán.

events.title: Kõpu Lighthouse is completed
events.blurb: Kõpu Lighthouse is completed.

events.title: A severe drought in Henan province, China, coupled with a gigantic swarm of…
events.blurb: A severe drought in Henan province, China, coupled with a gigantic swarm of locusts in the summer, forces many in destitute agricultural communities to turn to cannibalism to avoid dying by starvation.

events.title: Andrea Alciato publishes Emblemata
events.blurb: Andrea Alciato publishes Emblemata.

events.title: The University of Sarajevo is founded by Gazi Husrev-beg based on Sufi philosophy
events.blurb: The University of Sarajevo is founded by Gazi Husrev-beg based on Sufi philosophy.

events.title: 1531 Lisbon earthquake
events.blurb: 1531 Lisbon earthquake: More than 30,000 people are killed in Portugal in an earthquake and subsequent tsunami.

events.title: Battle of Antukyah
events.blurb: or March – Battle of Antukyah: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi of the Adal Sultanate defeats the Ethiopian army.

events.title: Lutheran princes in the Holy Roman Empire form an alliance known as the…
events.blurb: Lutheran princes in the Holy Roman Empire form an alliance known as the Schmalkaldic League.

events.title: In India, the fortress of Mandu, capital of the Malwa Sultanate, falls as…
events.blurb: In India, the fortress of Mandu, capital of the Malwa Sultanate, falls as Malwa's Sultan Mahmúd II and his sons surrender to Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.

events.title: Poisoning Act 1530
events.blurb: King Henry VIII gives royal assent to numerous acts at the close of the session of the English Parliament, including the Poisoning Act 1530 (providing for boiling to death people convicted of poisioning other persons);

events.title: Battle of Puná
events.blurb: Battle of Puná: Francisco Pizarro defeats the native inhabitants of the island of Puná, off of the coast of what is now the South American nation of Ecuador.

events.title: In the Songhai Empire that rules most of West Africa and the Niger River…
events.blurb: In the Songhai Empire that rules most of West Africa and the Niger River valley, the Emperor Askiya Musa is assassinated by his brothers after less than two years on the throne. Askia Mohammad Benkan is enthroned the same day.

events.title: The third Dalecarlian rebellion in Sweden is settled on St

events.title: Minkhaung of Mrauk-U, the Burmese King of Arakan since 1521, is killed in a…
events.blurb: (11th waxing of Nayon 893 ME) Minkhaung of Mrauk-U, the Burmese King of Arakan since 1521, is killed in a coup d'etat by the rebellious Governor of Thandwe, Min Pa.

events.title: The city of San Juan del Río, Mexico, is founded

events.blurb: Battle of Obertyn: The Moldavians are defeated by Polish forces under Jan Tarnowski, allowing the Poles to recapture Pokucie.

events.title: The first Parliament of Ireland in more than nine years is opened at Kilkea…
events.blurb: The first Parliament of Ireland in more than nine years is opened at Kilkea Castle, near Castledermot, County Kildare, and continues until its adjournment on October 31.

events.title: In Burma (now Myanmar), the formal coronation of General Min Pa as King Min…
events.blurb: (5th waxing of Thadingyut 893 ME) In Burma (now Myanmar), the formal coronation of General Min Pa as King Min Bin of Arakan takes place in the Arakan capital, Mrauk U.

events.title: At the age of 35, King Gustav I Vasa of Sweden is married for the first time,…
events.blurb: At the age of 35, King Gustav I Vasa of Sweden is married for the first time, taking Catherine of Saxe-Lauenburg as his bride on her 18th birthday.

events.title: Battle of Amba Sel
events.blurb: Battle of Amba Sel: Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi again defeats the army of Dawit II, Emperor of Ethiopia. The southern part of Ethiopia thus falls under Imam Ahmad's control.

events.title: Mary, mother of Jesus, in the guise of Our Lady of Guadalupe, appears…
events.blurb: Mary, mother of Jesus, in the guise of Our Lady of Guadalupe, appears imprinted on the tilmàtli of Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin, an Aztec convert to Catholicism, in Tepeyac near Mexico City.

events.title: The Prince is published, five years after the death of the author, Niccolò…
events.blurb: The Prince is published, five years after the death of the author, Niccolò Machiavelli.

events.title: Battle of the Maule
events.blurb: Possible date for the Battle of the Maule between Incas and Mapuches, according to historian Osvaldo Silva.

events.title: Stamford School is founded in England by William Radcliffe

events.title: São Vicente is established as the first permanent Portuguese settlement in Brazil
events.blurb: São Vicente is established as the first permanent Portuguese settlement in Brazil.

events.title: The Deceived Ones (Gl'ingannati), a stage comedy written collectively by the…
events.blurb: The Deceived Ones (Gl'ingannati), a stage comedy written collectively by the Accademia degli Intronati in Siena, makes its debut as part of the festivities of the Italian city's annual carnival.

events.title: William Warham, the 81-year-old Roman Catholic Archbishop of Canterbury,…
events.blurb: William Warham, the 81-year-old Roman Catholic Archbishop of Canterbury, publicly declares that he is disassociating himself from all acts of the English Parliament that are prejudicial to papal authority.

events.title: The Supplication against the Ordinaries is presented to Henry VIII by Thomas…
events.blurb: The Supplication against the Ordinaries is presented to Henry VIII by Thomas More the Speaker of the House of Commons.

events.title: Anne Boleyn is created Marquess of Pembroke by her fiancé, King Henry VIII of…
events.blurb: Anne Boleyn is created Marquess of Pembroke by her fiancé, King Henry VIII of England.

events.title: The Burmese monarch Min Bin, King of Arrakan, leads a combined invasion force…
events.blurb: (9th waxing of Tazaungmon 894 ME) The Burmese monarch Min Bin, King of Arrakan, leads a combined invasion force of 12,000 people (three armies of 11,000 men in a three-pronged attack,

events.blurb: A fire strikes the cathedral in Chambéry, now a part of France, but at the time a part of Italy's Duchy of Savoy.

events.title: Cartagena, Colombia, is founded by Pedro de Heredia
events.blurb: Cartagena, Colombia, is founded by Pedro de Heredia.

events.title: Pechenga Monastery is founded, in the far north of the Grand Duchy of Moscow
events.blurb: Pechenga Monastery is founded, in the far north of the Grand Duchy of Moscow.

events.title: Thomas Audley, 1st Baron Audley of Walden, is appointed Lord Chancellor of England
events.blurb: Thomas Audley, 1st Baron Audley of Walden, is appointed Lord Chancellor of England.

events.title: The order of the Clerics Regular of Saint Paul, more commonly called the…
events.blurb: The order of the Clerics Regular of Saint Paul, more commonly called the Barnabites, is given papal approval by Pope Clement VII in the brief Vota per quae vos.

events.title: Thomas Cranmer becomes Archbishop of Canterbury
events.blurb: Thomas Cranmer becomes Archbishop of Canterbury.

events.title: Sapa Inca Atahualpa is executed by garotte, at the orders of Francisco Pizarro…
events.blurb: Sapa Inca Atahualpa is executed by garotte, at the orders of Francisco Pizarro in Cajamarca.

events.title: Antonio Sedeño, the Spanish Colonial Governor of Trinidad, comes under attack…
events.blurb: Antonio Sedeño, the Spanish Colonial Governor of Trinidad, comes under attack along with his troops by the Kalinago people, indigenous to the area.

events.title: The 14-year olds Henry, Duke of Orléans
events.blurb: The 14-year olds Henry, Duke of Orléans – the future King Henry II of France – and Catherine de' Medici are married at the Église Saint-Ferréol les Augustins in Marseille.

events.title: Ivan IV succeeds his father Vasili III as Grand Prince of Muscovy at the age…
events.blurb: Ivan IV succeeds his father Vasili III as Grand Prince of Muscovy at the age of three; he will rule in Russia until his death in 1584.

events.title: Thomas the Apostle
events.blurb: (Feast of St Thomas the Apostle) – Hernando de Grijalva and his crew become the first persons discover the uninhabited Revillagigedo Islands, off the Pacific coast of Mexico, reporting the finding of what Grijalva names Isla Santo Tomé,

events.title: Grijalva and his crew discover Isla de los Inocentes, probably San Benedicto…
events.blurb: Grijalva and his crew discover Isla de los Inocentes, probably San Benedicto Island.

events.title: Gargantua is published by François Rabelais
events.blurb: Gargantua is published by François Rabelais.

events.title: Manco Inca Yupanqui is crowned as Sapa Inca in Cusco, Peru by Spanish…
events.blurb: Manco Inca Yupanqui is crowned as Sapa Inca in Cusco, Peru by Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro, in succession to his brother Túpac Huallpa (d. October 1533).

events.title: The Parliament of England passes the Act Respecting the Oath to the…
events.blurb: The Parliament of England passes the Act Respecting the Oath to the Succession, recognising the marriage of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn, and their children as the legitimate heirs to the throne.

events.title: Submission of the Clergy Act 1533
events.blurb: The Submission of the Clergy Act 1533 becomes law in England, requiring submission of the clergy, that is, churchmen are to submit to the king and the publication of ecclesiastical laws without royal permission is forbidden.

events.title: Easter
events.blurb: (Easter Sunday) – Anabaptist Jan Matthys is killed by the Landsknechte, who laid siege to Münster on the day he predicted as the Second Coming of Christ. His follower John of Leiden takes control of the city.

events.title: Jacques Cartier explores Newfoundland, while searching for the Northwest Passage
events.blurb: Jacques Cartier explores Newfoundland, while searching for the Northwest Passage.

events.title: Copenhagen opens its gates to Count Christopher of Oldenburg, leading the army…
events.blurb: Copenhagen opens its gates to Count Christopher of Oldenburg, leading the army of Lübeck (and the Hanseatic League), nominally in the interests of the deposed King Christian II of Denmark.

events.title: Election of Christian III
events.blurb: The Election of Christian III, as King of Denmark, takes place in the town of Rye.

events.title: The first known exchange between Europeans and the natives of the Gulf of St
events.blurb: The first known exchange between Europeans and the natives of the Gulf of St. Lawrence occurs in what is now New Brunswick.

events.title: Ignatius of Loyola and six others take the vows that lead to the establishment…
events.blurb: Ignatius of Loyola and six others take the vows that lead to the establishment of the Jesuits (the Society of Jesus), in Montmartre,

events.title: Piero de Ponte becomes the 45th Grandmaster of the Knights Hospitaller
events.blurb: Piero de Ponte becomes the 45th Grandmaster of the Knights Hospitaller.

events.title: As the Michaelmas fair opens in Wittenberg, Martin Luther's translation of the…
events.blurb: As the Michaelmas fair opens in Wittenberg, Martin Luther's translation of the complete Christian Bible into German is offered for sale for the first time.

events.title: Huguenots post placards all over France attacking the Catholic Mass, provoking…
events.blurb: Huguenots post placards all over France attacking the Catholic Mass, provoking a violent sectarian reaction (Affair of the Placards).

events.title: The English Reformation Parliament passes the Act of Supremacy, establishing…
events.blurb: The English Reformation Parliament passes the Act of Supremacy, establishing Henry VIII as supreme head of the Church of England.

events.title: Spanish colonial administrator Antonio de Mendoza is appointed as the first…
events.blurb: Spanish colonial administrator Antonio de Mendoza is appointed as the first Viceroy of New Spain, with jurisdiction on behalf of King Carlos of Spain over a large area of what is now Mexico and the southwestern United States,

events.title: Lima, now the capital of Peru, is founded by Francisco Pizarro, as Ciudad de…
events.blurb: Lima, now the capital of Peru, is founded by Francisco Pizarro, as Ciudad de los Reyes.

events.title: The French Protestant leaders of the October 1534 Affaire des Placards are…
events.blurb: The French Protestant leaders of the October 1534 Affaire des Placards are burned to death in front of the Cathedral of Notre-Dame de Paris and witnessed by a large crowd that includes King François and the visiting Ottoman diplomats.

events.title: George Joye publishes his Apologye in Antwerp, to clear his name from the…
events.blurb: George Joye publishes his Apologye in Antwerp, to clear his name from the accusations of William Tyndale.

events.title: Go-Nara, who has ruled since 1526 is formally installed as the 105th Emperor…
events.blurb: (Tenbun 4, 26th day of 2nd month) Go-Nara, who has ruled since 1526 is formally installed as the 105th Emperor of Japan

events.title: The visiting Ottoman envoys to France depart from Marseille, six months after…
events.blurb: The visiting Ottoman envoys to France depart from Marseille, six months after having arrived from Istanbul in October.

events.title: The first of the English Carthusian Martyrs of London, John Houghton of…
events.blurb: The first of the English Carthusian Martyrs of London, John Houghton of London, Robert Lawrence of Beauvale, and Augustine Webster of Axholme are executed at Tyburn after refusing to sign the English Oath of Supremacy.

events.title: In Amsterdam, a small troop of Anabaptists, led by the minister Jacob van…
events.blurb: In Amsterdam, a small troop of Anabaptists, led by the minister Jacob van Geel, attacks the city hall, in an attempted coup to seize the city.

events.title: William Tyndale is arrested in Antwerp for heresy, in relation to his Bible…
events.blurb: William Tyndale is arrested in Antwerp for heresy, in relation to his Bible translation, and imprisoned in Vilvoorde.

events.title: The Conquest of Tunis by Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, begins with the…
events.blurb: The Conquest of Tunis by Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, begins with the destruction of Barbarossa's fleet. Following the eventual capture of the city from the Ottoman Empire, around 30,000 inhabitants are massacred.

events.title: Battle of Bornholm
events.blurb: Battle of Bornholm: Combined Swedish and Danish fleets defeat the Hanseatic navy.

events.title: Cardinal John Fisher, Bishop of Rochester, is executed for his refusal to…
events.blurb: Cardinal John Fisher, Bishop of Rochester, is executed for his refusal to swear an oath of loyalty to King Henry VIII of England.

events.title: Diego de Almagro leaves the recently conquered Inca capital of Cuzco to lead…
events.blurb: Diego de Almagro leaves the recently conquered Inca capital of Cuzco to lead an expedition to Chile.

events.title: Sir Thomas More, author of Utopia and one time Lord Chancellor of England, is…
events.blurb: Sir Thomas More, author of Utopia and one time Lord Chancellor of England, is executed for treason, after refusing to recognize King Henry VIII as head of the English Church, and separate from the Roman Catholic Church.

events.title: Archdeacon Charles Reynolds (cleric), envoy to James V, Charles V, and Pope…
events.blurb: Archdeacon Charles Reynolds (cleric), envoy to James V, Charles V, and Pope Paul III, is buried in Rome. He died of malaria while lobbying for the excommunication of King Henry VIII for heresy.

events.title: Pope Paul III issues a papal bull, Sublimis Deus, to appoint a commission of…
events.blurb: Pope Paul III issues a papal bull, Sublimis Deus, to appoint a commission of five cardinals and three bishops to carry out a reform of the city of Rome and the Roman Curia,

events.title: The first complete English-language Bible is printed in Antwerp, with…
events.blurb: The first complete English-language Bible is printed in Antwerp, with translations by William Tyndale and Myles Coverdale.

events.title: Eighteen days after the death of Francesco II Sforza, Charles V, Holy Roman…
events.blurb: Eighteen days after the death of Francesco II Sforza, Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor and King of Spain Charles V claims the Duchy of Milan as his inheritance under Sforza's will.

events.title: Jakob Hutter, leader of the Hutterites is arrested along with his wife in…
events.blurb: Jakob Hutter, leader of the Hutterites is arrested along with his wife in Klausen in the Tyrol region on the Italian side of the Alps. The two are taken to the prison at the fortress in Bronzolo.

events.blurb: The Consejo de i Diexe, governing body for the Republic of Venice, votes to replace the republic's treasury, made of wood, with the Zecca a structure that has stone vaults, and invites architects to submit designs.

events.title: Battle of Reynogüelén
events.blurb: Battle of Reynogüelén: Spanish conquistadors defeat a group of Mapuches in Chile, during the expedition of Diego de Almagro.

events.title: On "a great misty morning such as hath seldom been seen", Robert Pakington, a…
events.blurb: On "a great misty morning such as hath seldom been seen", Robert Pakington, a London merchant and a member of the English Parliament, becomes the first person in Britain to be murdered with a handgun,

events.title: Italian War of 1536–1538
events.blurb: The Italian War of 1536–1538 resumes between Francis I of France and Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor. Francis seizes control of Savoy, and captures Turin.

events.title: Battle of Un no Kuchi
events.blurb: Battle of Un no Kuchi: Takeda Family forces defeat Hiraga Genshin.

events.title: Luis Sarmento is the Imperial ambassador to Portugal
events.blurb: Luis Sarmento is the Imperial ambassador to Portugal.

events.blurb: The Colegio de Santa Cruz de Tlatelolco, the oldest European school of higher learning in the Americas, is established by Franciscans in Mexico City.

events.blurb: John of Leiden, Bernhard Knipperdolling and Bernhard Krechting are executed in Münster for their roles in the Münster Rebellion.

events.title: A Franco-Ottoman alliance exempts French merchants from Ottoman law and allows…
events.blurb: A Franco-Ottoman alliance exempts French merchants from Ottoman law and allows them to travel, buy and sell throughout the sultan's dominions, and to pay low customs duties on French imports and exports. The compact is confirmed in 1569.

events.blurb: Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha, Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire since 1523, is executed after falling into disfavor with Hürrem Sultan, the wife of Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent.

events.blurb: Ayas Mehmed Pasha is appointed by the Sultan Suleiman to be the new Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Count's Feud

events.title: The Reformation Parliament in England passes an Act for the Dissolution of the…
events.blurb: The Reformation Parliament in England passes an Act for the Dissolution of the monasteries.

events.title: San Juan Bautista del Teul is founded by Cristóbal de Oñate in New Spain
events.blurb: San Juan Bautista del Teul is founded by Cristóbal de Oñate in New Spain.

events.title: Spanish navigator Andrés de Urdaneta and a few companions arrive in Lisbon…
events.blurb: Spanish navigator Andrés de Urdaneta and a few companions arrive in Lisbon from the Maluku Islands, completing a westward circumnavigation which began with the Loaísa expedition of 1525.

events.title: San Pedro Sula is founded by Pedro de Alvarado in Honduras
events.blurb: San Pedro Sula is founded by Pedro de Alvarado in Honduras.

events.title: The papal legation of Cardinals Marino Caracciolo, Francisco Quiñones, and…
events.blurb: The papal legation of Cardinals Marino Caracciolo, Francisco Quiñones, and Agostino Trivulzio meets with Emperor Charles V at Savigliano, south of Turin on orders of Pope Paul III.

events.title: The papal legation arrives in France, arriving at Lyon, to meet with King…
events.blurb: The papal legation arrives in France, arriving at Lyon, to meet with King Francois I.

events.title: Three days after the arrival of the peacekeeping team in Lyon, and 15 days…
events.blurb: Three days after the arrival of the peacekeeping team in Lyon, and 15 days after the legation had met with the Holy Roman Emperor to avoid war, troops of the Holy Roman Empire invade France,

events.title: Guelders Wars
events.blurb: Guelders Wars: Battle of Heiligerlee – Danish allies of Charles II, Duke of Guelders, under command of Meindert van Ham, are defeated by Habsburg forces under Georg Schenck van Toutenburg in the Low Countries.

events.title: Francis III of Brittany, Dauphin of France, dies having caught a chill after a…
events.blurb: Francis III of Brittany, Dauphin of France, dies having caught a chill after a game of tennis which had developed into a fever;

events.title: The Pilgrimage of Grace, a rebellion in England against Henry VIII's church…
events.blurb: The Pilgrimage of Grace, a rebellion in England against Henry VIII's church reforms, begins in Lincolnshire and spreads across the kingdom to most of Yorkshire, and parts of Northumberland, Durham, Cumberland and Westmorland.

events.title: Cardinal Agostino Trivulzio, the envoy of Pope Paul III, files his report of…
events.blurb: Cardinal Agostino Trivulzio, the envoy of Pope Paul III, files his report of his peace mission to negotiate an agreement between the Holy Roman Empire and France.

events.title: Siege of Steinvikholm (1537)
events.blurb: The siege by Norwegian and Danish Protestants of Steinvikholm Castle in Norway, the former residence of the last Roman Catholic Archbishop of Norway, ended after a month when the Catholic defenders surrendered to the Danish commander,

events.title: Kashmiri sultan Muhammad Shah dies and he is succeeded by Shams al-Din Shah II…
events.blurb: Kashmiri sultan Muhammad Shah dies and he is succeeded by Shams al-Din Shah II as sultan of Kashmiri Shah Mir Sultanate in 1537.

events.title: Kiritimati (Acea or "Christmas Island") is probably sighted by the Spanish…
events.blurb: Kiritimati (Acea or "Christmas Island") is probably sighted by the Spanish mutineers from Hernando de Grijalva's expedition.

events.title: Publication is made of two complete Bible translations into English, both…
events.blurb: Publication is made of two complete Bible translations into English, both based on Tyndale's.

events.title: Princess Madeleine of Valois, the 16-year-old daughter of François I, King of…
events.blurb: Princess Madeleine of Valois, the 16-year-old daughter of François I, King of France, is married to King James V of Scotland in a ceremony at the cathedral of Notre-Dame de Paris.

events.title: Alessandro de' Medici, Duke of Florence is assassinated by Lorenzino de'…
events.blurb: Alessandro de' Medici, Duke of Florence is assassinated by Lorenzino de' Medici, a distant cousin, who claims that he wants to reintroduce republican rule but has to flee to Venice.

events.title: Francis Bigod, leader of Bigod's rebellion is captured at Cumberland by the…
events.blurb: Francis Bigod, leader of Bigod's rebellion is captured at Cumberland by the English Army and imprisoned at Carlisle Castle. He is hanged at Tyburn on June 2.

events.title: Chipatá, now in the Santander Department of the Republic of Colombia, is…
events.blurb: Chipatá, now in the Santander Department of the Republic of Colombia, is founded by the Spanish conquistadors Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada and his brother Hernán Pérez de Quesada as the first settlement in what will become the Spanish colony…

events.title: Recife is founded by the Portuguese, in Brazil
events.blurb: Recife is founded by the Portuguese, in Brazil.

events.title: The Archbishop of Norway, Olav Engelbrektsson, flees from Trondheim to Lier,…
events.blurb: The Archbishop of Norway, Olav Engelbrektsson, flees from Trondheim to Lier, Belgium.

events.title: Spanish conquest of the Muisca
events.blurb: Spanish conquest of the Muisca: Bacatá, the main settlement of the Muisca Confederation, is conquered by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada, effectively ending the Confederation in the Colombian Eastern Andes.

events.title: Rodrigo Orgóñez occupies and sacks the Inca center of Vitcos at the battle of…
events.blurb: Rodrigo Orgóñez occupies and sacks the Inca center of Vitcos at the battle of Abancay, but Manco Inca Yupanqui escapes and establishes the independent Neo-Inca State elsewhere in Vilcabamba, Peru.

events.title: Upon the death of his father, Bhim Singh, Ratan Singh becomes the new ruler of…
events.blurb: Upon the death of his father, Bhim Singh, Ratan Singh becomes the new ruler of the Kingdom of Amber with a capital at Amber in what is now the Rajasthan state in India

events.title: Ottoman–Venetian War (1537–1540)
events.blurb: The third Ottoman–Venetian War begins as the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent leads an invasion of the Republic of Venice. The war will continue until October 2, 1540.

events.title: The city of Asunción, now the capital of the South American nation of…
events.blurb: The city of Asunción, now the capital of the South American nation of Paraguay, is founded by Juan de Salazar de Espinosa.

events.title: The Honourable Artillery Company, the oldest surviving regiment in the British…
events.blurb: The Honourable Artillery Company, the oldest surviving regiment in the British Army, and the second most senior, is formed.

events.title: Siege of Corfu (1537)
events.blurb: The siege of the island of Corfu is started by the Ottoman Empire Navy, commanded by Suleiman the Magnificent. Suleiman abandons the siege in September after an outbreak of plague, and the Ottoman troops return home.

events.title: King Christian III of Denmark and Norway appoints Gjeble Pederssøn as Norway's…
events.blurb: King Christian III of Denmark and Norway appoints Gjeble Pederssøn as Norway's first Lutheran bishop for the Church of Norway.

events.title: Following the baptism of her son, the future Edward VI of England, Jane…
events.blurb: Following the baptism of her son, the future Edward VI of England, Jane Seymour begins suffering from puerperal fever. The Queen consort dies nine days later.

events.title: In what is now the Central American nation of Honduras, the Spanish…
events.blurb: In what is now the Central American nation of Honduras, the Spanish conquistadore Alonso de Cáceres arrives at the Peñol de Cerquín, the mountaintop fortress of King Lempira of the Lencas,

events.title: Alfonso d'Avalos, the Marquis of Vasto in Italy, enters into a three-month…
events.blurb: Alfonso d'Avalos, the Marquis of Vasto in Italy, enters into a three-month truce with the French Duke of Montmorency to negotiate a peace for which areas would be under French control.

events.title: Petar Keglević takes office as the new Ottoman Governor of Croatia and of Slavonia
events.blurb: Petar Keglević takes office as the new Ottoman Governor of Croatia and of Slavonia.

events.title: The Ordonnance de Montpellier, establishing the first system in Europe for all…
events.blurb: The Ordonnance de Montpellier, establishing the first system in Europe for all writers to submit copies of their printed work to the government for review and maintenance in a library, is signed into law by King François I of France.

events.title: Dissolution of the Monasteries in England
events.blurb: Dissolution of the Monasteries in England: Byland Abbey is dissolved.

events.title: The formal wedding of Mary of Guise and King James V of Scotland takes place…
events.blurb: The formal wedding of Mary of Guise and King James V of Scotland takes place at St Andrews Cathedral.

events.title: Sucre, Bolivia, is founded under the name Ciudad de la Plata de la Nueva Toledo
events.blurb: Sucre, Bolivia, is founded under the name Ciudad de la Plata de la Nueva Toledo.

events.title: Leonard Grey, England's Lord Deputy of Ireland, successfully negotiates a…
events.blurb: Leonard Grey, England's Lord Deputy of Ireland, successfully negotiates a truce in the semi-independent County Laois, formerly an Irish Kingdom, over the areas leadership. between Peter O'Moore and Rory Lysaght.

events.title: General Johann Katzianer of the Holy Roman Empire, on trial in Vienna for the…
events.blurb: General Johann Katzianer of the Holy Roman Empire, on trial in Vienna for the disastrous Imperial campaign against the Ottoman Empire and for desertion during the Battle of Gorjani,

events.title: The Holy League, an alliance of Christian nations (the Papal States and the…
events.blurb: The Holy League, an alliance of Christian nations (the Papal States and the Republic of Venice, the Knights Hospitaller of Malta, Spain and the Spanish-ruled Viceroyalty of Naples and Sicily),

events.title: Treaty of Nagyvárad
events.blurb: Treaty of Nagyvárad: Peace is declared between Ferdinand I, future Holy Roman Emperor and the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Garcia de Noronha is appointed as the new Governor-General of Portuguese India…
events.blurb: Garcia de Noronha is appointed as the new Governor-General of Portuguese India by King João III. He sails to Goa and arrives less than three weeks later.

events.title: Battle of Las Salinas
events.blurb: Battle of Las Salinas: In Peru, Almagro is defeated by Francisco Pizarro, who then seizes Cusco.

events.title: Mary of Guise is wed by proxy to King James V of Scotland, while she is at the…
events.blurb: Mary of Guise is wed by proxy to King James V of Scotland, while she is at the Château de Châteaudun and he is in London, with neither of the two seeing each other.

events.title: A joint delegation of Lutherans from various German cities arrives in England…
events.blurb: A joint delegation of Lutherans from various German cities arrives in England for meetings with King Henry VIII; Thomas Cranmer, Archbishop of Canterbury; and Thomas Cromwell, the former Chief Minister of England.

events.title: The betrothal ceremony of 12-year-old Princess Elisabeth, niece of Charles V,…
events.blurb: The betrothal ceremony of 12-year-old Princess Elisabeth, niece of Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor to the 17-year-old Prince Sigismund II Augustus,

events.title: The city of Guayaquil, now the largest city in the South American nation of…
events.blurb: The city of Guayaquil, now the largest city in the South American nation of Ecuador is founded by Spanish conqueror Francisco de Orellana in the location of a Quechua native village of the same name.

events.title: Bogotá, Colombia is founded by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada
events.blurb: Bogotá, Colombia is founded by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada.

events.title: Ştefan V Lăcustă of the Bogdan-Musat dynasty in Romania is appointed as the…
events.blurb: Ştefan V Lăcustă of the Bogdan-Musat dynasty in Romania is appointed as the new Prince of Moldavia by the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman, replacing uncle, Petru Rareș.

events.title: Battle of Preveza
events.blurb: Battle of Preveza: The Ottoman fleet of Suleiman the Magnificent, under the command of Hayreddin Barbarossa, defeats the Holy League of Emperor Charles V, under the command of Andrea Doria.

events.title: The last significant volcanic eruption in the Phlegraean Fields of Italy…
events.blurb: The last significant volcanic eruption in the Phlegraean Fields of Italy begins and lasts one week.

events.title: The eruption the Italian volcano ends after seven days, having created Monte Nuovo
events.blurb: The eruption the Italian volcano ends after seven days, having created Monte Nuovo.

events.title: The first university of the New World, the Universidad Santo Tomás de Aquino,…
events.blurb: The first university of the New World, the Universidad Santo Tomás de Aquino, is founded on the island of Hispaniola in Santo Domingo.

events.title: Siege of Diu (1538)
events.blurb: The siege of the Indian city of Diu ends as the Gujarat and Ottoman forces withdraw from the Portuguese held city.

events.title: Teseo Ambrogio's Introductio in Chaldaicam lingua, Syriaca atq Armenica, &…
events.blurb: Teseo Ambrogio's Introductio in Chaldaicam lingua, Syriaca atq Armenica, & dece alias linguas, published in Pavia, introduces several Middle Eastern languages to western Europe for the first time.

events.title: The first printing press in North America is set up in Mexico City
events.blurb: The first printing press in North America is set up in Mexico City.

events.title: Beaulieu Abbey, Bolton Abbey, Colchester Abbey, Newstead Abbey, St Albans…
events.blurb: Beaulieu Abbey, Bolton Abbey, Colchester Abbey, Newstead Abbey, St Albans Abbey, St Mary's Abbey, York and Hartland Abbey (the last) fall prey to the Dissolution of the monasteries in England.

events.title: Giannandrea Giustiniani Longo is elected to a two year term as Doge of the…
events.blurb: Giannandrea Giustiniani Longo is elected to a two year term as Doge of the Republic of Genoa in Italy, succeeding Giovanni Battista Doria.

events.title: The first horse race is held at Chester Racecourse, the oldest still in use in…
events.blurb: The first horse race is held at Chester Racecourse, the oldest still in use in England.

events.title: Askia Isma'il, ruler of the Songhai Empire in West Africa, dies after a reign…
events.blurb: Askia Isma'il, ruler of the Songhai Empire in West Africa, dies after a reign of slightly less than two years and is succeeded by Askia Ishaq I.

events.title: Canterbury Cathedral surrenders, and reverts to its previous status of 'a…
events.blurb: Canterbury Cathedral surrenders, and reverts to its previous status of 'a college of secular canons.

events.title: At Dresden in Germany, Heinrich IV of the House of Wettin, nicknamed "Heinrich…
events.blurb: At Dresden in Germany, Heinrich IV of the House of Wettin, nicknamed "Heinrich der Fromme" (Henry the Pious) becomes the new Duke of Saxony within the Holy Roman Empire upon the death of his older brother,

events.title: Treaty of Frankfurt (1539)
events.blurb: The Treaty of Frankfurt is signed at Frankfurt-am-Main by Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor on behalf of the Empire's Roman Catholic states, and the Lutheran theologian Philip Melanchthon,

events.title: The English House of Lords creates a committee, balanced between religious…
events.blurb: The English House of Lords creates a committee, balanced between religious reformers and religious conservatives, to examine and determine doctrine, eventually forming the "Six Articles".

events.title: Hernando de Soto lands at Tampa Bay, Florida with 600 soldiers, with the goal…
events.blurb: Hernando de Soto lands at Tampa Bay, Florida with 600 soldiers, with the goal of finding gold. He also introduces pigs into North America.

events.title: Battle of Chausa in modern-day Buxar, India
events.blurb: Battle of Chausa in modern-day Buxar, India: Sher Shah Suri defeats the Mughal emperor, Humayun (Sher Shah goes on to form the Sur Empire, and take control of nearly all Mughal territory).

events.title: The Six Articles, an Act of the Parliament of England, is given royal assent…
events.blurb: The Six Articles, an Act of the Parliament of England, is given royal assent reaffirms certain Catholic principles in Henry VIII's Church of England.

events.title: Lütfi Pasha becomes the new Grand vizier of the Ottoman Empire after being…
events.blurb: Lütfi Pasha becomes the new Grand vizier of the Ottoman Empire after being appointed by the Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent following the death of Ayas Mehmed Pasha

events.title: The revolt of Ghent begins in the Spanish Netherlands (now Belgium) as members…
events.blurb: The revolt of Ghent begins in the Spanish Netherlands (now Belgium) as members of the city's guilds demand the right to choose their own leaders, and the resignation of the Spanish-sponsored city leaders.

events.title: Joachim II Hector introduces Lutheranism in the Margraviate of Brandenburg,…
events.blurb: Joachim II Hector introduces Lutheranism in the Margraviate of Brandenburg, becoming the second Prince-Elector after the Prince-Elector of Saxony to turn Protestant.

events.title: Abbot Marmaduke Bradley and 31 monks sign the deed surrendering Fountains…
events.blurb: Abbot Marmaduke Bradley and 31 monks sign the deed surrendering Fountains Abbey to the English Crown.

events.title: Juan Pardo de Tavera, Archbishop of Toledo, begins his administration as the…
events.blurb: Juan Pardo de Tavera, Archbishop of Toledo, begins his administration as the Grand Inquisitor of Spain.

events.title: In the Spanish colony of Nueva Granada (now the Republic of Colombia, Spanish…
events.blurb: In the Spanish colony of Nueva Granada (now the Republic of Colombia, Spanish conquistador Baltasar Maldonado and his troops fight a final battle at Duitama (now the Boyacá Department) against the indigenous armies of the Muisca…

events.title: Anne of Cleves arrives in England in fulfillment of the October 4 contract for…
events.blurb: Anne of Cleves arrives in England in fulfillment of the October 4 contract for marriage to King Henry VIII and the payment of a dowry of 100,000 florins to her brother.

events.title: Georg Joachim Rheticus publishes De libris revolutionum Copernici narratio…
events.blurb: Georg Joachim Rheticus publishes De libris revolutionum Copernici narratio prima in Danzig, an abstract of Copernicus' as yet unpublished De revolutionibus orbium coelestium.

events.title: Waltham Abbey is the last to be closed as part of Henry VIII of England's…
events.blurb: Waltham Abbey is the last to be closed as part of Henry VIII of England's dissolution of the monasteries.

events.title: Estêvão da Gama becomes the new Governor of Portuguese India
events.blurb: Estêvão da Gama becomes the new Governor of Portuguese India.

events.title: Printing of the first translation of the New Testament into the Icelandic…
events.blurb: Printing of the first translation of the New Testament into the Icelandic language is completed after King Christian III of Denmark finishes having Oddur Gottskálksson's text compared to the original Latin.

events.title: Battle of Kannauj
events.blurb: Battle of Kannauj: Sher Shah Suri defeats and deposes Mughal Emperor Humayan, establishing the Sur Empire.

events.title: Thomas Cromwell, Chief Minister for King Henry VIII, is arrested at meeting of…
events.blurb: Thomas Cromwell, Chief Minister for King Henry VIII, is arrested at meeting of the Privy Council of England at Westminster and charged with treason.

events.title: Spanish conquistador Francisco Vázquez de Coronado captures Hawikuh in…
events.blurb: Spanish conquistador Francisco Vázquez de Coronado captures Hawikuh in modern-day New Mexico, at this time known as part of Cíbola, but fails to find the legendary gold.

events.title: At Smithfield, London, three Lutheran pastors, Robert Barnes, Thomas Gerrard…
events.blurb: At Smithfield, London, three Lutheran pastors, Robert Barnes, Thomas Gerrard and William Jerome, are burnt at the stake on a charge of heresy and three Roman Catholic priests, Thomas Abel, Richard Fetherstone and Edward Powell, are hanged,

events.title: In Peru, Spanish captain Garcí Manuel de Carbajal founds the Villa Hermosa de…
events.blurb: In Peru, Spanish captain Garcí Manuel de Carbajal founds the Villa Hermosa de Arequipa; one year later, Charles V of Germany and I of Spain will give the valley a status of 'city' by royal decree.

events.title: Gelawdewos succeeds his father Lebna Dengel as Emperor of Ethiopia
events.blurb: Gelawdewos succeeds his father Lebna Dengel as Emperor of Ethiopia.

events.title: Gibraltar is sacked by the fleet of Barbary pirate Ali Hamet, a Sardinian…
events.blurb: Gibraltar is sacked by the fleet of Barbary pirate Ali Hamet, a Sardinian renegade in the service of the Ottoman Empire, and many of its leading citizens are taken as captives to Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera in Morocco.

events.title: Battle of Alborán
events.blurb: Battle of Alborán: A Habsburg Spanish fleet, under the command of Bernardino de Mendoza, destroys an Ottoman fleet commanded by Ali Hamet off Alborán Island in the Mediterranean.

events.title: William Whorwood becomes the new Attorney General for England and Wales,…
events.blurb: William Whorwood becomes the new Attorney General for England and Wales, succeeding Sir John Baker

events.title: Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent seals off The Golden Gate in…
events.blurb: Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent seals off The Golden Gate in Jerusalem, likely because of a prophecy that the Messiah would return through this gate to Jerusalem.

events.title: The first official translation of the entire Bible into Swedish is made, and…
events.blurb: The first official translation of the entire Bible into Swedish is made, and is called the Gustav Vasa Bible.

events.title: Gerardus Mercator makes his first globe
events.blurb: Gerardus Mercator makes his first globe.

events.title: Elia Levita's chivalric romance, the Bovo-Bukh, is first printed, the earliest…
events.blurb: Elia Levita's chivalric romance, the Bovo-Bukh, is first printed, the earliest published secular work in Yiddish.

events.title: Leonardo Cattaneo della Volta is elected to a two-year term as the new Doge of…
events.blurb: Leonardo Cattaneo della Volta is elected to a two-year term as the new Doge of the Republic of Genoa, succeeding Giannandrea Giustiniani Longo

events.title: Pedro de Valdivia founds Santiago del Nuevo Extremo, which will become the…
events.blurb: Pedro de Valdivia founds Santiago del Nuevo Extremo, which will become the capital of Chile.

events.title: Petru Rareș becomes the Prince of Moldavia for a second time, overthrowing the…
events.blurb: Petru Rareș becomes the Prince of Moldavia for a second time, overthrowing the Voivode Alexandru Cornea at Suceava (now in Romania) at the direction of the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman.

events.title: Battle of Suakin (1541)
events.blurb: At the Battle of Suakin, fought at an Ottoman port city on the Red Sea in what is now Sudan, Portuguese General Estêvão da Gama and his brother Cristóvão da Gama lead an attack against the Ottoman ruler and plunder the city.

events.title: The Portuguese Empire's fortress at Agadir falls to the Moroccan general…
events.blurb: The Portuguese Empire's fortress at Agadir falls to the Moroccan general Mohammed al-Shaykh after a siege of 24 days.

events.title: In what is now the capital of Ecuador, San Francisco de Quito is declared a…
events.blurb: In what is now the capital of Ecuador, San Francisco de Quito is declared a city by the decree of King Charles I of Spain and the Viceroyalty of Peru.

events.title: Francis Xavier leaves Lisbon, on a mission to the Portuguese East Indies
events.blurb: Francis Xavier leaves Lisbon, on a mission to the Portuguese East Indies.

events.title: Battle of Sahart
events.blurb: Battle of Sahart: Gelawdewos is defeated by the forces of Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi.

events.title: Şehzade Mustafa, the son of the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent, is…
events.blurb: Şehzade Mustafa, the son of the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent, is appointed as the new Ottoman Governor of the Amasya region of Turkey.

events.title: Takeda Shingen becomes head of Japan's powerful Takeda clan of samurais that…
events.blurb: (Tenbun 10, 14th day of the 6th month) Takeda Shingen becomes head of Japan's powerful Takeda clan of samurais that rules the Kai Province, overthrowing and banishing his father, Takeda Nobutora.

events.title: Spanish noblewoman Beatriz de la Cueva serves as governor of the colony of…
events.blurb: Spanish noblewoman Beatriz de la Cueva serves as governor of the colony of Guatemala, before she is killed in a mudslide from Volcán de Agua, which ruins the capital city, Ciudad Vieja.

events.title: After three years of exile, John Calvin returns to Geneva to reform the church…
events.blurb: After three years of exile, John Calvin returns to Geneva to reform the church under a body of doctrine that comes to be known as Calvinism.

events.title: Through royal decree, the city of Arequipa is granted its coat of arms
events.blurb: Through royal decree, the city of Arequipa is granted its coat of arms.

events.title: The Holy Roman Emperor Charles V is finally able to return to Spain, arriving…
events.blurb: The Holy Roman Emperor Charles V is finally able to return to Spain, arriving at Cartagena

events.title: Thomas Culpeper and Francis Dereham are both executed at Tyburn after being…
events.blurb: Thomas Culpeper and Francis Dereham are both executed at Tyburn after being convicted of treason in committing adultery with Queen Catherine. Culpeper is beheaded, while Dereham is hanged, drawn and quartered.

events.title: The first legislature for the Voivode of Transylvania meets at Vásárhely in…
events.blurb: The first legislature for the Voivode of Transylvania meets at Vásárhely in the Kingdom of Hungary (now Târgu Mureș in Romania).

events.title: Tutul-Xiu, the Mayan ruler of the Maní in Yucatán, arrives at the Spanish…
