events.blurb: Tutul-Xiu, the Mayan ruler of the Maní in Yucatán, arrives at the Spanish settlement of Merida with food supplies for the colonists and offers to assist the Spaniards in their conquest of Yucatan in return for being installed as the…

events.title: Battle of Baçente
events.blurb: Battle of Baçente: The Portuguese under Cristóvão da Gama capture a Muslim-occupied hillfort in northern Ethiopia.

events.title: Catherine Howard, until recently the Queen consort of England and the wife of…
events.blurb: Catherine Howard, until recently the Queen consort of England and the wife of King Henry VIII, is executed by beheading, two days after the King gives royal assent to a bill of attainder passed by the English Parliament on February 7.

events.title: Guadalajara, Mexico, is founded by the Spaniards after three previous attempts…
events.blurb: Guadalajara, Mexico, is founded by the Spaniards after three previous attempts failed, due to aggressive opposition from local tribes.

events.title: Antoine Escalin des Aimars of France completes the negotiation with the…
events.blurb: Antoine Escalin des Aimars of France completes the negotiation with the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman for the Franco-Ottoman alliance.

events.title: Battle of Jarte
events.blurb: The Battle of Jarte begins in Ethiopia as the Army of the Portuguese Empire, commanded by Cristóvão da Gama encounters the army of the Ethiopian ruler, the Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi, achieving a victory on April 16.

events.title: Battle of Haddon Rig
events.blurb: Battle of Haddon Rig: Scotland defeats England.

events.title: Citizens of Hildesheim in the Holy Roman Empire profess themselves to the…
events.blurb: Citizens of Hildesheim in the Holy Roman Empire profess themselves to the Lutheran teachings, thus joining the Schmalkaldic League.

events.title: Battle of Wofla in Ethiopia
events.blurb: Battle of Wofla in Ethiopia: Reinforced with at least 2900 arquebusiers and cavalry, the Imam Ahmed ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi attacks the Portuguese camp. The Portuguese are scattered; Cristóvão da Gama is captured and executed.

events.title: Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo lands in what is now San Diego Bay, and names it "San…
events.blurb: Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo lands in what is now San Diego Bay, and names it "San Miguel", claiming it for the Spanish Empire. San Miguel will later become the city of San Diego. This marks the first time a European sees what is now the U.S.

events.title: Battle of Solway Moss
events.blurb: Battle of Solway Moss: An English army invades Scotland, and defeats a Scottish army.

events.title: Palace plot of Renyin year
events.blurb: Palace plot of Renyin year: A group of Ming dynasty palace women fail to murder the Jiajing Emperor, and are executed by slow-slicing.

events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots, aged six days, becomes queen regnant on the death of her…
events.blurb: Mary, Queen of Scots, aged six days, becomes queen regnant on the death of her father, James V of Scotland.

events.title: Mikael Agricola publishes Abckiria
events.blurb: Mikael Agricola publishes Abckiria.

events.title: Battle of Muros Bay
events.blurb: The first large naval battle in the Atlantic Ocean, the Battle of Muros Bay, takes place off of the coast of Galicia in Spain between the French fleet and the Spanish fleet.

events.title: Act for the Advancement of True Religion
events.blurb: King Henry VIII of England gives royal assent to numerous laws passed by parliament, including the Act for the Advancement of True Religion, restricting the reading of the Bible to clerics, noblemen, and upper class society.

events.title: The Lighthouse of Genoa is completed in present form
events.blurb: The Lighthouse of Genoa is completed in present form.

events.title: Laws in Wales Act 1542, second phase of the Consolidating Act of Welsh Union,…
events.blurb: Laws in Wales Act 1542, second phase of the Consolidating Act of Welsh Union, is given royal assent, establishing counties and regularizing parliamentary representation in Wales.

events.title: Andrea Centurione Pietrasanta begins a two-year term as the new Doge of the…
events.blurb: Andrea Centurione Pietrasanta begins a two-year term as the new Doge of the Republic of Genoa, replacing Leonardo Cattaneo della Volta.

events.title: Battle of Wayna Daga
events.blurb: Battle of Wayna Daga: A joint Ethiopian-Portuguese force of 8,500, under Emperor Gelawdewos of Ethiopia, defeats Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi's army of over 14,000, ending the Ethiopian–Adal War.

events.title: James Hamilton, 2nd Earl of Arran, is elected by the Scottish Parliament as…
events.blurb: James Hamilton, 2nd Earl of Arran, is elected by the Scottish Parliament as the Regent for the infant Mary Queen of Scots.

events.title: In Nuremberg, De revolutionibus orbium coelestium (On the Revolutions of the…
events.blurb: In Nuremberg, De revolutionibus orbium coelestium (On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres) is printed during the illness of Nicholas Copernicus, offering mathematical arguments for the existence of the heliocentric universe,

events.title: Andreas Vesalius publishes De humani corporis fabrica (On the Fabric of the…
events.blurb: Andreas Vesalius publishes De humani corporis fabrica (On the Fabric of the Human Body), revolutionising the science of human anatomy.

events.title: Treaty of Greenwich
events.blurb: The Treaty of Greenwich is signed between representatives of the Kingdoms of England and Scotland as part of a plan to eventually unify the two nations under one monarch.

events.title: Siege of Nice
events.blurb: The Siege of Nice by the Ottoman Empire and French forces (under the Franco-Ottoman alliance), led by Admiral Hayreddin Barbarossa, begins.

events.title: Esztergom surrenders to the Ottomans led by Suleiman the Magnificent
events.blurb: Esztergom surrenders to the Ottomans led by Suleiman the Magnificent.

events.title: The city of Nice is captured by the Ottomans and Barbarossa after a long…
events.blurb: The city of Nice is captured by the Ottomans and Barbarossa after a long bombardment. The Ottomans pillage the city and take away 2,500 captives to be sold into slavery.

events.title: Coronation of Mary, Queen of Scots
events.blurb: Mary Stuart is crowned the Queen of Scots in Stirling at the age of nine months old.

events.title: Shan States
events.blurb: (11 waxing of Natdaw 905 ME) – The land and naval forces of the Confederation of Shan States (consisting of the principalities of Mohnyin, Mogaung, Bhamo, Momeik and Kale), led by Prince Sawlon of Mohnyin and King Hkonmaing,

events.title: The Eight Years War, also called the "War of Rough Wooing", begins as…
events.blurb: The Eight Years War, also called the "War of Rough Wooing", begins as Scotland's Parliament votes to declare war on the Kingdom of England.

events.title: Abraham Ortelius becomes a geographer to Philip II of Spain
events.blurb: Abraham Ortelius becomes a geographer to Philip II of Spain.

events.title: Ottoman forces led by Ferhad Pasha Sokolović defeat the Austrian Army, led by…
events.blurb: Ottoman forces led by Ferhad Pasha Sokolović defeat the Austrian Army, led by Herbard VIII von Auersperg, in the Battle of Budačka. Auersperg is decapitated and Ferhad Pasha leaves Croatia with the head as a trophy.

events.title: Venceslaus Agrippa Lituanus is the Great Scribe of Lithuania
events.blurb: Venceslaus Agrippa Lituanus is the Great Scribe of Lithuania.

events.title: Russians occupy Pernau in western Estonia, and the fortress of Weissenstein
events.blurb: Russians occupy Pernau in western Estonia, and the fortress of Weissenstein.

events.title: Queen Elizabeth I of England grants a monopoly on producing printed sheet…
events.blurb: Queen Elizabeth I of England grants a monopoly on producing printed sheet music, to Thomas Tallis and William Byrd.

events.title: Portuguese explorer Paulo Dias de Novais arrives in southeastern Africa to…
events.blurb: Portuguese explorer Paulo Dias de Novais arrives in southeastern Africa to colonize what is now Angola.

events.title: The formal coronation of Henry III as King of France takes place at the Reims…
events.blurb: The formal coronation of Henry III as King of France takes place at the Reims Cathedral. Henry inherited the throne on May 30, 1574, upon the death of his older brother, Charles IX. He marries Louise of Lorraine.

events.title: Battle of Tukaroi
events.blurb: Battle of Tukaroi: The Mughal Empire decisively defeats the Karrani dynasty of Bengal. The battle took place near the village of Tukaroi in present-day Balasore District of Odisha.

events.title: Antoine I de Gramont, Lord Sovereign of the Principality of Bidache in the…
events.blurb: Antoine I de Gramont, Lord Sovereign of the Principality of Bidache in the French Pyrennees Mountains, promulgates a legal code for his people.

events.title: Bayinnaung, King of Burma, returns to his capital at Pegu from Vientiane after…
events.blurb: Bayinnaung, King of Burma, returns to his capital at Pegu from Vientiane after installing Voravongsa I as the Burmese-appointed monarch of the Kingdom of Lan Xang (now Laos).

events.title: In an attempt to reform the Eastern Orthodox Church, Lutheran missionaries…
events.blurb: In an attempt to reform the Eastern Orthodox Church, Lutheran missionaries meet with Jeremias II Tranos, the Ecumenical Patriarch, at his residence in Constantinople, and present him with a Greek translation of the Augsburg Confession.

events.title: William the Silent, Prince of Orange, marries Charlotte of Bourbon
events.blurb: William the Silent, Prince of Orange, marries Charlotte of Bourbon.

events.title: Battle of Nagashino
events.blurb: Battle of Nagashino: Oda Nobunaga defeats Takeda Katsuyori in Japan's first modern battle.

events.title: Raid of the Redeswire
events.blurb: Raid of the Redeswire: Sir John Carmichael defeats Sir John Forster, in the last battle between England and Scotland.

events.title: Edmund Grindal succeeds Matthew Parker as Archbishop of Canterbury
events.blurb: Edmund Grindal succeeds Matthew Parker as Archbishop of Canterbury.

events.title: Henry Sidney is appointed Lord Lieutenant of Ireland
events.blurb: Henry Sidney is appointed Lord Lieutenant of Ireland.

events.title: St. Vitus Cathedral
events.blurb: At St. Vitus Cathedral in Prague, Rudolf of Habsburg, son of the Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian II, is crowned King of Bohemia by the Archbishop Antonín Brus of Mohelnice.

events.title: Future Spanish author and playwright Miguel de Cervantes, then 28, is taken…
events.blurb: Future Spanish author and playwright Miguel de Cervantes, then 28, is taken hostage by the Ottoman Albanian pirate Arnaut Mami after an attack on the Spanish galley Sol off of the Catalan coast.

events.title: Battle of Dormans
events.blurb: Battle of Dormans: Catholic forces under Henry I, Duke of Guise defeat the Protestants, capturing Philippe de Mornay among others.

events.title: 1576 Polish–Lithuanian royal election
events.blurb: The Sejm of Poland meets in Warsaw to elect a new King of Poland after King Henryk has failed to return from France, and considers 11 candidates.

events.title: Portuguese navigator Manuel de Mesquita Perestrelo departs from Mozambique on…
events.blurb: Portuguese navigator Manuel de Mesquita Perestrelo departs from Mozambique on a mission for to map the coastline, completing the task on March 13.

events.title: Under pressure from Papal nuncio Vincenzo Lauro when a majority of the Sejm…
events.blurb: Under pressure from Papal nuncio Vincenzo Lauro when a majority of the Sejm has still not agreed on a candidate, the Primate of Poland, Jakub Uchański, declares Maximilian II new King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania.

events.title: 1575 Valdivia earthquake
events.blurb: An earthquake hits Valdivia.

events.title: Konstanty Wasyl Ostrogski founds Ostroh Academy, the first university-level…
events.blurb: Konstanty Wasyl Ostrogski founds Ostroh Academy, the first university-level school in Eastern Europe.

events.title: Dartford Grammar School, by William d'Aeth, Edward Gwyn and William Vaughn
events.blurb: Dartford Grammar School, by William d'Aeth, Edward Gwyn and William Vaughn.

events.title: The Loci Communes of Peter Martyr Vermigli (d
events.blurb: The Loci Communes of Peter Martyr Vermigli (d. 1562), edited by Robert le Maçon, are published in London.

events.title: Sutton Valence School, by William Lambe
events.blurb: Sutton Valence School, by William Lambe.

events.title: Martín Enríquez de Almanza, Viceroy of New Spain, founds the settlement of…
events.blurb: Martín Enríquez de Almanza, Viceroy of New Spain, founds the settlement of León, in what is later the state of Guanajuato in Mexico.

events.title: King Henry of Navarre, captive in France since 1572 and alive only because he…
events.blurb: King Henry of Navarre, captive in France since 1572 and alive only because he converted to Catholicism, escapes to Tours and formally reverts to the Protestant faith.

events.title: Peter Wentworth, a Puritan M
events.blurb: Peter Wentworth, a Puritan M.P. of the Parliament of England, is arrested in the middle of giving an address criticizing "rumours and messages" given to suppress freedom of speech.

events.title: The city of Fez, part of the Saadi Sultanate in modern-day Morocco is captured…
events.blurb: The city of Fez, part of the Saadi Sultanate in modern-day Morocco is captured by Ottoman forces led by Abd al-Malik, in an attempt to overthrow the Sultan Muhammed al-Mutawakkil and to make the Sultanate a vassal of the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Ishiyama Hongan-ji War
events.blurb: Ishiyama Hongan-ji War: In Japan, the Third Battle of Ishiyama begins as Oda Nobunaga sends 10,000 soldiers against the Ashikaga shogunate to capture the Honganji Temple.

events.title: Union of Delft
events.blurb: Documents for the Union of Delft are signed by Dutch leader Willem van Oranj to create a federation of Holland and Zeeland.

events.title: Stephen Báthory, the Hungarian Prince of Transylvania, is crowned king of Poland
events.blurb: Stephen Báthory, the Hungarian Prince of Transylvania, is crowned king of Poland.

events.title: Edict of Beaulieu
events.blurb: The Edict of Beaulieu, negotiated by Monsieur Francois, Duke of Anjou and brother of King Henry III of France, ends the Fifth War of Religion.

events.title: Tahmap's son Haydar Mirza Safavi declares himself the new Safavid Shah of…
events.blurb: Tahmap's son Haydar Mirza Safavi declares himself the new Safavid Shah of Iran, the day after the death of his father. Later in the day, Haydar is assassinated by members of the palace guard who are loyal to Haydar's brother, Ismail Mirza.

events.title: Siege of Zierikzee
events.blurb: An attempt by the Dutch Republic to end the Siege of Zierikzee and free the city from Spain fails after Spanish forces are tipped off about a surprise attack. Dutch Admiral Lodewijk van Boisot is killed in the battle.

events.title: Dutch forces withdraw to free Zierikzee, and the city is left to defend itself
events.blurb: Dutch forces withdraw to free Zierikzee, and the city is left to defend itself. The defenders then attempt negotiations with the Spanish attackers, commanded by General Cristóbal de Mondragón.

events.title: Battle of Haldighati
events.blurb: In the Battle of Haldighati in India, Mughal Imperial forces, led by Man Singh I of Amer, decisively defeat the Mewar Kingdom led by Maharana Pratap.

events.title: Alonso de Solís, who was appointed by Spain as Governor of the colony of La…
events.blurb: Alonso de Solís, who was appointed by Spain as Governor of the colony of La Florida, is killed in the colonial capital at San Augustin, the modern U.S. city of St. Augustine, Florida.

events.title: The Mughal Empire annexes Bengal after defeating the Bengal Sultanate at the…
events.blurb: The Mughal Empire annexes Bengal after defeating the Bengal Sultanate at the Battle of Rajmahal.

events.title: English navigator Martin Frobisher, on his search for the Northwest Passage…
events.blurb: English navigator Martin Frobisher, on his search for the Northwest Passage through North America, enters the bay now named after him in Canada.

events.title: Ismail Mirza, who has proclaimed himself the Shah of Safavid Iran, marches…
events.blurb: Ismail Mirza, who has proclaimed himself the Shah of Safavid Iran, marches into the capital at Qazvin and ascends the throne as Shah Ismail II.

events.title: Simeon Bekbulatovich, who has served since the previous October as the Grand…
events.blurb: Simeon Bekbulatovich, who has served since the previous October as the Grand Prince of All Russia after the Tsar Ivan IV ("Ivan the Terrible") had taken leave of absence from the throne, steps down as Ivan returns to Moscow.

events.title: In Brussels, rebels led by Jacques de Glymes of Brabant arrest the members of…
events.blurb: In Brussels, rebels led by Jacques de Glymes of Brabant arrest the members of the Council of State that administers the city.

events.title: The States General of the Netherlands is convened by the leaders of the States…
events.blurb: The States General of the Netherlands is convened by the leaders of the States of Brabant and the County of Hainaut in order to respond to mutineering Spanish troops.

events.title: After a siege that has lasted a year and two days, the Spanish Army abandons…
events.blurb: After a siege that has lasted a year and two days, the Spanish Army abandons its siege of the Dutch city of Woerden.

events.title: Maximilian II, ruler of the Holy Roman Empire and most of Central Europe since…
events.blurb: Maximilian II, ruler of the Holy Roman Empire and most of Central Europe since 1564, dies suddenly in Regensburg while preparing for an Imperial invasion of Poland.

events.title: In Germany, Ludwig of Simmern becomes the new Elector Palatine of the Rhine 10…
events.blurb: In Germany, Ludwig of Simmern becomes the new Elector Palatine of the Rhine 10 days after the death of his father, Frederick III, taking office at the Palatinate capital at Heidelberg as Ludwig VI.

events.title: Coronation of Rudolf II, Holy Roman Emperor
events.blurb: Coronation of Rudolf II, Holy Roman Emperor.

events.title: Eighty Years' War – Sack of Antwerp
events.blurb: Eighty Years' War – Sack of Antwerp: In the Low Countries, mutinous Spanish soldiers sack Antwerp; after three days the city is nearly destroyed.

events.title: Pacification of Ghent
events.blurb: Pacification of Ghent: The States General of the Netherlands meet and unite to oppose pillaging Spanish mutineers.

events.title: Shah Ismail II of Iran begins the execution of all persons whom he believes…
events.blurb: Shah Ismail II of Iran begins the execution of all persons whom he believes are a threat to his rule, starting with his half-brothers Suleiman Mirza, Governor of Shiraz, and Mustafa Mirza.

events.title: James Burbage opens the first permanent public playhouse in Britain, The Theatre
events.blurb: James Burbage opens the first permanent public playhouse in Britain, The Theatre.

events.title: Representatives of France's three estates convene at the Estates General of…
events.blurb: Representatives of France's three estates convene at the Estates General of 1576 in Blois at the invitation of King Henri III.

events.title: The church in San Pedro de Atacama is built, in the Atacama Desert in Chile
events.blurb: The church in San Pedro de Atacama is built, in the Atacama Desert in Chile.

events.title: Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge over the Drina in Višegrad is completed in the…
events.blurb: Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge over the Drina in Višegrad is completed in the Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Supposed massacre of the MacDonald inhabitants of the Scottish island of Eigg,…
events.blurb: Supposed massacre of the MacDonald inhabitants of the Scottish island of Eigg, by the Clan MacLeod.

events.title: Casiodoro de Reina publishes his "Declaracion, o confesion de fe", the first…
events.blurb: Casiodoro de Reina publishes his "Declaracion, o confesion de fe", the first and only Spanish confession of faith in the post Reformation period.

events.title: Union of Brussels
events.blurb: The second Union of Brussels is formed, first without the Protestant counties of Holland and Zeeland (which is accepted by King Philip II of Spain), later with the Protestants, which means open rebellion of the whole of the Netherlands.

events.title: Edict of 1577
events.blurb: The "Perpetual Edict", providing for the removal of Spanish troops from what is now the Netherlands, is signed in the city of Marche-en-Famenne in the Spanish Netherlands (now Belgium) by the Spanish Governor-General,

events.title: Battle of Lubieszów
events.blurb: Battle of Lubieszów: General Jan Zborowski leads the army of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth in the catastrophic defeat of most of Jan Winkelbruch's 12,000 rebels and mercenaries from the Commonwealth's richest city, Danzig,

events.title: The Bergen Book, better known as the Solid Declaration of the Formula of…
events.blurb: The Bergen Book, better known as the Solid Declaration of the Formula of Concord, one of the Lutheran confessional writings, is published.

events.title: Sebastiano Venier becomes the new Doge of the Republic of Venice, succeeding…
events.blurb: Sebastiano Venier becomes the new Doge of the Republic of Venice, succeeding Alvise Mocenigo, who died on June 4.

events.title: The French city of Issoire surrenders and 3,000 of its Protestant Huguenots…
events.blurb: The French city of Issoire surrenders and 3,000 of its Protestant Huguenots are massacred by the troops of the French Catholic General Francis, Duke of Anjou, on orders by King Henry III of France.

events.title: Mirza Salman Jaberi is appointed as the new Grand Vizier of Persia by Shah…
events.blurb: Mirza Salman Jaberi is appointed as the new Grand Vizier of Persia by Shah Ismail II, replacing Mirza Shokrollah Isfahani.

events.title: Mehmed II Giray becomes the new Khan of Crimea for the Ottoman Empire, after…
events.blurb: Mehmed II Giray becomes the new Khan of Crimea for the Ottoman Empire, after the death of his father, Devlet I Giray, from a plague.

events.title: Ludvig Munk is appointed Governor-General of Norway
events.blurb: Ludvig Munk is appointed Governor-General of Norway.

events.title: Treaty of Bergerac
events.blurb: The Treaty of Bergerac is signed between Henry III of France and the Huguenots.

events.title: The first Inuit to see Europe— Kalicho, Arnaq, and Arnaq's son, Nutaaq— are…
events.blurb: The first Inuit to see Europe— Kalicho, Arnaq, and Arnaq's son, Nutaaq— are brought as captives of Martin Frobisher when HMS Gabriel arrived in England at Bristol.

events.title: In Italy, Giovanni Battista Gentile Pignolo is elected as the new Doge of the…
events.blurb: In Italy, Giovanni Battista Gentile Pignolo is elected as the new Doge of the Republic of Genoa for a two-year term, replacing Prospero Centurione Fattinanti.

events.title: In Flanders (now part of Belgium), two Protestant members of the city council…
events.blurb: In Flanders (now part of Belgium), two Protestant members of the city council of Ghent, Jan van Hembyze and François van Ryhove, proclaim the Calvinist Republic of Ghent.

events.title: The first recorded observation from Earth of the Great Comet of 1577 takes…
events.blurb: The first recorded observation from Earth of the Great Comet of 1577 takes place by Aztec astronomers in Mexico, followed by reports from Italy on November 7 and Japan on November 8.

events.title: Battle of Tedorigawa
events.blurb: In the Battle of Tedorigawa, Uesugi Kenshin's forces decisively defeat the forces of Oda Nobunaga, in what will be Kenshin's last victory before his death the following year.

events.title: Francis Drake leaves Plymouth, England, aboard the Pelican, with four other…
events.blurb: Francis Drake leaves Plymouth, England, aboard the Pelican, with four other ships and 164 men, on an expedition against the Spanish, along the Pacific coast of the Americas, which will become his circumnavigation.

events.title: Sonam Gyrso receives from Prince Atlan Khan the title of Talaï, and becomes…
events.blurb: Sonam Gyrso receives from Prince Atlan Khan the title of Talaï, and becomes the third Dalai Lama of Tibet.

events.title: Battle of the Spoiling Dyke at Trumpan on the Scottish Isle of Skye
events.blurb: Battle of the Spoiling Dyke at Trumpan on the Scottish Isle of Skye: the Clan MacLeod are victorious over the MacDonalds of Uist in a feud.

events.title: Fur trade begins in Newfoundland in North America
events.blurb: Fur trade begins in Newfoundland in North America.

events.title: Sarsa Dengel, Emperor of Ethiopia, defeats and kills Bahr negus Yeshaq along…
events.blurb: Sarsa Dengel, Emperor of Ethiopia, defeats and kills Bahr negus Yeshaq along with his Ottoman allies, finally ending his rebellion.

events.title: Siege of Gvozdansko
events.blurb: The Siege of Gvozdansko ends in the Kingdom of Croatia as Ottoman Empire troops led by Ferhad Pasha Sokolović capture the fortress at Gvozdansko.

events.title: Battle of Gembloux
events.blurb: Battle of Gembloux: Spanish forces under Don John of Austria and Alexander Farnese defeat the Dutch; Farnese begins to recover control of the French-speaking Southern Netherlands.

events.title: Pope Gregory XIII issues the papal bull Illius fulti praesidio and creates the…
events.blurb: Pope Gregory XIII issues the papal bull Illius fulti praesidio and creates the Diocese of Manila, the first Roman Catholic diocese in the Philippines, with Domingo de Salazar as the first Bishop of Manila.

events.title: Mohammad Khodabanda, older brother of the late Shah Ismail II, begins his…
events.blurb: Mohammad Khodabanda, older brother of the late Shah Ismail II, begins his reign as the new Shah of Persia (now Iran) after entering the Persian capital at Qazvin, after removing his sister Pari Khan Khanum,

events.title: Two days after the Battle of Gembloux, Spanish troops capture the city of…
events.blurb: Two days after the Battle of Gembloux, Spanish troops capture the city of Leuven, forcing Willem, Prince of Orange, to flee Brussels and relocate to Antwerp.Geoffrey Parker, The Dutch Revolt (Cornell University Press, 1977) p.186

events.title: Nicolò da Ponte is elected as the new Doge of the Republic of Venice after 44…
events.blurb: Nicolò da Ponte is elected as the new Doge of the Republic of Venice after 44 ballots, following the March 3 death of Sebastiano Venier.

events.title: Siege of Otate
events.blurb: (17th day of 3rd month, Tensho 6) The Siege of Otate begins in Japan after the death of Uesugi Kenshin, the warlord of the Echigo Province.

events.title: The Alteratie takes place in Amsterdam, expelling the 24 Catholic members of…
events.blurb: The Alteratie takes place in Amsterdam, expelling the 24 Catholic members of the 40-man city government, and forming a new council is formed with 30 Calvinist Protestants and 10 Catholics.

events.title: Humphrey Gilbert is granted letters patent from the English crown to establish…
events.blurb: Humphrey Gilbert is granted letters patent from the English crown to establish a colony in North America.

events.title: The Frobisher expedition reaches Greenland
events.blurb: The Frobisher expedition reaches Greenland.

events.title: After having come into conflict on May 17 with his fellow officer, Thomas…
events.blurb: After having come into conflict on May 17 with his fellow officer, Thomas Doughty, during their circumnavigation of the world, Francis Drake puts Doughty on trial while the flagship Pelican is docked at what is now Argentina.

events.title: The Frobisher expedition reaches Canada and enters what is now Frobisher Bay
events.blurb: The Frobisher expedition reaches Canada and enters what is now Frobisher Bay. One of the ships, the Dennis, is wrecked on an iceberg.

events.title: Sebastian, King of Portugal is killed in the Battle of Alcácer Quibir in North…
events.blurb: Sebastian, King of Portugal is killed in the Battle of Alcácer Quibir in North Africa while fighting the Saadi Sultanate.

events.title: Alessandro Farnese succeeds his uncle, Don John, as Governor of the Spanish…
events.blurb: Alessandro Farnese succeeds his uncle, Don John, as Governor of the Spanish Netherlands.

events.title: After more than five years of combat in southern France, the Protestant…
events.blurb: After more than five years of combat in southern France, the Protestant Huguenot citadel of Ménerbes negotiates a surrender to its French Catholic attackers.

events.title: The municipality of Boac in Marinduque, Philippines is founded
events.blurb: The municipality of Boac in Marinduque, Philippines is founded.

events.title: The Bible of Kralice begins publication
events.blurb: The Bible of Kralice begins publication. The first complete translation of the Bible into the Czech language (with notes), it is prepared by the Unity of the Brethren, and published at Kralice nad Oslavou, Bohemia.

events.title: In the Mughal Empire in India, Akbar abolishes the jizya, the tax placed upon…
events.blurb: In the Mughal Empire in India, Akbar abolishes the jizya, the tax placed upon non-Muslim residents.

events.title: Union of Arras
events.blurb: The Union of Arras unites the southern Netherlands under the Duke of Parma, governor in the name of king Philip II of Spain.

events.title: Union of Utrecht
events.blurb: The Union of Utrecht unites the northern Netherlands in a confederation called the United Provinces.

events.title: The Ghent Republic joins the Union of Utrecht
events.blurb: The Ghent Republic joins the Union of Utrecht.

events.title: The seizure in September by Willem IV van den Bergh, of the Boxmeer Castle in…
events.blurb: The seizure in September by Willem IV van den Bergh, of the Boxmeer Castle in September in the Netherlands is condemned by the other Dutch members of the Union of Utrecht.

events.title: Battle of Borgerhout in Brabant (now Belgium)
events.blurb: Battle of Borgerhout in Brabant (now Belgium): Spanish troops under the command of the Duke of Parma overwhelm rebels fighting for the Union of Utrecht.

events.title: Siege of Maastricht (1579)
events.blurb: The Siege of Maastricht, a center of the Dutch resistance to Spanish rule, is started in the Netherlands by Spanish troops under the command of Alexander Farnese, Duke of Parma.

events.title: In the village of Cuers in France, near Toulon rebel peasants kill 600 nobles…
events.blurb: In the village of Cuers in France, near Toulon rebel peasants kill 600 nobles and upper-class gentlemen of the Catholic League serving the Count of Carces.

events.title: Treaty of Arras (1579)
events.blurb: The Treaty of Arras is concluded between Spain (represented by the Duke of Parma), and members of the Union of Arras that had been formed in January.

events.title: Battle of Mimaomote
events.blurb: Battle of Mimaomote: In Japan, Doi Kiyonaga defeats the forces of Kumu Yorinobu.

events.title: Karlovac in Croatia is founded
events.blurb: Karlovac in Croatia is founded.

events.title: James FitzMaurice FitzGerald lands with a small force of Irish, Spanish, and…
events.blurb: James FitzMaurice FitzGerald lands with a small force of Irish, Spanish, and Italian troops at Smerwick, on the Dingle Peninsula in south-western Ireland,

events.title: "Yasuke", a man of African origin who has been hired as a manager by the…
events.blurb: "Yasuke", a man of African origin who has been hired as a manager by the Chancellor of the Realm, Oda Nobunaga, arrives in Japan.

events.title: Livonian War
events.blurb: Livonian War: In what is now Belarus, the city of Polotsk falls to the forces of Stephen Báthory, Grand Duke of Lithuania and King of Poland.

events.title: Amendments are made to the May 17 Treaty of Arras, with further concessions to…
events.blurb: Amendments are made to the May 17 Treaty of Arras, with further concessions to Spain by the Union of Arras. The final version is promulgated by King Philip of Spain in Mons, one of the regions in the Arras Union.

events.title: In Switzerland, a mutual assistance pact was signed at Lucerne between…
events.blurb: In Switzerland, a mutual assistance pact was signed at Lucerne between representatives of Roman Catholic cantons by the efforts of the Catholic Bishop of Basel, Jakob Christoph Blarer von Wartensee.

events.title: At Banda Aceh, on the island of Sumatra in what is now Indonesia, Alauddin…
events.blurb: At Banda Aceh, on the island of Sumatra in what is now Indonesia, Alauddin Mansur Syah becomes the new Sultan of Aceh upon the death of Sultan Zainul Abidin.

events.title: Sokollu Mehmed Pasha, Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire for more than 14…
events.blurb: Sokollu Mehmed Pasha, Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire for more than 14 years, is assassinated in Constantinople.

events.title: Semiz Ahmed Pasha is appointed as the new Ottoman Grand Vizier by Sultan Murad III
events.blurb: Semiz Ahmed Pasha is appointed as the new Ottoman Grand Vizier by Sultan Murad III.

events.title: King James VI of Scotland makes his ceremonial entry into Edinburgh to assume…
events.blurb: King James VI of Scotland makes his ceremonial entry into Edinburgh to assume the throne at the age of 13, after being declared to have reached the age of majority.

events.title: Nicolò Doria is elected to a two-year term as the new Doge of the Republic of…
events.blurb: Nicolò Doria is elected to a two-year term as the new Doge of the Republic of Genoa.Sergio Buonadonna and Mario Marcenaro, Rosso Doge: I dogi della Repubblica di Genova dal 1339 al 1797 (De Ferrari Press, 2000).

events.title: The English puritan John Stubbs, author of numerous pamphlets against the…
events.blurb: The English puritan John Stubbs, author of numerous pamphlets against the doctrines of the Church of England, is convicted of sedition, and his right hand is amputated as punishment.

events.title: Second Desmond Rebellion
events.blurb: During the Second Desmond Rebellion, rebel troops in Ireland, led by Gerald FitzGerald, 14th Earl of Desmond, carry out the Sack of Youghal and massacre the English Army garrison, then pillage and burn the homes of local residents.

events.title: Iancu Sasul becomes the new Prince of Moldavia as Peter the Lame steps down…
events.blurb: Iancu Sasul becomes the new Prince of Moldavia as Peter the Lame steps down for the second time. Peter will replace Sasul on October 17, 1582.

events.title: Jeremias II Tranos is removed from office as Ecumenical Patriarch of…
events.blurb: Jeremias II Tranos is removed from office as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, leader of the Eastern Orthodox Church, and replaced by his rival Metrophanes III of Constantinople, whom he deposed on May 4, 1572.

events.title: After Willem van Pamele, the Spanish Governor of Flanders, is forced to flee…
events.blurb: After Willem van Pamele, the Spanish Governor of Flanders, is forced to flee during the Dutch Revolt, the Duke of Parma orders Pamele and the Catholic members of the Council of Flanders to convene at Douai as the temporary Flemish capital.

events.title: German astronomer Michael Maestlin makes the first cataloging of the Pleiades…
events.blurb: German astronomer Michael Maestlin makes the first cataloging of the Pleiades cluster, recording 11 separate stars visible to the naked eye, with a detailed illustration and measurements.

events.title: In France, Protestant French troops under the command of Matthieu Merle, make…
events.blurb: In France, Protestant French troops under the command of Matthieu Merle, make a surprise attack on the Roman Catholic cathedral in the village of Mende during Mass, and kill 400 civilians.

events.title: The 1580 influenza pandemic sweeps the world, starting in Asia and moving…
events.blurb: The 1580 influenza pandemic sweeps the world, starting in Asia and moving rapidly through Africa, Europe, and eventually the Americas. More than 10% of the population of Rome dies, and whole towns in Spain are depopulated.

events.title: The first session of the Jewish Vaad (Council of Four Lands) is held in…
events.blurb: The first session of the Jewish Vaad (Council of Four Lands) is held in Lublin, Poland; 70 delegates of Jewish local qahals meet to discuss taxation, and other issues important to Jewish communities.

events.title: In Southern India, Ibrahim Adil Shah II becomes the new Sultan of Bijapur upon…
events.blurb: In Southern India, Ibrahim Adil Shah II becomes the new Sultan of Bijapur upon the death of his father, Ali Adil Shah I.

events.title: The Billy Mitchell volcano, on the island of Bougainville, undergoes a…
events.blurb: The Billy Mitchell volcano, on the island of Bougainville, undergoes a catastrophic eruption (VEI 6).

events.title: Portuguese succession crisis of 1580
events.blurb: Portuguese succession crisis of 1580: The death of Henry, King of Portugal, with no direct heirs, leads to conflict between his potential successors, including King Philip II of Spain and Infanta Catherine, Duchess of Braganza.

events.title: The massacre of 20 artists at the Mardi Gras festivities, at the annual…
events.blurb: The massacre of 20 artists at the Mardi Gras festivities, at the annual Carnaval de Romans during the festival, takes place in France at Romans-sur-Isère.

events.title: Michel de Montaigne signs the preface to his most significant work, Essays
events.blurb: Michel de Montaigne signs the preface to his most significant work, Essays. They are published later this year.

events.title: George de Lalaing, Count of Rennenberg defects from the Union of Utrecht and…
events.blurb: George de Lalaing, Count of Rennenberg defects from the Union of Utrecht and the Dutch Republic, and turns over the province of Groningen to King Philip II of Spain.

events.title: Iberian Union
events.blurb: Iberian Union: King Philip II of Spain becomes King of Portugal under the name Philip I, following the death without heirs of King Henry of Portugal, in a personal union of the crowns,

events.title: 1580 Dover Straits earthquake
events.blurb: The Dover Straits earthquake occurs.

events.title: English Fury at Mechelen
events.blurb: English Fury at Mechelen: English and Scottish mercenaries, assisting the Dutch Republic, storm the Spanish Netherlands city of Mechelen (in modern-day Belgium), killing 60 civilians and plundering the town's houses and churches.

events.title: The Lipizzan stud is established by Charles II, Archduke of Austria
events.blurb: The Lipizzan stud is established by Charles II, Archduke of Austria.

events.title: In the Kingdom of Golconda (part of the modern-day Indian state of Telangana),…
events.blurb: In the Kingdom of Golconda (part of the modern-day Indian state of Telangana), 15-year-old Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is proclaimed as the new Sultan upon the death of his father, Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah Wali.

events.title: Rebels of the Dutch Union of Utrecht, aided by French soldiers, make a…
events.blurb: Rebels of the Dutch Union of Utrecht, aided by French soldiers, make a surprise attack on the Spanish Netherlands city of Diest in the Duchy of Brabant, and overwhelm the strategic location, now in Belgium, in one day.

events.title: Within the Viceroyalty of Peru in South America Spanish explorer Juan de Garay…
events.blurb: Within the Viceroyalty of Peru in South America Spanish explorer Juan de Garay founds the first permanent Spanish settlement at what is now the capital of Argentina, on the Rio de la Plata.

events.title: The Book of Concord, a collection of Lutheran confessional documents, is published
events.blurb: The Book of Concord, a collection of Lutheran confessional documents, is published.

events.title: The Ostrog Bible, the first complete printed Bible translation into a Slavic…
events.blurb: The Ostrog Bible, the first complete printed Bible translation into a Slavic language (Old Church Slavonic), is first printed at Ostroh in the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth (modern-day Ukraine) by Ivan Fyodorov.

events.title: Battle of Alcântara
events.blurb: Battle of Alcântara: Spanish armies, led by Fernando Álvarez de Toledo, defending the claim of King Philip II of Spain to the Portuguese throne, defeat the armies of Portuguese claimant António, Prior of Crato.

events.title: Five of the seven provinces of the Dutch Republic (with the exception of…
events.blurb: Five of the seven provinces of the Dutch Republic (with the exception of Zeeland and Holland) sign the Treaty of Plessis-les-Tours, recognizing Francis, Duke of Anjou as the Republic's sovereign.

events.title: Lorenzo Suárez de Mendoza, the Spanish Count of Coruña, arrives in Mexico City…
events.blurb: Lorenzo Suárez de Mendoza, the Spanish Count of Coruña, arrives in Mexico City to take office as the Viceroy of New Spain, administering Mexico and Central America on behalf of King Philip II.

events.title: Siege of Steenwijk (1580–1581)
events.blurb: The Siege of Steenwijk in the Dutch Republic is started by the Spanish Netherlands. The siege will last four months and the Spanish troops will capture Steenwijk on February 23.

events.title: War of the Portuguese Succession
events.blurb: The War of the Portuguese Succession comes to an end as Spanish forces crush the final Portuguese resistance in the last stronghold in mainland Portugal, Porto. For the next 60 years, Portugal will be ruled by the Kings of Spain.

events.title: James Douglas, 4th Earl of Morton, formerly the regent for King James VI of…
events.blurb: James Douglas, 4th Earl of Morton, formerly the regent for King James VI of Scotland, is arrested during a meeting of Scotland's Privy Council at Holyrood on the accusation of James Stewart,

events.title: A meteorite strikes the Earth in Thuringia in the Holy Roman Empire
events.blurb: A meteorite strikes the Earth in Thuringia in the Holy Roman Empire.

events.title: John Dee practices angel magic with Barnabas Saul, but with no success
events.blurb: John Dee practices angel magic with Barnabas Saul, but with no success.

events.title: The Trier witch trials begin
events.blurb: The Trier witch trials begin.

events.title: Chandrasen Rathore, ruler of the Kingdom of Marwar (now part of the state of…
events.blurb: Chandrasen Rathore, ruler of the Kingdom of Marwar (now part of the state of Rajasthan in India) dies at the age of 39, leaving a power vacuum that allows the Mughal Empire to take control of the kingdom.

events.title: Treaty of Drohiczyn
events.blurb: The Treaty of Drohiczyn is concluded, ending the Livonian War and adding the conquered city of Riga to the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

events.title: Treaty of Plessis-les-Tours
events.blurb: The Treaty of Plessis-les-Tours between the Duchy of Anjou and most of the states of the Dutch Republic is ratified at Bourdeaux, granting Francis,

events.title: Prince Shin Thissa, later to become King of Burma in 1599 as Nyaungyan Min,…
events.blurb: (7th waxing of Tabaung 942 ME) Prince Shin Thissa, later to become King of Burma in 1599 as Nyaungyan Min, receives his first executive job when he is appointed to be Governor of Nyaungyan by his father, King Bayinnaung.

events.title: Zsigmond Báthory, the 8-year-old son of Kristóf Báthory, ruler of the…
events.blurb: Zsigmond Báthory, the 8-year-old son of Kristóf Báthory, ruler of the Principality of Transylvania, is elected by the Diet of Transylvania as the new voivode at the request of Kristóf, who dies 12 days later.

events.title: In Burma, Thiri Thudhamma Yaza of Martaban becomes the new Viceroy of Martaban…
events.blurb: (10th waning of Nayon 943 ME) In Burma, Thiri Thudhamma Yaza of Martaban becomes the new Viceroy of Martaban (now Mottama in the Mon State of Myanmar) after the demise of Minye Nandameit.

events.title: The Knights Hospitaller depose Jean de la Cassière as Grandmaster and appoint…
events.blurb: The Knights Hospitaller depose Jean de la Cassière as Grandmaster and appoint Mathurin Romegas in his place.

events.title: Act of Abjuration
events.blurb: At a meeting of the States General of the Union of Utrecht at Antwerp, the representatives vote to proclaim their independence from Spain in the Act of Abjuration, abjuring loyalty to Philip II of Spain as their sovereign,

events.title: Capture of Breda
events.blurb: Capture of Breda: After a surprise attack the day before, Spanish troops under the command of Claude de Berlaymont, Lord of Haultepenne, take the walled city Breda in the Netherlands.

events.title: A mercenary army of Sweden, under Pontus De la Gardie, captures Narva from Russia
events.blurb: A mercenary army of Sweden, under Pontus De la Gardie, captures Narva from Russia.

events.title: In Japan, warlord Oda Nobunaga invades the Iga Province
events.blurb: In Japan, warlord Oda Nobunaga invades the Iga Province. With 42,000 troops under his command against 10,000 defenders led by Takino Jurobei, Nobunaga controls most of central Japan within eight days.

events.title: Tenshō Iga War
events.blurb: The Tenshō Iga War ends in Japan with the surrender of Kashiwara Castle to Oda Nobunaga.

events.title: Ballet Comique de la Reine, the first narrative ballet, devised by Louise of…
events.blurb: Ballet Comique de la Reine, the first narrative ballet, devised by Louise of Lorraine, wife of Henry III of France, and choreographed by Balthasar de Beaujoyeulx, opens in its first performance at the court of Catherine de' Medici,

events.title: Jean de la Cassière is restored as Grandmaster of the Knights Hospitaller, by…
events.blurb: Jean de la Cassière is restored as Grandmaster of the Knights Hospitaller, by Pope Gregory XIII.

events.title: The temple complex of Kumbum is founded in Tibet
events.blurb: The temple complex of Kumbum is founded in Tibet.

events.title: The Cagayan battles in the Philippines, the only recorded clashes between…
events.blurb: The Cagayan battles in the Philippines, the only recorded clashes between Spanish regular soldiers and samurai warriors.

events.title: The University of Würzburg is refounded
events.blurb: The University of Würzburg is refounded.

events.title: Russia cedes its conquered areas in Livonia (Northern Latvia and Southern…
events.blurb: Russia cedes its conquered areas in Livonia (Northern Latvia and Southern Estonia), to the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

events.title: 1582 Ancuancu earthquake
events.blurb: 1582 Ancuancu earthquake: Ancuancu (in modern-day La Paz Department, Bolivia) is struck by an earthquake that reportedly buries all of the inhabitants, except for one chief, who reportedly loses the ability to speak.

events.title: Spanish conquistador Hernando de Lerma founds the settlement of Salta, Argentina
events.blurb: Spanish conquistador Hernando de Lerma founds the settlement of Salta, Argentina.

events.title: Siege of Takamatsu
events.blurb: Siege of Takamatsu: In Japan, Toyotomi Hideyoshi departs from the Himeji Castle in the modern-day Hyōgo Prefecture and begins his march westward with 20,000 soldiers to the Bitchū Province in the modern-day Okayama Prefecture.

events.title: The Honnō-ji Incident occurs in Kyoto in Japan, as Japanese warlord Oda…
events.blurb: (2nd day of the sixth month, Tenshō 10) The Honnō-ji Incident occurs in Kyoto in Japan, as Japanese warlord Oda Nobunaga, on the verge of unifying Japan under his rule, is assassinated following a betrayal by a rebel subject,

events.title: Shimizu Muneharu surrenders Takamatsu Castle to Toyotomi Hideyoshi and, in…
events.blurb: Shimizu Muneharu surrenders Takamatsu Castle to Toyotomi Hideyoshi and, in return for the pledge that the castle's defenders will be spared, commits the ritual suicide of seppuku.

events.title: Battle of Yamazaki
events.blurb: Battle of Yamazaki: Counterattacking forces led by Toyotomi Hideyoshi decisively defeat Akechi Mitsuhide's smaller army; Akechi is killed while retreating to his domain.

events.title: Raid of Ruthven in Scotland
events.blurb: Raid of Ruthven in Scotland: Presbyterian nobles led by William Ruthven, 1st Earl of Gowrie kidnap King James VI of Scotland, the kingdom's 16-year-old ruler, while he is hunting in Perthshire.

events.title: Ruthven and his co-conspirators arrange for John Maxwell, 8th Lord Maxwell,…
events.blurb: Ruthven and his co-conspirators arrange for John Maxwell, 8th Lord Maxwell, heir to former regent James Douglas, 4th Earl of Morton, to be installed as Scotland's regent.

events.title: (October 14 Gregorian)
events.blurb: (Julian) (October 14 Gregorian) – The Julian calendar is discarded at the end of the day in Italy, Poland, Portugal, and Spain as Pope Gregory XIII implements the Gregorian calendar.

events.title: (November 5 Gregorian)
events.blurb: (Julian) (November 5 Gregorian) – General Yermak Timofeyevich completes the Russian conquest of Siberia in the Battle of Chuvash Cape as Kuchum Khan abandons Qashliq, the capital of the Khanate of Sibir.

events.title: Ten years before he begins writing his first known plays, William Shakespeare,…
events.blurb: Ten years before he begins writing his first known plays, William Shakespeare, 18 years old, marries pregnant 26-year-old Anne Hathaway in England.

events.title: (December 19 Gregorian)
events.blurb: (Julian) (December 19 Gregorian) – France discards the Julian Calendar at the end of the day and adopts the Gregorian Calendar at midnight. Sunday, December 9 is followed the next day in France by Monday, December 20.

events.title: French Carthusian monks at Grande Chartreuse perfect a commercial recipe for…
events.blurb: French Carthusian monks at Grande Chartreuse perfect a commercial recipe for Chartreuse (liqueur).

events.title: Cesare Beccaria - On Crimes and Punishments (Dei delitti e delle pene), a…
events.blurb: Cesare Beccaria - On Crimes and Punishments (Dei delitti e delle pene), a founding work of penology

events.title: Horace Walpole - The Castle of Otranto "a story, translated by William…
events.blurb: Horace Walpole - The Castle of Otranto "a story, translated by William Marshal, Gent., from the original Italian of Onuphrio Muralto", the first Gothic novel

events.title: Immanuel Kant - Observations on the Feeling of the Beautiful and Sublime…
events.blurb: Immanuel Kant - Observations on the Feeling of the Beautiful and Sublime (Beobachtungen über das Gefühl des Schönen und Erhabenen)

events.title: The Siculicidium is carried out as hundreds of the Székely minority in…
events.blurb: The Siculicidium is carried out as hundreds of the Székely minority in Transylvania are massacred by the Austrian Army at Madéfalva.

events.title: John Wilkes is expelled from the House of Commons of Great Britain, for…
events.blurb: John Wilkes is expelled from the House of Commons of Great Britain, for seditious libel.

events.title: The settlement of St
events.blurb: The settlement of St. Louis is established.

events.title: The day after his return to Paris from a nine-year mission, French explorer…
events.blurb: The day after his return to Paris from a nine-year mission, French explorer and scholar Anquetil Du Perron presents a complete copy of the Zoroastrian sacred text, the Zend Avesta, to the Bibliothèque Royale in Paris,

events.title: Francisco Javier de la Torre arrives in Manila to become the new Spanish…
events.blurb: Francisco Javier de la Torre arrives in Manila to become the new Spanish Governor-General of the Philippines.

events.title: French and Indian War
events.blurb: After the British victory in the French and Indian War, the first post-war British expedition to explore the newly acquired territories east of the Mississippi River comes under attack by Tunica warriors.

events.title: Following lobbying by George Johnstone, the Governor of British West Florida,…
events.blurb: Following lobbying by George Johnstone, the Governor of British West Florida, Britain's Lords of Trade vote to recommend the northern boundary for the new province to run from the confluence of the Yazoo River and the Mississippi (at…

events.title: A mutual defense treaty between the Russian Empire and the Kingdom of Prussia…
events.blurb: A mutual defense treaty between the Russian Empire and the Kingdom of Prussia is signed in Saint Petersburg between representatives of Russia's Empress Catherine the Great and Prussia's King Frederick the Great.

events.title: Sugar Act
events.blurb: The Sugar Act is passed in Great Britain.

events.title: Residents of French Louisiana are informed for the first time that they will…
events.blurb: Residents of French Louisiana are informed for the first time that they will come under Spanish rule as the result of a secret agreement of November 13,

events.title: Eight-year-old child prodigy Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart performs a private…
events.blurb: Eight-year-old child prodigy Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart performs a private concert before King George III and Queen Charlotte in Great Britain, and has an encore on May 19.

events.title: Baden, one of the member states of the Confederation of Switzerland, declares…
events.blurb: Baden, one of the member states of the Confederation of Switzerland, declares a policy of remaining neutral in future conflicts,

events.title: One of the strongest tornadoes ever recorded hits Woldegk, Germany
events.blurb: One of the strongest tornadoes ever recorded hits Woldegk, Germany.

events.title: The last British troops depart Havana, Cuba, two years after having captured…
events.blurb: The last British troops depart Havana, Cuba, two years after having captured it from Spain during the Seven Years' War.

events.title: Conditional repatriation of the Acadians in Canada, French colonists who took…
events.blurb: Conditional repatriation of the Acadians in Canada, French colonists who took up arms against the British during the war, is approved by order of King George III on advice of the Privy Council.

events.title: King George, on advice of the Privy Council, issues the Royal Determination of…
events.blurb: King George, on advice of the Privy Council, issues the Royal Determination of the disputed boundary between the colonial provinces of New York and New Hampshire.

events.title: Enoch Brown school massacre
events.blurb: In what is described 250 years later as "The first documented United States school shooting", a group of four Delaware Indians invade a schoolhouse near what is now Greencastle, Pennsylvania and kill ten schoolchildren and their teacher,

events.title: Treaty of Fort Niagara
events.blurb: The Treaty of Fort Niagara is signed between Great Britain and 44 North American Indian nations, bring an end to the ongoing war that had started in 1756 with most of the northern Indian tribes.

events.title: Stanisław August Poniatowski is elected as the King of the Polish–Lithuanian…
events.blurb: Stanisław August Poniatowski is elected as the King of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

events.title: English scholar Edward Gibbon conceives the idea of writing The History of the…
events.blurb: English scholar Edward Gibbon conceives the idea of writing The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, "as I sat musing amid the ruins of the Capitol".

events.title: Battle of Buxar
events.blurb: Battle of Buxar: The British East India Company defeats the combined armies of Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Bengal, the Nawab of Awadh, and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II.

events.title: Mary Campbell, a captive of the Lenape during the French and Indian War, is…
events.blurb: Mary Campbell, a captive of the Lenape during the French and Indian War, is turned over to forces commanded by Colonel Henry Bouquet.

events.title: The first chocolate factory in the Thirteen Colonies is established by Dr
events.blurb: The first chocolate factory in the Thirteen Colonies is established by Dr. James Baker at Dorchester, Massachusetts.

events.title: Frederick the Great, the King of Prussia, issues a decree abolishing the…
events.blurb: Frederick the Great, the King of Prussia, issues a decree abolishing the historic punishments against unmarried women in Germany for "sex crimes", particularly the Hurenstrafen (literally "whore shaming") practices of public humiliation.

events.title: Desai Atash Behram is established in Navsari, India
events.blurb: Desai Atash Behram is established in Navsari, India.

events.title: Isaac Barré, a member of the British House of Commons for Wycombe and a…
events.blurb: Isaac Barré, a member of the British House of Commons for Wycombe and a veteran of the French and Indian War in the British American colonies,

events.title: Prince Joseph of Austria marries Princess Maria Josepha of Bavaria in Vienna
events.blurb: Prince Joseph of Austria marries Princess Maria Josepha of Bavaria in Vienna.

events.title: One week before his death, Mir Jafar, who had been enthroned as the Nawab of…
events.blurb: One week before his death, Mir Jafar, who had been enthroned as the Nawab of Bengal and ruler of the Bengali people with the support and protection of the British East India Company, abdicates in favor of his 18-year-old son,

events.title: After a public campaign by the writer Voltaire, judges in Paris posthumously…
events.blurb: After a public campaign by the writer Voltaire, judges in Paris posthumously exonerate Jean Calas of murdering his son. Calas had been tortured and executed in 1762 on the charge, though his son may have committed suicide.

events.title: At Fort Tombecbe, near what is now the town of Epes, Alabama, representatives…
events.blurb: At Fort Tombecbe, near what is now the town of Epes, Alabama, representatives of the British Empire and of the Choctaw Indian tribe in Mississippi sign a peace treaty in the wake of French cession of claims to the British.

events.title: After completing the portion of the Mason–Dixon line marking the semi-circular…
events.blurb: After completing the portion of the Mason–Dixon line marking the semi-circular boundary between Pennsylvania and Delaware,

events.title: At Saint Petersburg, German engineer Christian Kratzenstein presents to the…
events.blurb: At Saint Petersburg, German engineer Christian Kratzenstein presents to the Russian Academy of Sciences a perfected version of the arithmetical machine originally invented by Gottfried Leibniz.

events.title: Not long after British rule has started over the formerly French colony of…
events.blurb: Not long after British rule has started over the formerly French colony of Quebec, an accidental fire destroys one quarter of the town of Montreal.

events.title: During a stroll in the park "on a fine Sabbath afternoon" at Glasgow Green,…
events.blurb: During a stroll in the park "on a fine Sabbath afternoon" at Glasgow Green, Scottish engineer James Watt receives the inspiration that provides the breakthrough in his development of the steam engine;

events.title: The Isle of Man is brought under British control, the Isle of Man Purchase Act…
events.blurb: The Isle of Man is brought under British control, the Isle of Man Purchase Act (coming into force 10 May) confirming HM Treasury's purchase of the feudal rights of the Dukes of Atholl, as Lord of Mann over the island,

events.title: King George III dismisses George Grenville from the office of Prime Minister…
events.blurb: King George III dismisses George Grenville from the office of Prime Minister of Great Britain, and replaces him with another Whig Party statesman, Charles Watson-Wentworth, Lord Rockingham.

events.title: Qianlong, the Emperor of China issues a decree that copper engravings be made…
events.blurb: Qianlong, the Emperor of China issues a decree that copper engravings be made to depict all of his victories in battle.

events.title: Headed by Odawa Chief Pontiac and George Croghan, a party of Great Lakes…
events.blurb: Headed by Odawa Chief Pontiac and George Croghan, a party of Great Lakes tribesmen and British soldiers travel along the Wabash River and obtain the release of all white prisoners of war remaining in the Miami people and Odawa villages…

events.title: At Yale College, eight students attack the residence of Yale's President…
events.blurb: At Yale College, eight students attack the residence of Yale's President Thomas Clap because of his promotion of "New Light" Calvinist doctrine;

events.title: Russian Empress Catherine II issues a decree authorizing the new way to…
events.blurb: Russian Empress Catherine II issues a decree authorizing the new way to produce vodka (by freezing).

events.title: Stamp Act 1765
events.blurb: In protest of the Stamp Act, Bostonians attack the home of official Andrew Oliver.

events.title: Treaty of Allahabad
events.blurb: The Treaty of Allahabad is signed. The Treaty marks the political and constitutional involvement and the beginning of Company rule in India.

events.title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau's house in Switzerland is stoned by a mob
events.blurb: Jean-Jacques Rousseau's house in Switzerland is stoned by a mob.

events.title: François Antoine announces he has killed the Beast of Gévaudan
events.blurb: François Antoine announces he has killed the Beast of Gévaudan.

events.title: Childsburgh, the Orange County, North Carolina seat laid out as Corbin Town in…
events.blurb: Childsburgh, the Orange County, North Carolina seat laid out as Corbin Town in 1754, and renamed in 1759, is renamed Hillsborough, in honor of Wills Hill, 1st Marquess of Downshire, Earl of Hillsborough.

events.title: American botanist John Bartram completes his first exploration and cataloging…
events.blurb: American botanist John Bartram completes his first exploration and cataloging of North American plants after more than nine months.

events.title: James Fordyce
events.blurb: Dr. James Fordyce's two-volume compendium Sermons to Young Women is published in London.

events.title: Charles Edward Stuart ("Bonnie Prince Charlie") becomes the new Stuart…
events.blurb: Charles Edward Stuart ("Bonnie Prince Charlie") becomes the new Stuart claimant to the throne of Great Britain, as King Charles III, and figurehead for Jacobitism.

events.title: Christian VII becomes King of Denmark-Norway
events.blurb: Christian VII becomes King of Denmark-Norway.

events.title: An observer in Wilmington, North Carolina reports to the Edinburgh newspaper…
events.blurb: An observer in Wilmington, North Carolina reports to the Edinburgh newspaper Caledonian Mercury that three ships have been seized by British men-of-war, on the charge of carrying official documents without stamps.

events.title: Meermin Slave Mutiny
events.blurb: Meermin Slave Mutiny: Captive Malagasy people seize a Dutch East India Company slave ship in the Indian Ocean.

events.title: Antonio de Ulloa, the first Spanish governor of Louisiana, arrives in New Orleans
events.blurb: Antonio de Ulloa, the first Spanish governor of Louisiana, arrives in New Orleans.

events.title: American Revolution
events.blurb: American Revolution: The British Parliament repeals the Stamp Act, which has been very unpopular in the British colonies; the persuasion of Benjamin Franklin is considered partly responsible.

events.title: King Carlos III of Spain issues a royal cédula from Aranjuez to round up all…
events.blurb: King Carlos III of Spain issues a royal cédula from Aranjuez to round up all ethnic Chinese in the Philippines and to move them to ghettoes in various provinces.

events.blurb: The Theatre Royal, Bristol, opens in England. Also this year in England, the surviving Georgian Theatre (Stockton-on-Tees) opens as a playhouse.

events.blurb: On the occasion of the 28th birthday of King George III, members of the Sons of Liberty in Manhattan erect a liberty pole as a protest for the first time.

events.blurb: The revolt in Quito (at this time part of Spain's Viceroyalty of Nueva Granada; the modern-day capital of Ecuador) is ended peacefully as royal forces enter the city under the command of Guayaquil Governor Pedro Zelaya.

events.blurb: The position of Patriarch of the Serbs, established on April 9, 1346 as the authority over the Serbian Orthodox Church, is abolished by order of Sultan Mustafa III of the Ottoman Empire;

events.blurb: John Penn, the Colonial Governor of Pennsylvania and one of the four Penn family owners of the Pennsylvania land grant,

events.blurb: Crown Prince Gustav of Sweden weds Princess Sophia Magdalena of Denmark. They become King Gustav III and Queen Consort Sophia of Sweden upon his ascension to the throne in 1771.
