events.title: Jim Beam is founded as Old Jake Beam Sour Mash
events.blurb: Jim Beam is founded as Old Jake Beam Sour Mash.

events.title: Former Governor-General of India Warren Hastings is acquitted by the British…
events.blurb: Former Governor-General of India Warren Hastings is acquitted by the British House of Lords of misconduct.

events.title: The Hudson's Bay Company trading post Fort Edmonton is constructed
events.blurb: The Hudson's Bay Company trading post Fort Edmonton is constructed; the city of Edmonton, Alberta, eventually grows from it.

events.title: Batavian Revolution in Amsterdam
events.blurb: Batavian Revolution in Amsterdam: William V, Prince of Orange, Stadtholder of the Dutch Republic (Republic of the Seven United Netherlands), flees the country.

events.title: The Batavian Republic is proclaimed in Amsterdam, ending the Dutch Republic…
events.blurb: The Batavian Republic is proclaimed in Amsterdam, ending the Dutch Republic (Republic of the Seven United Netherlands).

events.title: Flanders campaign
events.blurb: Flanders campaign: Capture of the Dutch fleet at Den Helder: The Dutch fleet, frozen in Zuiderzee, is captured by the French 8th Hussars.

events.title: War of the First Coalition Battle of Genoa
events.blurb: War of the First Coalition Battle of Genoa: The British and Neapolitan fleets are victorious over the French.

events.title: Ludwig van Beethoven makes his public debut in Vienna performing his Second…
events.blurb: Ludwig van Beethoven makes his public debut in Vienna performing his Second Piano Concerto under the baton of his teacher Antonio Salieri.

events.title: Peace of Basel
events.blurb: The Peace of Basel is signed, between France and Prussia.

events.title: George, Prince of Wales, marries Caroline of Brunswick
events.blurb: George, Prince of Wales, marries Caroline of Brunswick.

events.title: Battle of Richmond Hill
events.blurb: June – The Battle of Richmond Hill is fought in the colony of New South Wales, between the Darug people and British colonial forces.

events.title: The Dialectic and Philanthropic Societies are founded at the University of…
events.blurb: The Dialectic and Philanthropic Societies are founded at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

events.title: The Copenhagen Fire of 1795, starting in a naval warehouse, destroys 941 houses
events.blurb: The Copenhagen Fire of 1795, starting in a naval warehouse, destroys 941 houses.

events.title: Louis XVII, Prince Royal and titular King of France, dies in captivity in the…
events.blurb: Louis XVII, Prince Royal and titular King of France, dies in captivity in the Temple (Paris) and will be buried in an unmarked grave.

events.title: Construction of the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct in Wales begins
events.blurb: Construction of the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct in Wales begins.

events.title: Treaty of Greenville
events.blurb: The signing of the Treaty of Greenville puts an end to the Northwest Indian War.

events.title: A large slave rebellion occurs in Curaçao, suppressed the following month
events.blurb: A large slave rebellion occurs in Curaçao, suppressed the following month.

events.title: British forces capture Trincomalee, Ceylon
events.blurb: British forces capture Trincomalee, Ceylon.

events.title: Battle of Krtsanisi
events.blurb: Battle of Krtsanisi: The Persian emperor Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar defeats the forces of Heraclius II of Georgia.

events.title: Battle of the Diamond
events.blurb: Battle of the Diamond: Protestant forces defeat Catholic troops in Loughgall, Ireland, leading to the foundation of the Orange Order.

events.title: British forces capture the Île d'Yeu off the coast of Brittany
events.blurb: British forces capture the Île d'Yeu off the coast of Brittany.

events.title: 13 Vendémiaire: Royalist riots in Paris are crushed by troops under Paul…
events.blurb: 13 Vendémiaire: Royalist riots in Paris are crushed by troops under Paul Barras and newly-reinstalled artillery officer Napoleon Bonaparte.

events.title: Third Partition of Poland
events.blurb: The Third Partition of Poland is made, dividing the territory of the Commonwealth of Poland between the Habsburg monarchy, Prussia and the Russian Empire.

events.title: Wold Cottage meteorite
events.blurb: Wold Cottage meteorite: A meteorite falls at Wold Newton, a hamlet in Yorkshire in England.

events.title: Tennessee is admitted as the 16th U
events.blurb: Tennessee is admitted as the 16th U.S. state.

events.title: Catherine the Great dies, and is succeeded by her son Paul I of Russia
events.blurb: Catherine the Great dies, and is succeeded by her son Paul I of Russia. His wife Sophie Marie Dorothea of Württemberg becomes Empress consort.

events.title: Groton, New Hampshire is incorporated as a town
events.blurb: Groton, New Hampshire is incorporated as a town.

events.title: French forces (9,500 men) under Masséna attack the Austrian army at Fontaniva
events.blurb: French forces (9,500 men) under Masséna attack the Austrian army at Fontaniva. After a desperate assault he is outnumbered, and forced to retreat to Verona.

events.title: Battle of Caldiero
events.blurb: Battle of Caldiero: French forces are defeated by the Austrians at Caldiero, and pushed back to Verona. This marks Napoleon's first defeat, losing nearly 2,000 men and 2 guns.

events.title: The French-Republican army divisions of the Army of Italy invade the…
events.blurb: The French-Republican army divisions of the Army of Italy invade the territories of Venice.

events.title: War of the First Coalition – Battle of Lodi
events.blurb: War of the First Coalition – Battle of Lodi: General Napoleon Bonaparte defeats the Austrian rearguard, in forcing a crossing of the bridge over the Adda River in Italy. The Austrians lose some 2,000 men, 14 guns, and 30 ammunition wagons.

events.title: The first Dutch (and general) elections are held for the National Assembly of…
events.blurb: The first Dutch (and general) elections are held for the National Assembly of the Batavian Republic. (The next Dutch general elections are held in 1888).

events.title: The capital of Upper Canada is moved from Newark to York
events.blurb: The capital of Upper Canada is moved from Newark to York.

events.title: Widow Joséphine de Beauharnais marries General Napoleon Bonaparte
events.blurb: Widow Joséphine de Beauharnais marries General Napoleon Bonaparte.

events.title: War of the First Coalition – Battle of Dego
events.blurb: War of the First Coalition – Battle of Dego: French troops under Napoleon Bonaparte defeat the Austro-Sardinian forces near Dego. The hamlet changes hands for two days in hard fighting.

events.title: War of the First Coalition – Battle of Ceva
events.blurb: War of the First Coalition – Battle of Ceva: French troops (some 8,000 men) under General Pierre Augereau assault the Sardinian defensive positions at Ceva. After fierce fighting, the defensive system gives way under French pressure.

events.title: The French proclaim the Republic of Alba on the occupied territories
events.blurb: The French proclaim the Republic of Alba on the occupied territories. Two days later, King Victor Amadeus III of Sardinia signs the Armistice of Cherasco, in the headquarters of Napoleon.

events.title: Case of the Lyons Mail
events.blurb: Case of the Lyons Mail: During the night, five highwaymen attack the mail between Paris and Lyon, kill the postmen and steal the funds sent to the armies in Italy.

events.title: In an impassioned speech, U
events.blurb: In an impassioned speech, U.S. Representative Fisher Ames of Massachusetts persuades his fellow members of the House to support the Jay Treaty.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte forms an advanced guard (3,500 infantry and 1,500 cavalry)…
events.blurb: Napoleon Bonaparte forms an advanced guard (3,500 infantry and 1,500 cavalry) under General Claude Dallemagne. He sends this force along the south bank of the Po River, to cross it with boats at Piacenza.

events.title: Edward Jenner administers the first smallpox vaccination, in England
events.blurb: Edward Jenner administers the first smallpox vaccination, in England.

events.title: The last mock Garrat Elections are held in Surrey, England
events.blurb: The last mock Garrat Elections are held in Surrey, England.

events.title: War of the First Coalition - Battle of Borghetto
events.blurb: War of the First Coalition - Battle of Borghetto: French troops (28,000 men) under Napoleon Bonaparte force a crossing of the Mincio River and push the Austrian army back towards the Tyrol.

events.title: Ragunda lake in Sweden bursts and drains completely, leaving the Döda fallet dry
events.blurb: Ragunda lake in Sweden bursts and drains completely, leaving the Döda fallet dry.

events.title: Scottish explorer Mungo Park becomes the first European to reach the Niger River
events.blurb: Scottish explorer Mungo Park becomes the first European to reach the Niger River.

events.title: Carl Friedrich Gauss discovers that every positive integer is representable as…
events.blurb: Carl Friedrich Gauss discovers that every positive integer is representable as a sum of at most 3 triangular numbers.

events.title: The United States takes possession of Detroit from Great Britain, under the…
events.blurb: The United States takes possession of Detroit from Great Britain, under the terms of the Jay Treaty.

events.title: Surveyors of the Connecticut Land Company name an area in Ohio Cleveland,…
events.blurb: Surveyors of the Connecticut Land Company name an area in Ohio Cleveland, after Gen. Moses Cleaveland, the superintendent of the surveying party.

events.title: The Wearmouth Bridge in England, designed by Rowland Burdon in cast iron,…
events.blurb: The Wearmouth Bridge in England, designed by Rowland Burdon in cast iron, opens to traffic. Its span of makes it the world's longest single-span vehicular bridge extant at this date.

events.title: A mob of peasants overtakes the Convent of St
events.blurb: A mob of peasants overtakes the Convent of St. Peter (Bludenz, Austria) and murders Ignaz Anton von Indermauer.

events.title: Second Treaty of San Ildefonso
events.blurb: Second Treaty of San Ildefonso: Spain and France form an alliance against Great Britain.

events.title: Jewish emancipation in the Batavian Republic (Netherlands)
events.blurb: Jewish emancipation in the Batavian Republic (Netherlands).

events.title: Grenelle camp affair, a failed uprising by supporters of Gracchus Babeuf…
events.blurb: Grenelle camp affair, a failed uprising by supporters of Gracchus Babeuf against the French Directory

events.title: Jane Austen begins writing her first draft of Pride and Prejudice, under the…
events.blurb: Jane Austen begins writing her first draft of Pride and Prejudice, under the title First Impressions (the book will not be published until 1813).

events.title: Treaty of Tripoli
events.blurb: The Treaty of Tripoli (between the United States and Tripoli) is signed at Tripoli (see also 1797).

events.title: Battle of Arcole
events.blurb: Battle of Arcole: French forces under General Napoleon defeat the Austrians at Arcole. After a bold maneuver, he outflanks the Austrian army (24,000 men) under Freiherr József Alvinczi, and cuts off its line of retreat.

events.title: The British government begins work on a 40-acre (162,000 m²) site at Norman…
events.blurb: The British government begins work on a 40-acre (162,000 m²) site at Norman Cross, for the world's first purpose-built prisoner-of-war camp.

events.title: British Royal Navy ship HMS Courageux is wrecked on the Barbary Coast with the…
events.blurb: British Royal Navy ship HMS Courageux is wrecked on the Barbary Coast with the loss of 464 of the 593 onboard.

events.title: Veronese Easter
events.blurb: Veronese Easter: Citizens of Verona, Italy, began an unsuccessful eight-day rebellion against the French occupying forces.

events.title: Battle of San Juan
events.blurb: Battle of San Juan: Sir Ralph Abercromby unsuccessfully invades San Juan, Puerto Rico in what will be one of the largest British attacks on Spanish territories in the western hemisphere,

events.title: The secret Lautaro Lodge as the Logia de los Caballeros Racionales ("Lodge of…
events.blurb: The secret Lautaro Lodge as the Logia de los Caballeros Racionales ("Lodge of Rational Knights") is founded, perhaps in Cádiz;

events.title: The parliament of the Cisalpine Republic adopts the Italian green-white-red…
events.blurb: The parliament of the Cisalpine Republic adopts the Italian green-white-red tricolour as their official flag (this is considered the birth of the flag of Italy).

events.title: Action of 13 January 1797, part of the War of the First Coalition
events.blurb: Action of 13 January 1797, part of the War of the First Coalition: Two British Royal Navy frigates, HMS Indefatigable and HMS Amazon, drive the French 74-gun ship of the line Droits de l'Homme aground on the coast of Brittany,

events.title: War of the First Coalition – Battle of La Favorita
events.blurb: War of the First Coalition – Battle of La Favorita: French forces (28,000 men) under Napoleon Bonaparte stop the Austrian push to relieve Mantua. The garrison under Field Marshal Dagobert von Wurmser is deprived of food and reinforcements.

events.title: Battle of Faenza
events.blurb: Battle of Faenza: A French corps (9,000 men) under General Claude-Victor Perrin defeats the forces from the Papal States, at Castel Bolognese near Faenza, Italy.

events.title: 1797 Riobamba earthquake
events.blurb: The Riobamba earthquake in Ecuador, estimated magnitude 8.3, causes up to 40,000 casualties.

events.title: "Gott erhalte Franz den Kaiser" is first performed, with the music composed in…
events.blurb: "Gott erhalte Franz den Kaiser" is first performed, with the music composed in January by Joseph Haydn, and it also becomes the tune of the Deutschlandlied, the German national anthem (Deutschland, Deutschland über alles,

events.title: Treaty of Tolentino
events.blurb: Treaty of Tolentino: Pope Pius VI signs a peace treaty with Revolutionary France. He is forced to deliver works of art, treasures, territory, the Comtat Venaissin, and 30 million francs.

events.title: William Tate surrenders to the British at Fishguard
events.blurb: William Tate surrenders to the British at Fishguard.

events.title: Bank Restriction Act 1797
events.blurb: Bank Restriction Act removes the requirement for the Bank of England (the national bank of Great Britain) to convert banknotes into gold – Restriction period lasts until 1821.

events.title: Protestant missionaries from the London Missionary Society land in Tahiti,…
events.blurb: Protestant missionaries from the London Missionary Society land in Tahiti, from the Duff (celebrated as Missionary Day in French Polynesia).

events.title: Médée, an opera by Luigi Cherubini, is premiered in Paris
events.blurb: Médée, an opera by Luigi Cherubini, is premiered in Paris.

events.title: Battle of Parramatta
events.blurb: Battle of Parramatta: Resistance leader Pemulwuy leads a group of aboriginal warriors, estimated to be at least 100, in an attack on a government farm at Toongabbie in Sydney, Australia.

events.title: The Spithead and Nore mutinies break out in the British Royal Navy
events.blurb: The Spithead and Nore mutinies break out in the British Royal Navy.

events.title: The first ship of the United States Navy, the frigate USS United States, is…
events.blurb: The first ship of the United States Navy, the frigate USS United States, is commissioned.

events.title: English abolitionist William Wilberforce marries Barbara Ann Spooner about six…
events.blurb: English abolitionist William Wilberforce marries Barbara Ann Spooner about six weeks after their first meeting.

events.title: French troops disembark in Corfu, beginning the First period of French rule in…
events.blurb: French troops disembark in Corfu, beginning the First period of French rule in the Ionian Islands.

events.title: William Blount
events.blurb: U.S. Senator William Blount becomes the first federal legislator to be expelled from office, as his fellow Senators vote 25 to 1 to block him from his seat during an investigation against him on charges of criminal conspiracy.

events.title: Gual and España conspiracy against Spanish rule in Colonial Venezuela is exposed
events.blurb: Gual and España conspiracy against Spanish rule in Colonial Venezuela is exposed.

events.title: Massacre of Tranent
events.blurb: Massacre of Tranent: British troops attack protestors against enforced recruitment into the militia at Tranent, Scotland, killing 11 and injuring 8.

events.title: Coup of 18 Fructidor
events.blurb: The Coup of 18 Fructidor is carried out in France as three of the five members of The Directory, France's executive council, arrested royalist members of the Council of Five Hundred, the national legislature,

events.title: Dominique-Vincent Ramel-Nogaret, French finance minister, repudiates two…
events.blurb: Dominique-Vincent Ramel-Nogaret, French finance minister, repudiates two thirds of France's debt.

events.title: Battle of Camperdown
events.blurb: Battle of Camperdown: the British Royal Navy defeats the fleet of the Batavian Republic off the coast of Holland.

events.title: Treaty of Campo Formio
events.blurb: The Treaty of Campo Formio ends the War of the First Coalition.

events.title: The XYZ Affair inflames tensions between France and the United States when…
events.blurb: The XYZ Affair inflames tensions between France and the United States when American negotiators Charles Cotesworth Pinckney, John Marshall, and Elbridge Gerry meet with French government representatives Jean-Conrad Hottinguer,

events.title: In Boston Harbor, the 44-gun United States Navy frigate is launched to fight…
events.blurb: In Boston Harbor, the 44-gun United States Navy frigate is launched to fight Barbary pirates off the coast of Tripoli; the ship will remain in commission in the 21st century.

events.title: André-Jacques Garnerin makes the first parachute descent, at Parc Monceau, Paris
events.blurb: André-Jacques Garnerin makes the first parachute descent, at Parc Monceau, Paris; he uses a silk parachute to descend approximately from a hot air balloon.

events.title: 1797 Rugby School rebellion
events.blurb: 1797 Rugby School rebellion: The students at Rugby School in England rebel against the headmaster, Henry Ingles, after he decrees that the damage to a tradesman's windows should be paid for by the students.

events.title: The Piedmontese Republic is declared in the territory of Piedmont
events.blurb: The Piedmontese Republic is declared in the territory of Piedmont.

events.title: Battle of Tory Island
events.blurb: Battle of Tory Island: A British Royal Navy squadron, under Sir John Borlase Warren, prevents French Republican ships, commanded by Jean-Baptiste-François Bompart,

events.title: Alois Senefelder invents lithography
events.blurb: Alois Senefelder invents lithography.

events.title: French invasion of Malta
events.blurb: French invasion of Malta: French forces under Napoleon Bonaparte capture the island fortress of Malta on the way to Egypt.

events.title: Battle of St. George's Caye
events.blurb: Battle of St. George's Caye: Off the coast of British Honduras (modern-day Belize), a group of European settlers and Africans defeats a Spanish force sent from Mexico to drive them out.

events.title: Nathan Mayer Rothschild moves from Frankfurt in the Holy Roman Empire to…
events.blurb: Nathan Mayer Rothschild moves from Frankfurt in the Holy Roman Empire to England, settling up in business as a textile trader and financier in Manchester.

events.title: Constantine Hangerli enters Bucharest, as Prince of Wallachia
events.blurb: Constantine Hangerli enters Bucharest, as Prince of Wallachia.

events.title: The Pope is taken captive, and the Papacy is removed from power, by French…
events.blurb: The Pope is taken captive, and the Papacy is removed from power, by French General Louis-Alexandre Berthier.

events.title: Roger Griswold
events.blurb: U.S. Representative Roger Griswold (Fed-CT) beats Congressman Matthew Lyon (Dem-Rep-VT) with a cane, after the House declines to censure Lyon for earlier spitting in Griswold's face; the House declines to discipline either man.

events.title: Irish Rebellion of 1798
events.blurb: the Irish Rebellion of 1798 begins when the Irish Militia arrest the leadership of the Society of United Irishmen, a group unique amongst Irish republican and nationalist movements in that it unifies Catholics and Protestants (Anglican,

events.title: French troops enter Bern
events.blurb: French troops enter Bern.

events.title: The Mississippi Territory is organized by the United States, from territory…
events.blurb: The Mississippi Territory is organized by the United States, from territory ceded by Georgia and South Carolina; later it is twice expanded, to include disputed territory claimed by both the U.S.

events.title: The Helvetic Republic, a French client republic, is proclaimed following the…
events.blurb: The Helvetic Republic, a French client republic, is proclaimed following the collapse of the Old Swiss Confederacy after the French invasion; Aarau becomes the republic's temporary capital.

events.title: The United States Department of the Navy is established as a cabinet-level…
events.blurb: The United States Department of the Navy is established as a cabinet-level department. Benjamin Stoddert, a civilian businessman, is appointed as the first Navy Secretary by President Adams.

events.title: Pitt–Tierney duel takes place on Putney Heath
events.blurb: Pitt–Tierney duel takes place on Putney Heath. British Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger fights a duel against opposition politician George Tierney

events.title: Mission San Luis Rey de Francia is founded in California
events.blurb: Mission San Luis Rey de Francia is founded in California.

events.title: The first of the four Alien and Sedition Acts, the Naturalization Act of 1798,…
events.blurb: The first of the four Alien and Sedition Acts, the Naturalization Act of 1798, is signed into law by U.S. President Adams, requiring immigrants to wait 14 years rather than five years to become naturalized citizens of the United States.

events.title: The United States Marine Corps is re-established under its present name
events.blurb: The United States Marine Corps is re-established under its present name.

events.title: Battle of Shubra Khit
events.blurb: Battle of Shubra Khit: French troops defeat the Mamelukes, during Napoleon's march from Alexandria to take Cairo.

events.title: An Act for the relief of sick and disabled seamen
events.blurb: The Relief of Sick and Disabled Seamen Act is signed into law, creating the Marine Hospital Service, the forerunner to the current United States Public Health Service Commissioned Corps.

events.title: Battle of the Pyramids
events.blurb: Battle of the Pyramids: Napoleon Bonaparte defeats the Ottoman forces near the Pyramids. French forces claim control over Egypt's political center.

events.title: Battle of the Nile (near Abu Qir)
events.blurb: Battle of the Nile (near Abu Qir): Lord Nelson defeats the French navy under Admiral Brueys.

events.title: French troops land at Kilcummin in County Mayo to assist the Irish Rebellion
events.blurb: French troops land at Kilcummin in County Mayo to assist the Irish Rebellion.

events.title: Charles Brockden Brown publishes the first significant American novel, the…
events.blurb: Charles Brockden Brown publishes the first significant American novel, the Gothic fiction Wieland: or, The Transformation; an American Tale.

events.title: Conscription is made mandatory in France by the Jourdan Law
events.blurb: Conscription is made mandatory in France by the Jourdan Law.

events.title: Lyrical Ballads is published anonymously by Samuel Taylor Coleridge and…
events.blurb: Lyrical Ballads is published anonymously by Samuel Taylor Coleridge and William Wordsworth, inaugurating the English Romantic movement in literature.

events.title: Battle of Killala
events.blurb: Battle of Killala: in the last land battle of the Irish Rebellion of 1798, British troops defeat the remaining rebel Irish and French forces at Killala.

events.title: Matthew Lyon
events.blurb: U.S. Representative Matthew Lyon of Vermont becomes the first member of Congress to be put on trial for violating the new Sedition Act of 1798.

events.title: Revolt of Cairo
events.blurb: Revolt of Cairo: Napoleon Bonaparte suppresses a revolt in Cairo. French occupation survives but becomes more dependent on force and administration.

events.title: Capitulation of the French garrison at Hyderabad to East India Company troops…
events.blurb: Capitulation of the French garrison at Hyderabad to East India Company troops under James Kirkpatrick, British Resident.

events.title: British whaler John Fearn becomes the first European to land on Nauru
events.blurb: British whaler John Fearn becomes the first European to land on Nauru.

events.title: Trade between the United States and modern-day Uruguay begins when John…
events.blurb: Trade between the United States and modern-day Uruguay begins when John Leamy's frigate John arrives in Montevideo.

events.title: Peasants War in the Southern Netherlands
events.blurb: Peasants War in the Southern Netherlands: The revolt is crushed in Hasselt; during the uprising it is estimated that 5,000 to 10,000 people have been killed.

events.title: General Joubert of the Piedmontese Republic occupies the Sardinian capital of…
events.blurb: General Joubert of the Piedmontese Republic occupies the Sardinian capital of Turin.

events.title: Conrad John Reed, 12, finds what he describes as a "heavy yellow rock" along…
events.blurb: Conrad John Reed, 12, finds what he describes as a "heavy yellow rock" along Little Meadow Creek in Cabarrus County, North Carolina, and makes it a doorstop in his home.

events.title: The Nawab (provincial governor) of Oudh in northern India sends to George III…
events.blurb: The Nawab (provincial governor) of Oudh in northern India sends to George III of Great Britain the Padshah Nama, an official history of the reign of Shah Jahan.

events.title: William Cockerill begins building cotton-spinning machinery in Belgium
events.blurb: William Cockerill begins building cotton-spinning machinery in Belgium.

events.title: The Place Royale in Paris is renamed Place des Vosges, when the Department of…
events.blurb: The Place Royale in Paris is renamed Place des Vosges, when the Department of Vosges becomes the first to pay new Revolutionary taxes.

events.title: Maltese patriot Dun Mikiel Xerri, along with a number of other patriots, is…
events.blurb: Maltese patriot Dun Mikiel Xerri, along with a number of other patriots, is executed.

events.title: The Parthenopean Republic is established in Naples by French General Jean…
events.blurb: The Parthenopean Republic is established in Naples by French General Jean Étienne Championnet; King Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies flees.

events.title: The Jiaqing Emperor of China comes into his full powers on the death of his…
events.blurb: The Jiaqing Emperor of China comes into his full powers on the death of his father, the Qianlong Emperor. He prosecutes corrupt court official Heshen and issues a decree prohibiting the import of opium to China.

events.title: Quasi-War
events.blurb: Quasi-War: In the single-ship action of USS Constellation vs L'Insurgente in the Caribbean, the American ship is the victor.

events.title: Federalist James Ross becomes President pro tempore of the United States Senate
events.blurb: Federalist James Ross becomes President pro tempore of the United States Senate.

events.title: Siege of Corfu (1798–1799)
events.blurb: The Russo-Ottoman Siege of Corfu (1798–1799) ends with the surrender of the French garrison, bringing an end to the first period of French rule in the Ionian Islands (1797–1799).

events.title: War of the Second Coalition
events.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Siege of Jaffa – Napoleon captures Jaffa in Palestine from the Ottomans and his troops proceed to kill more than 2,000 Albanian captives.

events.title: War of the Second Coalition
events.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Victory of Franjo Jelačić and the Austrian army over the French army of André Masséna at the Battle of Feldkirch.

events.title: French Revolutionary Wars
events.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: The Battle of Cassano takes place outside of Milan, as Russian and Austrian troops commanded by General Alexander Suvorov rout the French Army under the command of General Jean Moreau.

events.title: Second Congress of Rastatt
events.blurb: Two French diplomats to the Second Congress of Rastatt are killed and another badly injured by Austrian cavalry, as they tried to leave the town. An inquiry was held, which blamed French emigres.

events.title: Siege of Acre (1799)
events.blurb: The Siege of Acre ends after two months; Napoleon's attempt to widen his Middle Eastern campaign into Syria is frustrated by Ottoman forces, and he withdraws to Egypt.

events.title: War of the Second Coalition
events.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Battle of Winterthur – Habsburg forces secure control of north-east Switzerland from the French Army of the Danube.

events.title: War of the Second Coalition
events.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: First Battle of Zurich – Four days of fighting ends in victory for Archduke Charles and the Austrian army over the French army under André Masséna.

events.title: War of the Second Coalition
events.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Battle of the Trebbia – The beginning of the battle that marked the debacle of Étienne Macdonald's French army. Suvorov scores a comprehensive victory.

events.title: French Revolutionary Wars
events.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Action of 18 June 1799 – A French frigate squadron, under Rear-admiral Perrée, is captured by the British fleet under Lord Keith, off Toulon.

events.title: Ranjit Singh's men take their positions outside Lahore
events.blurb: Ranjit Singh's men take their positions outside Lahore.

events.title: In the Egyptian port city of Rosetta, French Captain Pierre Bouchard finds the…
events.blurb: In the Egyptian port city of Rosetta, French Captain Pierre Bouchard finds the Rosetta Stone.

events.title: Battle of Abukir
events.blurb: Battle of Abukir: French forces under Napoleon Bonaparte defeat 20,000 Ottoman Mamluk troops under Mustafa Pasha at Abukir.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte leaves the command of the French army (some 10,000 men) to…
events.blurb: Napoleon Bonaparte leaves the command of the French army (some 10,000 men) to General Jean-Baptiste Kléber.

events.title: War of the Second Coalition
events.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Anglo-Russian invasion of Holland – Britain and Russia send an expedition to the Batavian Republic.

events.title: Anglo-Russian invasion of Holland
events.blurb: Anglo-Russian invasion of Holland: Battle of Krabbendam – The Russo-British expedition force defends its initial gains from attacks by Franco-Dutch forces.

events.title: War of the Second Coalition
events.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Battle of Mannheim – Victory of Archduke Charles and the Austrian army over a French force under Jacques Léonard Muller

events.title: Anglo-Russian invasion of Holland

events.blurb: The Dutch East India Company's charter is allowed to expire by the Batavian Republic.

events.title: April 12

events.title: Gia Long

events.title: October 15

events.title: August 2
events.blurb: August 2 – In a plebiscite, Napoleon Bonaparte is confirmed as the First Consul of France.

events.title: William Wordsworth
events.blurb: July 31 – William Wordsworth, leaving London for Dover and Calais with his sister Dorothy, witnesses the early morning scene which he captures in his sonnet "Composed upon Westminster Bridge".

events.title: March 11
events.blurb: March 11 – The Rosetta Stone is presented to the Society of Antiquaries of London, which in turn presents it to the British Museum.

events.title: Éleuthère Irénée du Pont
events.blurb: July 19 – Éleuthère Irénée du Pont founds E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company, the modern DuPont chemical company, as a gunpowder manufactory near Wilmington, Delaware.

events.blurb: The Rosetta Stone is brought to England by Colonel Tomkyns Hilgrove Turner, who arrives at Portsmouth on the captured French frigate L'Egyptiane.

events.blurb: Madame Marie Tussaud first exhibits her wax sculptures in London, having been commissioned, during the Reign of Terror in France, to make death masks of the victims.

events.blurb: The first account of Thomas Wedgwood's experiments in photography is published by Humphry Davy in the Journal of the Royal Institution in London. Since a fixative for the image has not yet been developed, the early photographs quickly fade.

events.blurb: John Dalton, British scientist, begins using symbols to represent the atoms of different elements.

events.blurb: The proposed Twelfth Amendment to the United States Constitution, requiring that electoral ballots distinctly list the choice for president and the choice for vice president,

events.blurb: John Wedgwood founds the Royal Horticultural Society.

events.blurb: The Dutch Cape Colony capitulates to British forces, the origin of its status as a colony within the British Empire.

events.blurb: Stéphanie de Beauharnais, adopted daughter of Emperor Napoleon I, marries Prince Karl Ludwig Friedrich of Baden.

events.blurb: Future President of the United States Andrew Jackson fights his third duel, killing lawyer Charles Dickinson following a dispute over payment of a forfeit.

events.blurb: Louis Bonaparte is appointed as King of Holland by his brother, Emperor Napoleon, replacing the Batavian Republic.

events.blurb: 1806 Birgu polverista explosion: A gunpowder magazine explosion in Birgu, Malta kills around 200 people.

events.blurb: Battle of Jena–Auerstedt: At Jena, Napoleon defeats the Prussian army of Prince Hohenlohe, while at Auerstedt, Marshal Davout defeats the main Prussian army under Karl Wilhelm Ferdinand, Duke of Brunswick (who is fatally wounded).

events.blurb: The last major Prussian field force, under Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher, surrenders to the French near Lübeck. Frederick William III has by this time fled to Memel in East Prussia.
